items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
UPI Gets MDR Makeover
After a decade of free UPI payments, NPCI will now impose an MDR for select high-value transactions starting October 15. The move marks UPI’s most consequential monetisation shift yet. Can the infrastructure commercialise without compromising its inclusivity?
The New UPI Math: Under the framework, P2M UPI payments above ₹2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above. The charge will apply to merchants, not customers. Banks have been instructed to prevent merchants from passing on the costs to end users.
Meanwhile, P2P payments remain free, while small merchants receiving up to ₹1 Lakh a month through QR-code transactions will continue to face zero MDR.
Paying For The Rails: The policy acknowledges a reality UPI has long deferred. Transaction volumes are setting new records, but infrastructure, cybersecurity and operational expenses are rising alongside them. MDR revenue will be split among issuer banks, payment service providers and app providers. This will create a clearer financial incentive for the ecosystem to maintain and upgrade the network that supports billions of transactions every month.
A Boost For Fintechs: For fintechs, MDR could finally turn UPI scale into a predictable revenue opportunity. The existing market has for years struggled to build viable economics. A shared revenue pool could fund fraud detection, encryption and rural payment infrastructure, while reducing the sector’s dependence on annual government incentives.
The Merchant Question: The framework protects small merchants on paper, but larger businesses will now have to absorb a new cost of accepting UPI payments. The risk is that merchants may find indirect ways to recover it through pricing, even if direct pass-through is prohibited.
All said and done, the viability of the regime and its impact on inclusivity will be tested at the checkout counter. So, what does this new MDR regime mean for India’s digital payments ecosystem? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Fibe Gets SEBI Nod For IPO
The markets regulator has given its nod to the lending tech startup to move ahead with its public issue. SEBI issued its final observation on the offer documents of Fibe parent Social Worth Technologies Ltd yesterday.
Fibe filed its DRHP with the market regulator in June for an IPO, which will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹750 Cr and an offer-for-sale component of more than 4 Cr equity shares. TPG and Norwest will offload their stakes in the OFS.
Founded in 2015, Fibe operates a lending platform that offers personal loans and purpose-driven financing solutions. Having raised $300 Mn to date, the startup closed FY26 with a profit of ₹257.5 Cr against an operating revenue of ₹1,584.6 Cr.
Flam Nets $40 Mn
The AI-powered content platform has raised around ₹383 Cr in its Series B round led by QED Investors. The round also comprised a “small” secondary transaction.
Founded in 2021, Flam enables enterprises to create immersive, interactive experiences for marketing and product visualisation. The startup claims to hold more than 15 patents and caters to 100 customers globally. It is eyeing $100 Mn in ARR by next year.
The fundraise comes as the concept of mixed reality is gaining traction as D2C and ecommerce players deploy XR offerings for marketing and engaging their audiences. The broader Indian AR market is projected to become a $11 Bn opportunity by 2031.
Rebel Foods’ FY26 Show
The cloud kitchen unicorn managed to trim its net losses by 16.3% YoY to ₹281.8 Cr in FY26. This came on the back of operating revenue rising 20.7% YoY to ₹1,951.6 Cr in the fiscal under review.
Buoyed by stronger engagement, continued improvements across the board and margin expansion, Rebel Foods also managed to narrow its EBITDA by 50% YoY to ₹62.4 Cr in FY26. However, expenses continued to bite and rose 14.1% YoY to ₹2,265 Cr.
Founded in 2011, Rebel Foods operates 45+ food brands and serves customers across 120+ cities in India, the UAE and the UK. It has raised $773 Mn in funding to date. It has also been recalibrating its financial and operational strategy with an eye on an IPO soon.
PayU’s Legal Battle With Visa
The Delhi HC has directed the RBI to mediate a dispute involving the Prosus-owned fintech platform, Visa and other acquiring banks. Till the next hearing on October 27, the HC directed all parties to maintain status quo on claims arising from past transactions.
The Court has also barred acquiring banks from making further deductions from PayU’s settlements while the mediation is underway. It also restrained Visa from issuing final determinations on pending IRF claims concerning past transactions.
The case pertains to interchange reimbursement fee claims arising from the alleged misclassification of merchant category codes. PayU claims that it does not assign MCCs, adding that it is the responsibility of acquiring banks to assign the appropriate codes.
CCPA Orders Probe Into Apple
The Central Consumer Protection Authority has ordered a detailed investigation into the OEM’s software warranty terms. This is part of wider probe into the iOS 18 update, which damaged iPhone functionality and compelled users to pay heavy sums for repairs.
In response, Apple has publicly said that it primarily sells hardware and that no tech company across the globe offers warranty on software.
Separately, CCPA has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on mobility unicorn Rapido for misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices and dark patterns. It is also under the radar for prompting users to pay more before their rides are confirmed.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Serendipity Space Build A Pharma Factory In Orbit?
Drugs must be manufactured with consistent crystal structure, purity and stability. But gravity can complicate crystallisation on Earth. Serendipity Space is exploring whether microgravity can improve the process through autonomous pharmaceutical factories aboard satellites.
The Orbital Factory: Founded in 2024, Serendipity Space is developing reusable satellites for in-space pharmaceutical manufacturing. Its long-term plan is to process drug and protein compounds in low Earth orbit and return the resulting material to Earth.
The Alchemy Module: At the centre of the startup’s tech stack is Alchemy, an autonomous pharmaceutical-processing module designed to grow drug and protein crystals in microgravity. With less gravity-driven convection and sedimentation, the startup believes crystals could form more uniformly, potentially improving properties such as solubility, stability and formulation.
A Near-Space Proof Point: In March 2026, Serendipity Space flight-tested an orbital-class prototype from the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research’s Balloon Facility in Hyderabad. The stratospheric-balloon mission tested Alchemy’s autonomous operations, avionics, thermal protection and controlled recovery systems.
Now focused on developing its satellite platform and autonomous crystallisation technology, can Serendipity make orbital pharmaceutical manufacturing a viable business?
Infographic Of The Day
New-age mithai wallahs are reinventing everything from packaging to flavour, while legacy names like Haldiram’s, Bikaji and Jiwaram hold their ground as the OGs of the category. So, why is India’s packaged sweets market booming?

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Apple telah memastikan iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, dan iPhone 18 Pro Max akan segara hadir di Indonesia. Hal ini diperkuat dengan ketiga HP baru Apple tersebut tercatat mengantongi nilai TKDN 40 persen.
Meski harga resmi dan jadwal penjualan ponsel ini masih belum diumumkan secara langsung, bocoran tentang kemungkinan harga iPhone Duo dan iPhone 18 Pro series.
Informasi tersebut dibagikan Apple enthusiast Bhaguz Hernawan melalui akun X pribadinya di @bhaguz_403. Dalam cuitannya, Bhaguz menyebut kemungkinan iPhone 18 Pro dibanderol mulai Rp 27.999.000.
Baca Juga: Pelatnas Timnas Esports Indonesia Disiapkan hingga 2027, Ini Agenda Besar PB ESI
Sedangkan untuk iPhone 18 Pro Max mulai dari Rp 29.999.000. Lalu untuk harga iPhone Duo dibanderol mulai Rp 44.999.000.
Apple sendiri belum mengumumkan harga iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, dan iPhone 18 Pro Max di Tanah Air. Karena itu, angka yang dibagikan Bhaguz ini masih sebatas bocoran atau perkiraan hingga ada pengumuman resmi dari Apple atau jaringan reseller.
Jika bocoran tersebut benar, iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max bakal mengalami kenaikan harga cukup besar dibanding generasi sebelumnya. Sedangkan harga iPhone Duo akan menjadi kategori baru.
Saat pertama dijual di Indonesia pada Oktober 2025, harga iPhone 17 Pro 256GB dibanderol mulai dari Rp 23.749.000. Sedangkan untuk varian iPhone 17 Pro Max 256GB dijual dengan harga Rp 25.749.000.
Berikut perbandingan Harga iPhone 17 Pro Series dengan iPhone 18 Pro Series:
ModelHarga Generasi SebelumnyaBocoran Harga BaruSelisih
iPhone 17 Pro → iPhone 18 ProRp 23.749.000Rp 27.999.000Rp 4.250.000
iPhone 17 Pro Max → iPhone 18 Pro MaxRp 25.749.000Rp 29.999.000Rp 4.250.000
Jika bocoran harga ini benar, maka harga iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max ini naik sekitar Rp 4.250.000. Kenaikan tersebut juga sejalan dengan perubahan harga di pasar Amerika Serikat.
Meski demikian, harga global tidak bisa dijadikan patokan langsung untuk Indonesia. Harga iPhone Duo dan iPhone 18 Pro Series lokal dapat dipengaruhi berbagai faktor, termasuk struktur harga Apple untuk setiap pasar.
iPhone Duo Bisa Jadi iPhone Termahal di Indonesia
Dari ketiga model tersebut, iPhone Duo menjadi perangkat yang paling berbeda. Ini merupakan iPhone pertama dengan desain layar lipat yang pernah dirilis Apple. 
Ketika dibuka, perangkat tersebut memiliki layar dalam 7,6 inci, sementara layar luar berukuran 5,4 inci. Apple membekalinya dengan chip A20 Pro yang juga digunakan pada iPhone 18 Pro.
Jika bocoran harga iPhone Duo Rp 44.999.000 benar, model 256GB saja memiliki selisih Rp 15 juta dibanding kemungkinan harga awal iPhone 18 Pro Max yang berada di Rp 29.999.000.
Posisi harga tersebut juga menarik jika dibandingkan dengan jajaran iPhone tahun lalu. Ketika iPhone 17 Pro Max pertama kali dipasarkan di Indonesia, varian tertingginya dengan penyimpanan 2TB dibanderol Rp 43.999.000. 
Artinya, bocoran harga awal iPhone Duo 256GB Rp1 juta lebih tinggi dibanding harga peluncuran iPhone 17 Pro Max 2TB.
Harga iPhone Duo dinilai Rp 44,999 juta juga tidak terlalu jauh dari negara tetangga. Di Singapura, Apple menetapkan harga iPhone Duo 256GB sebesar SGD3.099, setara sekitar Rp 43,1 juta berdasarkan konversi saat harga diumumkan. Di Amerika Serikat, perangkat yang sama dibanderol mulai USD 1.999.
Tetap saja, konversi harga negara lain tidak bisa digunakan untuk memastikan harga Indonesia karena struktur harga, pajak, distribusi, serta kebijakan Apple dapat berbeda di setiap pasar.
iPhone Duo dan iPhone 18 Pro Sudah Kantongi TKDN
iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max akan hadir di Indonesia, tetapi Apple belum mengumumkan tanggal penjualan. (Foto: Apple)
Kehadiran ketiga model tersebut di Indonesia sendiri bukan lagi sebatas spekulasi.
Apple telah mencantumkan iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max sebagai produk yang akan segera hadir di Indonesia. Hal yang sama juga tercantum dalam pengumuman resmi iPhone Duo untuk pasar Indonesia.
Selain itu, tiga perangkat dengan nomor model A3714, A3717, dan A3720 telah tercatat atas nama PT Apple Indonesia dengan nilai TKDN 40 persen. Ketiganya masing-masing dikaitkan dengan iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, dan iPhone Duo.
Namun, sertifikasi TKDN belum berarti perangkat bisa langsung dipasarkan. Masih ada proses sertifikasi perangkat telekomunikasi yang perlu diselesaikan sebelum penjualan resmi dapat dilakukan.
Untuk iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max, Bhaguz sebelumnya juga menyebut kemungkinan penjualan di Indonesia dimulai pada 16 Oktober 2026. Hingga saat ini Apple belum mengumumkan tanggal tersebut secara resmi.
Sementara jadwal iPhone Duo di Indonesia masih belum diketahui. Meski perangkat lipat tersebut akan membuka pre-order global pada 16 Oktober, Apple Indonesia sejauh ini hanya menyebut iPhone Duo akan “segera hadir”.
Dengan harga resmi yang belum diumumkan, angka Rp27.999.000 untuk iPhone 18 Pro, Rp29.999.000 untuk iPhone 18 Pro Max, dan Rp44.999.000 untuk iPhone Duo masih harus menunggu konfirmasi. Namun jika bocoran tersebut akurat, bukan hanya seri Pro yang akan mengalami kenaikan harga cukup besar—iPhone Duo juga akan membawa Apple ke kelas harga baru, mendekati Rp45 juta untuk varian awal.

items.title: A closer look at the Zero Rated Access Initiative, by Okoh Aihe
items.summary:
The NCC programme wasn’t part of my schedule last week but the insistence of a young employee drew me to the Hilton, venue of the programme, and I left very appreciative that I found my way there. items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
The NCC programme wasn’t part of my schedule last week but the insistence of a young employee drew me to the Hilton, venue of the programme, and I left very appreciative that I found my way there. Sometimes, you need to clear your schedule to do certain things. This was one of them. As I write now, I am still checking my body to see whether there are some tiny pieces of confetti that rained down at the launch of the Zero Rated Access Initiative by the Commission’s Board.
I was only too happy to see history unfold and, all the while, contemplating how this will affect the education sector and the future of the young ones who will inherit this nation. Yet, this is a project creatively minted by the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) and the telecommunications operators that reached out to the Ministry of Education with life-transforming news of giving out free data to enable young Nigerians to access some education platforms free of charge. I have always written in this column that a good working relationship between top government functionaries, between ministries and their parastatals, between chief executives and their counterparts, and even between the National Assembly and agencies and industries, will generate something great for the nation. Last week, there was a demonstration of that, and what seems like a well-nurtured traction between NCC, under the Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, and the Ministry of Education, has led to something great that will positively transform young lives well beyond our time.
The idea behind the Zero Rated Access Initiative, according to the NCC Board, is to promote digital inclusion and enhance access to educational resources for students; thus prompting a valuable collaboration of the Federal Ministry of Education and other stakeholders, including the telecom operators, whose role provides the real oxygen for the entire process. One of its members, Rimini H. Makama, Executive Commissioner Stakeholder Management (ECSM), said at the launch on September 10, that the initiative is built to give every Nigerian learner a fair chance at digital education, pointing out that learning has moved online, prompting students to rely on online courses and digital libraries, among others, which all depend on connectivity that may be a scarce resource to some learners.
In her words: “The Zero-Rated Access Initiative exists to erase that line. Its principle is simple: no learner should be shut out of educational content because of where they live or what their family earns. By providing data allowances for approved educational platforms, it turns potential into opportunity, so that more young Nigerians can learn, research, build and acquire the skills a digital economy demands.” Dr Tunji Alausa, the Education Minister, who could hardly contain himself, declared excitedly, “Today’s launch represents much more than a telecommunications initiative. It is an education intervention. And most importantly, it is an investment in the future of millions of young Nigerians.”
He appealed for us to build a Nigeria where geography does not determine educational opportunity, where poverty does not prevent a child from accessing knowledge, but a country with an education system where technology becomes a great equaliser—opening doors, expanding possibilities and empowering every learner to realise his or her full potential. In simple terms, the Zero-Rated Access Initiative (ZRAI) is designed to give a data allowance of 100MB to 5 million learners or students at N100 per day. This comes to N15bn a month and totals a whopping N180bn a year for 5 million students. 
This amount can give a learning average of between 2 and 5 hours daily on education websites—Reading texts/PDFs and Google searches: 5–15 MB/hour (7–20 hours); online learning platforms (mostly text): 10–25 MB/hour (4–10 hours). For some of us who could only afford education because the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo offered free education through his party, UPN, and could hardly encounter a telephone until well into the university, the launch last Thursday meant so much. It was almost very emotional as it destroyed status, class, and privileges. I have seen so many young people condemn the initiative, saying 100MB is hardly a drop in the ocean. I think this needs an explanation. The Zero Rated Access Initiative is a major corporate social responsibility (CSR) package put together by the regulator and the telecom operators for Nigerian students because of a shared concern for those who suffer digital exclusion.
The NCC Board said the Initiative will go live on October 1, 2026, and reaffirmed its commitment to monitoring its sustainable implementation. Meanwhile, the Education Minister informed that the initiative will commence with learners at the senior secondary school level and tertiary institutions and subsequently expand to other categories of learners across the country. Some operators—Karl Toriola, CEO of MTN, Dinesh Balsingh of Airtel, and Obafemi Banigbe of T2 Mobile—addressed the launch virtually and promised continuing support and sustainability of the initiative. However, it was the industry representative at the event, Engr. Gbenga Adebayo, who is the chairman of the Association of Licensed Telecom Operators of Nigeria (ALTON), who further articulated the position of his members to this writer, shortly after the launch. “For a student,” he explained, “100MB can provide meaningful daily access to learning materials, examination preparation, research and educational platforms without worrying about the cost of data. The programme currently provides 100 MB of daily access to approved platforms, including the Ministry of Education platforms and WAEC learning resources.”
Adebayo is excited about the tripartite initiative, which, he said, “is essentially a partnership around a common national objective. The Ministry identifies and provides the educational content and platforms; NCC provides the regulatory coordination and oversight; and the operators provide the network infrastructure and connectivity that allow students and educators to access the content. So, it is a good example of government and industry working together to achieve digital inclusion and improve education.” He canvassed the position of ALTON members not to allow the initiative to flag or fail, saying, “They have willingly supported the programme because we believe that investing in education is investing in Nigeria’s future. But zero-rating has a real cost to the operators—it consumes network resources and creates an open-ended financial and operational obligation if participation and usage are not properly managed.” Adebayo argued that “sustainability of the initiative should not necessarily mean that the operators want a commercial return from the students. What we need is a fair, predictable and sustainable framework—including proper beneficiary registration or opt-in, user controls, monitoring of usage and mechanisms to prevent abuse. This ensures that the benefits reach genuine students and learners while allowing operators to continue investing in the networks on which the programme depends.”
“In short, the operators are saying: we are willing to support the national education agenda, but the programme must be designed in a way that can survive and be sustained. The objective is not to withdraw the benefit; it is to make sure we can keep providing it for the long term,” as he painted a picture of hope. In the week following the furore generated by New York City’s new guidelines and restrictions, limiting student screen time and technology use in public schools, including the use of AI, starting from September 2026, a move being watched by the rest of the United States, it was interesting to see whether such fears would haunt the introduction of the Zero Rated Access Initiative.
The Education Minister seems to have addressed such fears when he declared that Zero-rating should not mean indiscriminate access to every platform that describes itself as educational. The content made available to our children must be appropriate, credible, safe, and aligned with our educational objectives and curriculum, Alausa said.  However, beautiful as the initiative may look, I have my fears that it will exacerbate the digital divide immediately. Digital connectivity is poor in most rural parts of the country I have been to, and although the Board informed that infrastructure commitments by the operators are being met—8,526 out of 12,179 sites built recently to expand network coverage, capacity and quality of experience (QoE)—I am constrained to wonder whether vandalism of telecommunications infrastructure is not happening at a faster pace. 
Apart from the pervasive insecurity, telecom service delivery is sabotaged, even by state agencies. 
This will demand further rigorous planning by the regulator to build more alliances that can strengthen the industry and position operators to meet fresh demands from the state for its citizens. The Zero-Rated Access Initiative is a good one, but the guardrails need to be strong enough to lead to a future that looks very promising.
The post A closer look at the Zero Rated Access Initiative, by Okoh Aihe appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe
The Gombe State Government has reiterated its determination to improve the water, sanitation and hygiene, WASH, sector and achieve an open-defecation-free state.
The commitment was reaffirmed as the Gombe State Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency, RUWASSA, under the Sustainable Urban and Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene, SURWASH, programme, intensified sensitisation and mobilisation campaigns across Local Government Areas that have claimed Open Defecation Free, ODF, status.
The campaign commenced with a mega rally in Nafada Local Government Area, where RUWASSA engaged traditional rulers, community leaders, government officials and other stakeholders to strengthen community ownership of sanitation initiatives and sustain hygiene practices ahead of the ODF validation exercise.
The RUWASSA delegation, led by its General Manager, Engr. Mohammed Ahmed Gibrimu, FNSE, FNICE, who was represented by the Sector Lead, WASH, Yahaya Umaru, began the mobilisation at the Nafada Local Government Secretariat before proceeding to the palace of the Emir of Nafada.
Speaking at the palace, Umaru, who conveyed the General Manager’s message, commended the Emir of Nafada, HRH Alhaji Muhammadu Dadum Hamza, as well as residents and stakeholders in the LGA for their collective efforts towards improving sanitation and hygiene.
He said RUWASSA, in collaboration with the local government and other stakeholders, had continued to provide technical and institutional support towards achieving and sustaining ODF status in the area.
According to him, following Nafada LGA’s declaration of ODF status, RUWASSA had submitted the required documentation to the National Task Group on Sanitation, NTGS, for review ahead of the anticipated validation exercise.
He urged residents to sustain the momentum by maintaining proper sanitation and hygiene practices before, during and after the validation exercise.
Also speaking, the Sanitation Specialist, Alhaji Hussaini Abdulkadir, commended the people and stakeholders of Nafada for the progress recorded, stressing the need for sustained public awareness and, where necessary, effective enforcement of sanitation laws.
Earlier, in a welcome address, the Chairman of Nafada LGA, Hon. Babangida Adamu Jigawa, represented by his Deputy, Hon. Gambo Yahaya, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his continued support for the WASH sector.
He also appreciated RUWASSA for its technical support, assuring that the local government was prepared and committed to a successful ODF validation exercise.
Responding, the Emir of Nafada, HRH Alhaji Muhammadu Dadum Hamza, welcomed the RUWASSA delegation and commended the agency for prioritising Nafada in its sanitation and hygiene interventions.
The traditional ruler noted that while attaining ODF status was a significant milestone, the ultimate objective remained the protection of the health and wellbeing of residents.
He urged the people of the emirate to support and sustain the sanitation campaign, disclosing that sanctions had already been introduced against persons who violate sanitation laws.
According to him, offenders would face a fine of N10,000, in addition to community service or heavy labour.
As part of the mobilisation exercise, the Emir directed the eight district heads in the area to appear before the gathering and provide updates on the preparedness of their respective communities for the ODF validation.
Reports and testimonies presented by traditional and community leaders indicated a high level of preparedness across the LGA and reinforced the area’s readiness for the anticipated validation exercise.
The mega rally attracted government officials, WASH stakeholders, traditional and community leaders, civil society organisations, security agencies and members of the media.
The participation of the Makadan Sarki also added traditional colour to the mobilisation, which formed part of RUWASSA’s broader efforts to strengthen sanitation and hygiene practices, consolidate ODF achievements and contribute to the realisation of a cleaner, healthier and open-defecation-free Gombe State.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
ABUJA — President of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has said petrol is relatively cheaper in Nigeria than in neighbouring countries, a price difference he said has continued to encourage cross-border smuggling.
Dangote spoke in an interview with Arise Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about rising petrol prices in Nigeria.
He said the cost of petrol should be considered in relation to prices in neighbouring countries, noting that consumers in some of those countries pay between 30 and 50 per cent more.
“Expensive is relative in the sense that today, for a lot of them, there’s ignorance also. What they need to do is to ask what the neighbour’s price is,” he said.
According to Dangote, the price differential creates an incentive for traders to move petrol across Nigeria’s borders for higher returns.
“I don’t know if you know that there’s still a lot of smuggling of the same petrol we are producing to our neighbouring countries because those neighbouring countries are about 30 percent to 50 percent more expensive than Nigeria,” he said.
He cited Niger Republic as an example, saying petrol there was about 20 to 25 per cent more expensive than in Nigeria at a domestic price of N1,350 per litre.
“So what business are you going to do that will make you a 25 percent return?” he asked.
Dangote said the price difference could encourage traders to divert petrol intended for domestic markets to border communities for resale.
He also spoke about the potential impact of the ongoing crisis in the Middle East on energy supplies, saying availability could become a greater concern.
The businessman, however, assured Nigerians that the Dangote Refinery would continue supplying the domestic market.
“We will make sure that Nigeria will be fully delivered. We will deliver to Nigeria. Nigerians don’t need to worry,” he said.
“There will not be any shortage from our own part. There won’t be any shortage. There will not be any queues.
“And we’ll make sure that we keep satisfying the market.”
The comments came after petrol prices reportedly increased at some filling stations on Monday, with prices reaching about N1,400 per litre in Lagos and N1,450 per litre in Abuja.
Policy inconsistency, power supply
Dangote also identified what he described as inconsistent government policies and inadequate electricity supply as major challenges facing businesses in Nigeria.
“The greatest problem, there are two, which are still existing. One is inconsistencies in government policies. The second one is to do with lack of electricity,” he said.
He said the cost of alternative sources of energy, particularly diesel, was putting pressure on manufacturers and making production increasingly expensive.
“You cannot manufacture goods with diesel. You can see where diesel is today. You can’t even produce bread and make money today. So, we have to look at that today,” Dangote said.
The businessman also highlighted Africa’s electricity access deficit, saying about 600 million people on the continent lack access to electricity.
“We must make sure, even for us, really, as Africans, we cannot sit down and see that everybody is complaining. 600 million of our people, they actually don’t have power,” he said.
Dangote said the scale of the electricity challenge had prompted some African business leaders to consider taking direct action to help address the continent’s power deficit.

items.content: Washington: The six-month-old U.S. war against Iran has cost $38 billion so far and that amount is projected to rise by $3 billion a month, Congress' nonpartisan bookkeeper reported on Tuesday, as the Trump administration searches for ways to end the conflict and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz.The war is expected to increase inflation by 0.5% in the first three months of 2027, according to the Congressional Budget Office accounting, which totaled expenses through August 1.Also read: Trump’s ‘little war’ with Iran just got a lot biggerThe mounting costs have strained U.S. munitions stockpiles and driven up energy prices, raising concerns about the country's ability to respond to other potential conflicts and adding pressure on an already stretched federal budget.The cost was close to the $37.5 billion that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth reported at a Senate hearing on July 21.The budget office said the majority of the costs stem from the rapid drawdown of munitions, estimating that it could take five years to replenish U.S. stockpiles. Reuters reported in August that the U.S. had used "virtually all" of its long-range precision missiles during the war.The Department of Defense did not cooperate with congressional financial auditors, CBO reported.White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly described President Donald Trump's attacks on Iran as "decisive action" to prevent Tehran from harming U.S. personnel or interests. She said in a statement that the U.S. military has "more than enough munitions, ammo, and stockpiles to serve all of the Commander-in-Chief's strategic goals and beyond."Chief Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell disputed the report's findings of munitions shortages and said, "We have everything required to strike at the time and place of the president's choosing."The cost inquiry was conducted at the request of the top Democrat on the U.S. House of Representatives Budget Committee, Brendan Boyle of Pennsylvania."Donald Trump's disastrous war in Iran has already taken the lives of brave American servicemembers and left others wounded," Boyle said in a statement."Beyond that human toll, this nonpartisan CBO report makes clear that the war has also cost American taxpayers tens of billions of dollars and counting, while continuing to drive up costs."Eighteen U.S. military service members have died in the Iran war.The report did not include costs of recent strikes on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and attacks on U.S. military installations in the region. It also did not factor in the borrowing expenses associated with financing the war, which could add tens of billions of dollars to the total cost.IMPACT ON US READINESS The CBO accounting found the war could have sprawling consequences for the U.S. defense posture and the domestic economy.The deficit in critical munitions, including missile interceptors, risks hampering the Pentagon's response in the event of another major conflict, such as potential hostilities involving China and Taiwan, CBO said.At the July hearing in the Senate, Hegseth pleaded for nearly $90 billion in emergency funding to restock munitions supplies."Without these funds, we face critical shortfalls," Hegseth said.The Pentagon's inspector general reported this week that Iran had damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings on U.S. bases in the Middle East as well as aircraft including fighter jets, refueling planes and drones.It put the war cost through June 19 at $33.4 billion, saying the amount included about $184 million in damages to U.S. diplomatic facilities from Iranian strikes.Also read: Iran rejects Trump talks, says no negotiations until its conditions are metEnergy shocks caused by attacks in the Strait of Hormuz - the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil traveled before the war - and on energy facilities in neighboring Gulf countries have sharply increased prices for consumers and global producers.The rising cost of the war also threatens to weigh on deteriorating U.S. fiscal health. The nation's total public debt surpassed $40 trillion in August.Trump regularly contrasts the Iran war with the U.S. invasions of Iraq and Afghanistan that followed the September 11, 2001, attacks.The eight-year U.S. war in Iraq, which involved more than 100,000 ground troops at its peak, cost $2 trillion, Reuters reported. The two-decade-long U.S. conflict in Afghanistan, which also involved more than 100,000 troops at its most intense, cost $2.3 trillion, according to Brown University's Costs of War project.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi
The Nigeria Police Force (NPF) is set to host the sixth Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers (CARSPO 2026) in Imo State from September 21 to 24, with election security expected to feature prominently in discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The conference, themed “Developing a Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections,” is expected to bring together senior police officers, security experts, policymakers, election stakeholders and representatives of relevant institutions to review election security arrangements and identify emerging challenges.
CARSPO 2026 is being organised by the Nigeria Police Force in partnership with Lenders Consult International.
According to the organisers, discussions at the four-day conference will focus on the development of a security roadmap for the 2027 elections, with issues including election-related violence, intelligence gathering, inter-agency cooperation, deployment strategies, technology in election policing and public confidence in the electoral process.
Senior police officers from across the country, representatives of government agencies, civil society organisations, election management bodies, development partners and security experts are expected to participate.
The organisers said the conference would provide an opportunity for stakeholders to assess existing approaches to election security and consider measures for improving coordination and operational preparedness before, during and after elections.
Lenders Consult International also reaffirmed its partnership with the Nigeria Police Force, saying it had worked with the Force since 2019 on sponsorship and operational support initiatives.
Ahead of the conference, the organisers said proactive planning, training and inter-agency coordination remained important to election security, given the range of security challenges that can arise during electoral activities.
The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, is expected to lead discussions at the conference and provide strategic direction on the Force’s preparations for future electoral engagements.
Disu stressed the role of the police in maintaining security during elections.
“Stability of the electoral process largely depends on the Police as the lead agency in internal democracy,” the IGP stated.
He also emphasised the responsibility of the Force to provide a secure environment for the conduct of elections.
The organisers said recommendations from CARSPO 2026 would inform the Nigeria Police Force’s preparations and operational planning for election security ahead of the 2027 general elections.

items.title: Desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition Diungkap, Terinspirasi Hogwarts
items.summary:
Setelah merilis teaser smartphone edisi kolaborasi spesialnya, realme akhirnya mengungkap secara penuh tampilan desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition. Menggandeng Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products, smartphone tersebut siap dijual pada pekan depan, atau lebih tepatnya 21 September 2026. Lantas seperti apa tampilan perangkatnya? Tidak hanya spesial pada desain perangkat, namun juga kelengkapannya.
Ya, ini bukanlah pertama kali realme berkolaborasi dengan Warner Bros. untuk menghadirkan sebuah smartphone edisi spesial—pada generasi sebelumnya, hadir realme 15 Pro Game of Thrones Limited Edition yang juga tampil eksklusif dan dijual dalam jumlah terbatas. Tentunya dengan inspirasi dari Harry Potter, edisi baru kali ini ingin membawa konsumen alias pengguna muda untuk seolah berada di dalam dunia sihir ikonis.
Sesuai namanya, selain dari aspek desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition masih identik dengan varian standar, yang merupakan varian lebih sederhana dari opsi real
items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
tags: Desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition
items.content:
Setelah merilis teaser smartphone edisi kolaborasi spesialnya, realme akhirnya mengungkap secara penuh tampilan desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition. Menggandeng Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products, smartphone tersebut siap dijual pada pekan depan, atau lebih tepatnya 21 September 2026. Lantas seperti apa tampilan perangkatnya? Tidak hanya spesial pada desain perangkat, namun juga kelengkapannya.
Ya, ini bukanlah pertama kali realme berkolaborasi dengan Warner Bros. untuk menghadirkan sebuah smartphone edisi spesial—pada generasi sebelumnya, hadir realme 15 Pro Game of Thrones Limited Edition yang juga tampil eksklusif dan dijual dalam jumlah terbatas. Tentunya dengan inspirasi dari Harry Potter, edisi baru kali ini ingin membawa konsumen alias pengguna muda untuk seolah berada di dalam dunia sihir ikonis.
Sesuai namanya, selain dari aspek desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition masih identik dengan varian standar, yang merupakan varian lebih sederhana dari opsi realme 16 Pro+. Meski begitu, tetap andalkan teknologi kamera LumaColor yang optimalkan penangkapan warna hingga detail, untuk kualitas portrait lebih baik.

Seperti yang terlihat pada visual di atas, desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition tampil menggunakan sentuhan warna yang memang identik dengan nuansa Hogwarts—realme sendiri menyebutnya dengan “The Hogwarts Inspired Design”, di mana pada beberapa bagian bodi belakang disematkan sejumlah elemen ikonik yang menjadi sentuhan detail-detail menarik sebagai sebuah smartphone kolaborasi eksklusif.
Permukaan bodi belakang pada desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition didominasi oleh warna cokelat, dengan pola dan tekstur khusus, dirancang menyerupai kulit premium dalam motif Argyle yang terinspirasi dari adegan Wizard’s Chess. Bagian ini dirancang untuk menghidupkan estetika klasik dunia sihir di dalam Harry Potter sendiri, dengan lambing Hogwarts yang tercetak besar pada bagian tengah.
Selain lambang ikonik yang cukup mendominasi, bagian sisi kiri atas desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition tampil berkilau, di mana Metal Mirror Camera Deco hadir dengan aksen khusus yang mereplikasi mata burung hantu ikonik di Harry Potter, yakni Hedwig. Warnanya yang cerah dan berkilau dinilai mampu memberikan impresi rasa semangat ketika dipandang.
Menariknya, bagian yang membuat desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition spesial, tidak hanya sebatas permukaan bodi belakangnya saja. Pada sisi samping alias bingkai perangkat, selain juga punya warna keemasan, juga terdapat slogan “Welcome to Hogwarts” yang tercetak untuk sentuhan tambahan. Di luar desain perangkat, kemasan alias Gift Box realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition juga dibuat eksklusif.
Tersedia hanya 5000 unit di seluruh dunia, kotak sekolah yang terinspirasi dari Hogwarts tersebut hadir sebagai replika berukuran nyata 1:1. Di dalamnya, terdapat sebuah paket Hogwarts Welcome Pack, berisi sejumlah merchandise eksklusif. Mulai dari surat penerimaan Hogwarts dan tiket kereta, pembatas buku dengan lambang Hogwarts, kartu pos dengan karakter khusus, hingga casing smartphone dengan emboss logo Hogwarts.
Spesifikasi realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition Tetap Sama dengan Versi Standar
Resmi hadir di Indonesia pada 21 September 2026, spesifikasi realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition bakal dibuat identik seperti varian standar. Di belakang, disematkan sensor utama 200MP yang ditemani sensor ultra-wide dan kamera selfie 50MP di depan, diperkuat algoritma LumaColor Camera terbaru, dan realme turut memberikan kemampuan potret andal hingga 4x lossless zoom.

Di sisi depan, disematkan layar AMOLED 144Hz yang mendukung tingkat kecerahan maksimum sampai 6500 nits, dengan keempat sisi bezel yang dibuat lebih ramping.
Dan tidak hanya tampil eksklusif, desain realme 16 Pro Harry Potter Edition juga tetap diperkuat dengan sertifikasi hingga IP69K, yang membuatnya tidak hanya tahan dari debu, namun juga air bertekanan tinggi, bahkan dengan mode fotografi bawah air khusus. items.content:
By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin
The Federal Government has commissioned a TETFund/Renewed Hope Initiative-backed ICT Experience Centre at the Kwara State University (KWASU), Malete, to equip Nigerian youths with digital skills needed to thrive in a modern and competitive world.
Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, who was represented at the commissioning on Tuesday by the wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima, said the initiative aligned with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration, particularly its focus on youth empowerment, education, innovation and economic transformation.
She said the President was committed to creating opportunities that would equip Nigerian youths with the knowledge and skills required to compete in a rapidly changing world.
According to her, the ICT Experience Centre was a testament to the Federal Government’s commitment to advancing education, promoting digital inclusion and enhancing graduate employability.
“The TETFund/Renewed Hope Initiative ICT Experience Centre we are commissioning today represents opportunity, innovation, knowledge and the future of young people in Kwara State and beyond,” she said.
She explained that the facility was designed as a modern technology centre equipped with an ICT laboratory, interactive digital displays, conference facilities and exhibition spaces to provide an environment for learning, creativity, research and technological advancement.
KWASU is one of six tertiary institutions selected for the pilot phase of the intervention, with one institution representing each of the country’s six geopolitical zones.
Tinubu said similar centres had been commissioned at Ekiti State University on May 28, University of Cross River State on September 4 and Anambra State Polytechnic on September 10.
She added that the centres at Kaduna State University and Taraba State University would be commissioned soon.
According to her, the next phase of the intervention would cover 15 institutions in Adamawa, Bayelsa, Borno, Delta, Edo, Enugu, Imo, Katsina, Nasarawa, Niger, Ondo, Osun, Rivers, Yobe and Zamfara states, where construction is ongoing.
She said the expansion demonstrated the administration’s commitment to ensuring that more Nigerian youths, regardless of their locations, had access to digital learning opportunities.
Tinubu urged students to take ownership of the facility, maximise the opportunities it provides and use technology positively to improve their lives, communities and the nation.
Earlier, Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq said his administration’s vision was to ensure that every young person in the state acquired the skills and opportunities needed to succeed in a changing world.
He urged the university management to make judicious use of the facility, saying it should support students and help generate innovations, businesses, jobs and sustainable solutions to challenges facing communities.
“Technology and digital skills now shape how we learn, work and create opportunities. Our young people must, therefore, have access to the skills and techniques they need to compete anywhere in Nigeria and across the world,” AbdulRazaq said.
The governor said his administration would continue to invest in education and human capital development.
He noted that the state had expanded KWASU into a multi-campus institution, with the completion of its Osi and Ilesha Baruba campuses, while plans were underway for another campus in Ajase-Ipo.
Also speaking, the Executive Secretary of TETFund, Architect Sonny Echono, said the centres were being established across selected universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, with KWASU hosting the facility for the North-Central zone.
He said the initiative was designed to enhance graduate employability, foster innovation and position Nigeria to participate more effectively in the global technology-driven economy through practical training and digital skills acquisition.
Echono said the ICT Experience Centre would equip students and lecturers with critical digital skills in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics and software development.
“The centre being commissioned today is one of the foremost ICT Experience Centres being delivered across the country, and the third to be commissioned this year,” he said.
He added that the facility was equipped with modern digital devices, computer systems and relevant software to facilitate training, practical learning and skills development.
The centre, according to him, was also furnished and fully air-conditioned, with supporting power and municipal infrastructure.
The Vice-Chancellor of KWASU, Prof. Shaykh-Luqman Jimoh, described the facility as an investment in human capital, innovation, entrepreneurship and the future of Nigeria.
He said the centre would provide students with opportunities to develop practical digital skills and engage with contemporary technologies, while also serving as a hub for interdisciplinary engagement.
“The centre represents vision, belief and an investment in the Nigerian youth to better shape the future of our nation,” Jimoh said.
The post FG Commissions KWASU ICT Centre for Youths appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, ABUJA
A new report by ThinkBusiness Africa has warned that the proposed increase in Nigeria’s excise duty on sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs) could significantly raise prices of soft drinks, while its impact on obesity, diabetes and hypertension remains uncertain.
The report examined the proposed amendment to the Customs, Excise Tariff, Etc. (Consolidation) Act (CETA), which seeks to replace the existing N10-per-litre excise duty with an ad valorem tax.
According to the report, the proposed system could raise the effective tax burden to about N130 per litre based on prevailing beverage prices.
It said the change would make taxation dependent on the value of beverages rather than the volume produced, potentially increasing prices and placing additional administrative pressure on manufacturers.
Citing modelling by the Centre for the Study of the Economies of Africa (CSEA), as referenced in a submission by the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, ThinkBusiness Africa said a N130-per-litre tax could result in a 39 per cent increase in retail prices and a 29 per cent reduction in annual per capita consumption of SSBs.
It also projected that annual industry output could decline from N1.5 trillion to N1.1 trillion by 2030, while the production index could fall from 78 to about 40.
The report, however, stressed that the figures were modelled scenarios and did not represent observed outcomes.
On the public health implications, ThinkBusiness Africa acknowledged evidence that taxes on SSBs could reduce purchases of taxed beverages, but said evidence was less conclusive on whether such reductions would translate into lower rates of obesity, diabetes and hypertension.
“Chronic diseases are influenced by several factors, including overall diet, physical activity, income, education and access to healthcare,” the report said.
It also questioned the proposed use of beverage value as the basis for the tax, arguing that a levy directly linked to sugar content could better achieve the health objective.
The report cited South Africa and the United Kingdom, where sugar-related taxes are linked to sugar content or specified thresholds, saying such systems could encourage manufacturers to reformulate products and reduce sugar levels.
ThinkBusiness Africa said more than 133 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, with households already facing weak purchasing power and rising living costs.
“For many households, the immediate effect of a higher SSB tax will be straightforward: higher prices.
“For manufacturers, distributors and retailers, the consequences may include higher costs, weaker demand and pressure on production. This matters because the beverage sector is not an isolated industry. It is connected to agriculture, sugar supply, packaging, logistics, transportation, wholesale and retail,” it said.
The report also cited data from the National Sugar Development Council showing that total sugar consumption fell from about 1.72 million tonnes in 2022 to 1.44 million tonnes in 2023, while domestic production dropped from 46,479 tonnes to 30,053 tonnes.
Although the declines could not be attributed solely to the existing SSB tax, the report said they reflected a difficult operating environment characterised by inflation, exchange-rate pressures, rising input costs and weaker consumer demand.
It further warned that a higher tax would not necessarily guarantee increased or sustainable government revenue, as reduced consumption, lower formal-sector production and a shift to informal markets could shrink the taxable base.
ThinkBusiness Africa therefore called for a comprehensive assessment of the proposed tax, greater transparency on revenue generated from the existing N10-per-litre levy and consideration of a sugar-content-based tax.
It also recommended stronger non-tax measures, including public health campaigns, promotion of physical activity, early screening for diabetes and hypertension, and improved primary healthcare.
The report said Nigeria needed stronger measures to tackle diabetes, obesity and hypertension, but cautioned that a substantially higher SSB tax should not automatically be equated with an effective public health policy.
The post Higher SSB Tax may raise prices – Report warns appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto
SOKOTO — Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State has distributed food items and cash assistance to 150 households displaced by bandit attacks across several communities.
The intervention, supervised by the council chairman, Hon. Musa Garba Kuchi, was carried out on Monday at the palace of the District Head of Kebbe, Sarkin Kabbin Kebbe, Hon. Lawal Labbo Margai, in Kebbe town.
Kuchi said the beneficiaries were drawn from communities affected by bandit attacks, including Ungushi, Girkau, Margai, Kebbe East and Kebbe West.
He said the beneficiaries were residents who had been forced to abandon their homes and livelihoods because of insecurity and were currently taking refuge in Kebbe town.
“The beneficiaries are people who have been forced to abandon their homes and livelihoods because of insecurity and are currently taking refuge in Kebbe town,” he said.
Kuchi said the intervention was intended to cushion the hardship faced by displaced households, adding that the council would continue to support residents affected by insecurity.
“The council remains committed to standing with our people in these difficult times. This support may be little, but it is our way of showing that you are not forgotten,” he said.
The chairman commended Sokoto State Governor Ahmed Aliyu for what he described as sustained efforts to strengthen security and protect communities affected by banditry.
He said investments in security, including the provision of combat vehicles and other equipment to security agencies, had boosted the operational capacity of personnel deployed to affected areas.
“Government’s investment in security is already yielding positive results. Our troops are taking the fight to the bandits in their hideouts, and this has given some of our communities the confidence to begin returning to their homes,” Kuchi said.
He called for continued support for security agencies, stressing that tackling banditry required collaboration among government authorities, security agencies, traditional institutions and communities.
Kuchi pledged that the council would sustain humanitarian assistance to victims of insecurity until displaced residents could safely return to their communities and rebuild their livelihoods.
He also called for stronger collaboration among the federal, state and local governments to address the causes and consequences of banditry.
The chairman urged religious leaders and residents to intensify prayers and support peace-building efforts, saying lasting security was essential for the restoration of economic activities and development in Kebbe and the wider state.
In his remarks, the District Head of Kebbe, Hon. Lawal Labbo Margai, commended the council and state government for responding to the plight of residents displaced by insecurity.
“We appreciate the concern demonstrated by the local government and the state government towards our people who have been compelled by insecurity to abandon their communities,” Margai said.
The traditional ruler, a former Speaker of the Sokoto State House of Assembly, urged those handling the distribution to ensure that the relief materials and financial assistance reached genuine beneficiaries.
“Let the relief materials and financial assistance reach the genuine beneficiaries. There must be fairness, justice and transparency in the distribution so that no vulnerable household is deprived of what has been provided for them,” he said.
Margai also prayed for the success of ongoing security operations and expressed hope that affected communities would regain sufficient security for displaced residents to return home.
The exercise was witnessed by the Secretary of Kebbe Local Government, Alhaji Shamsudeen Umar Mai’akwai, councillors, including Hon. S.A. Maitunbi, imams, traditional title holders and community leaders.
The post Kebbe Council assists 150 households displaced by banditry appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) Women Leader in Ebonyi State, Mrs Chinyere Nwele, has criticised the administration of Governor Francis Nwifuru, alleging hardship, neglect and unfulfilled promises under the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) government.
Nwele spoke during a meeting with women from Umu Ekumaenyi in Ezza land, where she assessed the performance of the state government and declared support for the PDP governorship candidate, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii, ahead of the 2027 election.
She said the women had expressed concerns over what they described as a sense of neglect and exclusion from the affairs of the state.
Nwele alleged that the APC administration lacked clear direction and had failed to meet the expectations of residents in key areas of governance.
“When a square peg is forced into a round hole, there is bound to be heavy failure of the entire system,” she said.
The PDP leader also alleged that despite receiving substantial monthly allocations, the state government had not done enough in human capital development, education, infrastructure and healthcare.
She, however, presented Odii, popularly known as Anyichucks, as an alternative, describing him as a candidate with the vision, capacity, exposure and business experience to reposition the state.
According to Nwele, an Odii administration would prioritise road construction, healthcare, rehabilitation of infrastructure, innovation and human capital development, while empowering farmers and creating an enabling environment for businesses to thrive.
She expressed confidence that the proposed changes would become reality if Odii is elected governor in February 2027.
Nwele also urged the women to remain focused on the 2027 election, arguing that good governance should be measured by development and service delivery rather than threats or intimidation.
“Ebonyi is now wiser,” she declared.
The meeting ended with the women of Umu Ekumaenyi expressing readiness to mobilise support for the PDP ahead of the 2027 governorship election.
The post Ebonyi PDP women decry hardship, back Odii appeared first on Vanguard News.

Nigeria and the Republic of Serbia have renewed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations following the presentation of Letters of Credence by Nigeria’s Ambassador to Hungary, Engr. Abass Braimah, to Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić.
The ceremony, held on Monday at the Palace of Serbia in Belgrade, formally accredited Braimah as the Non-Resident Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Federal Republic of Nigeria to Serbia, with residence in Budapest, Hungary.
In his remarks, Braimah expressed his readiness to work closely with the Serbian government, diplomatic community, private-sector actors and other stakeholders to identify new opportunities for engagement and consolidate existing areas of cooperation.
A statement issued yesterday by his office and made available to Vanguard said the ceremony represented an important moment in the continuing diplomatic engagement between Nigeria and Serbia, whose relations span more than six decades.
The statement said the presentation provided an opportunity for both countries to reaffirm their commitment to building on their historic ties and translating their longstanding friendship into deeper and mutually beneficial cooperation.
Braimah, while conveying the warm greetings of the Nigerian government and people to President Vučić, as well as the government and people of Serbia, reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to strengthening the bonds of friendship, mutual respect and cooperation between the two countries.
The former member of the House of Representatives emphasised the importance of expanding existing collaboration in areas of mutual interest, including political and diplomatic engagement, trade and investment, economic cooperation, education and culture.
He said stronger cooperation in those areas would create tangible benefits for the peoples of both countries.
According to the statement, Braimah’s diplomatic mandate comes at a time when stronger bilateral partnerships, economic diplomacy and people-to-people relations have assumed greater importance in the international system.
It added that the renewed engagement between Nigeria and Serbia was expected to deepen understanding of the respective priorities of both countries and create fresh avenues for cooperation in areas of mutual benefit.
The accreditation of Braimah therefore marks a new phase in Nigeria-Serbia relations, with both countries expected to build on their historical ties through sustained dialogue, increased economic interaction and stronger institutional partnerships.

items.content:
By Henry Obetta
LAGOS — The governorship candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in Lagos State, Prince Adelaja Adeoye, has said his ambition for the 2027 election is driven by a desire to provide what he described as accountable and people-oriented governance.
Adeoye, a real estate entrepreneur, said he was seeking to lead Lagos not merely to occupy the seat of government at Alausa, but to implement his development agenda, which he described as Atunto Eko.
“Lagos does not need another ruler. Lagos needs a servant-leader. A leader who cares, a leader who listens, a leader who delivers,” he said.
According to him, his proposed agenda would focus on housing, poverty reduction, job creation, healthcare, environmental management, education, infrastructure, transportation and security.
On housing, Adeoye cited what he described as a deficit of more than three million housing units in Lagos and said, if elected, he would provide 50,000 affordable rent-to-own homes within four years in Ikorodu, Epe, Badagry, Alimosho and Ibeju-Lekki.
He also promised to establish a Lagos Rent Protection Scheme and reform land administration, saying the measures would address challenges associated with housing and tenancy.
On poverty reduction and wealth creation, the APM candidate proposed a N10 billion revolving micro-credit scheme, which he called Ekoowo, for market women, artisans, fishermen and nano-businesses.
He said the fund would be made available through cooperatives at single-digit interest rates, while 20 major markets would be upgraded with facilities including solar power, cold rooms and creches.
Adeoye also proposed industrial clusters in Badagry for coconut and aquaculture, Ikorodu for building materials, Epe for food processing, and the Mainland/Yaba axis for fashion, film and technology.
He said the clusters would be equipped with power and internet infrastructure and linked to off-takers, with a target of creating 100,000 direct jobs within two years.
Under his proposed Eko Skill Code programme, Adeoye said 20,000 youths would be trained annually in areas including solar installation, plumbing, coding and creative skills, with participants linked to employment opportunities.
On healthcare, he promised to upgrade 250 primary healthcare centres to operate round the clock, with personnel, medicines, solar power and ambulances.
He also proposed an Eko Health Card, which he said would operate as a N1,000 monthly contributory scheme for informal-sector workers, while antenatal care and childbirth would be free in public hospitals under his administration.
On the environment, Adeoye said Lagos generates more than 13,000 tonnes of waste daily and proposed reforms to the Lagos State Waste Management Authority (LAWMA), including waste sorting at source and incentives for recyclable materials.
He also proposed clearing primary drainage channels, constructing 100 kilometres of lined drains and creating what he described as 15,000 green jobs in recycling and composting.
In education, Adeoye promised to revive 10 technical colleges, introduce free school meals sourced from Lagos farmers, increase teachers’ welfare by 30 per cent and deploy solar-powered digital classrooms in public secondary schools.
He also promised to fix 500 inner roads through direct labour, introduce integrated ticketing across BRT, the Blue Line and ferries, and expand water transportation to Ikorodu, Epe and Badagry.
On security, the candidate proposed community policing, solar-powered streetlights and an Eko Safety App for emergency response.
Adeoye also pledged to publish government contracts and expenditure online every month to promote public scrutiny of government spending.
On his party’s presidential candidate, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, Adeoye said the APM candidate’s record in Oyo State demonstrated what he described as people-focused governance.
Makinde was nominated as the APM’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election and is listed by the Independent National Electoral Commission among the presidential candidates for the poll.
Adeoye said Makinde would address challenges including insecurity, food insecurity, youth unemployment, irregular power supply and the migration of young Nigerians if elected president.
He also called on Lagos residents to support the APM’s candidates in the 2027 elections.
“For a better Lagos and a better Nigeria, vote APM from top to bottom. Vote Seyi Makinde for President and vote Adeoye for Governor. This is how we reset Lagos and reset Nigeria together,” he said.

It said the SMS notifications have also been sent to the shortlisted candidates’ registered phone numbers.
ZITDA also urged the candidates to visit the official recruitment portal (https://recruitment.zamfara.gov.ng/ube) to check their application status and print their examination/invitation slip.
It said the examination slip contains all the necessary information about the CBT examination, including the CBT centre, examination date, examination time, and venue.
Candidates were therefore advised to carefully check all the information contained on their slips.
They were also advised to come along with the printed examination slip and a valid means of identification to the CBT examination.
“The examination slip is mandatory for admission into the CBT examination hall. Candidates are therefore strongly advised to print their slips ahead of the examination,” the circular said.
It warned that applicants who have not received an SMS or email notification are advised to remain patient and regularly check the recruitment portal for updates and further opportunities.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto
SOKOTO — The Sokoto State Government has defended its decision to reopen only schools within the state capital, saying the continued closure of schools outside the metropolis is a security measure taken in compliance with a directive from the Federal Government.
Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Prof. Muhammad Ladan Ala, stated this on Monday in Sokoto while briefing journalists on the status of schools following the recent resumption arrangement.
Ala explained that schools within the Sokoto metropolis were currently operating, while those outside the designated area remained closed pending further directives from the appropriate authorities.
“What we said is that schools within Sokoto metropolis are the ones that are in operation. Other schools that are not within Sokoto metropolis are still closed. We are awaiting directives from the top so that they will go ahead,” he said.
He said the metropolis, for the purpose of the arrangement, covered Kware, Dange-Shuni, Wamakko, Sokoto North and Sokoto South Local Government Areas.
The commissioner said the government would not compromise the safety of pupils and students in its determination to reopen schools, stressing that security considerations remained paramount.
“Security is more important than anything you are thinking about. It is only when you have security, when you have peace, then you will be able to go to your farms, you will be able to go to your school,” Ala said.
He disclosed that the state’s Safe School Initiative remained operational, with the ministry maintaining regular consultations and engagements with security agencies, including the Nigerian Army, Police and Department of State Services.
According to him, the ministry had also participated in strategic meetings in Abuja aimed at strengthening security around schools and other educational institutions, particularly against threats capable of disrupting academic activities.
Ala said the government was also strengthening community-based surveillance through School-Based Management Committees, Parent-Teacher Associations and vigilante groups across the local government areas.
“We are working with our SBMCs, with our PTA, in fact with the vigilante groups in the various local governments,” he said.
He urged the groups to conduct coordinated surveillance visits to schools, adding that vigilante personnel had been encouraged to maintain a visible presence around schools, particularly in communities where students commute from surrounding villages.
This, he said, would enable security intervention to be activated quickly whenever an alarm was raised.
The commissioner clarified that although the state government had identified some local government areas as relatively safe, security remained principally a federal responsibility, making compliance with the directive on school closures imperative.
On allegations regarding the feeding of students in boarding schools, Ala dismissed claims that principals were being given funds to feed students, describing the reports as inaccurate.
“There is no principal that is giving any money. The money is paid to the contractors,” he said.
He explained that contractors engaged by the state government supplied food to schools on a rotational weekly basis, adding that the arrangement was supervised by a committee established by the governor to ensure accountability, transparency and compliance with approved standards.
“The contractors are being rotated among the schools so that you don’t become so used to the food,” he said.
Ala also disclosed that the ministry had intensified health and disease prevention measures in schools through its Health Coordinator and collaboration with the State Ministry of Health.
He said the government had taken steps to address diphtheria and other communicable diseases, adding that drugs were supplied to principals of girls’ schools last year as part of efforts to strengthen school health services.
According to him, school supervision had also been expanded to cover 30 key performance indicators, including sanitation, hygiene and other conditions required for a safe and conducive learning environment.
On transportation, the commissioner said the state government had deployed free buses to convey students within the metropolis and those travelling from surrounding communities.
“The buses are free of charge, within the town and outside. Every morning we send them to bring students. By 2 o’clock, the buses will convey them back to their respective villages or bus stops,” he said.
Ala maintained that the government’s overriding objective was to ensure that the resumption of academic activities did not expose students to avoidable security risks.
He assured parents and other stakeholders that the government would continue to monitor the security situation and respond to directives from the relevant authorities before extending the resumption arrangement to schools currently under closure.
