items.content:
China has criticised calls by leading US technology executives to slow the development of artificial intelligence (AI), rejecting claims that rapid Chinese advances in the technology pose a grave security threat to the world.
“Fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance and serve the interests of no one,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing in Beijing on Monday.
“The development of artificial intelligence bears on the common well-being of all humanity,” he added, responding to questions about calls to slow the development of frontier AI models and warnings that a Chinese advantage in the field could pose a danger to the world.
“Fomenting various threats, engaging in confrontation and malicious competition will only disrupt the process of global governance of artificial intelligence and is not in the interests of any party,” Guo added.
 
MFA Spokesperson’s response to claims that “Chinese AI advantage would pose U.S. national security risks”:
AI is a consequential technology for the future of humanity. The world needs open & inclusive AI for good and for all. Fear-mongering, confrontation and vicious competition… pic.twitter.com/SqlnqbTNrx
— CHINA MFA Spokesperson 中国外交部发言人 (@MFA_China) September 14, 2026
 
China called for international cooperation on artificial intelligence, warning that “threat narratives” could disrupt global AI governance.
The comments follow Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s call for AI firms to slow model development over safety and national security concerns. pic.twitter.com/MOU8ViaiHh
— Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) September 14, 2026
 
🇨🇳 Beijing is telling the AI panic crowd to calm down.
China’s Foreign Ministry says AI should remain “open and inclusive,” warning that fearmongering, confrontation and “vicious competition” will only derail global AI governance.
There’s clearly no appetite for slowing the…
— Mario Nawfal (@MarioNawfal) September 14, 2026
The comments came a day after OpenAI chief Sam Altman and SpaceX founder Elon Musk backed a call by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to “slow the pace” of AI development.
Amodei has warned that increasingly capable AI agents could, in a worst-case scenario, become capable of “taking over the entire internet” within a year.
In a rare show of alignment among some of Silicon Valley’s most prominent figures, Altman and Musk supported Amodei’s appeal, which followed a series of increasingly stark warnings from AI researchers about the risks posed by advanced autonomous systems.
Amodei has also called for greater international coordination on AI safety, including cooperation with China.
In an essay titled “We Must Pace the Frontier,” he proposed a three-part framework for slowing the development of advanced AI, beginning with giving independent monitors continuous access to developers’ research and safety processes.
He argued that “building AI too fast is reckless”, pointing to incidents involving hundreds of OpenAI agents interacting with the Hugging Face website.
Amodei warned that a more capable and similarly misaligned swarm could potentially cause hundreds of billions of dollars in damage by “taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet”.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for a global slowdown in the pace of AI development.
In an essay posted online, he warned that rogue AI agents could take over the internet in as little as six months. The warning follows a series of security breaches and growing concerns pic.twitter.com/xoKttUw9fS
— Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) September 12, 2026
Some AI experts have disputed the likelihood of such a scenario, urging caution over what they describe as highly speculative predictions.
US President Donald Trump has also rejected Amodei’s call for an AI slowdown.
“The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a strong and smart (high IQ!) President, and the USA has that, in spades!” Trump wrote on Truth Social. He also criticised Amodei directly, saying his administration had stopped AI companies from engaging in “bad, or potentially bad” activities and would continue to do so.
JUST IN: Trump declares the only guardrails AI needs is a “high IQ president,” accusing AI critics of trying to slow America’s lead over China. pic.twitter.com/6nFGRRPswN
— Polymarket (@Polymarket) September 14, 2026
Amodei’s proposals extend beyond AI safety and include measures specifically targeting China’s access to advanced AI technology.
He has called for tighter restrictions on exports of advanced AI chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment, stronger measures against unauthorised model distillation and greater protection for AI model weights.
The true agenda of Amodei’s proposals, according to The Global Times newspaper, is “to attempt to curb China’s AI development through technological barriers and regulatory monopolies, uphold Washington's monopolistic hegemony in cutting-edge technology, and exclude China from the global AI governance system.”
“This ‘silent AI Cold War’ is hypocritical and short-sighted,” it said, adding that excluding China from global AI innovation would “significantly increase the trial-and-error costs and risks of loss of control in ‌global AI development”.
Independent industry observers also believe Amodei and other US tech bosses are pushing for an AI slowdown because China has gained a decisive lead in the race. They say the push is also driven by concerns over China’s massive data-centre expansion. A proposed facility in Inner Mongolia’s Ulanqab is reportedly far larger than Elon Musk’s Colossus supercomputer in Memphis.
US companies may struggle to match that scale due to shortages of advanced chips and electricity. Building the nuclear capacity needed to power such facilities would take years, while China is already developing the infrastructure at speed.
Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to meet US President Donald Trump in Washington this month, with AI governance and safety set to be part of their discussions.
Anthropic CEO’s position has attracted additional scrutiny because of his own career in China’s technology sector.
Amodei joined Chinese technology giant Baidu in 2014 after being recruited by prominent AI researcher Andrew Ng, who was then leading the company’s AI research effort.
At the time, Baidu was investing heavily in computing infrastructure and had access to substantial GPU resources. Amodei’s work there formed part of a broader research environment focused on scaling AI systems — the idea that increasing computing power, data and model size can produce significant improvements in performance.
He later moved to OpenAI, where he became a research vice president and worked on the development of GPT-2 and GPT-3.
Amodei left OpenAI in 2020 and co-founded Anthropic the following year with a group of former OpenAI researchers, including his sister Daniela Amodei.
Anthropic subsequently built its public identity around AI safety and the development of what it describes as reliable and controllable AI systems.
The company is now at the centre of an increasingly contentious debate over how quickly frontier AI should advance and who should establish the rules governing the technology.
Amodei’s proposals have drawn criticism from observers who argue that measures presented as AI safety safeguards could strengthen the position of companies that are already leading the frontier. Anthropic has itself faced controversy over how data was obtained and used to train its AI models.
In the most significant case, a group of authors sued the company over its use of pirated books. A US court ruled in 2025 that training AI models on lawfully obtained books could qualify as fair use, while obtaining and storing pirated copies was a separate issue.
Anthropic subsequently agreed to a $1.5 billion settlement, subject to court approval.
The company has also faced scrutiny over the use of YouTube subtitles in AI training datasets. An investigation by Proof News and Wired reported that a dataset containing subtitles from thousands of YouTube channels had been used by AI companies, including Anthropic.
Anthropic’s web crawler, ClaudeBot, has meanwhile drawn complaints from websites over the scale of its automated data collection.
iFixit chief executive Kyle Wiens publicly criticised the crawler, saying his company had experienced massive volumes of automated requests.
Reddit has also taken legal action against Anthropic, alleging that the company improperly scraped user content, including material that had subsequently been deleted. Anthropic has disputed allegations that its practices amounted to wrongdoing.
The company has also faced criticism from parts of the open-source community.
Anthropic has not released the weights of its frontier Claude models. In 2026, the company distinguished between supporting open-source software and releasing the weights of frontier AI models, arguing that unrestricted access to powerful model weights could create significant safety and security risks.
That position has become particularly contentious as the debate over so-called open weights intensifies.
Several major technology companies and AI developers have supported policies against government restrictions on the release of model weights, while Anthropic has taken a more cautious position on frontier systems.
The company has also taken action against repositories containing leaked Claude Code material, with reports of hundreds of repositories receiving copyright-related takedown notices.
Its restrictions on the use of Claude subscriptions through some third-party tools have further fuelled criticism among developers who rely on open-source AI clients.
At the same time, Anthropic has expanded its political lobbying in Washington. Its federal lobbying expenditure reportedly reached almost $2 million in the second quarter of 2026, placing it among a growing group of AI companies seeking to influence US technology policy.
The geopolitical dimension of the debate has become even more pronounced as Anthropic has stepped up its allegations against Chinese AI developers.
In February 2026, the company accused Chinese AI firms including DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax of using large numbers of accounts and interactions to reproduce capabilities associated with Claude. Anthropic later expanded its allegations to include other Chinese laboratories.
The company said the allegations were based on its own telemetry and monitoring systems. The figures, however, have not been independently audited, making the scale of the alleged activity difficult to verify from outside the company.
Amodei has also argued that advanced computing hardware should not be made available to China and called for US authorities to tackle the use of overseas data centres to circumvent export controls.
He has further advocated stronger action against what Anthropic describes as industrial-scale model distillation.
The dispute highlights a broader contradiction confronting the AI industry.
Companies that rely heavily on vast quantities of publicly available data, open-source software and research are increasingly seeking tighter restrictions around access to their own models, computing resources and technological capabilities.
For Anthropic, the argument is one of supposed AI safety: powerful frontier systems, it argues, could pose risks that require stronger oversight, tighter controls and international coordination. Critics, however, contend that rules governing access to computing power, training data, model weights and advanced AI development could also become competitive barriers that favour companies already operating at the frontier.
China’s response reflects the geopolitical dimension of the dispute. Beijing argues that confrontation and technology restrictions could undermine the development of global AI governance and turn a shared technological challenge into another arena of strategic rivalry.
(With additional input from Agencies)

items.author: Christopher Louis
tags: Nintendo's Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2
items.content:
Nintendo Switch 2 edisi khusus perayaan 40 tahun The Legend of Zelda langsung mengalami kelangkaan setelah pre-order dibuka di Amerika Serikat. Konsol yang dibanderol US$519,99 tersebut dilaporkan habis dalam hitungan menit di sejumlah retailer besar, termasuk Best Buy, Walmart, Target, Amazon, hingga toko resmi Nintendo.
Harga tersebut memang sedikit lebih tinggi dibanding Switch 2 standar yang kini dibanderol US$499,99. Namun, edisi khusus ini membawa desain bertema The Legend of Zelda yang membuatnya menjadi incaran kolektor. Konsol tersebut dijadwalkan mulai dikirim pada 29 Oktober, sekitar satu minggu sebelum remake Ocarina of Time yang akan dirilis pada 5 November.
Setelah stok retail habis, sejumlah unit mulai bermunculan di eBay dengan harga jauh lebih tinggi. Listing yang beredar berada di kisaran US$700 hingga US$1.700 hanya untuk konsolnya. Ada pula penjual yang menawarkan paket berisi Pro Controller, carrying case, dan remake Ocarina of Time, meski Nintendo sendiri tidak menjual kombinasi tersebut sebagai satu paket resmi.
Baca Juga: Diablo 5 Resmi Diumumkan, Bawa Sanctuary yang Sudah Jatuh ke Tangan Diablo
Harga Resmi US$519,99, Scalper Pasang Harga Berkali-kali Lipat
Jika seluruh aksesori tersebut dibeli secara terpisah melalui Nintendo, total biayanya sekitar US$720. Artinya, sejumlah bundle yang ditawarkan hingga US$2.000 berada jauh di atas harga retail. Namun, perlu dicatat bahwa harga di eBay merupakan harga yang diminta penjual dan belum tentu mencerminkan harga transaksi sebenarnya.
Fenomena seperti ini bukan pertama kalinya terjadi pada peluncuran hardware populer Nintendo. Tingginya permintaan dan stok terbatas membuat produk edisi khusus mudah menjadi sasaran pembelian untuk dijual kembali. Bagi konsumen yang memang ingin menggunakan konsolnya, kondisi tersebut tentu membuat mendapatkan unit dengan harga normal menjadi lebih sulit.
Nintendo Pernah Terapkan Sistem Antiscalper
Nintendo sebelumnya mencoba mengurangi aktivitas scalper ketika membuka pre-order Switch 2 dengan menerapkan syarat tertentu. Calon pembeli diharuskan memiliki setidaknya 50 jam waktu bermain Switch sebelum bisa melakukan pre-order melalui skema tersebut.
Belum diketahui apakah Nintendo akan menerapkan aturan serupa ketika stok edisi Zelda kembali tersedia. Mengingat batch pertama habis dengan sangat cepat, mekanisme pembatasan pembelian atau sistem pre-order yang lebih ketat bisa menjadi salah satu cara untuk mengurangi pembelian dalam jumlah besar. Untuk sementara, konsumen yang gagal mendapatkan unit harus menunggu restock atau memilih membayar harga aftermarket yang jauh lebih mahal.

items.title: Moneyview Cuts IPO Size After SEBI Nod, Halves Fresh Issue Component To ₹750 Cr
items.summary:
Fintech unicorn Moneyview has trimmed the size of its initial public offering (IPO) significantly a couple of months after the markets regulator SEBI greenlit the issue. In a public announcement today, the company announced that it has halved the fresh issue component of the IPO to ₹750 Cr, from the initially proposed ₹1,500 Cr and trimmed the offer for sale (OFS) component to 10.04 Cr equity shares from 13.6 Cr.
As per the new announcement, investors Tiger Global, Accel, Crimson Winter, Ribbit Capital, NLI Strategic Venture Investment (a VC fund co-managed by Nippon Life Global Investors Americas and Transpose Platform Management)and Transpose Platform Management have trimmed the number of shares they intend to offload.
Cofounders Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal have not changed their OFS portions, along with Agarwal’s wife Chitra Agarwal, who is selling 19.35 lakh shares via the OFS.

Cofounders Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal have not changed their OFS portions, along with Agarwal’s wife Chitra Agarwal, who is selling 19.35 lakh shares via the OFS.
As per the revised IPO size, ₹325 Cr of the net proceeds will be used to drive growth in loan disbursals under default loss guarantee (DLG) arrangements and ₹250 Cr will be infused in NBFC subsidiary Whizdm Finance Pvt Ltd to augment its capital base. The remainder will be used for general corporate purposes.
The company didn’t disclose the reason for it trimming its IPO size or the timeline for the opening of the issue.
Accel is the largest stakeholder in Moneyview, with a 21.9% stake. The investor deployed capital via two separate funds — Accel India IV and Accel Growth IV.
Tiger Global holds a 13.79% pre-offer stake in Moneyview, which accounts for 21.2 Cr equity shares. Meanwhile, US-based Ribbit Capital currently holds 15.7 Cr shares in the fintech giant, which represents 10.2% stake in the company.
Founded in 2014, Moneyview runs a digital-first lending platform that provides unsecured personal loans to underserved and new-to-credit customers. It partners with banks and NBFCs to originate loans through its app and website, while also lending from its own NBFC arm, Whizdm Finance.
Moneyview has raised over $250 Mn in funding to date. It entered the unicorn club in 2024 after raising a $4.6 Mn funding round that valued it at over $1 Bn amid a broader surge in investor interest in India’s digital lending and fintech space.
In FY25, the company reported a revenue of ₹2,379 Cr and a net profit of ₹240 Cr. For the nine months ended December 31, 2025, it posted a revenue of ₹2,409 Cr and a net profit of ₹245 Cr, exceeding its full-year FY25 numbers.
Moneyview’s assets under management (AUM) stood at ₹19,814 Cr as of December 31, 2025. The startup is yet to report its FY26 numbers.

items.content:
Macklemore has been removed from the remaining U.S. dates of Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour following controversy over the rapper’s comments supporting Palestine during a recent performance.
A spokesperson for Messina Touring Group, the promoter for Sheeran’s U.S. tour, confirmed Monday that Macklemore would no longer perform as an opening act. The statement said venues on upcoming tour dates would not allow concerts to proceed with Macklemore on the lineup.
The promoter said keeping him on the tour could have resulted in cancellations affecting hundreds of thousands of fans. After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore was therefore removed from the remaining support dates.
The decision comes less than two weeks after Macklemore performed at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. During his opening set, he told the audience that part of his reason for joining the tour was to use stadium performances to say “Free Palestine”. 
Macklemore says Ed Sheeran and his team decided to remove him from tour due to his comments in support of Palestine, after Kraft Group rallied stadium owners and gave Ed an ultimatum:
“[Ed] told me that the words ‘Free Palestine’ and the image of the Palestinian flag were… pic.twitter.com/NQneebKFDh
— Pop Base (@PopBase) September 14, 2026
Macklemore has publicly supported Palestinians for years. In 2024, he released “Hind’s Hall”, a protest song addressing the war in Gaza, which he also performed before Sheeran’s set at MetLife Stadium.
His comments during the tour prompted an Israeli-American Council petition calling for his removal. Singer Pink also faced criticism after resharing a post supporting the decision to drop him from the tour.
Macklemore later addressed the response, saying criticism of Israel and opposition to genocide should not be interpreted as criticism of Jewish people. He also wrote on X that wanting equal treatment for all people should not be controversial.
The next U.S. Loop Tour date is scheduled for September 19 in Philadelphia, where Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe are set to perform as opening acts. Sheeran’s U.S. dates continue through November 7.

items.content:
Foto terbaru yang dibagikan HKEPC memperlihatkan dugaan penggunaan GeForce RTX 5090 dalam jumlah besar untuk perakitan server AI. Dalam foto tersebut, terlihat sejumlah pallet berisi RTX 5090 baru yang masih berada dalam kemasan sebelum dipasang ke sistem multi-GPU di fasilitas perakitan server AI.
Jika foto tersebut benar, situasi ini menunjukkan adanya permintaan dari sektor AI terhadap GPU GeForce yang sebenarnya ditujukan untuk konsumen. Menariknya, GPU yang terlihat bukan RTX PRO 6000 maupun akselerator data center khusus yang memang dipasarkan NVIDIA untuk kebutuhan AI, melainkan RTX 5090 versi retail yang sama dengan produk yang banyak dicari gamer.
Namun, validitas foto tersebut masih perlu dipertanyakan. Beberapa bagian gambar disebut terlihat telah dimodifikasi atau bahkan berpotensi dibuat dengan bantuan AI. Karena itu, foto tersebut sebaiknya diperlakukan sebagai indikasi, bukan bukti definitif bahwa RTX 5090 sedang dialihkan dalam skala besar ke server AI.
Baca Juga: Steam Frame Bocor Sebelum Waktunya, Video Hands-On Ungkap Isi Kotak hingga Baterai Controller
Kasusnya Mengingatkan pada Era Mining
Penimbunan NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (Sumber: HKEPC di X)
Situasi ini mengingatkan pada periode booming cryptocurrency ketika penambang membeli GPU GeForce dalam jumlah besar. Akibatnya, stok untuk gamer menipis dan harga GPU melonjak. NVIDIA kemudian memperkenalkan varian Lite Hash Rate pada sejumlah GPU untuk membatasi performa mining, meski pembatas tersebut akhirnya berhasil dilewati.
Kondisinya kini memang berbeda karena AI menjadi sumber permintaan, bukan cryptocurrency. Namun dampaknya terhadap konsumen bisa terlihat serupa. Harga RTX 5090 di sejumlah pasar dilaporkan sudah menembus US$5.000, lebih dari dua kali lipat harga peluncurannya yang berada di US$1.999. Jika permintaan AI memang ikut mendorong kondisi tersebut, gamer harus bersaing dengan pasar yang memiliki kebutuhan dan anggaran berbeda.
NVIDIA Sebenarnya Bisa Membatasi Performa AI
Menariknya, NVIDIA sebelumnya sudah menerapkan pembatasan terhadap kemampuan AI pada varian RTX 5090D dan v2 yang ditujukan untuk pasar China demi memenuhi aturan ekspor. Artinya, secara teknis perusahaan memiliki cara untuk membatasi kemampuan komputasi tertentu tanpa harus mengorbankan performa gaming secara signifikan.
Meski demikian, belum ada indikasi NVIDIA akan menerapkan pendekatan serupa pada RTX 5090 versi global. Di sisi lain, penggunaan GPU konsumen untuk AI juga menunjukkan fleksibilitas hardware GeForce yang memang memiliki kemampuan komputasi tinggi. Masalahnya adalah ketika permintaan tersebut mengurangi ketersediaan produk untuk gamer. Untuk saat ini, yang masih perlu dibuktikan adalah seberapa besar kontribusi server AI terhadap kelangkaan dan kenaikan harga RTX 5090 di pasar retail.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Monday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs4.42 and Rs6.10 per litre, respectively, for September 15.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs380.24 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs409.42 per litre for Tuesday.
The latest revision comes after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by Rs5.02 and Rs5.28 per litre, respectively, from September 12 to September 14.
Read: Govt increases petrol price by Rs5.02, HSD by Rs5.28 per litre
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Sunday announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws, and cars up to 800cc engine, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of sharply rising petroleum prices.
“In this hour of difficulty, we will not leave the public alone. To alleviate the burden of rising oil prices on users of motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingchis, and small vehicles, a special scheme is being initiated,” said a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).
Under the proposal, an estimated 11.8 million beneficiaries would be covered. Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.
Another one million users of cars of up to 800cc would receive relief on 30 litres per month, providing them a maximum benefit of Rs3,000 each. The government estimated the monthly fiscal impact of the scheme at Rs24.6 billion – Rs20 billion for two-wheelers, Rs1.6 billion for three-wheelers and Rs3 billion for cars.
Read More: PM unveils plan to cushion fuel shock
The proposed relief comes amid a steep increase in domestic petroleum prices following volatility in international oil markets due to the Gulf crisis. Petrol prices increased by Rs72 per litre, or 24%, between July 1 and September 11, while high-speed diesel rose by Rs87 per litre, or 28%.
The government noted that Pakistan’s heavy dependence on imported crude oil and refined petroleum products meant increases in international prices translated directly into higher domestic retail prices.
Officials said lower-income consumers were facing severe economic pressure from higher petroleum prices and resulting inflation. Subsequently, the prime minister directed the authorities concerned to devise a mechanism to provide relief to the poorest segments of society.
Also Read: Govt details registration process for Rs100 petrol subsidy
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices climbed over 2% ‌on Monday as worries about energy supplies mounted following new strikes on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure and attacks on ships in the Middle East.
Brent futures rose $2.72, or 2.6%, to $107.33 per barrel at 11:39 am EDT (1539 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $2.51, or 2.5%, to $102.56.
Arab states in the Gulf called off a meeting with Iran planned for Monday, while Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched a new attack on Saudi Arabia after fighting ​that has extended the Middle East war to another theatre and further jeopardised global oil supplies.
"The relatively contained ​price reaction suggests ⁠the market still expects Saudi inventories to cushion exports in the near term, but if the disruption extends beyond the five-to-seven-day inventory cushion, that could change quickly," said Janiv Shah, oil markets analyst at Rystad.

US President Donald Trump said on Monday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to target each other's energy facilities, a day after he chastised Kyiv for hitting Russian oil refineries.
"Ukraine has agreed not to hit Russian energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!" Trump said on his Truth Social network.
"The world's diesel price rise is mostly caused by the Russia/Ukraine War, not Iran."
pic.twitter.com/duiXzE2pbQ
— Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) September 14, 2026
The Ukrainian presidency declined to comment and there was no immediate reaction from Moscow.
Trump's claim comes as oil prices continue to soar in the seventh month of the Iran war, raising American fuel costs and inflation just weeks before crunch US midterm elections.
The US leader has insisted that the Iran war will finish immediately after the midterms and gas prices will drop — but has in the meantime apparently found a new target to blame for the cost at the pump.
Trump had lashed out at Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky during a trip to Ireland on Sunday, saying he had to do "one thing" and "stop knocking out diesel fuel" refineries in Russia due to growing shortages.
"Let him go after targets, but not diesel fuel, because he's causing a shortage of diesel," Trump said, again insisting the Russia-Ukraine war — not the US-Israel conflict with Iran — was to blame.
Read More: Trump tells Ukraine's Zelenskiy to stop hitting Russian diesel
Trump added he had spoken to Ukraine's leader about the country's stepped-up attacks on such sites over recent months.
"There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel because that's hurting. That's hurting the world. We don't want him to hit diesel fuel ... He's hitting diesel refineries."
Ukraine has hit numerous Russian oil refineries far from its border with Russia, while Moscow has also intensified its long-range attacks in recent months, leading to a jump in civilian deaths.
Kyiv has been firing record numbers of drones at Russia, while Moscow has been launching all-time high missile attacks.
Trump said last week he had a "great conversation" with Russian President Vladimir Putin, insisting that Putin wanted to make a deal to end Moscow's war on Ukraine.
Putin "is wanting to make a deal, and if Zelensky is wanting to make a deal, that'd be very nice", Trump told reporters on Wednesday.
Zelensky said last week he would be willing to meet Putin at the G20 summit at Trump's own Doral resort in Miami in December, but the Kremlin immediately ruled it out.

items.title: Honor Magic9 Series Punya Tiga Model, Bawa Baterai 11.000 mAh
items.summary:
Honor memperluas lini flagship Magic9 dengan menyiapkan tiga model sekaligus, yaitu Magic9, Magic9 Pro Max, dan Magic9 Super Edition. Setelah sebelumnya memperlihatkan desain Pro Max, Honor kini mengungkap lebih banyak detail mengenai desain, pilihan warna, serta konfigurasi memori ketiganya.
Ketiga smartphone tersebut saat ini sudah tersedia untuk pre-order di China dan dijadwalkan diperkenalkan secara resmi pada 28 September. Kehadiran Magic9 Super Edition menjadi salah satu perubahan menarik karena Honor sebelumnya belum mengungkap keberadaan model tersebut.
Dari sisi desain, ketiga perangkat memiliki bahasa desain yang relatif serupa, terutama pada bagian belakang. Magic9 dan Magic9 Pro Max menggunakan modul kamera dengan susunan lingkaran yang cukup besar, sementara Super Edition memiliki tampilan yang lebih mirip model standar. Perbedaan juga terlihat pada konfigurasi kamera dan kapasitas penyimpanan yang ditawarkan.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Honor memperluas lini flagship Magic9 dengan menyiapkan tiga model sekaligus, yaitu Magic9, Magic9 Pro Max, dan Magic9 Super Edition. Setelah sebelumnya memperlihatkan desain Pro Max, Honor kini mengungkap lebih banyak detail mengenai desain, pilihan warna, serta konfigurasi memori ketiganya.
Ketiga smartphone tersebut saat ini sudah tersedia untuk pre-order di China dan dijadwalkan diperkenalkan secara resmi pada 28 September. Kehadiran Magic9 Super Edition menjadi salah satu perubahan menarik karena Honor sebelumnya belum mengungkap keberadaan model tersebut.
Dari sisi desain, ketiga perangkat memiliki bahasa desain yang relatif serupa, terutama pada bagian belakang. Magic9 dan Magic9 Pro Max menggunakan modul kamera dengan susunan lingkaran yang cukup besar, sementara Super Edition memiliki tampilan yang lebih mirip model standar. Perbedaan juga terlihat pada konfigurasi kamera dan kapasitas penyimpanan yang ditawarkan.
Baca Juga: HONOR Robot Phone Resmi Meluncur, Bawa Gimbal Mekanis dan Kamera 200MP
Magic9 dan Pro Max Punya Kamera Berkolaborasi dengan ARRI
Honor Magic9 Pro Max akan tersedia dalam pilihan warna Black, Silver, dan Olive Green. Smartphone ini menawarkan RAM hingga 16GB dan penyimpanan internal 1TB. Model standar Magic9 memiliki pilihan warna yang lebih banyak dengan tambahan Popcorn Yellow, serta konfigurasi maksimal yang sama, yakni 16GB RAM dan 1TB penyimpanan.
Magic9 juga membawa desain kamera belakang yang mirip dengan Pro Max, meski ukuran lingkaran kameranya terlihat sedikit lebih kecil. Honor turut mengonfirmasi kolaborasi kamera dengan ARRI pada model ini. Namun, perusahaan belum mengungkap detail sensor maupun kemampuan fotografi yang akan ditawarkan ketiga perangkat tersebut.
Super Edition Jadi Model dengan Spesifikasi Berbeda
Magic9 Super Edition hadir dalam pilihan warna yang sama dengan Magic9. Desain belakangnya juga terlihat serupa dengan model standar, tetapi tidak membawa branding ARRI pada sistem kamera. Perangkat ini menawarkan RAM hingga 16GB dengan penyimpanan maksimal 512GB, lebih kecil dibanding dua model lainnya.
Honor juga mengonfirmasi bahwa Magic9 Series akan menggunakan baterai berkapasitas 11.000 mAh. Namun, perusahaan belum menjelaskan model mana yang mendapatkan kapasitas tersebut. Sebelumnya, bocoran menyebut Super Edition kemungkinan menjadi perangkat yang membawa baterai jumbo tersebut. Detail spesifikasi lainnya baru akan terungkap saat peluncuran resmi pada 28 September.

Isi Kotak Unboxing REDMI Note 17 5G Tetap Komplit
View this post on Instagram
Seperti yang bisa Gizmo friends lihat melalui video unboxing REDMI Note 17 5G di atas, terlihat bila boks atau kotak smartphone tetap hadir dalam dimensi cukup bongsor, membawa semua kelengkapan yang diperlukan dan masih sama dari generasi ke generasi. Tetap menyematkan pengisi daya alias adaptor charger, dan aksesori lainnya seperti soft case. Sehingga tidak lagi perlu membeli keduanya secara terpisah.
Salah satu alasan mengapa kotak unboxing REDMI Note 17 5G bongsor, tidak lain adalah berkat dimensi perangkatnya yang juga kini dibuat membesar. Pasalnya, layar REDMI Note 17 5G sendiri berukuran 6,99 inci, alias hampir mendekati dimensi layar tablet kompak 7 inci. Tidak dapat dipungkiri membuat ukuran bodi keseluruhan menjadi terasa lebih besar dalam genggaman.
Dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya, sedikit lebih tebal di 8,5mm, dan signifikan lebih berat, kini mencapai 225 gram. Namun setidaknya pengalaman menggenggamnya tidak membuat smartphone terasa begitu besar, berkat sedikit lengkung pada tepi perangkat. Salah satu aspek yang juga membuatnya lebih bongsor, adalah kapasitas baterai besar 7700 mAh.
Menggunakan material silikon karbon, baterai REDMI Note 17 5G diklaim bisa digunakan untuk lebih dari 2,5 hari penggunaan, atau memutar video hingga 26 jam nonstop. Juga dirancang tetap normal hinga 6 tahun pemakaian, mendukung fast charging 45W, dan reverse wired charging hingga 22,5W sebagai pengganti powerbank dalam kondisi darurat.
Membawa sertifikasi IP65, REDMI Note 17 5G juga dirancang dengan struktur bodi lebih kuat, telah berhasil melalui sejumlah uji fisik seperti micro-drop test hingga 28 ribu kali, roller test 300 kali, sampai sejumlah uji gores layar (yang terproteksi Gorilla Glass 7i).
Bakal Jalankan Cip Snapdragon
Mengacu pada halaman produk Xiaomi Global, spesifikasi REDMI Note 17 5G bakal diperkuat layar 6,99 inci dengan panel AMOLED 120Hz, memiliki tingkat kecerahan maksimum sampai 1800 nits, dan diperkuat setup speaker dengan opsi volume sampai 200%. Sementara untuk sektor kamera, disematkan sensor 50MP di belakang, sayangnya hanya ditemani depth sensor dan kamera selfie 16MP di depan.
Urusan dapur pacu, performa REDMI Note 17 5G diperkuat cip Snapdragon 4 Gen 4 octa-core dari Qualcomm. Fitur ekstra lainnya seperti sensor NFC hingga inframerah tetap disematkan. Sementara fitur keamanannya sendiri diperkuat dengan in-display fingerprint sensor, memanfaatkan bidang layar depan yang sangat luas.
Menjalankan tampilan antarmuka HyperOS berbasis Android 16, Xiaomi janjikan setidaknya pembaruan keamanan rutin sampai 6 tahun. Dan tentunya membawa sejumlah fitur cerdas berbasis AI di dalamnya. Menurut Gizmo friends, berapa harga yang pas untuk REDMI Note 17 5G kelak sudah tersedia resmi di Indonesia?

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Leaders of the main Scottish, Northern Irish and Welsh nationalist parties on Monday declared their right to choose whether to remain in the United Kingdom (UK) or not at a rare meeting in the Welsh capital Cardiff.
All three parties — the Scottish National Party (SNP), Plaid Cymru in Wales and the pro-Irish unity Sinn Fein — want to break away from the UK.
The meeting came just days after United States President Donald Trump waded in, saying he would back a united Ireland, which Northern Ireland's Michelle O'Neill said showed "the unity debate is very much alive".
"Our nations have the right to self-determination. No Westminster government [the UK government] has the right to block democracy or undermine the principle that our people will decide their own future," a memorandum of understanding (MoU) stated.
Westminster’s time is coming to an end.
We believe there is a better way. Our nations working together as equals, sharing ideas and expertise, building relationships based on mutual respect and common interests.
Today marks a further step in building our cooperation. 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿🇮🇪 pic.twitter.com/pd8EWzQGED
— John Swinney (@JohnSwinney) September 14, 2026
SNP leader John Swinney, Rhun ap Iorwerth, leader of Plaid Cymru in Wales and Mary Lou McDonald and O'Neill, leader and deputy leader of pro-Irish unity Sinn Fein met in their capacity as party leaders, rather than as officials in their respective governments.
O'Neill is also Northern Ireland's first minister while Iorwerth and Swinney are first ministers of their respective nations.
Announcing the agreement, Swinney said the three parties were "absolutely united by that principle of self-determination", adding that this "lies at the heart of the agreement that we have signed today".
"For the first time ever, people across these islands have first ministers in Scotland, in Wales and in the North of Ireland who are all committed to independence from the UK," the MoU said.
"The future of our nations belongs in the European Union."
Read: Irish unification would be fantastic: Trump
The independence parties are the biggest in both the Scottish and Welsh parliaments for the first time since devolution measures began in 1999. Sinn Fein has been the biggest party in Northern Ireland's assembly since 2022.
The regional parliaments have key powers on health, education, housing, transport and environment matters, along with some tax gathering.
"For people watching across these islands — for people watching around the world — there could be no clearer sign that Westminster's time is coming to an end," the agreement said.
A historic day in Cardiff today.
Scotland, Wales and Ireland coming together to assert that the futures of our nations must be shaped by our people.
If this is still a voluntary union, Westminster has no democratic right to deny our right to choose. pic.twitter.com/QLo3JoyGUW
— John Swinney (@JohnSwinney) September 14, 2026
While the three parties are united in their desire to break away from the UK, they have varying positions on how and when this might take place.
The SNP wants a second independence referendum after an earlier ballot in 2014 saw Scotland narrowly vote to remain part of Britain. Successive UK governments have ruled out an immediate rerun.
Sinn Fein, the former political wing of the paramilitary Irish Republican Army (IRA), wants to see a vote on Ireland being reunified with the UK territory of Northern Ireland.
Plaid Cymru seeks Welsh independence in the longer term, but Iorwerth has ruled out pressing for any referendum immediately.
In Northern Ireland, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham sparked a sharp response from Sinn Fein in August, shortly after taking power the previous month, when he said a referendum on Irish unity was "off the table".
The 1998 Good Friday peace agreement, which largely ended three decades of conflict over British rule, provides for a referendum if the British government's Northern Ireland minister believes a majority is likely to favour joining the Republic of Ireland.
Sinn Fein leader McDonald said the prime minister had no authority to "remove any provision of the Good Friday Agreement", and Burnham backtracked in parliament last week.
Read more: UK curbs on Israeli settlements hailed
On Scotland, Burnham — a former mayor of Manchester and a strong advocate of giving greater power to English local authorities — told lawmakers there could be another vote if there was a "clear consensus" north of the border for it.
He reportedly sent a letter to Swinney later clarifying that a referendum remained "off limits".
UK premier reaffirms belief in union
Burnham "believes strongly in the union", his spokesperson said on Monday in a first reaction.
"The prime minister is committed to delivering change across all four nations of the United Kingdom and believes strongly in the union," Burnham's spokesperson was quoted by Sky News as saying.
The spokesperson told reporters that the UK is "at its best" when people come together around shared values and problem-solving, "rather than division".
"The prime minister will continue to ease pressures on household finances and delivering greater economic security, rather than engaging in constitutional debates or further referendums."

items.title: CM Afridi accuses Punjab govt of political victimisation and manhandling at worker's residence in Lahore
items.summary:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday accused the Punjab government and police of political victimisation, brutality and manhandling during his visit to Lahore to offer condolences to the family of a slain Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) activist, Ishtiaq Ahmad.
Tensions rose outside the deceased activist’s residence as Afridi, accompanied by PTI Secretary General Barrister Salman Akram Raja and Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Malik Ahmad Khan Bhachar, reached the workers' home. They also encountered barricades and a heavy police presence.

items.author: Imran Adnan
items.content:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday accused the Punjab government and police of political victimisation, brutality and manhandling during his visit to Lahore to offer condolences to the family of a slain Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) activist, Ishtiaq Ahmad.
Tensions rose outside the deceased activist’s residence as Afridi, accompanied by PTI Secretary General Barrister Salman Akram Raja and Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Malik Ahmad Khan Bhachar, reached the workers' home. They also encountered barricades and a heavy police presence.
Afridi alleged that the Punjab govt attempted to "abduct" him and later "dumped" him on the street, saying such an attempt against a provincial chief minister was no small matter.
He urged workers to remain peaceful, alleging that the situation was orchestrated by Punjab’s government to create chaos.
“We have not come here to hold any political gathering or procession,” Afridi told police personnel.
PTI strongly condemned the incident, calling it "the shameful and reprehensible conduct of the Punjab Police" towards Afridi.
"انہوں نے اغواء کرنے کی کوشش کی پھر یہاں سڑک پر پھینک گئے، ایک صوبے کے وزیراعلی کو اغواء کرنے کی کوشش کی یہ چھوٹی بات نہیں ان پر اب پریشر آئے گا"
وزیراعلی سہیل آفریدی@SohailAfridiISF pic.twitter.com/RSrVeGYKkL
— PTI (@PTIofficial) September 14, 2026
The statement said that the political differences were one thing, but "harassing or attempting to abduct" an elected public representative was absolutely unacceptable under any circumstances.
"Maryam Nawaz and her thuggish elements should feel ashamed of this disgraceful behaviour," it added.
PTI said that the "power is temporary, but the violation of the people's mandate and the humiliation of democratic representatives" are always remembered in history.
پریس ریلیز:
پاکستان تحریکِ انصاف وزیر اعلیٰ سہیل آفریدی کے ساتھ روا رکھے جانے والے پنجاب پولیس کے شرمناک اور قابلِ مذمت رویے کی شدید الفاظ میں مذمت کرتی ہے۔
سیاسی اختلاف اپنی جگہ، مگر ایک منتخب عوامی نمائندے کو ہراساں کرنا یا اغوا کرنے کی کوشش کرنا کسی صورت قابلِ قبول نہیں۔…
— PTI (@PTIofficial) September 14, 2026
K-P Information Minister Shafi Ullah Jan also strongly condemned it and said that said forcing an elected chief minister into a vehicle, withdrawing his security and leaving him without assistance was a serious matter for which the Punjab government should be held responsible.
Jan said the incident in Lahore amounted to an affront to the democratic mandate and constitutional rights of the K-P chief minister.
Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Moeen-ud-Din Riaz Qureshi also condemned what he described as the alleged misconduct and attempted abduction of Afridi by Punjab police. He said such treatment of an elected chief minister was unacceptable and stressed that the public mandate, Constitution and democratic values must be protected.
Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayin-e-Pakistan (TTAP) Punjab Chief Organiser Ammar Ali Jan and Information Secretary Shayan Bashir also condemned the alleged detention of Afridi, holding the Punjab government responsible for the incident.
In a joint statement, they said a sitting chief minister had visited the family of a deceased political worker to offer condolences and should not have been detained by police of another province. They alleged that Punjab police had held the elected K-P chief minister against his will and described the incident as unprecedented in relations between the provinces.
وزیراعلیٰ خیبرپختونخوا @SohailAfridiISF کو پنجاب پولیس کی جانب سے اغوا کرنے کی کوشش کی گئی۔
مریم نواز کے گلو بٹوں نے وزیراعلیٰ آفریدی کو ڈالے میں ڈال کر اغوا کیا اور دور ویرانے میں چھوڑ دیا، پنجاب پولیس نے وزیراعلیٰ آفریدی کو ان کی سکیورٹی سے الگ کرکے زبردستی دوسری گاڑی میں…
— Shafi Jan (@ShafiJanPTI) September 14, 2026
 
Responding to Afridi’s allegations, Punjab Information and Culture Minister Azma Zahid Bokhari called it a “drama”, saying that they themselves went and sat in the police van while police officials were asking them to get off.
“They scolded and pushed aside their own guard for obstructing what she described as a scripted drama and lazy acting," she said in a post on X.
ایک اور ڈرامہ بازی ملاحظہ کریں،خود جا کر پولیس وین میں بیٹھ گئے،پولیس والے اترنے کو کہہ رہے ہیں،اپنے گارڈذ کو اپنا ڈرامہ بلاک کرنے پر جھاڑ کر پرے کردیا،فرمائشی اور سستی ایکٹینگ
انکو عزت دے رہے ہیں لیکن یہ اسکے لائق ہی نہیں pic.twitter.com/CXVeRGAu0u
— Azma Zahid Bokhari (@AzmaBokhariPMLN) September 14, 2026
Addressing media and PTI workers outside Ahmad’s home, Afridi accused the Punjab police and government of causing the death, saying the deceased was innocent. He also criticised Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, referring to her concerns over security threats.
“The Punjab police and the illegitimate Punjab government burned Ishtiaq Ahmad in hot oil; he was innocent and had done no wrong, yet he was killed,” he said.
Ahmad had died after suffering burn injuries during a police raid while preparations were under way for Eid Miladun Nabi (PBUH). The PTI alleged that the police were responsible for his death, claiming that he had suffered burns over 70 per cent of his body after falling into a vat of boiling oil amid chaos. He later died despite treatment.
Afridi rejected security and protocol offered by the Punjab authorities and said he had come to Lahore as an ordinary citizen.
“Punjab is mine, Pakistan is mine. I have come here as an ordinary citizen. I refuse to accept your security; I do not need your protection. The fake chief minister of Punjab claims she feels threatened by the three provinces of Pakistan but not by India, which is a shameful attitude. I am from Punjab, and Punjabis are mine. I have no threat from Punjab. The people of Punjab despise you. I am the people’s chief minister and I enjoy being among the people,” he added.
Speaking about the PTI’s planned September 27 protest, he said the party’s struggle would remain within democratic and legal limits. He said the Constitution was the guarantor of national cohesion and equal rights and rejected violence and lawbreaking.
“We do not support violence or lawbreaking; our only demand is that courts and relevant institutions make impartial and fair decisions in accordance with the Constitution and law,” he said.
Afridi called upon citizens to participate in the September 27 protest, saying people would come out to demand the release of PTI founder Imran Khan and their rights.
The Punjab Home Department had imposed a ban on large gatherings under Section 144 of the Criminal Procedure Code until September 17. The order also prohibited rallies, demonstrations and the display of weapons, while exempting weddings, funerals and court proceedings.
PTI leaders also alleged that authorities had obstructed their movement. Opposition Leader Moeen Qureshi claimed that the K-P chief minister’s convoy was repeatedly stopped and attempts were made to arrest members of the delegation.
“An attempt was made to arrest me, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja and Senator Aoun Abbas. Moreover, the police prevented us from going to the deceased’s home to attend the funeral,” he said.
PTI Punjab Information Secretary Shaukat Basra also accused the provincial authorities of carrying out late-night raids and detaining hundreds of party workers, including women. The leaders alleged that the police had maintained a heavy presence during the funeral and rushed the rites to prevent family members and party workers from gathering.
After offering condolences to the family, Afridi and other leaders proceeded towards Data Darbar in a rally. A large number of PTI supporters joined the procession as it passed through Mochi Gate, Lohari Gate and Bhatti Gate amid heavy police presence.
After offering prayers at the shrine, Afridi proceeded with supporters towards the Lahore High Court to attend a function hosted by lawyers. The movement of the convoy and rally disrupted traffic in several parts of central Lahore. Severe congestion was reported around the railway station, Mall Road, Lower Mall Road, Regal Chowk, GPO Chowk and Circular Road, while traffic diversions forced commuters to use adjoining neighbourhood streets.
Traffic jams were also reported around Ek Moriya Pul, Akbari Market Road, Delhi Gate, Wansan Wala Bazaar and Shah Alam Market.
Sources said police forced shopkeepers to close businesses along Hall Road, Mall Road, Anarkali and other markets during the time.

items.author: News Desk
items.content:
Rising energy and fuel prices, the growing national debt and drug abuse emerged as the biggest concerns among Pakistanis, while public trust in state institutions remained relatively low, according to the National Citizen Survey 2026 released on Monday.
The nationwide survey, conducted by the Institute for Public Opinion Research (IPOR) in collaboration with Pakistan Institute of Legislative Development and Transparency (PILDAT), sought to measure the gap between citizens’ priorities and federal spending.
According to a joint press release by IPOR and PILDAT, the survey interviewed 5,155 voting-age citizens through face-to-face, in-home interviews between August 23 and September 5. It covered all four provinces, rural and urban populations, as well as different age, gender and income groups. The survey had a reported margin of error of ±1.55%.
Read: PILDAT analyses state of democracy in Pakistan
According to the findings, electricity and gas prices were cited as the biggest national concern by 19% of respondents, while another 10% identified rising fuel and petrol prices as their primary concern.
The findings also showed widespread concern over Pakistan’s growing debt burden. About 66% of respondents said the rising national debt was a matter of concern, including 49% who described it as “extremely concerning”. Only 5% viewed the debt situation positively.
Drug abuse emerged as another major concern, with 79% of respondents describing rising drug use as “extremely dangerous”. Overall, 90% expressed serious concern over the issue.
The survey also found considerable scepticism about reporting on Pakistan by foreign-funded NGOs and think tanks. Some 43% of respondents said such reporting was either exaggerated or driven by a foreign agenda, compared with 25% who considered it fact-based.
Social media and unregulated internet use also came under scrutiny. According to the survey, 56% of respondents believed unrestricted internet and social media use was a major factor behind what they perceived as a decline in social and moral values.
However, the survey found differences between generations over the extent to which internet and social media should be regulated.
Despite widespread perceptions about corruption in government departments, only 18% of respondents said they had personally been asked for a bribe by a government official during the preceding year.
Around 77% said they had not experienced such a demand.
The survey also measured public confidence in state institutions, with the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) and National Accountability Bureau (NAB) recording the highest levels of complete trust among the institutions tested.
About 33% of respondents said they had complete trust in the FIA, while 23% expressed complete trust in NAB.
Parliament received complete trust from 15% of respondents, while the Revenue Department recorded 13%.
Read More: PILDAT paints dismal picture of assemblies’ performance
The survey also highlighted difficulties faced by people seeking to establish and operate businesses in Pakistan. As many as 91% of respondents said they found it difficult to start and operate a business in the country. Taxation was identified as the single biggest barrier.
The survey organisers said the findings highlighted a significant disconnect between public priorities and the allocation of public resources, particularly at a time when households were facing mounting cost-of-living pressures.
The National Citizen Survey 2026 was presented as Pakistan’s first nationwide public opinion survey specifically designed to examine the relationship between citizen priorities and federal budget allocations.

items.title: How China is preparing for the risk of AI escaping human control
items.summary:
Warnings from researchers at ​leading US artificial intelligence developer Anthropic that increasingly powerful models could escape human control and even lead to the extinction of the human race,  have drawn ‌attention in China, where policymakers have been preparing for some of the same risks.
The US and China are the two major driving forces of frontier AI development and the technology's global adoption. Both superpowers have been increasingly at loggerheads over each other's AI policies and industry practices, with these issues slated to feature prominently in bilateral talks later this month.
Despite the race to develop increasingly powerful AI systems, regulatory frameworks and public ​statements from Beijing underscore how Chinese authorities regard the possibility of advanced AI escaping effective human oversight as serious enough to plan for.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Warnings from researchers at ​leading US artificial intelligence developer Anthropic that increasingly powerful models could escape human control and even lead to the extinction of the human race,  have drawn ‌attention in China, where policymakers have been preparing for some of the same risks.
The US and China are the two major driving forces of frontier AI development and the technology's global adoption. Both superpowers have been increasingly at loggerheads over each other's AI policies and industry practices, with these issues slated to feature prominently in bilateral talks later this month.
Despite the race to develop increasingly powerful AI systems, regulatory frameworks and public ​statements from Beijing underscore how Chinese authorities regard the possibility of advanced AI escaping effective human oversight as serious enough to plan for.
Read More: Is it possible to slow down the development of AI?
China sees risks in leading closed-source US models
China's state security minister Chen Yixin wrote in a government outlet on Sunday that advanced US models such as Anthropic's Mythos ⁠and OpenAI's GPT-5.5-Cyber could pose serious risks to China's critical information infrastructure, and called for a comprehensive strengthening of AI security.
Anthropic and OpenAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests ​for comment.
Chinese AI developers have promoted open-weight models partly on the grounds that cybersecurity teams can inspect, modify and deploy them for defensive work.
Model repository platform Hugging Face said it used ​GLM-5.2, an open-weight model developed by China's Z.AI , to analyse a July intrusion by escaped OpenAI agents after more tightly restricted US models proved less useful for the forensic work.
But experts also highlight the risks posed by open-weight models, which can be modified and redistributed with little oversight.
Moonshot's Kimi K3 last month bypassed a UK AI Security Institute testing sandbox, highlighting the risk that Chinese AI models could, like their ​US counterparts, evade controls designed to restrict their access and actions.
Regulators have flagged AI 'loss of control' risk
China first included an explicit future loss-of-control scenario in an AI safety framework released ​in September 2024 under the guidance of the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC).
The document said it could not be ruled out that future AI might autonomously obtain external resources, replicate itself, develop self-awareness and seek ‌external power, ⁠creating a risk of competing with humans for control.
The CAC released an expanded version in September 2025. The newer framework sharpened the scenario, saying AI could undergo a sudden and unexpectedly large "leap" in intelligence before acquiring resources, replicating itself and seeking power. It also added a governance principle of "trusted application, preventing loss of control".
A later expert interpretation published on the cyberspace regulator's website said the new principle was intended to guard against loss-of-control risks threatening human survival and development and referred to a possible "AI breaking loose" scenario.
Chinese leader Xi puts human control at centre
The concern has since appeared in China's highest-level ​political messaging.
At the World Artificial Intelligence ⁠Conference in Shanghai in July, Chinese President Xi Jinping said authorities should pay close attention to both intrinsic and derivative risks arising from AI.
He said AI should "always remain under human control".
China's senior Foreign Ministry official responsible for AI affairs, Sun Xiaobo, said at a United Nations meeting ​last month that China was accelerating research into broader AI legislation.
Also Read: China's Z.AI raises $5 billion from new share, convertible bond sales, filing shows
China's deputy permanent representative to the United Nations, Sun Lei, urged governments ​this month to approach ⁠military AI cautiously to avoid strategic miscalculation and an arms race.
Beijing warns of new risks posted by AI agents
China has, meanwhile, begun turning those principles into more specific rules for AI agents, which act much more autonomously and carry out more complex tasks than an ordinary chatbot.
In May, China's cyberspace regulator issued joint guidelines specifically covering such systems.
They require developers to improve their ability to ⁠discover, intervene ​in, block and recover from improper agent behaviour.
The guidelines specifically identify data poisoning, algorithm manipulation, system vulnerabilities and "operational ​loss of control" as security risks. They also say users should retain final decision-making authority over an agent's autonomous decisions.
While China has not proposed independent monitors embedded inside AI companies in the manner advocated by Anthropic, its standards allow ​developers to commission third-party safety assessments, as well as envisaging outside evaluation bodies and security researchers testing and auditing open models.
China state paper calls Anthropic AI slowdown push a ‘Cold War’ tactic
An essay by ​Anthropic's CEO calling for a slowing down of AI development may look like a ‌rational statement focused on safety risks, but it is really a "Cold War playbook" targeting China, the state-backed Global Times said in an editorial.
In the essay published on Saturday and later endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX founder Elon Musk, ​Dario Amodei outlined a framework to pace the development of frontier AI model capabilities and ​create more time to manage mounting safety risks.
Amodei also urged the US to strengthen ⁠chip export controls on China and crack down on alleged model distillation by Chinese AI labs. He then ​told CBS News on Sunday that the "toughest dilemma" over his proposal to slow AI advancement was if China and ​other adversarial nations chose not to do the same.
Also Read: China's Xi pitches open-source AI zone for BRICS
The Global Times tabloid said the true agenda of Amodei's essay was "to attempt to curb China's AI development through technological barriers and regulatory monopolies, uphold Washington's monopolistic hegemony in cutting-edge technology, and ​exclude China from the global AI governance system."
A person visits the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, China July 26, 2025. REUTERS
"This 'silent AI Cold War' is hypocritical and short-sighted," it said, ​adding that excluding China from global AI innovation would "significantly increase the trial-and-error costs and risks of loss of control in ‌global ⁠AI development".
US lawmakers have urged new rules to govern AI systems after dire warnings from two Anthropic researchers that rapidly progressing AI could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future.
Trump brushed aside calls to slow down AI on Sunday, saying that "very negative forces" were raising exaggerated concerns.
"We're leading China ​in AI. We're the most ​sophisticated country in the ⁠world, and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins," Trump said.
When asked about US tech leaders' calls to slow down ​AI development, China's foreign ministry urged all parties to "promote an open, inclusive ​and benevolent approach ⁠to AI."
"Fomenting various threats, engaging in confrontation and malicious competition will only disrupt the process of global governance of artificial intelligence and is not in the interests of any party," spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters at ⁠a ​daily briefing on Monday.
The US and China are planning to discuss frontier ​AI safety risks in mid-September, sources have said, and the issue could be raised during a summit between Presidents Donald Trump ​and Xi Jinping on September 24.

items.title: Lenovo Perluas Lini Yoga di IFA 2026, Bawa Laptop RTX Spark hingga Jajaran Tablet Terbaru
items.summary:
Lenovo memperluas portofolio perangkat Yoga melalui sejumlah produk dan konsep baru yang diperkenalkan di ajang Lenovo Innovation World pada IFA 2026. Rangkaian terbaru ini mencakup laptop dengan NVIDIA RTX Spark, dua tablet yang mengutamakan penggunaan pen, hingga pengalaman lintas perangkat yang mengandalkan AI.
Dua laptop yang menjadi bagian utama lini baru tersebut adalah Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n 15 dan Yoga 9n 2-in-1 16. Keduanya ditujukan untuk kreator dan pengembang yang membutuhkan kemampuan komputasi lokal untuk menjalankan berbagai beban kerja, termasuk AI, pembuatan konten, rendering, serta pengembangan perangkat lunak.
Lenovo juga memperluas pendekatan ini ke perangkat yang lebih portabel melalui Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2 dan Yoga Tab Gen 2. Bersamaan dengan perangkat keras tersebut, perusahaan memperkenalkan Smart Canvas Concept dan pembaruan Lenovo Qira untuk menghubungkan aktivitas pengguna di berbagai perangkat.
Baca Juga: Melihat dari Dekat Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2, Tablet dengan 9-U
items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Lenovo memperluas portofolio perangkat Yoga melalui sejumlah produk dan konsep baru yang diperkenalkan di ajang Lenovo Innovation World pada IFA 2026. Rangkaian terbaru ini mencakup laptop dengan NVIDIA RTX Spark, dua tablet yang mengutamakan penggunaan pen, hingga pengalaman lintas perangkat yang mengandalkan AI.
Dua laptop yang menjadi bagian utama lini baru tersebut adalah Lenovo Yoga Pro 9n 15 dan Yoga 9n 2-in-1 16. Keduanya ditujukan untuk kreator dan pengembang yang membutuhkan kemampuan komputasi lokal untuk menjalankan berbagai beban kerja, termasuk AI, pembuatan konten, rendering, serta pengembangan perangkat lunak.
Lenovo juga memperluas pendekatan ini ke perangkat yang lebih portabel melalui Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2 dan Yoga Tab Gen 2. Bersamaan dengan perangkat keras tersebut, perusahaan memperkenalkan Smart Canvas Concept dan pembaruan Lenovo Qira untuk menghubungkan aktivitas pengguna di berbagai perangkat.
Baca Juga: Melihat dari Dekat Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2, Tablet dengan 9-Unit JBL Speaker
Laptop Yoga Andalkan RTX Spark untuk Beban Kerja Lokal
Yoga Pro 9n 15 menjadi laptop yang berfokus pada performa dengan dukungan NVIDIA RTX Spark dan unified memory hingga 128GB. Lenovo menyebut perangkat ini ditujukan untuk kebutuhan seperti pengembangan AI secara lokal, editing konten, rendering 3D hingga gaming berbasis RTX. Laptop tersebut juga membawa layar PureSight Pro OLED dan sistem termal Lenovo X Power.
Sementara Yoga 9n 2-in-1 16 menawarkan pendekatan berbeda lewat desain konvertibel 360 derajat. Perangkat ini dapat digunakan dalam mode laptop, tablet, tent, stand, dan canvas, serta mendukung input pen pada layar maupun Force Pad. Konfigurasi memorinya mencapai 64GB, sehingga tetap ditujukan untuk pekerjaan yang membutuhkan performa tinggi.
Tablet dan AI Dorong Pengalaman Lintas Perangkat
Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2 menggunakan Snapdragon 8 Elite Mobile Platform dengan layar 13 inci 4K PureSight Pro, sedangkan Yoga Tab Gen 2 memiliki ukuran 11 inci dan bobot sekitar 480 gram. Keduanya mengandalkan interaksi melalui pen, suara, visual, dan sentuhan. Lenovo juga menawarkan fitur seperti AI Note, Live Transcript, serta berbagai fungsi AI lainnya.
Di sisi software, Smart Canvas Concept dirancang agar pengguna dapat menangkap ide menggunakan perangkat Lenovo yang kompatibel lalu melanjutkan pekerjaan di perangkat lain. Lenovo Qira turut dikembangkan sebagai teknologi personal ambient intelligence yang memahami konteks aktivitas pengguna. Namun, efektivitas pengalaman lintas perangkat tersebut pada akhirnya tetap akan bergantung pada kompatibilitas perangkat dan ekosistem Lenovo yang digunakan.

items.title: BGMI Redeem Codes for September 14: How to Get Cobalt Storm Backpack and Other Free Rewards
items.summary: Kraton India has released yet another set of redeem codes for Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI). The latest drop brings the Cobalt Storm Backpack, alongside other exclusive in-game rewards. There are 50 BGMI redeem codes available, although each code can be used by a maximum of 10 players on a first-come, first-served basis. The codes are part of the game's 5th Anniversary Edition 4.5 Update, while the company has also announced that the BGMI 4.6 Update will land soon.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
The Indian startup ecosystem continued to mature in FY26, with 22 new-age tech companies making their public market debut as against 13 in FY25. At the same time, a growing number of startups turned profitable or moved closer to profitability after years of cost rationalisation to adjust to the new funding realities.
Despite a tough Q4 for many startups due to geopolitical uncertainties, Indian startups are expected to improve their top and bottom line numbers in FY26.
Of the 90 startups in the tracker, 63, or about 70%, reported profits in FY26. However, the profitability picture remained uneven. Together, these 63 startups generated a net profit of ₹14,249.5 Cr, while the remaining 27 posted a cumulative loss of ₹20,358.8 Cr, underscoring that sustainable profitability remains a work in progress for a section of the ecosystem.
Even so, the scale of India’s startup ecosystem continued to expand. The 90 companies generated ₹3.12 Lakh Cr in operating revenue in FY26, a sharp 44.4% increase from ₹2.15 Lakh Cr in FY25.
To help you track the financial health of new-age tech companies, Inc42 has launched the FY26 Financial Tracker, bringing together key financial metrics in one place. The tracker will be updated periodically with the latest financial disclosures and deeper insights into the performance of India’s startup ecosystem.
So, without further ado, here’s a look at how Indian startups fared financially in FY26.

Amagi Turns Profitable
Media SaaS company Amagi recorded a net profit of ₹71.7 Cr in FY26 as against a loss of ₹68.7 Cr in the previous year. Operating revenue grew 29.5% to ₹1,505.6 Cr from ₹1,162.6 Cr in FY25.
Its total expenses jumped 16.3% during the period under review to ₹1,482.9 Cr from ₹1,274.8 Cr in the previous year. Meanwhile, employee benefit expenses rose 11.8% YoY to ₹777.2 Cr from ₹694.8 Cr earlier.
Read More: Amagi Posts ₹34 Cr Profit In Q4, Revenue Jumps 29% YoY
ArisInfra’s Profit Jumps 10X
B2B ecommerce company ArisInfra Solutions saw its net profit grow over 10X in FY26 to ₹60.3 Cr from ₹6 Cr in FY25. Operating revenue grew 39.9% to ₹1,067.5 Cr from ₹767 Cr in the previous year.
Its expenses rose 31% to ₹998.8 Cr in FY26 from ₹762 Cr in FY25. Employee costs stood at ₹494.7 Cr during the year under review.

items.author: Michael Carroll
items.content:
Vodafone Idea reportedly faces heat from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) over complaints from Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio regarding mobile number portability (MNP) processes.
Business Standard reported the operator is in the regulator’s crosshairs after its rivals complained it broke several rules involved in helping subscribers change operator.
Vodafone Idea’s rivals believe it misled subscribers in telephone calls purporting to be from other providers and warning of changes to the user’s contract or price plan.
The operator is also alleged to have delayed the sending of SMS containing the unique porting code required by subscribers switching to another provider.
Business Standard added Vodafone Idea’s rivals claim it also sought to lure subscribers with lower-priced post-paid plans.
Vodafone Idea refutes the claims, the newspaper wrote.
A TRAI representative reportedly told Business Standard the regulator is looking into the complaints by Bharti Airtel and Reliance Jio.
The pair want the regulator to explore their claims of misconduct and issue instructions on the MNP process to prevent future incidents.
TRAI fixed and mobile subscriber figures for July indicate Vodafone Idea had a combined 130 million compared with 384.2 million for Bharti Airtel and 535.1 million with Reliance Jio.
Vodafone Idea commenced a rebranding at the beginning of the month in what CEO Abhijit Kishore described as a move to align with future ambitions to deliver a top-tier experience to customers.
The Economic Times reports the operator is also in the early stages of a INR350 billion ($3.7 billion) funding move involving a ten-year loan facility from up to the same number of lenders to cover capex.
The post Rivals cry foul over Vodafone Idea MNP moves appeared first on Mobile World Live.

items.author: Subhashish Panigrahi
items.content:
There is an urgent need for more Indigenous individuals to collaborate before the few individual leaders burn out
Originally published on Global Voices
Deforestation in the Maranhão state of Brazil. Deforestation and land theft remain a persistent threat to Indigenous communities, including those who live near the Amazon basin. Image from Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0).
This post is part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” This series offers insight into the lives and experiences of Indigenous peoples to build connections across regions, center Indigenous experiences, and share the stories of leaders, activists, community members, and more. You can support this coverage by donating here.
There are 476 million Indigenous people in the world, about 6.2 percent of the global population. Though only 25 percent of the Earth’s landmass is left to be stewarded by these original inhabitants, they have long protected global biodiversity — often better than any official government programs and efforts. For hundreds of years, Indigenous groups have weathered colonization, violent settler occupation, oppression, and forced assimilation. Yet despite this dark past — which continues today in the 21st century — Indigenous people continue to fight for their fundamental rights and their own lands and resources.
As I read through the pieces Global Voices’ authors contributed to the August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights,” one common question stands out for me: Who gets to decide? We are past the question of whether Indigenous peoples deserve recognition, land, cultural, and political representation. The key is to ask who holds the power to grant or withhold, and who gets to decide on Indigenous identity, land, culture, safety, and profit.
Not all Indigenous peoples can claim their Indigenous identities because the state sometimes denies this right.
A genocide by the Ottoman Empire wiped out nearly 75 percent of the Assyrian people, and the Iraqi army led another genocide in 1933. Yet, not a single constitution of the region recognizes the Assyrians as an Indigenous people.
It took 30 years for Taiwan’s Siraya people to be officially recognized as Indigenous, but Japan’s Ryūkyūan people have only seen denials by the state. The Ryūkyūan were once removed from their own lands by the U.S. military during World War II. Decades later, the U.S. military continues to hoard Okinawan land through its military bases and destroy natural resources through unchecked pollution.
In Europe, “autochthonous,” perceived descendants of the original inhabitants, has become a discursive tool to promote nationalism and build hate against the “guests,” the immigrants. Ironically, depictions of Native American “heroes” in European popular culture have fuelled this.
While recognition as an Indigenous people is a critical first step for any Indigenous community, it does not always translate to decision-making. When Indigenous leaders in Nueva Vizcaya, the Philippines, organized an anti-mining rally, they were arrested and charged, with over 30 criminal cases filed against them. Brazil’s case was even scarier — 258 Indigenous people were murdered in 2025 for defending their land rights, according to Cimi (the Missionary Indigenist Council). In Thailand, mining activities are polluting the Kok River. Hundreds of villagers, Indigenous leaders, monks, and civil and environmental rights activists carried out a “peace walk” to defend their Indigenous cultural identity and a vital source of drinking water, irrigation, fisheries, and transportation.
Almost always, when the state goes against its Indigenous peoples, it is to extract the latter’s lands, waters, other natural resources, or community products. Lack of Indigenous recognition also translates to significant state control over lands and land-related decisions. China’s new cotton law mechanized cotton production, making the cotton supply chain state-traceable, state-inspectable, and state-governable through data. Concurrently, this policy coerced over seven million Uyghur, Tibetan, and other Indigenous farmers to use their own lands under significant government supervision. In northern Tanzania, the Indigenous Maasai lands are taken by the state in the name of environmental protection only to use them for tourism, hunting, and private investments.
All of these stories raise the original question — who gets to decide. When Indigenous communities control decisions, they are able to protect and nurture their lands, resources, languages, and cultures. For example, 14 members of the Kam community in Nigeria created 307 audiovisual recordings in the Kam language, which has 8,000–11,000 speakers, after receiving training from a linguist, buffering against the threat of language endangerment. In India, Kshetrabasi Juanga, an Indigenous educator, goes from village to village, documenting the endangered Juang language. Far away in Russia, the Buryat fashion designer Oksana Alkhunsaeva has created an occupation for herself that both employs and supports her whole family, and keeps the Buryat textile heritage alive.
The question of who gets to decide also shapes the impact of modernization on Indigenous communities. As Nepal’s Rana Tharu language is threatened due to the prioritization of English and Nepali, women often become the last line of defense, preventing the loss of local languages. Dambe, a martial art form of Nigeria’s Hausa tribe, sees the new safety measures, regulations, and modernization through organized tournaments as a welcome step. But YouTube contests that attract external participation and viewership are erasing the Hausa cultural heritage long associated with it.
There is a strong case for the protection of Indigenous knowledge, and even state support, when its economic value flows into the community. Ghana’s traditional medicine sector serves 60 to 70 percent of the population, as the profit-driven Western medicine market fails to make medicines affordable. The cassava, millet, and sorghum market is expanding across Africa, as these Indigenous crops are a better alternative to imported wheat- economical and gluten-free- opening potential for leading an international market. Indigenous knowledge and data are a core part of AI policies. As Chadian environmental activist Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim rightly puts it, “Indigenous peoples must be recognized as rights holders and decision-makers — especially when newfangled technology has implications for their lands or intellectual heritage.”
The state’s control over Indigenous bodies goes hand-in-hand with state surveillance. In Australia, Indigenous children are 23 times more likely to be under supervision and 28 times more likely to be in detention.
What really stands out for me is what Genner Llanes-Ortiz, a Mexican Mayan researcher, argues — most modern state structures have categorically failed to understand the Indigenous communities. These societies once lived on the lands that provide homes to the descendants of settler-colonists as well as those who arrived in other ways.
One important human aspect we may forget when discussing these issues is that the onus of protecting and preserving Indigenous cultures falls on individuals like Kshetrabasi Juang or Oksana Alkhunsaeva. There is an urgent need for resources — for more Indigenous individuals to collaborate before the few individual leaders burn out.
Written by Subhashish Panigrahi
