items.title: Ten Dangote Shares Will Not Save the North
items.summary:
Samaila Mohammed’s intervention, “The People’s Share: Democratising Wealth and Securing the North’s Stake in the Dangote Refinery,” raises an important question: should Northerners participate in the proposed Dangote Refinery share offer?
My answer is simple: yes, if they can afford it, understand the investment and are comfortable with the risks.
But I respectfully disagree with the larger proposition that subscribing to Dangote Refinery shares represents, in any meaningful structural sense, securing the North’s economic stake.
The IPO is not the problem.
Our definition of economic inclusion is.
If the response of the North to one of Africa’s greatest industrial achievements is to mobilise ordinary Northerners to buy ten shares, while the region continues to lose ownership of the businesses operating in its own communities, then we may once again be confusing financial participation with economic empowerment.
And that is a dangerous confusion.
The Northern Stake: Whose Stake?
The phra
items.content:
Samaila Mohammed’s intervention, “The People’s Share: Democratising Wealth and Securing the North’s Stake in the Dangote Refinery,” raises an important question: should Northerners participate in the proposed Dangote Refinery share offer?
My answer is simple: yes, if they can afford it, understand the investment and are comfortable with the risks.
But I respectfully disagree with the larger proposition that subscribing to Dangote Refinery shares represents, in any meaningful structural sense, securing the North’s economic stake.
The IPO is not the problem.
Our definition of economic inclusion is.
If the response of the North to one of Africa’s greatest industrial achievements is to mobilise ordinary Northerners to buy ten shares, while the region continues to lose ownership of the businesses operating in its own communities, then we may once again be confusing financial participation with economic empowerment.
And that is a dangerous confusion.
The Northern Stake: Whose Stake?
The phrase “Northern stake” sounds compelling. But we should pause and ask: what exactly constitutes a Northern stake?
Is it ten shares in Dangote Refinery?
One hundred shares?
A few wealthy Northern investors holding significant portfolios?
Or is it the capacity of ordinary Northerners to own and control productive enterprises across the economy?
I believe the latter is the real measure.
A region becomes economically powerful not merely because its citizens own shares in a few large corporations. It becomes powerful when its people own, manage, finance, process, manufacture, distribute and brand the goods and services consumed by their communities and the wider economy.
We need millions of owners.
Not merely millions of shareholders.
The uncomfortable reality around us
Walk through virtually any Northern city.
Look at the welders.
The mechanics.
The furniture makers.
The POP artisans.
The electricians.
The plumbers.
The building contractors.
The private schools.
The clinics.
The pharmacies.
The restaurants.
The transport operators.
The small manufacturers.
The food processors.
The distributors.
The question is not whether these businesses exist.
The question is:
Who owns them?
Too often, a significant proportion of the more organised and commercially successful businesses serving Northern markets are owned or managed by people who came from outside the region.
This is not an argument against them.
They have every right to invest, work and prosper anywhere in Nigeria.
Indeed, their entrepreneurial success should be studied rather than resented.
The uncomfortable question is why we are not producing enough owners ourselves.
That is the real Northern economic crisis.
The kuli-kuli paradox
Consider something as ordinary as kuli-kuli.
The North has produced groundnuts for generations. Yet a young entrepreneur arriving through NYSC can sometimes recognise the commercial opportunity in processing, packaging and branding kuli-kuli more quickly than the communities that have produced it for decades.
The same phenomenon can be seen in sugarcane juice and countless other products.
This should provoke reflection.
Why should an outsider come into our communities and commercialise opportunities that have always been available to us?
The problem is not a shortage of resources.
It is a shortage of enterprise formation, commercial organisation, branding, technology, access to capital and entrepreneurial confidence.
And until we confront this honestly, we will remain consumers in an economy whose opportunities we should be controlling.
The IPO is not the economic revolution
Let me be clear: there is nothing wrong with buying Dangote Refinery shares.
If a young Nigerian has ₦5,250 and chooses to invest it, that may be a perfectly reasonable financial decision, provided the investor understands that shares are investments and not guaranteed wealth.
But we should not oversell this as the great solution to Northern economic exclusion.
Ten shares will not create a welding business.
They will not establish a mechanic’s workshop.
They will not build a private school.
They will not finance a diagnostic centre.
They will not establish a grain-processing factory.
They will not create a logistics company.
And they will not turn a farmer into an industrialist.
The capital market is important.
But productive enterprise is foundational.
Agriculture: our greatest missed opportunity
Nowhere is this failure more obvious than agriculture.
The North possesses enormous comparative advantages in groundnuts, sesame, hibiscus, grains, onions, tomatoes, livestock, cotton and numerous other commodities.
Yet we remain too heavily concentrated at the bottom of the value chain.
We grow.
Others aggregate.
Others process.
Others package.
Others brand.
Others export.
And others capture the larger margins.
This is where the conversation should be.
Agriculture must become industry.
The farmer must become connected to storage, processing, manufacturing and markets.
Farmers should have equity in processing companies.
Cooperatives should own warehouses.
Young entrepreneurs should build brands around Northern commodities.
Local manufacturers should supply local and national markets.
And investment should move from merely financing production to financing the entire value chain.
The question should no longer be:
“How many tonnes did we produce?”
It should be:
“How much of the value created from those tonnes do we own?”
That is the economic question.
The North needs an MSME ownership revolution
The real transformation will come when the Northern MSME ecosystem becomes stronger, larger and increasingly owned by Northerners.
Imagine thousands of modern fabrication businesses replacing fragmented roadside welding operations.
Mechanics evolving into organised automotive-service companies.
Artisans becoming construction and finishing companies.
Women forming commercially viable food-processing enterprises.
Young graduates establishing technology and logistics businesses.
Farmers becoming shareholders in agro-processing companies.
Local enterprises becoming suppliers to major corporations.
That is how wealth becomes broad-based.
That is how jobs are created.
That is how communities accumulate capital.
That is how the next generation acquires productive assets rather than merely inheriting poverty or depending on government.
Let the elite buy Dangote
So, yes, let the Northern elite buy Dangote shares.
Let sophisticated investors participate in the capital market.
Let ordinary Nigerians who have surplus funds invest according to their capacity and risk appetite.
But while the elite are scrambling for the IPO, let us build something far more important for the ordinary Northerner.
Let us enable him to own the welding machine.
Let her own the food-processing equipment.
Let the farmer own part of the processing plant.
Let the cooperative own the warehouse.
Let the young entrepreneur own the brand.
Let the mechanic own the workshop.
Let the artisan become the contractor.
Let the small trader become the distributor.
Let the Northern consumer become the Northern producer.
Dangote should inspire us—not distract us
Perhaps the greatest lesson from Aliko Dangote’s achievement is not that Northerners should buy a small portion of what he has built.
It is that Northerners should build.
Dangote’s journey demonstrates what long-term capital, entrepreneurship, industrial vision, persistence and risk-taking can accomplish.
The North should seek to produce its own generation of industrialists.
Not merely traders.
Not merely politicians.
Not merely property owners.
But manufacturers, processors, technology entrepreneurs, logistics companies, pharmaceutical businesses, construction firms, agricultural conglomerates and globally competitive brands.
We should not merely seek a Northern stake in somebody else’s industrialisation.
We should become participants in—and leaders of—our own industrialisation.
From consumers to owners
The economic progression should be clear:
Consumer tovProducer to Processor to Manufacturer to Brand Owner to Investor to Global Entrepreneur.
We cannot jump from consumer directly to investor and pretend that structural transformation has occurred.
The foundation is productive enterprise.
Capital-market investment is important, but it should be the top of the pyramid, not the foundation.
This is why I believe the conversation initiated by Samaila Mohammed should be expanded rather than dismissed.
Let the Dangote IPO be an opportunity for investment.
But let it also be a wake-up call.
The real question for the North is not:
“How many shares of Dangote Refinery can we buy?”
It is:
“How many businesses can we own?”
How many Northern-owned MSMEs can we create?
How many can we scale?
How many agricultural value chains can we control?
How many Northern brands can we put on supermarket shelves across Nigeria and on international markets?
How many entrepreneurs can we turn into industrialists?
That is the conversation that matters.
The North does not need to remain permanently at the periphery of Nigeria’s wealth creation, celebrating small fragments of ownership in enterprises built by others.
We must build from the foundation upward.
The Dangote Refinery is an extraordinary Nigerian achievement.
Let us celebrate it.
Let those who can invest do so.
But let Dangote’s success provoke something bigger than an IPO subscription campaign.
Let it provoke an ownership revolution.
Because ultimately:
Ten Dangote shares will not save the North.
Millions of Northern owners might.

items.author: Baba Martins
items.content:
Vice-President Kashim Shettima has arrived in New Delhi, India, to represent President Bola Ahmed Tinubu at the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit.
The summit is part of Nigeria’s efforts to deepen bilateral relations, expand trade and investment opportunities, and strengthen cooperation with member and partner countries of the bloc.
The summit is being held under the theme: “Building Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”
Shettima is leading a high-level Nigerian delegation comprising the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Ojukwu; Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani; Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, amongst others.
Speaking ahead of the summit, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Ojukwu, said Nigeria will explore new partnerships and opportunities in agriculture, technology, artificial intelligence, trade, the digital economy and other critical sectors.
She said Nigeria also intends to draw lessons from India’s experience in deploying technology and artificial intelligence to create opportunities for its large youth population.
“India is firm in its expertise in agriculture and, of course, even in the digital economy. In fact, prior to this, we had a session dealing with women in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and we are leveraging on India’s greatest strength, which is in the engagement of its youth population,” the Minister said.
On her part, the Minister of Industry, Trade and Investment said the President Tinubu administration is working to deepen Nigeria’s trade relationship with India, which she noted had previously stood at about $14 billion.
She disclosed that major investors of Indian origin have indicated interest in meeting the Nigerian delegation, adding that Nigeria also maintains important trade relationships with several BRICS countries.
“And so, deepening those relationships will further strengthen the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration. India used to buy Nigerian oil a lot, so we are looking at how to expand that with everything going on in the world,” Oduwole said.
At the summit, Senator Shettima will join leaders of BRICS member and partner countries, as well as invited international organisations, for high-level discussions on inclusive global growth, resilience, innovation and sustainable development.
The Vice President will also participate in bilateral engagements aimed at advancing Nigeria’s economic and diplomatic interests, particularly in trade, investment, agriculture, technology, industrial development and other areas of mutual benefit.
Nigeria became a BRICS partner country in January 2025 and has since engaged the platform to strengthen South-South cooperation and broaden its relations with major emerging economies.

Former Islamabad Police chief Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi is set to assume his new role as Director General of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), sources told ProPakistani.
Rizvi served as Inspector General of Islamabad Police after taking charge in April 2024. During his tenure, he oversaw policing, security and law-and-order operations in the federal capital.
His transfer comes as part of a reshuffle in the federal capital’s policing and cybercrime investigation setup. Captain (Retd.) Sohail Chaudhry is his replacement as Islamabad Police chief.
The NCCIA is Pakistan’s specialized agency responsible for investigating cybercrime and taking legal action against cybercriminals. Its work includes handling complaints involving online fraud, harassment and data breaches, along with digital forensics and technical investigations.
The agency was established as the central body for cybercrime investigations, replacing the Federal Investigation Agency’s cybercrime wing. It now operates through offices across the country and directly receives complaints related to cyber offences.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
With an eye on expanding its financial services offerings, Amazon Pay is now reportedly doubling down on insurance in India.
Speaking with Reuters, Amazon Pay India CEO Vikas Bansal said that the company is expanding its insurance offerings to include travel insurance and ​other products.
As per Bansal, the expansion plans are reportedly part of Amazon Pay’s strategy to evolve from a mere payments processor to a broader financial service platform comprising credit, insurance and savings and investment products.
“Obviously travel…there could ⁠be others in the future as well,” Bansal reportedly added when asked if the company plans to launch other insurance products in ​the future.
This comes barely a day after Amazon Pay partnered with HDFC ERGO to foray into the health insurance space. “Health is our next frontier,” Bansal reportedly said, adding ‌that ⁠health insurance is an important area for expansion as a relatively small proportion of Indians have personal health insurance.
It is pertinent to note that Amazon first entered the insurance distribution business in 2020, when it partnered with ACKO General Insurance to offer car and two-wheeler insurance. The ecommerce giant’s fintech arm operates as a registered corporate agent, allowing it to distribute insurance products from licenced insurers.
Since then, Amazon Pay has onboarded HDFC ERGO and ICICI Lombard to offer vehicle insurance.
Amazon’s insurance push is part of a broader effort to build out its financial services stack in India. As of now, the fintech platform allows users to transfer money, pay bills, buy insurance, travel tickets, invest in mutual funds and purchase digital gold. But it is diversifying.
Earlier this year, Amazon Pay partnered with multiple non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) and small finance banks to roll out pan-India fixed deposit (FD) service.
At the recently concluded Global Fintech Fest 2026, Amazon Pay also partnered with Kotak Mahindra Bank to launch a co-branded credit card for small businesses registered on Amazon Business, the company’s dedicated B2B marketplace.
On the financial front, Amazon Pay India reported an operating revenue of ₹2,097 Cr in FY25, down 8.3% from ₹2,287 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. Meanwhile, net losses declined a mere 5% to ₹866 Cr from ₹911 Cr in FY24.

items.content:
By Salim Ashir Mahuta, Sokoto
Residents of communities in Tambuwal Local Government Area of Sokoto State on Friday took to the streets to protest incessant attacks and kidnappings, demanding urgent deployment of security personnel to their communities.
The protesters, who were said to have come from several villages displaced by bandit attacks, blocked the Tambuwal-Jega and Tambuwal-Aleiro roads Friday morning, according to a resident who witnessed the protest.
The resident, who asked not to be named, said the protesters are displaced residents from communities including Margai, Girkau, Romon Liman, Romon Sarki and Masu, and organised it in the early hours of Friday to demand improved security.
He said the protest started in the morning and continued until about 1pm, adding that the protesters were demanding protection after being forced to flee their communities with their families because of repeated attacks.

Yobe records 511 diphtheria cases, 13 deaths in 9 months
Videos obtained by Daily Trust showed residents expressing anger over the attacks and what they described as lack of government assistance after being displaced from their communities.
In one of the videos, a large number of youths were seen chanting, “We want justice”, while some protesters were also seen burning tyres.
The video did not show the APC office being set ablaze, The resident said the protesters later set fire to an APC office.
The resident also insisted that the protesters were not members of opposition political parties.
He said a person was shot during the protest.
A young man identified as Usama Ibrahim, who was shot in the thigh during the protest, alleged that security personnel fired the shot that injured him.
The protest came amid growing concerns over the security situation in parts of Tambuwal and Kebbe LGAs where attacks and abductions have continued to threaten residents and their livelihoods.
The residents said the insecurity had affected farming and other economic activities, with many people forced to leave their communities and seek safety in Tambuwal town.
They called on the Federal and Sokoto State governments to take urgent measures to protect residents and enable those displaced by the attacks to return to their communities.
When contacted, the Sokoto state Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufai, said the police deployed personnel to the area and brought the situation under control before the protest ended.

items.content:
Bank AL Habib has launched AL Habib Digital, a fully native mobile banking application and one of the most significant digital upgrades in the Bank’s history.
The launch arrives as mobile banking in Pakistan grows at pace. Mobile app-based payments accounted for 78 percent of all digital payments in the country in the January to March 2026 quarter, with 2.9 billion transactions processed through banking apps in that period alone. For a Bank operating 1,354 branches across 550 cities, the pressure to offer a mobile experience that matches rising customer expectations has grown accordingly, and AL Habib Digital is the Bank’s response.
What’s new in the app
Unlike a typical update, AL Habib Digital has been rebuilt as a fully native application, delivering faster performance and smoother navigation throughout.
A customizable dashboard lets customers organize the services they use most, while interactive widgets bring key actions within reach without navigating through multiple menus. Biometric login, FPIN authentication for transactions, and Dark and Light Mode round out an experience built to be secure without feeling restrictive.
&&&&&&&
Everyday banking, simplified
Instant fund transfers without payee registration, bill payments, mobile recharges and QR payments are all available within the app. Full debit card management, activating, blocking or unblocking a card, changing a PIN and managing transaction limits, is also included, removing the need for a branch visit or helpline call for routine requests.
Why the timing matters
Mobile banking users in Pakistan have reached 137 million, with retail digital transactions nearly doubling over the past year. As the market grows, AL Habib Digital positions Bank AL Habib with a product built around how customers already bank.
AL Habib Digital is available now on the App Store, Google Play and Huawei AppGallery.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Climate tech startup Mitti Labs has signed a four-year agreement with Google to supply 1 Mn Carbon credits till 2030, which it describes as one of the largest nature-based offtakes to date
The financial terms of the agreement have not been disclosed. However, Mitti Labs said the deal is a fixed contractual offtake covering 1 Mn credits, delivered between 2027 and 2030.
Mitti Labs said payments will be made upon delivery of the verified carbon credits, with no upfront financing involved in the agreement.
The credits will primarily be generated from Mitti Labs’ rice farming projects in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka. The startup currently has programmes covering more than 1 Lakh hectares in India.
“We are currently working on expanding both across India and Southeast Asia. This deal with Google doesn’t just validate the quality of the projects, the use of our MRV and the scalability of our projects, but will also help us scale our India projects,” cofounder Xavier Laguarta Soler told Inc42.
Kate Brandt, Google’s chief sustainability officer, said Mitti Labs’ approach could cut methane emissions while conserving water and helping smallholder farmers adopt more efficient irrigation practices.
“Mitti Labs’ approach delivers critical near-term atmospheric impact by cutting methane emissions, while conserving billions of gallons of water and empowering smallholder farmers to deploy advanced water-management practices. We’re excited to partner with them to help accelerate and scale their solution across India,” Brandt said.
The agreement comes a month after Mitti Labs raised $9.5 Mn in a Series A round led by Aramco Ventures. The funding is being used to expand its operations across India and develop new greenfield projects in the Philippines and Indonesia.
Cutting Methane By Changing How Rice Is Grown
Rice farming is a major Methane producer, a potent greenhouse gas. Flooding fields creates oxygen-poor conditions in which methane-producing microbes thrive.
Mitti Labs works with farmers to introduce a practice known as alternate wetting and drying (AWD).
Developed by the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI), the technique involves allowing fields to dry periodically before they are irrigated again.
The approach can reduce the conditions that produce methane while using less water, as per Mitti Labs, without affecting crop yields.
Mitti Labs trains farmers and provides support as they adopt the practice. It also shares revenue from the resulting carbon credits with participating farming communities.
Mitti Labs’ AI platform combines high-resolution synthetic aperture radar, remote sensing and biogeochemical models with on-the-ground measurements to estimate changes in greenhouse gas emissions and water use.
Water savings are also measured using flow meters. The GeoAI platform has been developed with support from NASA through a grant.
Mitti Labs has also begun expanding outside India, with the Philippines serving as its first south-east Asian pilot market. It is exploring other major rice-producing markets in the region.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Friday, four Yemeni government sources told Reuters, moving to tighten their grip on a vital global shipping route in the widening Middle East war.
Earlier, two sources from the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised Yemeni government said its forces had pulled out of Perim and that the Houthis had also taken the mainland Red Sea coastal town of Dhubab, which faces the island.
If the Houthis gain control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz, it could give their backer Iran a critical advantage in its war with the US, reducing supplies through a second major corridor and further raising oil prices.
The war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran six months ago and Hormuz, conduit for about a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade, was effectively closed. Since then Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter and a close US ally, has relied on the Red Sea route. Iran and the US have escalated attacks this week on Gulf shipping. US President Donald Trump has jacked up economic pressure on Tehran.
Iran confirmed on Friday that its representatives and those of Iraq and the Gulf Arab states would meet in Oman on Monday to resume discussions on safe commercial shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz.
In a speech marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks on the US, Trump called Iran "the world's number one sponsor of terror". Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian responded by saying the accusation came from "the same devils" responsible for an apparent US strike on a school at the start of the conflict in February.
Satellite imagery verified by Reuters showed smoke on Thursday in the vicinity of Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, a vital means for the kingdom to divert crude exports from Hormuz.
The pipeline was temporarily shut on Thursday following attacks, Saudi state media reported, citing a source in the energy ministry, who added that the attacks resulted in a number of injuries.
There was no confirmation from Saudi Arabia of any incident in the area. The Saudi government media office and state oil giant Aramco did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Saudi crude supply fell 2.3 million barrels per day on the month in August to 6 million bpd, the lowest in more than three decades, the International Energy Agency said on Friday, partly due to the targeting of ships transiting Bab el-Mandeb by Houthi-linked groups.
Oil prices dipped on Friday but were on track to end the week above $100 a barrel for the first time since mid-May.
Vessels tracked transiting the Strait of Hormuz fell to seven on Thursday from 11 the previous day, preliminary ship-tracking data showed on Friday, below the 10-day average. Before the war, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessels per day.
The Houthi military spokesperson, Yahya Saree, said maritime navigation remained safe for all shipping except Saudi vessels subject to a previously announced ban.
"We will continue to enforce blockade for blockade and escalation for escalation until the aggression stops and the blockade on our people is lifted," he said, referring to Saudi attacks on Yemen.
 
YEMENI GOVERNMENT FORCES PLOT COUNTER-OFFENSIVE
Yemeni government forces indicated they would try to retake areas captured by the Houthis - mountain fighters who withstood years of devastating Saudi airstrikes during Yemen's civil war - in their lightning offensive this week along the Red Sea coastline.
They announced they would deploy weapons and aircraft to eliminate any movement of the "terrorist" Houthi militias in strategic areas, including the road leading to the coastal city of Mocha, which the militant group captured on Thursday along with the Red Sea islands of Hanish.
Reuters reported on Thursday that the dramatic Houthi advance down Yemen's Red Sea coast came with direct guidance from Iran's Revolutionary Guards seeking to open a new front in the war with the US, according to Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources.
Iran told the Houthis last week to escalate their attacks on Saudi Arabia and promised more funding, weapons and senior officers to help them do so, two Iranian sources said.
Iran describes the Houthis as an ally but publicly denies giving them military direction, saying they are "not a proxy".
 
SAUDI CROWN PRINCE ASKED TRUMP FOR HELP, SOURCES SAY
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump at least twice on Thursday to request US military help in fighting the Houthis, two sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Friday, confirming an earlier report by Axios.
Washington told Riyadh it was not willing to take direct military action for now but would help with intelligence sharing and targeting, the two sources said.
The White House did not address a Reuters question on any phone calls between the two leaders, but a senior administration official speaking on the condition of anonymity said Washington was in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government.
The Saudi government media office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Trump's approval ratings have slid during the war to a record low ahead of November's US midterm elections.

items.author: Kamran Yousaf
items.content:
A senior security official has called for a fresh political and strategic approach to Balochistan, arguing that the province's complex problems cannot be resolved through the use of force alone and that the way forward lies in sustained dialogue with ordinary Baloch people.
"We need to win peace, not war, in Balochistan," the official told a group of journalists during a briefing held in Quetta on Friday, stressing the problem would not be solved through bullets but through dialogue, he said.
"The real issue is the narrative," he said, adding that while the challenges confronting Balochistan were serious, they were "not insurmountable".
The official said Pakistan needed a long-term strategic vision for the province, including what he described as a 10-year plan, rather than relying on short-term responses to security crises.
"There is no traitor in Balochistan. Ninety-nine point nine per cent are patriots, just like people in other parts of Pakistan," he said.
He acknowledged that people in the province had genuine grievances, although some concerns were being amplified or exploited for political purposes. "We respect them," he said, emphasising that the state should engage with common people rather than notables and sardars who only exploited the situation for their own benefits.
According to the official, authorities had held around 54,000 engagements with people in Balochistan last year and another 34,000 this year as part of efforts to reach out to local communities.
"We dialogue with the masses, not with Sardars," he said, arguing that the focus should remain on ordinary citizens.
The official said those who had taken up arms against the state would continue to be dealt with through security operations, but maintained that a political solution had to accompany the kinetic response.
"Those who take up arms are dealt with arms," he said, adding that the broader objective was to bring people into the political mainstream.
The official identified what he called political deprivation as one of the central problems facing Balochistan, rather than simply economic deprivation.
He pointed out that the province had only 16 seats in the National Assembly despite accounting for nearly half of Pakistan's landmass.
"When was the last time a major political party held a public rally in Balochistan?" he asked, suggesting that the absence of mainstream political parties had created a vacuum that was increasingly being filled by social movements and narratives promoted through social media.
He argued that the Baloch voice remained under-represented in parliament, noting that Balochistan was the only province where, in some areas, one National Assembly constituency covers as many as four districts.
The official also blamed elite capture and corruption for preventing available financial resources from translating into development, while saying that a large portion of the province's economy had historically remained outside the formal system.
He said the government needed to develop a strategic vision for the province and answer a basic question: "When shall Balochistan develop?"
The official described Balochistan as the centre of an emerging contest over strategic resources, arguing that the province's mineral wealth and its location had made it vulnerable to regional and international power competition.
"Balochistan is Pakistan's future," he said, pointing to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, mines and minerals and the province's strategic location.
He claimed the province possessed enormous deposits of gold, copper and rare-earth minerals, estimating their potential value at around $6 trillion. He also referred to the province's fisheries, gas reserves and other natural resources as major untapped economic opportunities.
He said the Sarona block contained gas reserves several times larger than those of Sui but had remained stalled because of tribal opposition.
The official argued that wherever large natural resources were discovered, competition and instability often followed, adding that efforts were under way to undermine CPEC and exploit local grievances.
He described Balochistan as a "victim of great-power competition" and said regional rivalries had further complicated the situation.
The official identified four broad categories of threats: kinetic terrorism, non-kinetic activity including social media campaigns, "sub-kinetic" activity and socially disruptive proxies.
He alleged that foreign-backed terrorist networks continued to operate against Pakistan and revealed that Baloch terrorist leader Dr Allah Nazar was hiding in one of the neighbouring countries.
He said Pakistan had sought the return of wanted terrorists and that red notices had been issued against a number of terrorists.
The official linked the recent increase in terrorism in Balochistan and elsewhere to developments following the US withdrawal from Afghanistan, saying the current year had witnessed the deadliest phase of terrorism in Balochistan in recent years.
He cited official security figures showing that 1,263 terrorists had been killed this year.
He also highlighted what he described as the significant improvement in counter-smuggling operations. According to him, around Rs1.2 trillion worth of smuggling had previously been taking place through Balochistan, but nearly 90% of it had now been curtailed.
He said the smuggling of Iranian oil had fallen sharply from around 20 million litres a day to about one million litres.
The official stressed that security measures alone could not produce lasting peace and called for a policy shift combining political engagement, development, security and diplomacy.
He said diplomatic manoeuvring also needed to be activated, particularly with Iran and Afghanistan, to ensure that wanted terrorists and those involved in terrorism could be brought to justice.
The official said the state had reached out to people across Balochistan and would continue doing so.
"Embrace Balochistan. If resisted, embrace more firmly," he said.
He acknowledged that the state had yet to find a political way out of the crisis but insisted that winning over the common Baloch was ultimately the key to success.
"We will win when we win over the common Baloch," he said.
The official also said attempts had been made to engage Mahrang Baloch, but she had declined to enter into dialogue on several occasions.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday took notice of increasing electricity load-shedding in various cities across the country and expressed displeasure over the situation, directing that no area should face load-shedding for more than two hours.
The prime minister gave these directions while chairing an important review meeting on power load management in the country, a Prime Minister's Office news release said.
The meeting was informed that due to the prevailing regional situation, tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and transportation difficulties affecting the supply of Regasified Liquefied Natural Gas (RLNG), electricity generation had been reduced, resulting in a decrease in power output. Consequently, load management had to be carried out to maintain balance between demand and supply.
The prime minister directed that keeping in view the regional situation and future requirements, immediate measures be taken to address the disruption in RLNG supply.
He directed that all available resources be utilized effectively so that no area faces load-shedding for more than two hours.
The prime minister also ordered the establishment of Consumer Grievance Redressal Committees at the level of power distribution companies (DISCOs) to address public complaints related to electricity supply and other issues across the country.
He directed that the redressal committees should also include public representation, and that the grievance committees be made functional within one week.
The meeting was informed that electricity consumers could lodge their complaints through helpline number 118, and that upon registering a complaint, the consumer is provided with a token number as well as the expected time for resolution of the complaint.
The meeting was further informed that at present, except for six electricity consumers in Rajanpur district, no consumer across the country was facing disruption in power supply due to monsoon rains.
 
Agriculture
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif stressed that effective coordination and partnership between the federal and provincial governments was essential for increasing per-acre agricultural productivity, introducing innovation in agriculture, developing the livestock sector and promoting agricultural exports.
Chairing a high-level meeting on promotion of agriculture sector and enhancement of agriculture exports, the prime minister directed that coordinated measures be taken to expand access for Pakistani agricultural products to international markets and explore new markets.
He directed commercial officers posted at Pakistan's missions abroad to play an effective role in promoting agricultural exports.
He also directed that an effective media campaign be launched to raise awareness among farmers about the mobile application available for monitoring crops.
The prime minister said value addition in agricultural products was essential for increasing exports from the agriculture sector.
He said that the agriculture sector played a key role in the growth and stability of Pakistan's economy.
Proposals were presented at the meeting for the development of the agriculture sector and promotion of agricultural exports.
The meeting was informed that Pakistan's agricultural exports stood at US$5.18 billion during the last financial year. Rice, fisheries, halal meat, potatoes, sesame, tobacco, mangoes and maize were among Pakistan's major agricultural exports.
The meeting proposed the development of value chains to increase agricultural exports.
China, Saudi Arabia, Iran and the Gulf countries were identified as important markets for Pakistan's agricultural exports, the briefing said adding that the National Agriculture and Food Security Council would be made functional.
The chief ministers would represent their respective provinces in the National Agriculture and Food Security Council, the briefing said.
The meeting was briefed on a proposal to establish a Digital Farmers' Diary-Agri Stack, under which farmers across the country and agricultural land records would be digitized. Under the Digital Farmers' Diary-Agri Stack, records related to soil and water testing would also be digitized.
A Pakistan-Good Agriculture Practices (Pak-GAP) system would be developed to promote agricultural practices that produce better results, it was further proposed. Facilities related to agricultural financing would be provided to promote exporters in the agriculture sector.

Broadband internet services will be restored across the capital city of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) on Sunday (tomorrow), providing residents with access to fixed-line internet after prolonged restrictions on mobile data services.
Sources told The Express Tribune, the DSL connectivity will also be restored while 3G and 4G mobile internet services will remain unavailable.
The move is expected to provide some relief to students, businesses, journalists, professionals and households that have faced difficulties accessing online services during the suspension of mobile internet.
However, the continued absence of 3G and 4G services means users dependent on mobile data will remain without connectivity, particularly those who do not have access to fixed-line DSL connections.
The restoration of DSL services comes amid continued demands from residents and business communities for the restoration of normal internet connectivity across the region.
AJK High Court Judge Justice Shahid Bahar had issued directions on Wednesday for the restoration of internet services within 10 days.
Justice Bahar issued the directions during the preliminary hearing of two separate petitions filed by the AJK Bar Association and a local citizen seeking the restoration of internet services. The court clubbed the petitions and directed the government to ensure restoration within 10 days, while allowing an exception for areas where law and order conditions did not permit the resumption of services.
The order comes after months of disruption to internet connectivity in AJK, which has severely affected education, businesses, government operations and digital services.
On August 31, on the directives of AJK Prime Minister Iftikhar Gilani, authorities issued a notification partially restoring internet services in several districts. The DSL services were subsequently restored in areas including Mirpur, Neelum and Haveli, but full connectivity remained unavailable in Muzaffarabad.
Internet services were initially suspended on June 5 following a long march and sit-in announced by the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee in Rawalakot. After around 48 days of disruption, services were partially restored, but connectivity in Muzaffarabad was suspended again on July 25 following a strike and clashes.
Prime Minister Gilani had announced the restoration of internet services during his first media interaction at the Muzaffarabad Press Club on August 31.
The prolonged suspension has taken a heavy toll on economic and professional activities. Students have been among the worst affected, while traders dependent on digital payments have suffered financial losses. Freelancers, government employees and other professionals have also faced difficulties performing routine work due to the lack of reliable internet access.

items.content:
Amid the looming September 27 protest, the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Friday stepped up efforts to bring opposition parties under one umbrella, reaching out to Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman while moving towards an all-parties conference on the country's political, constitutional and economic challenges.
The latest round of opposition consultations came as PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan invited Fazlur Rehman and the wider joint opposition to participate in the September 27 march, which the PTI says will be peaceful and aimed at seeking justice, fresh elections and protection of constitutional rights.
A PTI delegation led by Gohar and comprising former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser met Fazlur Rehman at his residence on Friday. The two sides discussed the September 27 protest, the proposed all-parties conference and the formation of a joint opposition.
The Maulana and other JUI-F leaders received the delegation.
Joint opposition in NA, Senate
Speaking to the media after the meeting, Gohar said the two sides had already agreed in principle on a joint opposition in both the National Assembly and Senate.
"Talks were held with Maulana Fazlur Rehman on a joint opposition. There had been an agreement on a joint opposition in the Senate and National Assembly," he said.
"We have decided that all political parties will be taken into confidence on national issues," Gohar said.
He said an all-parties conference was being planned to discuss the issue of new provinces, while the proposed joint opposition platform would also hold consultations on parliamentary sessions and the issue of prisoners.
"The first meeting today was encouraging and will continue in the future," he said.
Gohar separately said the opposition wanted broader political consultations on the country's worsening political and economic conditions.
"We decided that on all national issues, we will take political parties into confidence," he said, adding that "the current law and order situation, the economy, inflation, lawlessness, and the creation of new provinces' issue" called for an all-parties conference.
Meanwhile, according to a statement issued by the Tehreek-e-Tahaffuz Ayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP), the PTI delegation and the JUI-F chief also discussed "strengthening of the country's constitutional and democratic systems".
"The leaders also discussed the need for mutual consultation and a joint struggle among political parties to uphold the supremacy of the Constitution and the rule of law, and to safeguard democratic principles in the country," the statement added.
JUI-F leader Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haidri welcomed the PTI delegation and said the consultative ses-sion had also discussed preparations for the proposed all-parties conference.
"We welcome the arrival of the opposition," Haidri said.
He said the meeting covered the creation of provinces and various other national issues, adding that the situation in Balochistan, terrorism and other problems confronting the country would also come under discussion.
"We will try to play some role in dealing with the problems the country is facing," he said.
The latest outreach is part of a broader effort to turn the September 27 mobilisation into a joint opposi-tion campaign. PTI had begun reaching out to opposition parties last month, while on August 20 the TTAP and JUI-F announced plans to form a "united opposition" following consultations on cooperation and future political strategy.
The joint opposition subsequently held its first parliamentary meeting, attended by Fazlur Rehman, Op-position Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas Jafri, Go-har and other leaders. The meeting produced an agreement to pursue a collective strategy on political repression, the economic crisis and other national issues.
Achakzai later said he and Raja Nasir had met PTI leaders, including Gohar, and that an all-parties con-ference would be convened "at the earliest". The opposition also agreed to hold a meeting on Septem-ber 15 to review progress on preparations for the APC and decided to contact other political parties "as soon as possible".
Meanwhile, the September 27 protest has remained a firm point of convergence for the opposition. PTI leaders have repeatedly said the march will not be confined to Islamabad and have urged supporters across the country to mobilise.
On the other hand, the planned mobilisation has also become the subject of a legal challenge. A petition has been filed before the Islamabad High Court (IHC) against the PTI's planned sit-in and nationwide protest, in which the petitioner has contended that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activity in the capital and questioned the use of provincial resources for the march.
At the same time, the political landscape has seen an unusual parallel track of government-opposition engagement. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has invited Achakzai for consultations on the appointment of a new chief election commissioner, an overture that comes only days before the PTI-led September 27 march.

items.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Friday that the West is trying to regain its global leadership "by any means necessary," including through what he described as "unsavory" methods.
In an address at a BRICS Business Forum panel in the Indian capital New Delhi, Putin said that behind each corporate success story lies intense daily work amid "fierce competition."
"We have constantly been told that competition is a 'sacred cow' - something that must not be touched at all. Unfortunately, however, our Western competitors are currently trying to regain their former leadership by any means necessary," Putin said.
Saying that competition sometimes takes on "unsavory" forms, Putin said these forms can manifest even at the state level. Putin stated that the measures resorted to in this context include direct physical action against or the destruction of industrial and logistical facilities and pipelines.
"Attempts are being made to block international transport corridors and seize maritime vessels," Putin further said, noting that illegal restrictions are also being imposed, accompanied by threats of secondary sanctions against those refusing to act in the interests of others and, instead, defending their own.
He went on to say that more than 30,000 sanctions have been imposed on Russia, which he said is almost twice as many as those imposed on all countries in the world combined. "We have strengthened our national sovereignty and are developing ties with reliable, predictable partners," Putin said, adding that BRICS is ready to cooperate with all partners.
Putin arrived in India earlier on Friday on a three-day visit, during which he will attend the 18th BRICS summit taking place on Saturday and Sunday. The Russian president also held bilateral talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on trade, energy and defence.
The leaders discussed conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine, including the impact on "maritime trade and the safety and security of Indian seafarers", New Delhi's foreign ministry said in a statement after the meeting.
BRICS was created in 2009 as a forum for major emerging economies seeking greater influence in institutions dominated by Western powers. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who also arrived in New Delhi on Friday, said that "BRICS was established to counter unilateralism".
BRICS also includes Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates – countries with sharply differing positions on the war launched by the United States and Israel in February. All three have been admitted to the group in recent years, joining founding member states that include India, China and Russia.
Pezeshkian's participation – his first visit to India as Iranian president – will put the Middle East conflict firmly on the agenda. Chinese President Xi Jinping, UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan are also expected.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Two unusual games have appeared on Google Play that look remarkably similar to Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and GTA: Vice City, except they are being offered under completely different names and for free.
Screenshots circulating online show games called Mola Sola Gangstar and Barnala Tank City – Punjab, complete with imagery that closely resembles scenes from Rockstar’s classic GTA titles.
At least one of them is definitely still publicly available on Google Play.
Mola Sola Gangstar Is Live on Google Play
Mola Sola Gangstar, published by Farida Digital Innovations, currently has an active Google Play listing. Google Play describes it as a free open-world crime and action game and says it contains ads.
Its screenshots and gameplay shown on the store bear a striking resemblance to GTA: San Andreas. Even some users reviewing the game explicitly refer to San Andreas.
One reviewer thanked the developer for making what they described as GTA San Andreas available on the Play Store, while also mentioning versions with missions and unlocked content.
The listing says the game was last updated on August 22, 2026. Depending on the regional Google Play page, it has already accumulated thousands of downloads.
Another Game Looks Like Vice City
The second screenshot shows an app called Barnala Tank City – Punjab, published under the developer name Bubble Up Tech.
The listing shown in the screenshot has a 4.7-star rating from 153 reviews and appears to use gameplay imagery closely resembling GTA: Vice City.
However, we could not independently locate a currently indexed Google Play page for Barnala Tank City, so it may have already been removed, may be region-restricted, or may simply not yet be indexed by search engines.
Some mf literally uploaded GTA Vice City and GTA San Andreas on Play Store with different names for free pic.twitter.com/jNQ0I5TNdH
— 𝚂. (@cric_shub41) September 11, 2026
Rockstar’s Versions Are Paid Games
Rockstar itself continues to sell the official Android versions of both games.
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas costs $6.99 on Google Play and has more than five million downloads, while the original mobile version of GTA: Vice City is listed for $4.99. Both are published by Rockstar Games and carry Mature 17+ ratings.
That makes the appearance of free games seemingly using very similar assets particularly unusual.
There is not yet enough public evidence to establish whether the apps contain Rockstar’s original game files, modified versions of the games, emulation, or simply copied visual assets. Neither Google nor Rockstar appears to have publicly commented on the listings so far.
For now, though, at least one extremely GTA-looking game is sitting openly on the Play Store under the name Mola Sola Gangstar.

The government and opposition appeared to be moving towards a direct political engagement on Friday amid efforts to arrange a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and National Assembly Opposition Leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai.
Contacts between the offices of the prime minister and opposition leader have begun in the wake of the premier's response to Achakzai's letter on the appointment of a new chief election commissioner. At the same time, consultations are under way to schedule a meeting between the two leaders.
In a move potentially opening direct dialogue between the government and opposition, the prime minister has also invited Achakzai for mandatory consultations on the appointment of the new CEC. Achakzai has yet to respond to the invitation.
In August, a government delegation comprising Prime Minister's Adviser Rana Sanaullah, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Tariq Fazal Chaudhry met Achakzai at Parliament House, with the two sides agreeing to hold further rounds of dialogue.
Achakzai had sought the prime minister's direct involvement in discussions on political and constitutional matters.
The immediate basis for the renewed contact is the appointment of a new chief election commissioner and two members of the Election Commission of Pakistan from Sindh and Balochistan. Achakzai had written to the prime minister on August 10, urging the government to initiate the constitutional process for filling the posts.
According to reports, the premier assured the opposition leader that the constitutional procedure would be followed in making the appointments. Achakzai subsequently briefed Raja Nasir Abbas on the contents of the response, and the two agreed to share the development with other opposition leaders.
Meanwhile, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq had also recently called for political harmony and stability and urged the prime minister to initiate dialogue with the opposition, suggesting that consultations on the appointment of the new CEC could provide a starting point for the process.
A day earlier, the prime minister had sent a reply to opposition leader in the National Assembly regarding the appointment of a new chief election commissioner, sources said on Thursday.
Meanwhile, reports indicated that PM Shehbaz Sharif had moved to open a channel for dialogue by inviting Achakzai to consultations on the appointment of a new CEC.
However, the opposition leader has yet to respond to the invitation.
The timing of the move was notable, with the invitation coming just days before the PTI-led long march towards Islamabad on September 27.
It is pertinent to note that in a letter to the prime minister in August, Achakzai had urged the government to appoint a new chief election commissioner, along with two members representing Sindh and Balochistan.
Similarly, National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also recently called for political harmony and stability and urged the government to open a dialogue with the opposition.

items.content:
Pakistan called the recent upsurge of violence in the Middle East as "quite unsettling" for the peace prospects in the region, emphasizing the resolution of all outstanding issues through diplomatic engagement, when the UN Security Council debated the Iran nuclear issue on Thursday.
"Given the necessary space, diplomacy can still deliver results," Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, permanent representative of Pakistan to the UN, told the 15-member Council.
Pakistan, he said, has pursued diplomatic engagement in support of de-escalation, ceasefire and broader pursuit of stability in the region.
Convened by France, the Council President for September, Thursday's session reviewed the work of the 1737 Sanctions Committee concerning Iran, under the "Non-Proliferation" agenda item.
The 1737 Sanctions Committee was established by resolution 1737 (2006), with a requirement to report to the Council every 90 days.
Prior to the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) on Iran's nuclear programme, which the Council endorsed through resolution 2231 (2015), these briefings took place every three months under the "Non-Proliferation" agenda item.
Resolution 2231 (2015) had suspended all prior sanctions resolutions on Iran, including resolution 1737 (2006), rendering the 1737 Committee and its reporting requirement defunct.
In August 2025, France, Germany and the United Kingdom – the "E3" parties to the JCPOA – then triggered the agreement's "snapback" mechanism to reimpose UN sanctions on Iran.
In his remarks, Ambassador Asim Ahmad reaffirmed Pakistan's support for the resolution of all outstanding problems through peaceful means, diplomatic engagement and sustained dialogue, saying renewed violence and breakdown of diplomacy have also impacted the consideration of the Iran nuclear issue, including by the Security Council.
Pakistan, he said, has been undertaking constructive diplomatic engagement in supporting de-escalation, ceasefire, and the broader pursuit of stability in the region.
"Through sustained interaction at the leadership level, as well as with active coordination other partners in the region and beyond, we consistently sought to encourage dialogue, facilitate the exchange of messages, and help create space and conditions conducive to meaningful negotiations," the Pakistani envoy said.
"Our approach underscores Pakistan's enduring commitment to regional stability and international peace, reflecting our preference for principled, dialogue-oriented diplomacy in addressing geopolitical challenges."
Continued divisions have impacted the work of the Council's subsidiary bodies, he said. "We hope members will show unity and shoulder our responsibility and find common purpose in upholding international peace and security."

items.content:
The Global Fintech Festival (GFF) 2026 came to a close today with three days of conversations, launches, and partnerships. Following a day focused on partnership announcements between traditional financial institutions and fintech and AI startups, the ecosystem continued to capitalise on the momentum to roll out another wave of new developments.
Here are some of the top launches from the final day of GFF 2026…
BharatPeX Launches Enterprise Payment Gateway with Dynamic Routing
BharatPe’s enterprise payments division BharatPeX launched a payment gateway targeting ecommerce and fintechs enterprises.
The platform offers a single integration supporting over 100 payment options, including UPI, cards, net banking, and bank transfers via IMPS, NEFT, or RTGS. It consolidates checkout, settlements, refunds, payouts, and automated reconciliation into a unified operational dashboard.
It also features a dynamic routing engine that directs transactions to acquiring bank partners based on real-time success rates, card BIN performance as well as service availability.
Additionally, the BharatPeX Payment Gateway offers capabilities like native OTP, tokenisation and CVV-less payment experiences, as well as EMI options, recurring payments, and virtual account tracking.
PayU Rolls Out Agent HQ for SMB Merchants
Prosus-owned fintech startup PayU launched Agent HQ, an AI agent storefront designed to help small and medium business (SMB) merchants deploy autonomous agents across sales, marketing, and operations.
As search traffic transitions toward GenAI platforms, Agent HQ enables merchants to make their product catalogs discoverable and transactable directly on AI search systems like ChatGPT and Claude.
The no-code tool integrates directly into existing PayU dashboard without requiring additional developer integration. It is built on historical platform data from PayU’s network of over 4.5 Lakh merchants.
“By putting a personalized team of AI agents to work across the business – from improving discoverability and driving growth to managing chargebacks, reconciliations, refunds, settlements, etc. – we want to put control back in merchants’ hands, enabling them to focus on their growth,” said PayU’s CPO Manas Mishra.
Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Launches OneTag To Enable FASTag Portability
Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari launched OneTag, a portability solution for FASTags jointly developed by the Indian Highways Management Company (IHMCL) and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
As it currently stands, vehicle owners looking to switch their issuer bank must replace the physical windshield tag and undergo onboarding again. OneTag reduces this friction by enabling users retain the same tag, bringing down reissuance costs.
NPCI provides the underlying central architecture to update issuer records across the toll network. Meanwhile, users can avail the service through NHAI’s Rajmargyatra mobile app.
Existing issuer banks manage customer verification, wallet closures, refunds, and pending settlements, while the user’s selected new bank will complete the onboarding and provide services after the tag is ported. The new tag will retain the same Tag ID linked to the same vehicle registration number.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
The government has approved another $200 million foreign loan to reform the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), bringing total loans for tax system modernisation to almost $5 billion.
The Central Development Working Party (CDWP) has recommended the Transforming and Digitalising Revenue Administration (TADRA) project worth Rs57.1 billion or $200 million for approval, the Ministry of Planning said on Friday. It added that the project has been sent to the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) for further consideration. The project is proposed to be financed through foreign funding under an Asian Development Bank (ADB) loan, the ministry said.
Of the total cost, $81 million or Rs22.5 billion has been earmarked for consultancy services, which the FBR would procure for project implementation over five years. Another $10 million has been approved for project management cost.
Successive governments have taken loans in the name of reforming the FBR, but the tax machinery has failed to meet expectations. It has missed the last two fiscal years' tax targets and the tax-to-GDP ratio remained stagnant at 10.3% in fiscal year 2025-26.
Official records showed that during a meeting held to scrutinise the project, the Planning Commission observed that approximately $4.7 billion had been obtained from development partners to reform Pakistan's tax system. With the fresh lending, foreign loans for tax system reforms would reach $4.9 billion.
The Planning Commission had asked the FBR to conduct an impact assessment of previous reform interventions under foreign-funded projects: the Tax Administration and Reforms Project (TARP), Pakistan Single Window (PSW), Integrated Transit Trade Management Systems (ITTMS), Pakistan Raises Revenue Programme (PRRP) and now TADRA.
The loan will be repaid over 25 years, with taxpayers paying an interest rate of 1.5%–2.0% per annum.
Responding to the Planning Commission's observations, the FBR stated that the PRRP component established only foundational ICT capabilities. It said the TADRA justification explains why PRRP-era infrastructure was inadequate, noting that PRRP data centres were "designed for conventional transaction processing rather than GPU-intensive machine learning operations", demonstrating an evidence-based need assessment.
The Planning Commission also observed that the project's targets for enhancing tax collection and the number of filers were "generic in nature".
While reviewing the project, Deputy Chairman Planning Commission Ahsan Iqbal stressed the need for clearly defined and measurable outcomes, particularly in revenue generation, tax-to-GDP improvement and expansion of the taxpayer base, the Ministry of Planning said.
The ministry said the FBR assured the CDWP that the investment would increase the tax-to-GDP ratio to 13.5% by 2029 and bring more taxpayers into the tax net. The DCPC recommended the project to ECNEC on condition that PIDE thoroughly review its business model.
However, similar assurances were given to raise the tax-to-GDP ratio to 18% and then to over 13% under the $400 million World Bank-funded Pakistan Raises Revenue programme. Neither the World Bank headquarters questioned its staff nor did the government hold the FBR accountable for missing these targets.
The FBR has now promised to increase active registered taxpayers from seven million to 12 million and tax-to-GDP from 10.3% to 13.5%.
The planning ministry said the main objective of the FBR's project was to strengthen domestic resource mobilisation by accelerating digital transformation of the revenue administration ecosystem to operationalise the FBR Transformation Plan (2024-28), focusing on enhancing operational efficiency, improving taxpayer compliance and elevating Pakistan's global competitiveness.
An assistant economic advisor in the Finance Division proposed a detailed feasibility study to assess existing gaps and ascertain specific requirements.
The meeting was informed that loan negotiations would be held soon.
During scrutiny, an assistant professor from the Cyber Security Department at the National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences observed that the project lacks gap analysis, a comprehensive data security framework and clarity on the basis of the artificial intelligence model proposed for system design, while highlighting the availability of open-source options for a customised AI model and adequate data governance mechanisms.
An assistant professor from the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at the National University of Sciences and Technology also raised observations to incorporate analysis of existing systems and details on AI models proposed for the new systems, official documents showed.
The FBR said its Transformation Plan (2024-2028) had been approved by the Federal Cabinet at a total cost of Rs350 billion. The interventions proposed under different programmes and projects are part of the FBR transformation programme, which includes upgrading both hardware and software. FBR servers are being upgraded from 850TB to 3PB, according to these details.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan's short-term inflation accelerated again as the Sensitive Price Indicator (SPI) rose 8.62% year-on-year in the week ended September 10, up from 8.35% a week earlier, after a sharp jump in fuel and cooking-gas prices more than offset cheaper perishables.
The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) put the combined SPI at 364.26, against 363.42 in the previous week and 335.35 in the corresponding week of 2025. The week-on-week increase was 0.23%. The SPI tracks 51 essential items from 50 markets in 17 cities and is used to gauge weekly price pressure on households.
Energy dominated the weekly move. Petrol Super rose 6.18% to Rs369.75 a litre, high-speed diesel 5.49% to Rs394.68 and LPG 4.32% to Rs4,810.14 per 11.67kg cylinder. Other gains included pulse mash (0.79%), washing soap (0.49%), wheat flour (0.47%), pulse masoor (0.46%), mustard oil (0.36%) and 5-litre cooking oil (0.23%).
Relief came from food. Bananas fell 7.73%, tomatoes 5.24%, chicken 4.22%, onions 3.72%, potatoes 1.88%, eggs 0.68%, garlic 0.44% and sugar 0.42%. Of 51 items, prices of 14 (27.45%) rose, 10 (19.61%) fell and 27 (52.94%) were unchanged.
The annual picture remains harsh for staples and energy. Onions were 125.52% dearer than a year ago, LPG 55.42%, diesel 45.26%, petrol 39.10%, wheat flour 30.18% and first-slab electricity 25.24%. Chilli powder, mutton, beef, bananas, fresh milk and plain bread also posted double-digit or high-single-digit yearly increases. Offsetting that, potatoes were 35.21% cheaper than a year earlier, chicken 24.30%, sugar 20.88%, eggs 19.95% and tomatoes 17.65%.
The burden was uneven. The lowest expenditure group (Q1, up to Rs17,732 a month) saw a 0.30% week-on-week drop and a 7.38% yearly rise. Q2 and Q3 also eased on a weekly basis. Higher-income groups absorbed the fuel shock: Q5 (above Rs44,175) rose 0.47% week-on-week and 8.92% year-on-year.
The weekly reading comes after August's broader inflation rebound. National CPI rose 11.1% year-on-year in August 2026, against 9.2% in July and 3.1% in August 2025, and was unchanged at 1.2% month-on-month. Urban CPI was up 10.4% year-on-year and 0.9% month-on-month; rural CPI rose 12.2% and 1.6% respectively. Monthly SPI inflation was 9.5% year-on-year and 0.9% month-on-month in August, while Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation climbed 11.8% year-on-year and 2.0% month-on-month.
The latest weekly data show that cheaper fruit, vegetables and poultry are still cushioning the poorest households, but imported energy continues to keep the yearly SPI elevated and to lift the index for higher-income groups.

items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
A short video, a few product photographs and a social-media post are increasingly becoming the simplest digital strategy for Pakistan's small businesses. From clothing and carpets to electronics, home appliances, confectionery and home-based kitchens, businesses are using platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, X, TikTok and WhatsApp channels or groups to show what they have to sell and reach customers without building a separate digital operation.
Among established businesses, the shift is visible in retail fashion brands such as Kayseria, Beechtree, Misk by Fivestar, Farah Talib Aziz, Kastoor, Salitex, Sapphire, Waniya, Almeerah Studio, Cleren Online Store and Cross Stitch. Many are retail arms of textile mills, such as Gul Ahmed's Ideas, with strong Instagram presences that showcase collections and direct customers to their websites. Their professional digital teams also engage users through queries such as "How can I help you?" and follow requests designed to capture and retain attention. Smaller sellers use the same tools to reach customers who may never walk into their outlet.
For many businesses, the work is handled by an existing employee with social-media skills rather than a specialised e-commerce team. Two people – one dealing in unstitched two- and three-piece lawn suits and another wholesaling and installing CCTV cameras – said they manage online sales through social media and prepare advertisements in-house using product photographs and short videos.
A graphic designer at a leading advertising agency, Mannat Jahan, said the process can be as simple as inserting short product videos into PowerPoint presentations used for promotion. Using relevant keywords can also help customers find content online. Businesses do not need specialised designers; basic knowledge of layout, product photography, short videos and simple promotional design is often enough to keep products visible, she said.
Her version also supports Search Engine Optimisation (SEO) as another simple tool. By using words and phrases customers are likely to type into search engines, businesses can make their products easier to discover. For smaller operators, basic SEO can complement social-media promotion by helping potential customers find them even when they do not follow their pages.
SEO is no longer simply about ranking a website higher on Google; it has become an important business-development tool, Si Global CEO Dr Noman Ahmed Said told The Express Tribune. "A website should not be a digital post office where businesses simply leave their information and wait for visitors. It should be their most active salesperson – working 24/7 and reaching customers beyond geographical boundaries. SEO is what makes that salesperson visible," he said.
A Pakistani software company offering cybersecurity, software development or business process outsourcing does not need a customer in Karachi or Lahore. That customer could be searching from Dubai, London, New York or Singapore. Through the right keywords, useful content, technical SEO and a well-structured website, a Pakistani SME can compete for that enquiry alongside companies from India, Eastern Europe or Southeast Asia. The same applies to exporters of textiles, surgical instruments, sports goods, leather products and handicrafts. For smaller businesses, this approach avoids the cost of a separate digital department. Small business operators at Gul Plaza, including Bilal, Anas and Kubaib, who ran shops there before the blaze, are still selling online with family members managing social-media presence. They promote decoration pieces, artificial flowers and furniture through short videos and images, while enquiries are handled through mobile phones.
The appeal is not limited to retail. A home kitchen can promote daily offerings; a solar vendor can display customised orders; an appliance dealer can demonstrate a product; and a traditional shop can announce new stock. Social media is less a separate sales channel than an extension of the business. Customers can discover a product, ask questions and contact the seller.
Digital skills are also becoming more accessible. A smartphone, basic editing tools and familiarity with social platforms can be enough to begin. "Digital selling is no longer a specialised frontier or an optional add-on; it has fundamentally evolved into the natural extension of everyday commerce," said Kapeel Kumar, Founder of Founder's Space and a corporate consultant. For small businesses especially, going digital means meeting the modern consumer precisely where their intent lives: immediate, frictionless, and accessible. If your operations still treat the digital space as a separate department rather than the core nervous system of your customer journey, you aren't just losing sales – you're missing the entire point of modern trade, he said.
He added that digital integration unlocks predictive value. "By leveraging basic analytics and digital feedback loops, even local ventures can anticipate customer needs, hyper-personalise interactions, and build long-term retention strategies that traditional storefronts could never achieve," he said.
Government initiatives are reinforcing this adoption. In August, the government and Meta launched the Small Business Growth Academy to train more than 1,000 small businesses in digital platforms and AI-enabled tools. The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority has also partnered with Alibaba to promote digital trade and help Pakistani SMEs access international markets.
Yet the experience of businesses already using these tools suggests the digital transition does not always begin with an elaborate strategy. It begins with making the product visible. Home delivery has helped turn social-media interest into sales: customers can see a product online, order through a message or phone call and have it delivered. E-commerce platforms such as Daraz also demonstrate locally how search, product optimisation and digital visibility can move a consumer from discovery to purchase, the Si CEO added.
Facebook also offers businesses a way to promote pages and posts by paying to reach a wider or more targeted audience. Sellers can select location, age and interests, set a budget and duration, and put products before users beyond their existing followers. For small businesses, this turns a post into low-cost targeted advertising without a separate agency.
For Pakistan's small businesses, going digital may be less about replacing the physical shop than extending its reach. The shop still sells the product. The social-media account simply makes sure more people know it is there.

items.author: APP
items.content:
Chinese firm Jiangsu Ankura Intelligent Electric Co Ltd has secured an $11.728 million contract under a $40 million Asian Development Bank (ADB) power project to upgrade four 66kV grid stations of the Sukkur Electric Power Company (Sepco) to 132kV, a move aimed at strengthening the power transmission network in Sindh.
The contract, signed on February 4, 2026, covers the conversion of grid stations at Radhan, Thari Mir Wah, Nara-II and Padidan under package SEPCO-EPC-001. The contract value comprises $6.612 million and Rs1,432.444 million, according to project documents.
The upgrade forms part of a broader Sepco investment programme financed through ADB Loan No 4567-PAK, carrying a total loan amount of $40 million.
Implementation of the project is already under way, with the advance payment for the foreign-currency component disbursed. Letter of credit processing, design submissions and soil investigations are currently in progress.
The ADB-funded programme includes several other components aimed at modernising Sepco's electricity distribution system, including procurement of 1,200 Advanced Power Management System (APMS) units, an Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) project covering 50,000 units, and the bifurcation of 40 11kV feeders.
The programme also provides for project implementation consultancy services for the grid-station component, along with separate consultancy services covering the AMI, APMS and 11kV feeder bifurcation projects.
The conversion of the four stations from 66kV to 132kV is expected to strengthen the capacity and reliability of Sepco's power network as the utility moves ahead with a wider programme of grid and distribution-system modernisation.
