Bawa Desain Camera Island dengan Dua Modul Kamera
Salah satu konsep desain dari iPhone 18 Basic
Kita tahu bahwa dari iPhone 17 Pro Series dan juga iPhone 18 Pro Series, hadirnya camera island menjadi pembeda dari versi basic. Bahkan, desain dari iPhone 17 basic dan iPhone 16 basic juga memiliki kesamaan. Selain hadirnya camera island, isi dari kamera juga menjadi pembeda yang paling terlihat, walau sebagian besar iPhone 17 basic dan 17 Pro tidak begitu ada bedanya.
Nah, banyak rumor yang mengatakan juga bahwa Camera Island akan dibawa pada versi basic dari iPhone 18. Ini yang menjadi salah satu pembeda jika dibandingkan dengan iPhone 17 basic. Banyak yang berasumsi juga versi basic ini akan memberikan banyak peningkatan dari generasi sebelumnya, sehingga akan ada banyak konsumen dan antusias yang akan melakukan tukar tambah, mengingat pada gelaran Apple Event kemarin pihak Apple mulai membicarakan terkait program tukar tambah yang bisa dilakukan.
Bocoran Spesifikasi yang Menggunakan Chip A20
Karena peluncurannya masih beberapa bulan lagi, spesifikasi iPhone ini sejauh ini masih didasarkan pada berbagai laporan dan bocoran dari industri. Dari sisi layar, perangkat tersebut diperkirakan menggunakan panel Super Retina XDR OLED berukuran 6,1 atau 6,3 inci. Beberapa laporan juga menyebut Apple berpotensi membawa refresh rate 120Hz ProMotion ke model standar, yang selama ini menjadi salah satu pembeda antara iPhone reguler dan lini Pro.
Di sektor performa, iPhone ini diprediksi menggunakan varian standar chip A20 Bionic yang disebut akan dibuat dengan proses fabrikasi 2nm untuk meningkatkan efisiensi sekaligus performa. Kapasitas RAM juga dikabarkan mengalami peningkatan menjadi 9GB atau bahkan 12GB. Jika benar, peningkatan tersebut kemungkinan berkaitan dengan kebutuhan Apple Intelligence dan Siri generasi terbaru yang semakin banyak mengandalkan pemrosesan AI secara lokal di perangkat. Namun, seluruh spesifikasi tersebut masih sebatas rumor dan belum dikonfirmasi Apple.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Assembly Standing Committee on Information Technology and Telecommunication has expressed serious concerns over poor mobile and internet services across Pakistan, with members questioning the performance of telecom operators and the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA).
The committee, chaired by Amin ul Haque, reviewed complaints related to weak mobile signals, dropped calls, and unreliable internet connectivity. Members said service-quality problems were affecting users across large parts of the country.
Committee member Ahmed Atiq said around 70% of areas were facing mobile service problems, while other members described service quality in nearly 90% of the country as unsatisfactory.
Dr. Mahesh Kumar specifically criticized Ufone’s service, saying it was not working properly in many areas. Members also expressed dissatisfaction with PTA’s performance and called for stronger regulatory oversight.
Ahmed Atiq said that if PTA was facing legal or operational constraints, it should submit recommendations to Parliament so that lawmakers could consider necessary changes to the law.
The committee has now decided to summon Jazz, Zong and Ufone at its next meeting over the issue of substandard mobile services.
Lawmakers Highlight PIMS and Regional Connectivity Problems
Committee member Shazia Farid raised concerns over poor mobile coverage at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, saying the service was so weak that even phone calls could be difficult.
Dr. Zulfiqar Bhatti said mobile service was unavailable at his ancestral home despite repeated complaints. He also raised the issue of a university in Sargodha where, according to him, PTCL had received payment but failed to provide the required services.
The Secretary of IT told the committee that one reason behind poor service quality was the use of substandard equipment and infrastructure.
Committee member Ali Qasim Gilani proposed forming a subcommittee to coordinate with PTA and monitor service-quality issues more closely.
PTA officials acknowledged that mobile and internet quality problems existed across the country. They told the committee that four show-cause notices had been issued to telecom operators during the past six months.
Over the past few years, PTA said it had issued 48 show-cause notices and 22 warning letters, while penalties totaling Rs 68.9 million had been imposed over service-quality violations.
The regulator also informed the committee that it can impose a maximum fine of Rs 350 million on telecom operators under the existing framework.
Lawmakers said notices and penalties should lead to visible improvements in service quality for consumers.
The committee called for better network performance, stronger monitoring, and closer coordination between PTA, telecom operators, and Parliament.
Members also indicated that further legislative action could be considered if PTA identifies gaps in the existing legal framework, while the proposed subcommittee could provide a more focused mechanism for following up on mobile and internet service complaints nationwide.

items.title: Pakistan Govt Cuts Mobile Phone Duties by Up to 20% for FY2026-27
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The government has reduced duties on imported mobile phones for FY2026-27, cutting both regulatory duty and additional customs duty across multiple smartphone categories as part of a broader tariff rationalization drive.

The government has reduced duties on imported mobile phones for FY2026-27, cutting both regulatory duty and additional customs duty across multiple smartphone categories as part of a broader tariff rationalization drive.
According to the Ministry of Commerce, the regulatory duty on smartphones priced above $500 has been reduced by 20%, falling from Rs 22,000 to Rs 17,600 per handset. This change reduces the duty by Rs 4,400 on each high-end phone.
The Additional Customs Duty (ACD) on the listed smartphone and cellular-phone categories has also been reduced from 6% to 4%.

The revised structure applies a consistent 20% cut in regulatory duty across the listed CBU smartphone price slabs, with the biggest absolute saving coming on devices priced above $500.

The government has also reduced duties on smartphones and cellular phones imported in CKD/SKD condition.

The reductions are intended to lower the cost burden on imported components and support local mobile-phone assembly and manufacturing.
The Ministry of Commerce said the changes were introduced under the FY2026-27 Budget and form part of tariff rationalization measures under the National Tariff Policy 2025-30.
The duty cuts come after a sharp increase in Pakistan’s mobile-phone imports during FY2025-26.
Total imports of smartphones and cellular phones rose from $1.497 billion to $1.888 billion, while imports of completely built-up smartphones more than doubled to $357.7 million.
The increase highlights strong demand for imported handsets even as the government continues to promote domestic assembly and manufacturing.
The Ministry of Commerce also noted that the Mobile Device Manufacturing Policy 2020-25 has expired, while a new policy has yet to receive federal government approval.
However, incentives already available to mobile manufacturers and assemblers under the previous policy remain protected under the Fifth Schedule of the Customs Act, 1969.
The latest duty reductions are expected to ease the import burden on smartphones, although the actual impact on retail prices will depend on how much of the savings importers, distributors, and retailers pass on to consumers.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
D2C fashion and accessories startup Theater has raised ₹75 Cr (around $7.8 Mn) in a Series A funding round led by investment firm Niveshaay.
The round also saw participation from new investor Physis Capital and existing investors, including Prath Ventures, the startup said in a statement. It valued the startup at a post-money valuation of ₹410 Cr (about $43 Mn).
Theater plans to deploy the fresh capital to expand its offline retail footprint across Tier I and II cities. It will also invest in brand-building initiatives, including celebrity partnerships and marketing campaigns.
Theater is looking to combine its digital-first operations with an expanding physical retail presence as it seeks to build a nationally recognised mass-premium fashion brand.
Founded in 2021 by Sarthak Aggarwal, Vikram Jain, Karan Jain and Shruti Aggarwal, Theater offers footwear, stockings, perfumes, and bags. The startup focuses on cruelty-free fashion and accessories positioned between imported luxury products and mass-market offerings.
The company claims to have grown eightfold over the past two years while maintaining a focus on profitability. However, it did not disclose its revenue or profit figures in the statement.
Theater previously raised $1.5 Mn in a pre-Series A funding round led by Prath Ventures in September 2024.
Theater competes with the likes of FableStreet, Miraggio, Huemn in the Indian apparel space, which is projected to reach $117.05 Bn by 2034.
The funding comes as a growing number of Indian D2C fashion and lifestyle brands are expanding beyond online channels and building omnichannel businesses. Startups are increasingly using physical stores to improve brand discovery and customer experience while continuing to leverage ecommerce for scale.
For instance, D2C lifestyle brand Salty recently raised ₹30.1 Cr in January to expand its product portfolio, strengthen its ecommerce and quick commerce presence, and set up a flagship store.
In March, omnichannel streetwear brand Bonkers Corner raised $15 Mn to fuel its offline expansion plans.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Kenyan startup Flowcart has entered a strategic collaboration with Mastercard to embed secure, seamless card payments directly within social and conversational commerce journeys.
Kenya’s Flowcart is an AI-powered conversational commerce and CRM platform built on WhatsApp, which enables businesses to sell, engage customers and accept payments seamlessly.
The startup has partnered Mastercard in an initiative that allows consumers to discover products, place orders and complete payments within a single chat-based journey, eliminating the need to redirect users to external websites or apps.
By combining Flowcart’s AI-powered commerce orchestration platform with Mastercard’s global payment network, the collaboration enables merchants to capitalize on this growing trend to increase transaction frequency, drive repeat purchases and expand acceptance into underserved and informal commerce segments.
Initially launching in Kenya, the collaboration will expand across East Africa and into key high-growth markets including South Africa, Nigeria and Ivory Coast, supported by broader scaling across pan-African markets.
“We are excited to collaborate with Mastercard to transform how businesses transact in social channels, whether that’s an independent social seller, a fast-growing SME or a large enterprise brand running WhatsApp as a core commerce channel. Together, we are enabling a future where commerce and payments happen seamlessly within conversations, driving higher conversion, repeat purchases and meaningful growth for merchants,” said Ananth Gudipati, founder at Flowcart.
Shehryar Ali, senior vice president and country manager for East Africa and Indian Ocean Islands at Mastercard, said social commerce was redefining how consumers discover and engage with brands.
“Our collaboration with Flowcart enables us to embed secure, seamless payments directly into these experiences, unlocking new growth opportunities for merchants and expanding digital payment acceptance in one of Africa’s fastest-growing digital economies,” he said.

Salah satu daya tarik utama TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) adalah pilihan GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series. ASUS menyediakan tiga konfigurasi, yakni RTX 5050, RTX 5060, dan RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, seluruhnya dengan VRAM 8GB.
RTX 5060 dan RTX 5070 menggunakan memori GDDR7, sedangkan RTX 5050 masih menggunakan GDDR6. Ketiganya memiliki batas daya grafis maksimal hingga 85W melalui konfigurasi 70W + 15W Dynamic Boost.
Dalam pengujian teknis ASUS pada resolusi 1080p native tanpa DLSS, varian dengan RTX 5070 mencatat rata-rata 262,7 FPS di CS:GO. Pada Cyberpunk 2077, angkanya mencapai 75,1 FPS.
Sebagai pembanding, RTX 5060 mencatat 253 FPS di CS:GO dan 70,3 FPS di Cyberpunk 2077. Sementara RTX 5050 menghasilkan masing-masing 237,9 FPS dan 64,6 FPS.

Angka tersebut merupakan hasil pengujian teknis pada sampel ASUS, sehingga tidak serta-merta menggambarkan performa setiap konfigurasi dalam semua kondisi penggunaan.
GPU RTX 50 Series tersebut juga mendukung fitur seperti DLSS 4 dengan Multi-Frame Generation, NVIDIA Reflex, serta hardware-accelerated ray tracing. DLSS 4 dapat menghasilkan frame tambahan berbasis AI pada game yang mendukungnya.
2. Sistem Pendinginan Mampu Menyalurkan Daya hingga 105W
Performa tinggi pada laptop gaming perlu diimbangi sistem pendinginan yang mampu menjaga komponen tetap bekerja secara konsisten. ASUS TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) menggunakan sistem Thermal Equilibrium yang terdiri dari dua kipas 2nd Gen Arc Flow Fans dan tiga heat pipe berbahan tembaga.
Sistem tersebut dirancang menangani Total Platform Performance (TPP) hingga 105W, dengan alokasi 35W untuk CPU dan 70W untuk GPU.
ASUS juga menyebut tingkat kebisingan kipas berada di 40 dBA. Dalam perbandingan yang diberikan perusahaan, laptop sekelas rata-rata beroperasi pada daya 80W dengan tingkat kebisingan 42 dBA.
Dalam pengujian internal ASUS, frame rate pada jam ketiga disebut tetap berada pada tingkat yang sama dengan menit pertama. Laptop juga diuji menjalankan game bersamaan dengan aplikasi streaming OBS.
Poin ini menjadi penting karena performa laptop gaming bukan hanya soal angka FPS sesaat. Kemampuan mempertahankan performa dalam sesi panjang ikut menentukan pengalaman penggunaan, meski hasil aktual tetap dapat berbeda tergantung game, konfigurasi, suhu lingkungan, dan beban kerja.
3. Intel Core HX Generasi ke-14 untuk Gaming dan Multitasking
Laptop sedang digunakan dalam melakukan generating image secara intens (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
ASUS TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) tersedia dengan dua pilihan prosesor Intel Core HX Generasi ke-14, yaitu Core i5-14450HX dan Core i7-14650HX.
Core i7-14650HX memiliki 16 core yang terdiri dari delapan Performance-core dan delapan Efficient-core, serta 24 thread. Prosesor ini memiliki base clock 2,2GHz dan turbo hingga 5,2GHz dengan cache 30MB.
Sementara Core i5-14450HX memiliki 10 core, 16 thread, base clock 2,4GHz, turbo hingga 4,8GHz, dan cache 20MB.
Pada pengujian Cinebench R23, Core i7-14650HX mencatat skor 17.617,8 poin untuk Multi-Thread dan 2.014,6 poin untuk Single-Thread. Core i5-14450HX masing-masing menghasilkan 13.605,7 poin dan 1.846,6 poin.
Konfigurasi core dan thread tersebut memberikan ruang untuk menjalankan game bersamaan dengan aplikasi lain, seperti browser, komunikasi suara, maupun software perekam layar.
Namun, seperti benchmark GPU, skor Cinebench merupakan hasil pengujian tertentu dan bukan pengganti pengujian penggunaan sehari-hari.
4. Layar 16:10 144Hz dan RAM yang Masih Bisa Di-upgrade
Untuk gaming, ASUS TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) menggunakan panel IPS-level 16 inci dengan resolusi WUXGA 1.920 x 1.200 piksel dan refresh rate 144Hz. Rasio aspek 16:10 memberikan area vertikal lebih luas dibanding panel 16:9 beresolusi 1.920 x 1.080 piksel. ASUS menyebut area vertikalnya 11% lebih luas.
Panel tersebut juga memiliki cakupan warna 100% sRGB, tingkat kecerahan hingga 300 nits, lapisan anti-glare, serta screen-to-body ratio 85%. Kapasitas RAM bawaan adalah 16GB DDR5-5600 yang menggunakan dua slot SO-DIMM. Konfigurasinya dapat ditingkatkan hingga 64GB berdasarkan spesifikasi yang diberikan ASUS.
Untuk penyimpanan, tersedia SSD 512GB PCIe 4.0 NVMe M.2 dengan kecepatan baca hingga sekitar 7.000 MB/s. ASUS juga menyediakan slot M.2 2280 kedua untuk penambahan penyimpanan, dengan kapasitas sistem yang disebut mencapai 1TB.
Kombinasi ini membuat TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) tidak sepenuhnya bergantung pada konfigurasi bawaan. Pengguna dapat menyesuaikan kapasitas RAM dan penyimpanan sesuai kebutuhan, terutama ketika ukuran game modern semakin besar.
5. Bodi Tangguh dengan Garansi 2 Tahun dan Bonus Aksesori
ASUS TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) punya bobot 2.20kg (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
ASUS juga membekali TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) dengan aspek ketahanan dan perlindungan purnajual. Laptop ini telah melewati lima metode dan lima prosedur pengujian berdasarkan standar MIL-STD-810H, termasuk pengujian getaran, benturan, tekanan ketinggian, serta suhu tinggi dan rendah.
Dari sisi fisik, laptop memiliki dimensi 35,7 x 25,9 cm dengan ketebalan antara 1,94 hingga 2,69 cm dan bobot 2,2 kg. Engsel layarnya dapat dibuka hingga 180 derajat, sedangkan permukaan bodinya menggunakan Smudge-Free Technology untuk mengurangi noda sidik jari.
Baterainya berkapasitas 63WHrs dan laptop menggunakan adaptor 150W. ASUS juga menyertakan adaptor USB Type-C 100W yang lebih ringkas untuk kebutuhan pengisian daya portabel.
Untuk purnajual, seluruh unit mendapatkan 2 Tahun Garansi Internasional dan 2 Tahun ASUS VIP Perfect Warranty yang mencakup Accidental Damage Protection sesuai ketentuan layanan ASUS.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) will be able to establish and operate a centralised system for banking data under a recent amendment to the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001.
The amendment introduces a new Section 165AB, allowing the central bank to maintain a secure digital repository containing banking information, records, and financial transactions held by scheduled banks.
SBP to Get Access to Centralised Bank Data Under New Tax Amendment
The move aims to improve the process of matching banking and tax information while maintaining safeguards around the confidentiality of financial data.
Banks to Report Accounts With Transactions Above Rs100 Million
Under the new provision, banks and electronic money institutions (EMIs) will have to electronically submit prescribed information about account holders whose deposits or withdrawals exceed Rs100 million during a reporting period.
The information will be sent to a central data hub established for this purpose. The system will then use algorithms to cross-check banking information against tax records.
This means transactions above the Rs100 million threshold could come under greater scrutiny when the banking data does not match the information available in tax records.
Tax Authorities Will Not Directly See the Data
The amendment also sets limits on how the information will be accessed during the initial cross-matching process.
According to the provision, the digitally processed information will not be visible to income tax authorities while the system performs the initial comparison.
Only cases involving a significant mismatch between banking and tax information will move to the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) Compliance Risk Management (CRM) system.
The National Faceless Centre can then take further action on these cases.
New Data System to Include Confidentiality Safeguards
The amendment also defines several terms related to the new system, including reporting period, specified date, accounts, peak credits, central data hub, and compliance risk management.
It also includes confidentiality safeguards for the information collected through the system.
The framework will allow automated comparison of financial and tax information without giving tax officials direct access to all banking records during the initial screening stage.
See Also: SBP Makes Raast QR Payments Mandatory at Petrol Pumps by January 2027
What the Change Means
The new system could strengthen the government’s ability to identify major differences between reported income and banking activity.
Account holders with deposits or withdrawals exceeding Rs100 million during a reporting period will fall within the reporting framework. However, the system will refer only cases with significant mismatches for further action.
The measure therefore focuses on automated risk identification rather than automatically opening tax proceedings against every account covered by the Rs100 million threshold.
The new arrangement gives the SBP a central role in handling the banking data hub while establishing a process through which significant mismatches can reach the FBR’s compliance system.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is expanding its new Liquid Glass design to more iPhone users. The latest update brings the redesigned interface to the chat screen, completing a major part of WhatsApp’s transition to the new visual style on iOS.
According to WABetaInfo, the update is available with WhatsApp for iOS version 26.35.72 through the App Store. WhatsApp Business is also receiving the redesigned interface, giving users of both apps a more consistent experience.
WhatsApp Rolls Out Full Liquid Glass Design to More iPhone Users
WhatsApp started introducing the Liquid Glass design to different parts of its iOS app in earlier updates. The new look initially appeared across elements such as the navigation interface, buttons, and chat list.
However, the conversation screen continued to use the older design for many users. WhatsApp is now changing that with the latest update.
The full Liquid Glass experience covers several parts of the chat interface, including the chat bar, navigation bar, message menu, reaction tray, and message bubbles.
Chat Bar Gets a Floating Design
One of the most noticeable changes is the chat bar at the bottom of conversations. WhatsApp now gives it a floating appearance with a translucent background.
The design allows content behind the chat bar to remain partially visible. The button for jumping to the latest message also follows the same visual style.
The new chat bar gives WhatsApp a design that looks more closely aligned with Apple’s overall iOS interface.
See Also: WhatsApp Ended Support for Some Android Devices – Here’s Why
Navigation Bar Becomes Transparent
WhatsApp has also redesigned the navigation bar at the top of the conversation screen. It now uses a transparent appearance that allows the wallpaper and messages behind it to show through slightly.
The interface also uses a subtle fade effect to maintain readability while keeping the Liquid Glass appearance.
WhatsApp designed the new navigation bar to remain compatible with Apple’s Liquid Glass interface as newer iOS versions arrive.
Message Menu Also Gets the New Look
The Liquid Glass redesign extends to the menu that appears when users press and hold a message.
The reaction tray and context menu now use a translucent background instead of the previous appearance. Users can still see the conversation behind these elements without the traditional heavy blur effect.
The updated elements also adjust to both light and dark modes.
WhatsApp Refreshes Message Bubbles
WhatsApp has made another visual change to message bubbles. The new bubbles feature more rounded corners, giving conversations a softer and more modern appearance.
The app has also removed the traditional borders around photos, videos, and GIFs in conversations. This gives media a more frameless appearance and helps the entire chat screen follow the same modern design language.
WhatsApp Expands the Rollout
The full Liquid Glass experience is now reaching more users through WhatsApp for iOS 26.35.72. However, the rollout is still being expanded, so some users may not see every change immediately.
WhatsApp has gradually enabled the new design for users instead of making it available to everyone at once. Users who already have the latest App Store version but still see the older chat interface may receive the redesign in a future rollout.
The wider release also comes shortly before Apple’s expected iOS 27 launch on September 14. WhatsApp appears to be completing its Liquid Glass transition ahead of the new iOS version.
For users who have not received the redesign yet, there may not be anything else they need to do apart from keeping WhatsApp updated. The new interface should become available to more accounts as the rollout continues.
The post WhatsApp Rolls Out Full Liquid Glass Design to More iPhone Users appeared first on PhoneWorld.

Original | September 10, 2026, 12:54 IST
Furniture and appliance rental startup RentoMojo’s IPO was subscribed 2.82X on the second day of bidding, with investors placing bids for 6.14 Cr shares against the 2.18 Cr shares on offer as of 12:33 IST.
Non-institutional investors (NIIs) continued to lead the demand, with their portion subscribed 6.13X. The category received bids for 2.85 Cr shares against the 46.54 Lakh shares reserved for it.
Within the NII category, the portion for investors bidding for more than ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 5.46X, receiving bids for 1.69 Cr shares against the 31.03 Lakh shares on offer.
The portion reserved for investors bidding between ₹2 Lakh and ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 7.48X, with bids for 1.16 Cr shares against the 15.51 Lakh shares reserved for the category.
The retail portion was subscribed 2.77X, receiving bids for 3.01 Cr shares against the 1.09 Cr shares reserved for retail investors. The employee portion was subscribed 2.67X, getting bids for 1.39 Lakh shares against the 52,083 shares reserved for eligible employees.
Meanwhile, the portion reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) was subscribed 0.42X, receiving bids for 26.16 Lakh shares against the 62.06 Lakh shares on offer. Foreign institutional investors accounted for 24.80 Lakh of the shares bid for in the QIB category.
On the first day of bidding, RentoMojo’s IPO was subscribed 1.42X. The IPO opened for subscription yesterday and will close tomorrow. RentoMojo has fixed its price band at ₹384-₹404 per share and is looking to raise around ₹1,255.57 Cr through the public issue.
At the upper end of the price band, the IPO values RentoMojo at around ₹4,206 Cr (about $445 Mn). The public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.7 Cr shares worth ₹1,105.6 Cr.
Ahead of the IPO, RentoMojo raised nearly ₹376.1 Cr from anchor investors, allotting 93.1 Lakh equity shares to 41 investors at ₹404 apiece. Sixteen domestic mutual funds subscribed to 60.4 Lakh shares worth nearly ₹244.1 Cr through 30 schemes, accounting for 32.68% of the total anchor allocation, while five life insurance companies picked up 12.6 Lakh shares.
Of the ₹150 Cr fresh issue proceeds, around ₹70 Cr will be used to repay or prepay certain borrowings, while ₹42.5 Cr will go towards rental or licence payments for the company’s offline stores and warehouses. The remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes.
The OFS will see investors including Accel, Chiratae Ventures, Edelweiss Mutual Fund and GMO Venture offload their shares. Cofounder Geetansh Bamania will also sell up to 8.5 Lakh shares as part of the issue.
Founded in 2014 by Geetansh Bamania and Ajay Nain, RentoMojo operates a platform for subscription-based rental of furniture, appliances and home essentials.
On the financial front, the company’s net profit rose 142% YoY to ₹104.3 Cr in FY26, while operating revenue grew 45.5% to ₹387 Cr.

Online Application: https://www.go.eskas.ch/LoginServlet

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup Mariam Grey is an AI-powered platform that connects patients to verified pharmacies and licensed pharmacists remotely, allowing them to get prescriptions filled and access consultations without needing to travel to a physical pharmacy.
Founded in 2018, Mariam Grey has developed an AI assistant called Mummy Grey, which recommends over-the-counter medicines based on symptoms, screens uploaded prescriptions before routing them to a pharmacist for confirmation, and books doctor consultations.
“For patients without smartphones or reliable internet, we also built a USSD channel, so access isn’t limited to people with data or a modern phone. We work through a network of hundreds of partner pharmacies and support customers in multiple languages,” founder Jennifer Esiaba, a licensed pharmacist, told Disrupt Africa.
The startup is solving a serious problem – medication access in Nigeria breaks down at the last mile.
“Patients in underserved and semi-urban areas either can’t reach a reliable pharmacy or can’t verify that what they’re buying is genuine and appropriately dispensed,” Esiaba said. “Existing digital health players have largely been built for smartphone-owning, urban, English-speaking users.”
Mariam Grey, conversely, is built for the patient who doesn’t fit that profile, providing multilingual support, a USSD option for low connectivity, and AI triage that still routes anything clinically serious to a real pharmacist.
Rather than trying to compete only as an online pharmacy, we position as an AI-enabled integrated community healthcare platform,” said Esiaba.
The platform combines verified pharmacy inventory aggregation, telepharmacy consultations, home medicine delivery, home laboratory sample collection, digital doctor consultations, AI-powered medication guidance, HMO integration, community health programmes, and pharmacy network across multiple states.
This has proven popular. Mariam Grey has crossed 9,000 active paying patients across multiple Nigerian states, working through hundreds of partner pharmacies.
“We’ve since launched a subscription model and the Grey Card loyalty programme, which has four tiers up to Grey Elite VIP, to deepen retention among that base,” said Esiaba.
Bootstrapped to date, supported by angel investors through SAFE agreements, the startup is currently raising a US$350,000 pre-seed round to accelerate product development, strengthen technology infrastructure, and scale operations across Nigeria.
“Our near-term target is scaling from our current base toward 20,000 active patients within the next 18 months, with a longer-term ambition of reaching over 300,000 patients nationwide,” said Esiaba. “Horient Health represents our first vertical expansion — into paediatric care — and we see more condition- or demographic-specific verticals following the same model.”
Mariam Grey’s revenue is generated through patient orders, complemented by recurring subscription revenue from its loyalty programme. Esiaba said like many digital health startups operating in emerging markets, its biggest challenges have been building trust in digital healthcare, navigating a complex regulatory environment, and delivering reliable last-mile access in a fragmented healthcare system.
“Convincing patients to adopt digital pharmacy services required consistent education and strong execution, while expanding across multiple pharmacy partners meant investing heavily in operational excellence and quality assurance across partners,” she said.
“Rather than viewing these as barriers, we’ve treated them as opportunities to build durable competitive advantages. We’ve invested in trusted pharmacy partnerships, regulatory compliance, technology that works in low-resource settings, and a customer-first experience that has driven repeat usage and steady growth. These lessons have strengthened our execution and positioned us well for scale.”

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Quick food delivery startup Swish has raised $24 Mn (about ₹228.4 Cr) in a funding round led by Bertelsmann India Investments (BII), as it looks to expand its kitchen network and enter new cities.
Existing investors Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, and Hara Global also participated in the round.
Swish plans to use the funding to deepen its kitchen network across its existing markets, expand into new cities, strengthen its supply chain infrastructure, and increase its order-handling capacity. The startup is looking to build a network of more than 1,000 kitchens over the next five years.
The startup claimed that its monthly order volume has tripled since March 2026 and crossed 1 Mn orders.
Founded in 2024 by Aniket Shah, Ujjwal Sukheja, and Saran S, Swish owns and manages its kitchens, technology, and last-mile delivery operations. Its neighbourhood kitchens typically serve customers within a one-kilometre radius.
The startup promises food delivery in around 10 minutes and currently operates across Bengaluru, Gurugram, Noida, Delhi, and Ghaziabad. It said it covers nearly 50 pin codes and delivers more than 80% of its orders within 15 minutes.
Swish’s kitchens use dedicated preparation, cooking, and assembly stations, along with automated equipment. The company claimed that its kitchens process thousands of orders a day, with an average preparation time of under four minutes.
Its menu has expanded to more than 250 stock-keeping units (SKUs) across over 20 food categories. According to the startup, lunch and dinner have overtaken snacks and late-night orders as its biggest consumption occasions.
Swish cofounder and CEO Aniket Shah said the company intends to make quick food delivery available to 100 Mn consumers.
Quick Food Delivery Race
The latest funding comes less than six months after Swish raised $38 Mn in a Series B round led by Hara Global and Bain Capital Ventures. Accel also participated in the round, while Alteria Capital and Stride Ventures provided venture debt.
Including the latest round, Swish has raised $78 Mn in external funding to date.
The fundraise comes even as the viability of ultra-fast food delivery remains under scrutiny, with several companies recalibrating their operations in the segment.
Deep-pocketed quick commerce players have also experimented with the segment. Blinkit operates Bistro, while Zepto runs Zepto Cafe.
However, some companies have pulled back from quick food delivery. Swiggy shut down its standalone 10-minute food delivery app SNACC earlier this year amid profitability concerns.
Zing, which entered the segment around the same time as Swish, has also moved away from quick food delivery, citing weaker-than-expected demand and the model’s high operating costs.
Meanwhile, Flipkart is also exploring opportunities in food delivery, while Rapido entered the market through Ownly in select Bengaluru pincodes in March this year, potentially intensifying competition in a market dominated by Swiggy and Eternal-owned Zomato.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Apple memperluas fitur kesehatan di ekosistem perangkatnya melalui Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, dan aplikasi Health yang mendapat perombakan di iOS 27. Fokus utama pembaruan ini adalah memberikan lebih banyak data mengenai kondisi tubuh sekaligus menerjemahkan informasi tersebut menjadi insight yang lebih mudah dipahami pengguna.
Dua smartwatch terbaru Apple kini menggunakan Health Sensing System yang membawa sensor jantung optik dan elektrik baru. Sistem tersebut memungkinkan pengukuran detak jantung dan heart rate variability (HRV) dengan frekuensi lebih tinggi. Apple juga memperkenalkan Readiness, sebuah skor harian yang mencoba menggambarkan seberapa siap tubuh menghadapi aktivitas berdasarkan data kesehatan, tidur, dan aktivitas terbaru.
Di iPhone dan iPad, aplikasi Health nantinya tidak hanya menjadi tempat menyimpan data kesehatan. Dengan bantuan Apple Intelligence, aplikasi ini akan mengolah data jangka panjang untuk memberikan insight mengenai kesehatan dan kebugaran. Meski terdengar lebih komprehensif, sebagian fitur baru tersebut belum tersedia saat peluncuran dan tahap awalnya masih terbatas pada bahasa serta wilayah tertentu.
Baca Juga: Apple Watch Ultra 4 Bawa Health Sensing System Baru hingga Siri AI
Health Sensing System dan Readiness Jadi Fokus
Health Sensing System pada Apple Watch Series 12 dan Ultra 4 memungkinkan pengukuran detak jantung setiap lima detik sepanjang hari. Sementara itu, HRV dapat diukur hingga setiap lima menit atau 24 kali lebih sering dibanding sebelumnya. Data tersebut kemudian digunakan untuk memperbarui tampilan Vitals, termasuk Recovery HRV yang dibandingkan dengan baseline pribadi pengguna.
Apple juga memperkenalkan Readiness dengan skor 0–10 dan rekomendasi seperti Recover, Pace Yourself, Ready, atau Go For It. Algoritmanya mempertimbangkan aktivitas, vitals, dan sleep score, kemudian dapat berubah ketika data baru masuk. Apple menyebut sistem ini dikembangkan menggunakan data Apple Heart and Movement Study bersama ilmuwan olahraga dan dokter, tetapi skor tersebut tetap sebaiknya dipandang sebagai panduan kebugaran, bukan diagnosis kondisi kesehatan.
Health App Makin Banyak Mengandalkan AI
Perubahan besar lainnya hadir melalui aplikasi Health yang akan tersedia di iOS 27 dan iPadOS 27. Tab Insights dapat menampilkan rangkuman kondisi kesehatan sepanjang hari, sementara tab Longevity menggabungkan data dari iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods, rekam medis klinis, serta perangkat pihak ketiga. Salah satu fitur barunya adalah Health Age yang membandingkan sejumlah metrik dengan usia aktual pengguna.
Apple juga menambahkan Movement Evaluations yang memanfaatkan kamera iPhone dan Apple Watch untuk menilai fleksibilitas, kekuatan, keseimbangan, mekanik gerakan, hingga VO2 max. Proses ini berjalan di perangkat tanpa merekam atau menyimpan video. Namun, fitur seperti pemeriksaan laboratorium melalui Health app untuk lebih dari 50 biomarker saat ini baru direncanakan untuk pengguna di Amerika Serikat.
Secara keseluruhan, strategi Apple mulai bergeser dari sekadar mengumpulkan data kesehatan menjadi menginterpretasikan data tersebut. Tantangannya adalah memastikan insight berbasis AI tetap akurat dan mudah dipahami, terutama karena data kesehatan sangat bergantung pada kualitas sensor, kebiasaan pengguna, dan konteks masing-masing individu.

items.title: Apple Rilis Dua Casing Resmi untuk iPhone Duo, Harga Mulai US$79
items.summary:
Apple tak hanya memperkenalkan iPhone Duo sebagai smartphone lipat pertamanya, tetapi juga menyiapkan dua casing resmi untuk melindungi perangkat tersebut. Keduanya dirancang khusus untuk mengikuti bentuk perangkat sekaligus mempertahankan dukungan terhadap ekosistem pengisian daya nirkabel Apple.
Dua aksesori tersebut terdiri dari iPhone Duo Folio dan iPhone Duo Case. Keduanya memiliki pendekatan berbeda. Folio menawarkan desain dengan kickstand terintegrasi, sedangkan casing standar menggunakan konstruksi dua bagian yang membungkus kedua sisi iPhone Duo.
Dari sisi konektivitas, kedua casing mendukung MagSafe, Qi2 hingga 25W, serta charger bersertifikasi Qi. Apple juga menyematkan magnet internal yang diklaim dapat membantu casing terpasang secara presisi dengan perangkat sekaligus mendukung pengisian daya nirkabel. Namun, harga yang ditawarkan cukup tinggi untuk sebuah aksesori pelindung.

Apple tak hanya memperkenalkan iPhone Duo sebagai smartphone lipat pertamanya, tetapi juga menyiapkan dua casing resmi untuk melindungi perangkat tersebut. Keduanya dirancang khusus untuk mengikuti bentuk perangkat sekaligus mempertahankan dukungan terhadap ekosistem pengisian daya nirkabel Apple.
Dua aksesori tersebut terdiri dari iPhone Duo Folio dan iPhone Duo Case. Keduanya memiliki pendekatan berbeda. Folio menawarkan desain dengan kickstand terintegrasi, sedangkan casing standar menggunakan konstruksi dua bagian yang membungkus kedua sisi iPhone Duo.
Dari sisi konektivitas, kedua casing mendukung MagSafe, Qi2 hingga 25W, serta charger bersertifikasi Qi. Apple juga menyematkan magnet internal yang diklaim dapat membantu casing terpasang secara presisi dengan perangkat sekaligus mendukung pengisian daya nirkabel. Namun, harga yang ditawarkan cukup tinggi untuk sebuah aksesori pelindung.
Baca Juga: iPhone Duo Resmi Jadi Smartphone Lipat Pertama Apple, Ini Keunggulannya!
iPhone Duo Folio Punya Kickstand Terintegrasi
iPhone Duo Folio hadir dalam pilihan warna navy blue dan taupe. Casing ini memiliki desain folio yang menutupi perangkat sekaligus menyediakan kickstand bawaan. Pengguna dapat mengatur perangkat dalam berbagai sudut pandang ketika ingin menonton video atau menggunakan layar tanpa harus memegangnya.
Kickstand tersebut menjadi pembeda utama dibanding casing standar. Di sisi lain, konstruksi folio juga membuatnya berpotensi terasa lebih tebal ketika digunakan dibandingkan casing tipis biasa. Apple sendiri menyebut desainnya dapat dilipat rapi ketika kickstand tidak digunakan.
iPhone Duo Folio dibanderol US$129, £129, atau €149. Harga tersebut menjadikannya salah satu aksesori resmi yang cukup mahal, terutama jika pengguna hanya membutuhkan perlindungan dasar untuk smartphone.
Casing Standar Lebih Tipis dengan Desain Dua Bagian
Sementara itu, iPhone Duo Case hadir dalam warna sand dan navy blue dengan desain yang diklaim tipis dan ringan. Casing ini menggunakan konstruksi dua bagian yang melindungi kedua sisi perangkat, sehingga tetap mengikuti karakteristik iPhone Duo sebagai smartphone lipat.
Kedua casing sama-sama mendukung MagSafe, Qi2 25W, dan charger Qi. Magnet internal juga dirancang agar posisinya sejajar dengan iPhone Duo. Untuk pengguna yang tidak membutuhkan kickstand, casing standar mungkin menjadi pilihan yang lebih sederhana dengan harga US$79, £79, atau €89. Meski demikian, harga tersebut tetap perlu dipertimbangkan mengingat fungsinya lebih berfokus pada perlindungan dasar.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Global Fintech Fest 2026 Kicks Off
Indian startups basked in the spotlight as the Global Fintech Festival 2026 kicked off on a gala note yesterday. Be it the plethora of launches or top leaders making a beeline for the event, the first day was all about the aspirations and growth of the homegrown fintech ecosystem.
NPCI’s Android ATMs: National Payments Corporation of India rolled out open-source Android ATMs, designed to act as digital banking units for rural hubs and corporate parks. To be piloted in partnership with nine lenders and manufacturers, these machines will streamline account openings, instant RuPay card issuance and merchant onboarding.
AI Enters The Chat: NPCI also debuted AiNxt, an open-source platform for enterprises to deploy custom AI agents, and AtOM, a system for managing partner onboarding across UPI. The payments body also proposed an agentic framework to execute micro-payments autonomously.
Besides this, UIDAI also debuted its Face Auth SDK and Sandbox, which will make Aadhaar face authentication easier for developers to integrate and test across services. Meanwhile, Maharashtra is developing a framework to tokenise land and other immovable assets, potentially helping owners access liquidity against property.
Meanwhile, the Centre also broadened the scope of credit-on-UPI to cover government schemes, integrating over 7.7 Cr Kisan credit card accounts and 57 Cr PM MUDRA loans onto digital rails.
Payments Go Cardless: On the product front, PhonePe and Visa announced a partnership to roll out cardless transactions for consumers and small merchants in India and 14 other countries. Meanwhile, Jio Payments Solutions and Citi also banded together to launch a cross-border payments service, BharatPe and Pine Labs rolled out agentic AI tools, and Yubi launched a new lending platform for retail borrowers.
As the conversation moves beyond payments to agentic AI and credit, here is everything that made headlines on the first day of the Global Fintech Festival 2026…
From The Editor’s Desk
The Estate Planning Question
The recent passing away of prominent founders has forced the Indian startup ecosystem to confront what happens to equity, unvested shares and company control when a top executive passes away unexpectedly.
Without a will, founder shares devolve under intestate succession laws, which can create fragmented ownership and complicate cap tables. As such, advisors recommend using trusts to ringfence liabilities and separate ownership from benefits.
VC firms are also beginning to embed succession and exigency provisions more systematically, including accelerated vesting on death, direct transmission to nominees and pre-agreed secondary options.
RentoMojo’s IPO Day 1
The furniture and appliance rental platform’s public issue was subscribed 1.42X on the first day of bidding, receiving bids for 3.08 Cr shares against 2.18 Cr shares on offer.
NIIs subscribed their quota 2.46X, while retail investors and retail investors booked their portion 1.54X. However, QIB response remained muted and subscribed their portion a mere 0.41X.
RentoMojo’s IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹150 Cr and an OFS of up to 2.7 Cr shares worth ₹1,105 Cr. It has set a price band of ₹384-₹404 apiece for its public issue, valuing the company at around ₹4,206 Cr at the upper end of the spectrum.
QNu Labs Bags ₹200 Cr
The quantum cybersecurity startup has raised around $21 Mn in its Series A1 round co-led by National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest to scale R&D, sales and go-to-market strategy. With this, QNu Labs has raised ₹375 Cr to date.
Founded in 2016, QNu Labs is building cybersecurity products for the quantum era. Besides offering solutions based on quantum key distribution and post-quantum cryptography, it is also building security solutions for drones and satellites.
Quantum computing startups are on the rise in India due to massive state funding, a large talent pool and the need for advanced cybersecurity. For context, these computers, once they cross a certain threshold, can render current encryption standards obsolete.
Flipkart’s New Experiments
The ecommerce giant has launched a standalone app for its quick commerce service, Minutes. The app, which is still in beta mode, is live on Google Play Store and is currently only available for a select number of users.
This comes as Flipkart also began piloting its food delivery service, called Eat In, among its employees in Bengaluru. It now plans to roll out the offering for end consumers in the city before its flagship Big Billion Day sale.
The expansion comes as Flipkart has scaled Minutes to 1,000 micro-fulfilment centres across 130 cities. The ecommerce major has now set its eyes on expanding its quick commerce network to 1,500 centres across 180 cities.
Big Reprieve For Google
Following the ban on real money gaming last year, the Competition Commission of India has now closed its antitrust probe into Google over the big tech giant’s treatment of real money gaming apps.
The CCI said that the ban has made it impossible to grant the relief sought in the case. However, the watchdog clarified that closing the case did not imply that Google’s conduct was not anti-competitive.
The case stemmed from a complaint by WinZO, which accused Google of abusing its dominant position by allowing Daily Fantasy Sports and Rummy apps on the Play Store and Google Ads while excluding RMG apps.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How Invisel Is Using Nano-Coatings To Stop Stains
Hard-water marks, upholstery stains and everyday wear force homeowners into a cycle of deep cleaning and repairs. Invisel is trying to break this loop by bringing its industrial-grade nano-coating technology to households, creating an invisible protective layer.
Protective Film For Homes: Founded in November 2024, Invisel develops protective coatings for glass, tiles, fabric, marble and metal. Its nanotechnology-based formulations use silane-siloxane, graphene and curable silicone resins to create surface-specific barriers against stains, hard-water damage and daily wear.
Invisel’s D2C Kits: The startup sells DIY nano-coating kits directly to consumers, partners with furniture OEMs for pre-treated products. It also offers professional application services for bathrooms and sofas. All formulations are manufactured in-house at its facility in Pune, where the startup handles blending, filling and batch-level quality testing.
Building A New Category: In just over a year of commercial operations, Invisel claims to have served more than 60,000 customers across 900+ pincodes and generated ₹5.2 Cr in FY26 revenue profitably. Going forward, it plans to focus on ramping up manufacturing, expanding product portfolio, bolstering offline distribution and entering new markets.
As premiumisation reshapes the country’s ₹6 Lakh Cr home-care market, can Invisel bring industrial-grade cleaning solutions to Indian homes?

items.content:
Government begins advocacy campaign, plans enforcement against parents who keep children out of school
By Edwin Phillip, Lafia
LAFIA — The Nasarawa State Government has directed the State Universal Basic Education Board, SUBEB, to commence an advocacy campaign across the state to ensure that children of school age who are out of school return to the classroom.
The government also said it was considering the establishment of mobile courts to prosecute parents whose children are found loitering on the streets during school hours.
The Senior Special Assistant to Governor Abdullahi Sule on Public Affairs, Mr Peter Ahemba, disclosed this on Wednesday during his bi-monthly media briefing in Lafia.
Ahemba said the government had directed SUBEB to collaborate with the state Ministry of Justice on the possibility of establishing mobile courts to handle cases involving parents who fail to send their children to school.
He said the government would first embark on an advocacy campaign before commencing full enforcement.
According to him, a task force would subsequently be established to monitor the streets and identify school-age children found outside school during school hours.
He said the task force would trace the parents of such children, who could subsequently be prosecuted for failing to ensure that their children attend school.
“Because at the end of that advocacy tour by the State Universal Basic Education Board to ensure that our children of school age who are not in school are back to school, after that grace period of advocacy, government will now commence full enforcement.
“There will be a task force that will be charged with the responsibility to go around the streets. When such children are identified during school hours, they will be held to identify their parents.
“By the time they identify their parents, those parents will now be arrested and handed over for prosecution for failure to send their children to school,” Ahemba said.
He said the initiative was aimed at ensuring that no child in Nasarawa State was denied the opportunity to acquire education and addressing the rising number of out-of-school children.
Ahemba said parents would have no excuse for keeping their children out of school, noting that the government was also providing educational materials to support families and encourage school enrolment.
He disclosed that SUBEB had procured more than 10,000 exercise books, school uniforms and sandals, among other learning materials, for distribution to pupils in public schools across the state.
“In the same token, the state government, through the State Universal Basic Education Board, has procured over 10,000 exercise books and over 10,000 school uniforms, over 10,000 sandals, among other school materials, to be distributed to pupils across the public schools in Nasarawa State,” he said.
Government recruits 1,000 primary school teachers
On efforts to strengthen manpower in public schools, Ahemba said the state government had concluded the recruitment process for primary school teachers through SUBEB.
He said Governor Sule had directed that 1,000 successful candidates be released for immediate employment to teach in rural primary schools across the state.
According to him, the recruitment process was based on merit, following the submission of more than 10,000 applications.
“So in doing this, the board considered merit in arriving at the 1,000 applicants. You remember over 10,000 applied, but because only 1,000 will be recruited for now, government took meticulous observance of the qualified, doing it based on merit and not with any sentiment or any primordial sentiment whatsoever,” he said.

items.content:
…Says weak links could destabilise financial system
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief
ABUJA: The Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, has urged banks, fintechs and other financial institutions to treat cybersecurity and third-party technology risks as critical financial stability issues, warning that vulnerabilities in one institution could trigger widespread disruption across the financial system.
The Director, Payments System Supervision at the CBN and Chairperson of the Nigeria Electronic Fraud Forum, NeFF, Dr Rakiya Yusuf, gave the warning at the 19th Annual Banking and Finance Conference of the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria, CIBN, in Abuja.
Speaking during a session titled, “Navigating Cyber and Systemic Risks in the AI-Driven Future of Banking: Implications for Financial Stability and Business Resilience,” Yusuf said the growing reliance of financial institutions on fintechs, payment service providers, cloud operators and other technology vendors had created new channels for cyber and systemic risks.
She warned that a weakness in a bank, fintech, payment service provider or technology vendor could spread rapidly across interconnected institutions, creating what she described as a “one-fire” effect capable of destabilising the entire financial system.
Yusuf said financial institutions must therefore move beyond securing their internal systems to strengthening safeguards across the wider financial ecosystem.
She urged banks and other operators to continuously assess their dependencies, third-party relationships and technology partners to determine how disruptions in one part of the ecosystem could affect their operations.
The CBN director stressed that operational resilience involved more than preventing cyberattacks, noting that institutions must also be able to maintain critical services during disruptions and recover quickly from incidents.
She disclosed that the CBN was strengthening its regulatory framework, supervisory processes and policy measures to identify and address vulnerabilities capable of threatening financial stability before they materialise.
According to her, cyber and operational risk considerations were now being integrated into the product approval process to ensure that new financial products did not introduce systemic vulnerabilities.
Yusuf also urged financial institutions to extend cybersecurity and risk-management oversight to third-party service providers.
She said banks must assess the capacity of their technology partners to withstand and recover from cyberattacks and major operational failures.
The CBN director called for prompt reporting of cyber incidents and vulnerabilities to regulators, saying early disclosure would enable timely intervention before isolated breaches escalated into systemic threats.
She also advocated greater intelligence and information sharing among financial institutions, noting that stronger collaboration would improve the industry’s ability to detect emerging threats and coordinate responses.
Yusuf recommended the establishment of stronger Security Operations Centres, SOCs, capable of monitoring cyber threats across the financial ecosystem in real time.
On the growing adoption of artificial intelligence, she cautioned that innovation must be matched with accountability, insisting that automation should not eliminate human responsibility from financial decisions.
She described the approach as “automating accountability,” explaining that while AI could perform increasingly sophisticated tasks, human oversight must remain central to decisions affecting customers and the financial system.
Yusuf further urged financial institutions to strengthen data governance and pay greater attention to digital sovereignty by examining where critical data were stored, who had access to them, what intelligence could be derived from them and how such data influenced decision-making.
She warned that placing critical data or key technological capabilities beyond an institution’s effective control could expose the financial system to additional risks.
Yusuf maintained that safeguarding Nigeria’s financial system required a collective approach involving regulators, banks, fintechs, payment service providers and technology companies.
She said the objective should be to build a resilient ecosystem capable of absorbing shocks, containing cyber incidents and recovering swiftly without allowing the failure of one institution to threaten the stability of the entire financial system.

items.content:
… Says 53 suspected cases recorded this year
… Urges parents to complete children’s 3 immunization doses
By Chioma Obinna
The Lagos state Commissioner for Health, Prof Akin Abayomi on Wednesday raised its disease surveillance and preparedness against diphtheria, warning residents not to panic but to remain vigilant as the outbreak continues to spread in parts of Nigeria.
Abayomi, however, said there is currently no outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos, despite recording 53 suspected cases in 2026, six of which were laboratory-confirmed.
The Commissioner, who gave the assurance at a media briefing on the state’s diphtheria preparedness and response, said the government was taking precautionary measures because of the high level of movement between Lagos and states currently battling the disease.
According to him, the situation requires vigilance because Lagos’ huge population and extensive connections with other parts of the country could facilitate community transmission if imported cases are not detected and managed early.
“We are appealing to all Lagosians to remain calm. There is no current outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos. We are simply taking precautionary measures,” Abayomi said.
The Commissioner said the government was particularly concerned about the outbreak reported in states including Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Benue and Zamfara, noting that the continuous movement of people between Lagos and affected areas made surveillance imperative.
“We are watching this outbreak expand, and we are cautious in Lagos, as always. The Executive Council always likes to err on the side of caution and increase our prevention strategies in the state,” he said.
Abayomi explained that diphtheria is a serious bacterial respiratory infection capable of causing life-threatening complications when treatment is delayed.
He said the disease could produce a toxin capable of attacking the heart, while swelling and a thick membrane in the throat could obstruct breathing and swallowing.
“There are two major things that happen to a patient with diphtheria. First, it can block the breathing apparatus in the throat, preventing the person from breathing normally or swallowing liquids and food properly.
“Secondly, the toxin can enter the blood and travel to the heart, causing problems with the heartbeat and, eventually, heart failure.”
He warned that an undiagnosed infection could therefore progress rapidly into airway obstruction and inflammation of the heart.
Abayomi urged anyone developing severe sore throat, fever, weakness, neck swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing, particularly after travelling to an affected state or having contact with a confirmed case, to seek medical attention immediately.
“If you have any of these symptoms, present yourself quickly to one of our primary healthcare centres or your doctor so that we can make the diagnosis, carry out the necessary diagnostic workup and start treatment as quickly as possible,” he said.
Giving an update on the situation in Lagos, Abayomi disclosed that 53 suspected diphtheria cases had been recorded in the state so far in 2026.
Only six, he said, were confirmed through laboratory diagnosis, with all six cases appropriately managed.
He added that contacts of confirmed patients were traced and placed under observation throughout the incubation period to detect possible secondary infections.
“In Lagos, we have had sporadic cases of diphtheria. In fact, in 2026, we have had 53 suspected cases. Of those 53, only six have been confirmed through laboratory diagnosis,” he said.
The Commissioner stressed that early diagnosis significantly improves the chances of successful treatment.
“The treatment for diphtheria is very effective if the disease is diagnosed early,” Abayomi said, explaining that treatment involves antibiotics and medication capable of neutralising the toxin produced by the bacteria.
While stressing that immunisation remains the most effective protection against diphtheria, Abayomi disclosed that only about 64 per cent of children in Lagos have received full vaccination coverage.
He urged parents and guardians to check their children’s immunisation records and ensure that they receive all three doses of the pentavalent vaccine.
“If you have received three doses, then you have significant protection. If you have received two, one or none, then you are vulnerable,” he warned.
According to him, the three doses are expected to be administered at six, 10 and 14 weeks.
He said Lagos has more than 1,000 healthcare facilities providing routine immunisation services across the public and private sectors, with vaccines available free at government facilities.
The Commissioner clarified that primary healthcare centres are mainly vaccination points and are not the facilities designated to diagnose and manage suspected diphtheria cases.
He listed the four designated centres as the Infectious Disease Hospital, Yaba; Massey Street Children’s Hospital, Lagos Island; Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH; and Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH.
“If we suspect a case of diphtheria, we refer the patient to designated facilities. These are the four centres where we actively manage suspected cases of diphtheria. They have the capacity to make the diagnosis and manage the complications,” Abayomi said.
He noted that severe cases could require advanced intervention to maintain the patient’s airway and close monitoring of the heart to prevent fatal complications.
With schools expected to reopen soon, Abayomi said the Ministry of Health was working with the education sector to strengthen awareness and vaccination among schoolchildren.
He said suspected cases in schools would trigger contact tracing and other infection-control measures.
The Commissioner also urged residents to observe basic respiratory hygiene, including covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, washing hands regularly and avoiding close contact with others when experiencing respiratory symptoms.
Speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr. Dayo Lajide, also appealed to parents to ensure their children are fully vaccinated.
“More importantly, we have to make sure that all our children are vaccinated,” Lajide said.
She also urged the media to play a responsible role by providing accurate information to prevent unnecessary panic while encouraging residents to take appropriate preventive measures.
She added that the government’s heightened surveillance was not a declaration of an outbreak in Lagos, but a precautionary response designed to ensure that any suspected case is detected, isolated, investigated and treated before it can trigger wider transmission.
The post Diphtheria: No outbreak in Lagos – Abayomi appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Maryam Abdul-aziz Usman, Damaturu
DAMATURU — The Yobe State chapter of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, has accused the Yobe State Independent Electoral Commission, YSIEC, of excluding the party from crucial electoral information ahead of the 2026 local government election.
The party threatened to seek legal redress and organise peaceful protests if the commission fails to address its concerns.
ADC made the allegations in a letter of concern addressed to the Chairman of YSIEC, expressing what it described as “serious concern and disappointment” over the commission’s alleged failure to communicate election guidelines, timetable and other electoral decisions affecting its participation.
The party said equal and meaningful access to electoral information was essential to the lawful participation of political parties in an election.
It therefore demanded evidence of when, how and through which official channel the relevant guidelines, timetable and electoral decisions were communicated to it.
“We therefore request clear evidence of when, how and through what official channel the relevant Guidelines, timetable and electoral decisions were communicated to ADC,” the party stated.
According to ADC, failure to properly notify it of electoral requirements could prejudice its ability to participate fully in the council election.
The party cited Sections 7, 40 and 197 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the Third Schedule, applicable electoral laws and YSIEC regulations in support of its concerns.
ADC warned that it would pursue all lawful avenues if any action or omission by the commission affected its participation in the electoral process.
“ADC hereby puts YSIEC on notice that, if our lawful rights or participation have been prejudiced by any failure of notification, we will pursue every lawful avenue available to protect our rights,” it stated.
The party said such measures could include legal action, media engagement, social media advocacy and peaceful public protest.
ADC also called on the commission to provide clarification and take appropriate corrective action if its participation had been affected by any failure of notification.
The letter, dated September 2026, was addressed to the YSIEC Chairman, with copies sent to the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, the Yobe State Government, the Political Adviser to the Governor, the Commissioner of Police, the state command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps and the Department of State Services.
As of the time of filing this report, YSIEC had not publicly responded to the allegations contained in the ADC letter.
The development comes as political parties prepare for the 2026 local government election in the state.
The post Yobe LG poll: ADC alleges exclusion by YSIEC appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki
ABAKALIKI — Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, has distributed empowerment items to 500 indigent women in Ebonyi State to support them in starting new businesses or improving existing enterprises.
The items included deep freezers, gas cookers with ovens, power generators and industrial grinding machines.
Tinubu, who was represented by the wife of the Ebonyi State Governor, Mrs Mary-Maudline Uzoamaka Nwifuru, said the empowerment programme was being implemented simultaneously in the five states of the South-East.
She said the initiative was made possible through the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs.
According to her, the programme was designed to empower 18,000 women nationwide, with 500 beneficiaries selected from each state and the Federal Capital Territory.
She said: “This presentation is taking place across the five states of the zone simultaneously.
“This programme has been made possible through the Office of the SSA to the President on Sustainable Development Goals.
“The initiative was first launched in Abuja for the North-Central zone in February 2025, followed by the distribution of empowerment items in the South-South zone on April 25, 2026, and the South-West zone on August 23, 2025.
“By the end of the nationwide rollout of this initiative, 18,000 women would have been empowered across the country, with 500 beneficiaries selected from each state and the FCT.”
She said the programme aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Initiative, particularly in recognising the critical role women play in nation-building.
She urged the beneficiaries to use the items judiciously to achieve the objectives of the programme.
The representative of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on SDGs, Dr Ify Ukaegbu, also urged the beneficiaries not to sell the items.
Ukaegbu said the intervention was aimed at expanding economic opportunities for indigent and vulnerable women across the country.
Some of the beneficiaries expressed appreciation to the President’s wife and the wife of the Ebonyi State Governor for the gesture, saying the items would enable them to become self-reliant and support their families.
They pledged to use the items judiciously, adding that the intervention came at a time when they needed support to establish sustainable means of livelihood.
The post Tinubu’s wife empowers 500 women in Ebonyi appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Demola Akinyemi
ILORIN: A Professor of Agriculture and Fisheries at the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, Wasiu Adeyemi Jimoh, has urged the Federal Government to make sustainable aquaculture a strategic component of Nigeria’s food security, nutrition and economic development agenda.
Jimoh said increased investment in aquaculture could accelerate the development of a resilient, environmentally sustainable and globally competitive industry capable of creating jobs, reducing dependence on fish imports and contributing significantly to national economic growth.
He made the call while delivering the 306th inaugural lecture of the University of Ilorin, titled, “Green Feeds, Healthy Fish: Enhancing Aquaculture Productivity,” at the university auditorium on Monday.
The don said the sector could be strengthened through increased investment in research, innovation, human capacity development and the commercialisation of locally developed technologies.
According to him, “Investment in aquaculture will accelerate the transition towards a resilient, environmentally sustainable, and globally competitive industry, capable of creating employment, reducing import dependence, and contributing significantly to national economic development.”
He added that strategic implementation of the proposed measures would transform aquaculture into a resilient, environmentally restorative and economically viable sector.
Jimoh said the development of the sector was essential to achieving food and nutrition security, creating sustainable employment and improving livelihoods for present and future generations.
He explained that his research had focused on developing alternatives to conventional fish feed ingredients through the use of plant-based protein sources, phytogenic additives and circular-economy principles.
“These efforts aimed to reduce dependence on fishmeal and soybean meal, optimise nutrient utilisation, enhance fish health, and improve economic sustainability for fish farmers,” he said.
The professor noted that fish remained one of the most nutrient-dense and accessible sources of protein, providing high-quality amino acids, omega-3 fatty acids, vitamins and minerals.
He said fish was particularly important in developing countries where malnutrition and micronutrient deficiencies remained challenges, adding that it served as both a source of nutrition and livelihood for millions of people.
Jimoh also called on feed manufacturers, veterinary professionals, fish health specialists and regulatory agencies to formulate, certify and promote functional aquafeeds for fish farmers.
He advocated the routine use of aquafeeds containing probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics and natural immunostimulants, saying they could strengthen disease prevention, reduce antibiotic misuse and improve fish welfare and productivity.
“Fish occupy a unique and irreplaceable position in the global landscape, influencing dietary patterns, shaping economic activities, and fostering traditions that are deeply rooted in historical and ecological contexts.
“Fish are not merely food sources but a lifeline that sustains billions of people worldwide. From the bustling fish markets of Asia to the artisanal fisheries of Africa, fish form the bedrock of diets, livelihoods, and communities,” he said.
The post Unilorin don urges FG to prioritise aquaculture appeared first on Vanguard News.

Reflecting on his stewardship, Yusuf said his three years in office had provided valuable lessons in leadership, public service, accountability and human relations.
“Working directly under His Excellency, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has made me understand that leadership is ultimately about the impact one makes in the lives of others,” he said.
He said the experience had broadened his understanding of public service, particularly the importance of prudence, effective communication and listening to diverse opinions.
According to Yusuf, the agency has executed projects across the state’s 11 local government areas, covering infrastructure, grassroots administration, markets, traditional institutions, security facilities and renewable energy.
In Akko Local Government Area, he listed the reconstruction of the local government secretariat and Gona Emir’s Palace, installation of solar streetlights in Kumo and Tumfure, and construction of the Akko West LCDA Secretariat in Pindiga and Akko North LCDA Secretariat in Amada.
In Balanga, the agency provided a one-megawatt solar mini-grid for Tallasse and Swa communities and constructed the Balanga South LCDA Secretariat in Bambam.
Billiri benefited from the reconstruction of the Gada-Uku-Sansani Bridge, construction of a police outpost at Amtawalam, reconstruction of Kantoma Market, construction of the Billiri Grains Market and the Billiri West LCDA Secretariat at Tal.
In Dukku, projects included a motor park, grains and cattle market, solar streetlights and the Dukku North LCDA Secretariat at Malala.
Yusuf said Funakaye received the reconstruction of the Emir’s Palace and 12 district head palaces, construction of 66 shops in Bajoga, solar streetlights in Bajoga and Ashaka, and the Funakaye South LCDA Secretariat in Tongo.
In Gombe Local Government Area, the agency reconstructed the Idi Shopping Complex and Gombe Emir’s Palace, as well as constructed the Gombe South LCDA Secretariat in Bolari.
Projects in Kwami included the reconstruction and furnishing of 11 district head palaces, solar streetlights in several communities and the Kwami West LCDA Secretariat in Bojude.
In Kaltungo, the agency reconstructed the local government secretariat, constructed market stalls and built the Kaltungo East LCDA Secretariat at Tula Wange.
Nafada Local Government Area benefited from the construction of its local government secretariat, solar streetlights in Nafada and surrounding communities, and the Nafada South LCDA Secretariat at Birin Fulani.
In Shongom, projects included part of the local government secretariat, seven district head palaces, a 650KWH solar mini-grid in Filiya and the Pero-Chonge LCDA Secretariat.
In Yamaltu/Deba, the agency provided fencing, solar streetlights and a solar-powered borehole with four fetching points at the National Agricultural Land Development Authority, NALDA, Market in Kwadon.
Solar streetlights were also installed in Deba, Dadin Kowa, Hinna, Kwadon, Wajari, Gwani, Shinga and Wade, while the Yamaltu East and Yamaltu West LCDA secretariats were constructed at Dadin Kowa and Zambuk respectively.
Yusuf further disclosed that the construction of the Gombe State Council of Emirs and Chiefs Secretariat had reached about 95 per cent completion.
He said the project, when completed, would provide a befitting institutional structure for traditional leadership in the state.
The JPDA boss attributed the achievements to the support and guidance of Governor Inuwa Yahaya, as well as the cooperation of stakeholders, staff and communities.
He expressed optimism that the agency would continue to contribute to the implementation of projects aimed at improving the living conditions of residents.
“I sincerely thank everyone for their unwavering support throughout this journey. The achievements recorded are a product of collective effort, and I hope we will continue to work together to move our dear state forward,” Yusuf said.

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe
GOMBE — More than 6,000 women from across Gombe State on Wednesday converged on the APC Square, Gombe, for the maiden Gombe Women’s Unity and Progress Summit convened by Dr Zainab Jamil Gwamna.
The summit, held under the theme, “Stronger Voices, United Women, Greater Impact,” brought together women from the state’s 11 local government areas and 13 Local Council Development Areas, including entrepreneurs, professionals, community leaders, political stakeholders and women advocates.
According to a statement by Ibrahim Sani Shawai, spokesperson to the APC governorship candidate in Gombe State, Dr Jamil Isyaku Gwamna, the summit was designed to promote unity, empowerment, mentorship and greater participation of women in governance and socio-economic development.
Speaking at the event, the convener, Dr Zainab Gwamna, said the initiative was aimed at building a united women’s movement capable of supporting one another and creating opportunities for younger generations.
“This summit is about bringing Gombe women together to discover our collective strength and understand that the success of one woman should open doors for another,” she said.
“We must mentor our young girls, support women in business and professions, strengthen our families and contribute meaningfully to our communities.”
Gwamna commended the turnout, describing it as an indication of the potential of women to contribute to social and economic development.
She also commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for programmes targeted at women and youths, while appreciating her husband, Dr Jamil Gwamna, for his support.
The convener urged participants to take the lessons and relationships developed at the summit back to their communities, with emphasis on mentoring young girls, skills acquisition, confidence building and economic self-reliance.
Also speaking, the wife of the Gombe State Governor, Dr Asma’u Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, commended the initiative and the turnout of women from across the state.
She reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to programmes aimed at improving the welfare, empowerment and economic wellbeing of women and youths.
“Women are indispensable partners in the development of our families, communities and the state,” she said.
“I commend Dr Zainab Gwamna for bringing women together through this important summit and for creating a platform where they can learn, connect and support one another.”
Dr Asma’u encouraged the participants to sustain the spirit of unity, cooperation and mutual support demonstrated at the gathering.
Participants from different professional and community backgrounds also commended the initiative, saying sustained collaboration, mentorship and economic empowerment were important to increasing women’s participation in development.
Some participants expressed optimism that the networks established at the summit would continue beyond the event and create opportunities for women and young girls across the state.
The gathering also had political undertones, with some political stakeholders saying the mobilisation could strengthen the grassroots support base of the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections.
However, the central message of the summit was the need for women to support one another, mentor younger generations and use collective action to promote social and economic development in Gombe State.
