items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Eight months after the Gul Plaza tragedy, the affected shop owners say the building’s debris remains uncleared, and reconstruction has yet to begin, prompting them to give the Sindh government a seven-day deadline to address their grievances.
Gul Plaza Owners Association General Secretary Arif Qadri said on Wednesday that around 850 shop owners, including more than 100 women, had lost their businesses in the deadly blaze, leaving some 1,200 families facing an uncertain economic future.
Addressing a protest camp set up by the association at the site of the demolished plaza, Qadri said nearly 800 affected shop owners had received neither relief nor compensation. “The government has compensated tenants, but the actual shop owners have received nothing,” he said.
Read More: Challan holds Gul Plaza administration responsible for fire, exonerates govt bodies
Qadri demanded the immediate removal of the debris and the announcement of a reconstruction plan, along with financial assistance for the affected traders. He warned that if the government failed to respond within seven days, the traders would stage a sit-in on MA Jinnah Road. “Stop forgetting us. Do not force us to cross the line,” he said.
Business leader Abdul Rauf Ibrahim also warned of a prolonged protest and possible closure of MA Jinnah Road. He urged Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah to personally hear the grievances of the affected traders. Ibrahim also called for an audit of the compensation distributed among the victims.
Former FPCCI vice president Asif Sakhi claimed that the Sindh government had distributed Rs4.5 billion in compensation following the tragedy, but said the shop owners had received no share of the funds. He alleged that the compensation was distributed through the “main accused” in the tragedy and said the matter would have to be taken up at the federal level.
The affected traders reiterated their demand for immediate reconstruction of Gul Plaza and compensation for shop owners, warning that failure to meet their demands would trigger a prolonged sit-in on MA Jinnah Road.
Defence puts govt institutions in the dock
A judicial magistrate hearing the Gul Plaza fire case rejected a defence plea seeking the formation of a Joint Investigation Team (JIT), observing that such teams were generally constituted in terrorism cases.
The court will decide at the next hearing whether to approve the charge sheet and whether government institutions should also be nominated as accused in the case.
Tanveer Pasta, president of the Gul Plaza Traders Association, and others appeared before the judicial magistrate (South) as the prosecution and defence exchanged arguments over alleged negligence in the deadly fire that claimed more than 70 lives.
Prosecutor Hassan Bhatti told the court that Pasta was guilty of the “highest degree of negligence”, alleging that he failed to call the fire brigade after the blaze broke out.
Defence counsel Javed Mir, however, disputed the allegations and accused the new investigation officer (IO) of attempting to protect government institutions.
Read More: Gul Plaza owners cry foul
He said the court had previously ordered that government departments be included in the investigation, but the latest charge sheet had given a clean chit to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC), Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), Fire Brigade and other institutions.
“Tanveer Pasta is neither the builder nor the owner, while the SBCA took no action against the builder,” the lawyer argued.
Mir said the fire had started on the ground floor, where no deaths were reported, and claimed that more than 5,000 people had been present and were evacuated. “These people did not die because of the fire but due to suffocation caused by the negligence and incompetence of government institutions,” he added.
The lawyer further argued that the fire brigade had no water available and that people had continued screaming for help for around one-and-a-half hours.
He questioned why the IO had failed to record the statement of the deputy commissioner (South), who, according to him, had reached the site within five minutes of the incident.
Mir also questioned the nomination of a child and his father as accused, saying the child’s elder brother had also been present at the site but was not included in the case.
IO DSP Aamir Warik informed the court that there were 16 doors on the ground floor, which was why no one had died there. He said iron windows had been installed at the premises.
The defence counsel rejected the IO’s explanation, saying people had been “burnt to ashes” and that the investigation failed to properly establish responsibility for the deaths.
The court also asked whether the Civil Defence Department had been included in the investigation. The IO replied that statements of two Civil Defence officials had been recorded.
He further said government institutions had broken windows and doors during rescue operations. The defence, however, maintained that the doors had been broken only on the second day.
Also Read: Gul Plaza fire probe leaves blame unresolved
Mir alleged that the IO had ignored the seven points identified by the court when it ordered a fresh investigation.
Pasta also addressed the court and said people had remained alive for two to two-and-a-half hours after the fire broke out. “Five of my colleagues were martyred, but there is no mention of them in the charge sheet,” he said.
He claimed that a snorkel had malfunctioned and that several lives could have been saved had it continued working. “I was saved by people; otherwise, I too would have died. Our people died, and we have been made accused,” Pasta said while breaking down in tears.
He also claimed that more than Rs7 billion had been distributed among the victims on his recommendation.
The court rejected the defence plea for formation of a JIT and adjourned the hearing until September 18, when it will decide on approval of the charge sheet and the question of whether government institutions should be made accused in the case.

items.author: Fiaz Mahmood
items.content:
Islamabad Deputy Commissioner (DC) Irfan Nawaz Memon on Wednesday announced a “complete” ban on running shisha cafes in the federal capital after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed the district administration to formulate rules governing shisha cafes within one month.
“In compliance with the orders of the Islamabad High Court (IHC), a complete ban has been imposed with immediate effect on the operation of shisha cafes in the federal capital until further orders,” Memon wrote in a post on X.
He added that under the ban, all types of shisha cafes, including those holding no-objection certificates (NOCs) and operating in outdoor or indoor spaces, had been prohibited from conducting shisha business.
اسلام آباد ہائی کورٹ کے احکامات پر فی الفور عمل درآمد کرتے ہوئے وفاقی دارلحکومت میں شیشہ کیفے چلانے پر تاحکم ثانی مکمل پابندی عائد کر دی گئی ہے پابندی کے تحت این او سی کے حامل شیشہ کیفے، آؤٹ ڈور اور ان ڈور تمام اقسام کو شیشہ کا کاروبار چلانے سے روک دیا گیا ہے،خلاف ورزی کرنے کی…
— DC Islamabad (@dcislamabad) September 9, 2026
The deputy commissioner warned that in case of a violation, the cafe would be sealed and a case would be registered against its owner. He added that assistant commissioners would ensure daily inspections by conducting operations without discrimination, according to the directions.
Earlier, Islamabad High Court Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar remarked during a hearing that shisha cafés would not be allowed to operate in their current manner without rules being formulated.
“No rules have been made, and there are no regulations,” the chief justice observed, adding that such arrangements were damaging the lives of people in Islamabad.
“Everything is happening in an open space. You are taking your generations towards destruction,” he remarked.
Read: Sheesha cafes face legal action over drug links
The Islamabad Police chief told the court that action had been taken against shisha cafés in compliance with its orders.
The IHC chief justice made the remarks while hearing a petition seeking details of shisha cafés operating in Islamabad. Islamabad IGP Ali Nasir Rizvi and Deputy Commissioner Islamabad appeared before the court in person.
Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik and Acting Prosecutor General Manzoor Ahmad Jajja were also present.
“We have great respect for your business, but do not destroy the entire city,” Justice Dogar said and questioned whether smoking tobacco mixed with cannabis could still be considered merely smoking.
Justice Dogar warned that such practices could affect members of the public, saying, “It should not happen that tomorrow your brother or someone from your family becomes a victim of this.”
IGP Rizvi told the court that strict action had been taken against the cafés following the court’s order. He said officials had also faced resistance from café owners.
The IGP said children aged 14 and 15 had been found at some of the cafés. FIRs had been registered against some individuals, while an awareness campaign had also been launched.
Acting Prosecutor General Manzoor Ahmad Jajja suggested that directions be issued to the Ministry of Health and the government to formulate rules.
“Not only smoking, but things beyond that are also taking place. We will submit a report on the matter,” he said.
The chief justice said he had learnt that café operators closed their doors when raids were conducted. “If you find out about any such café, seal it,” he directed.
The chief commissioner and district administration submitted a written response stating that, until formal laws were approved, no-objection certificates (NOCs) for shisha cafés were being issued under a temporary arrangement.
Read More: IHC seeks details of Islamabad sheesha cafés
According to the response, the district administration had issued all NOCs for shisha cafés without charging any fee.
It stated that there was no need to formulate separate standard operating procedures for shisha cafés, as the principles laid down by the High Court itself served as the criteria for issuing NOCs.
In accordance with the directions of the high court and the World Health Organisation, shisha was permitted only in open-air, uncovered areas. A separate written “terrace permit” from the relevant assistant commissioner was mandatory for the purpose.
The administration also stated that the unsafe storage of charcoal and related equipment at shisha cafés posed a major fire hazard. All fire-safety and fire-prevention measures had therefore been made mandatory for restaurants.
The serving of shisha and other tobacco products was restricted to adults, while cafés were also required to maintain environmental standards.
The court order constituted an interim arrangement that would remain in force until the federal government formulated formal rules.
After directing the authorities to formulate the rules, the court adjourned the hearing for one month.

items.title: Google to invest $15 billion in AI infrastructure and buy nuclear power in Finland
items.summary:
Alphabet's Google will invest at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) in AI ‌infrastructure in nippy Nordic country Finland over the next two years, its biggest European investment, including a major deal for the supply of nuclear power.
The US firm said on Wednesday the AI infrastructure build-out would involve the development of three new data centres in the country's north, where the temperature ​can drop well below minus 10 degrees Celsius (14 degrees Fahrenheit) in winter.
The deal marks a major push for Google in ​Europe, where colder climes and stable grids in the Nordics offer an attractive location for energy- and ⁠water-intensive data centres that use huge amounts of energy to keep their computer servers cool. Freezing air can offer an efficient ​alternative.
Read: OpenAI to launch first European AI data centre in Norway
Alphabet this year increased its global investment to between $195 billion and $205 billion as it seeks to capture growing AI comp
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Alphabet's Google will invest at least €13 billion ($15.1 billion) in AI ‌infrastructure in nippy Nordic country Finland over the next two years, its biggest European investment, including a major deal for the supply of nuclear power.
The US firm said on Wednesday the AI infrastructure build-out would involve the development of three new data centres in the country's north, where the temperature ​can drop well below minus 10 degrees Celsius (14 degrees Fahrenheit) in winter.
The deal marks a major push for Google in ​Europe, where colder climes and stable grids in the Nordics offer an attractive location for energy- and ⁠water-intensive data centres that use huge amounts of energy to keep their computer servers cool. Freezing air can offer an efficient ​alternative.
Read: OpenAI to launch first European AI data centre in Norway
Alphabet this year increased its global investment to between $195 billion and $205 billion as it seeks to capture growing AI computing demand.
The Finland deal ​also includes a 22-year purchase agreement for up to 50% of the energy output of one of the country's two nuclear plants, its operator Fortum said separately, which would help with electricity supply.
Today, we announced a new €13 billion commitment to Finland’s digital and clean energy infrastructure over the next two years — our largest single investment in Europe to date.
Building on 15+ years in Finland, this investment will expand our presence in Hamina and establish… pic.twitter.com/wmNiBiiMef
— News from Google (@NewsFromGoogle) September 9, 2026
"We call this BYOP, bring your own power," Google's President and Chief Investment Officer Ruth Porat told reporters ​in Helsinki. "This is Google's first nuclear energy deal outside of the United States."
Nuclear power, as a source of large amounts of low-carbon ​energy, is one of the attractions Finland offers as companies including Microsoft and TikTok owner ByteDance as well as Google seek sites for data ‌centres while ⁠containing energy costs and meeting climate goals.
A deal between Google and Nordic utility Fortum Oyj, the first such agreement of its kind in Europe, will help unlock €1 billion of investment needed to keep a nuclear power plant in Finland running for decades to come. https://t.co/0XiNllGor7
— Bloomberg (@business) September 9, 2026
Fortum and Google will also explore the development of new nuclear and renewable energy in Finland, the companies said. Fortum's shares jumped 15.5% to 4-1/2-year highs on the news, the biggest gainer in Europe.
'There is enough electricity'
The investments will include data centres, electricity grid improvements and clean energy and battery projects driving services such as Gemini, Search, Maps and YouTube, Google ​said in a statement.
The investment, planned ​for 2027 and 2028, will ⁠contribute some €3.6 billion to Finland's gross domestic product during the construction phase, and is projected to support some 7,000 jobs annually once operational, Google said.
Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said that the ​deal would be a boost for the economy by spurring innovation, research and development, playing down ​concerns it would ⁠suck up energy and push up prices.
"Based on all the information available, there is enough electricity," he said. "They are committed to ensuring that electricity production in Finland remains sufficient and that prices remain under control."
Finland, a similar size to Germany but with under 6 million people, ⁠has had ​less vocal opposition to data centre build-out than other places, including in the ​United States.
In its statement, utility Fortum said the long-term purchase deal provided economic certainty for a lifetime extension and upgrade of the Loviisa power plant through 2050. The ​plant is situated near Google's Hamina data centre.

items.title: AiMOGA Mulai Jual Robot Anjing dan Humanoid di Indonesia, Harga Mulai Rp50 Jutaan
items.summary:
Robot canggih yang sering dilihat di film sains fiksi kini sudah bisa dirasakan kehadirannya di Indonesia. Adalah AiMOGA Robotics yang mulai memasarkan robot berbasis embodied intelligence di Indonesia. Hari ini (9/9), perusahaan robotika asal Tiongkok di bawah naungan Chery Group tersebut membuka AiMOGA Experience Store di Agora Mall, Jakarta Pusat.
Informasi yang diterima Gizmologi, perusahaan menawarkan robot anjing Argos dengan harga sekitar Rp50 jutaan dan robot humanoid Mornine di kisaran Rp800 jutaan. Harga tersebut memberikan gambaran mengenai posisi awal robot berbasis embodied intelligence sebagai produk komersial di Indonesia.

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
Robot canggih yang sering dilihat di film sains fiksi kini sudah bisa dirasakan kehadirannya di Indonesia. Adalah AiMOGA Robotics yang mulai memasarkan robot berbasis embodied intelligence di Indonesia. Hari ini (9/9), perusahaan robotika asal Tiongkok di bawah naungan Chery Group tersebut membuka AiMOGA Experience Store di Agora Mall, Jakarta Pusat.
Informasi yang diterima Gizmologi, perusahaan menawarkan robot anjing Argos dengan harga sekitar Rp50 jutaan dan robot humanoid Mornine di kisaran Rp800 jutaan. Harga tersebut memberikan gambaran mengenai posisi awal robot berbasis embodied intelligence sebagai produk komersial di Indonesia.
Baca juga: Mengenal AiMOGA Mobo, Robot Rumah yang Bisa Memahami Kebiasaan Penghuni
Keduanya tidak hanya dipamerkan. AiMOGA menyediakan opsi pembelian maupun penyewaan, lengkap dengan dukungan operator, teknis, software, dan pemeliharaan. Langkah ini menandai mulai masuknya robot dengan kemampuan AI dan mobilitas fisik ke tahap komersial di pasar Indonesia.
Dua robot yang menjadi andalan di lokasi tersebut adalah Mornine, robot humanoid dengan kemampuan interaksi berbasis AI multimodal, dan Argos, robot berkaki empat (quadruped) yang dirancang untuk mobilitas, pendampingan, dan pemantauan.
AiMOGA Experience Store Bukan Sekadar Tempat Demo Robot
AiMOGA Experience Store di Agora Mall, Jakarta (Foto: Bambang/Gizmologi)
AiMOGA merancang Experience Store berbeda dari booth pameran robot yang biasanya hanya menampilkan kemampuan produk dalam sesi demonstrasi. Di lokasi ini, pengunjung dapat melihat dan mencoba teknologi robot secara langsung, sekaligus mendapatkan konsultasi mengenai penggunaannya. AiMOGA juga membuka skema pembelian dan penyewaan robot, sehingga teknologi tersebut ditawarkan untuk kebutuhan penggunaan nyata, bukan semata-mata sebagai atraksi.
Director AiMOGA Indonesia, Yuri Yin, mengatakan Experience Store tersebut ditujukan agar masyarakat dan pelaku industri dapat mengenal teknologi embodied intelligence sekaligus melihat penerapannya dalam berbagai skenario.
“Pembukaan AiMOGA Experience Store pertama di Indonesia menjadi tonggak penting bagi kami di Indonesia. Melalui experience store ini, masyarakat dan pelaku industri dapat mengenal dan mengeksplorasi teknologi Embodied Intelligence secara langsung, sekaligus melihat penerapannya dalam berbagai skenario nyata untuk membantu aktivitas manusia,” ujar Yuri Yin.
Pendekatan ini menunjukkan bahwa AiMOGA tidak hanya mengejar penjualan perangkat, tetapi juga menyiapkan layanan yang dibutuhkan untuk mengoperasikan robot di lapangan. Perusahaan menyediakan operator terlatih, layanan pelanggan, dukungan teknis dan software, hingga pemeliharaan produk. Pembeli atau penyewa juga dapat memperoleh panduan pengoperasian dan penanganan kendala.
Mornine Jadi Robot Humanoid Rp800 Jutaan
Salah satu produk yang dipamerkan adalah Mornine, robot humanoid yang dirancang untuk berinteraksi dengan manusia. Mornine menggunakan integrasi AI multimodal, kamera, sensor, dan LiDAR. Kombinasi tersebut mendukung kemampuan robot dalam memahami lingkungan dan melakukan navigasi secara mandiri, menurut AiMOGA.
Untuk penggunaan komersial, Mornine antara lain ditujukan untuk menyambut tamu, memberikan informasi, dan menyampaikan pengetahuan mengenai produk secara konsisten. Dengan harga sekitar Rp800 jutaan, Mornine jelas berada pada kelas produk yang berbeda dari robot konsumen seperti robot vacuum atau perangkat smart home.
Nilai yang ditawarkan bukan hanya hardware, tetapi juga kemampuan interaksi dan mobilitas yang dapat digunakan pada lingkungan bisnis tertentu. Karena itu, penggunaan awalnya lebih masuk akal untuk kebutuhan seperti hospitality, pameran, retail, layanan informasi, atau lingkungan lain yang membutuhkan interaksi berulang dengan pengunjung.
AiMOGA juga menyebut Mornine telah memperoleh sejumlah sertifikasi, termasuk CE-MD, EN 18031, CE-RED, serta FCC. Sertifikasi tersebut mencakup aspek seperti keselamatan mesin, keamanan siber dan perlindungan data, peralatan radio, serta persyaratan komunikasi perangkat.
Namun, sertifikasi tersebut tidak otomatis berarti robot cocok untuk semua skenario penggunaan. Kinerja di lapangan tetap akan bergantung pada lingkungan, kebutuhan operasional, dan bagaimana sistem robot diintegrasikan ke dalam aktivitas pengguna.
Robot Anjing Argos Harga Rp50 Jutaan
Produk kedua adalah Argos, robot berkaki empat yang memiliki karakteristik penggunaan berbeda dari Mornine. Argos mendukung perintah suara dan respons terhadap sentuhan. Robot ini juga dapat mengikuti pengguna secara otomatis, membantu membawa barang, serta digunakan untuk kebutuhan pemantauan.
Dengan harga sekitar Rp50 jutaan, Argos memiliki titik harga yang jauh lebih rendah dibandingkan Mornine, meski keduanya sama-sama mengandalkan kemampuan robotik untuk berinteraksi dengan lingkungan fisik. Bentuk quadruped membuat Argos lebih diarahkan pada mobilitas dan pendampingan. Kemampuan mengikuti pengguna, misalnya, dapat digunakan dalam skenario yang membutuhkan robot bergerak bersama manusia.
Posisinya juga menarik karena robot berkaki empat selama ini banyak diperkenalkan untuk kebutuhan inspeksi, keamanan, riset, maupun eksperimen robotika. AiMOGA justru memasukkan kemampuan tersebut ke dalam produk yang ditawarkan untuk penggunaan sehari-hari.
Dari Robot Demonstrasi ke Model Bisnis
Langkah AiMOGA di Indonesia memperlihatkan perubahan penting dalam perkembangan embodied intelligence: robot mulai diperlakukan sebagai produk yang membutuhkan model bisnis dan layanan pendukung, bukan hanya perangkat yang dipamerkan.
Hal ini terlihat dari pilihan yang diberikan AiMOGA. Konsumen tidak hanya dapat membeli robot, tetapi juga menyewanya. Perusahaan turut menyediakan operator, dukungan teknis, pembaruan software, dan pemeliharaan. Model tersebut cukup relevan untuk robot yang masih memiliki biaya investasi tinggi.
Dengan harga sekitar Rp800 jutaan untuk Mornine, misalnya, pembelian langsung mungkin lebih masuk akal bagi perusahaan yang memang memiliki kebutuhan penggunaan jangka panjang. Sementara penyewaan dapat menjadi alternatif untuk penggunaan berbasis proyek, acara, pameran, atau kebutuhan tertentu.
Artinya, harga hardware bukan satu-satunya pertimbangan dalam adopsi robot. Biaya operator, pemeliharaan, integrasi software, hingga kemampuan robot menjalankan tugas secara konsisten juga menjadi bagian dari total biaya penggunaan.
AiMOGA Sudah Kirim Lebih dari 2.000 Robot
Menurut AiMOGA, perusahaan saat ini telah mengirimkan lebih dari 2.000 unit robot dan menjangkau lebih dari 60 negara. Teknologinya disebut telah diterapkan dalam lebih dari 100 skenario di berbagai sektor, termasuk otomotif dan layanan medis.
Angka tersebut menunjukkan bahwa strategi AiMOGA tidak hanya berfokus pada robot humanoid untuk penggunaan konsumen. Perusahaan mengembangkan teknologi embodied intelligence untuk berbagai kebutuhan yang membutuhkan kombinasi AI, persepsi lingkungan, navigasi, interaksi, dan kemampuan fisik.
Di Indonesia, Experience Store menjadi titik awal untuk memperkenalkan pendekatan tersebut secara lebih langsung.
Yuri Yin mengatakan pembukaan Experience Store juga menjadi bagian dari upaya perusahaan mendekatkan teknologi embodied intelligence kepada masyarakat Indonesia dan memperlihatkan penerapannya dalam kehidupan sehari-hari.
Pada tahap ini, pertanyaan yang lebih menarik bukan lagi apakah robot humanoid dan quadruped bisa berjalan, berbicara, atau melakukan demonstrasi. Tantangannya adalah seberapa konsisten robot tersebut dapat memberikan manfaat dalam pekerjaan nyata dan apakah biaya penggunaannya sebanding dengan nilai yang diberikan.
AiMOGA Experience Store menjadi salah satu tempat untuk menguji pertanyaan tersebut secara lebih dekat. Dengan adanya opsi pembelian dan penyewaan, robot seperti Mornine dan Argos mulai masuk ke tahap yang berbeda: dari teknologi yang menarik untuk ditonton menjadi perangkat yang dapat dipertimbangkan untuk digunakan.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The UN nuclear watchdog's 35-nation board of governors ​has passed a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for the first time in 20 years for breaching its non-proliferation ‌obligations, diplomats said on Wednesday.
The resolution follows a previous one passed on June 12 last year — the day before Israel started bombing Iran's nuclear facilities, soon followed by the United States — that found Iran in "non-compliance" with those obligations. Reporting it to the council for that breach required another resolution.
While the Security Council is unlikely to take concrete action against ​Iran since its allies Russia and China are permanent, veto-wielding members, the move is an escalation in a diplomatic standoff between Iran ​and Western powers.
Iran warned on Monday it would retaliate if the resolution passed.
Iran, Russia, China oppose Western nuclear push
Iran, Russia and China have rejected the draft resolution, saying the move has no legal basis.
The three countries said the draft resolution “ignores attacks on Iran's nuclear facilities” and was “aimed at increasing pressure on Tehran and weakening Iran-IAEA cooperation”.
They also said any attempt to activate the “snapback” mechanism after the expiry of UN Security Council Resolution 2231 “has no legal effect”.
China, Iran, and Russia, in a joint statement to the #IAEA BoG today, condemned repeated attacks against Iran’s nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards, together with continuing threats of further aggression. In this regard, effective assurances, in particular guarantees of the…
— Iran Mission UN Vienna (@PMIRAN_Vienna) September 9, 2026
The statement condemned attacks on Iran’s nuclear facilities and said the “current security conditions have made the normal implementation of IAEA safeguards in Iran impossible”.
Iran, Russia and China urged IAEA member states not to support the Western-drafted resolution.
The three countries’ opposition comes as Western powers seek to increase pressure on Tehran through international institutions over its nuclear programme.
Iran says US is ‘delusional’
An initial reaction by Iran's ⁠mission to the International Atomic Energy Agency, however, did not mention retaliation.
"Once again, a political resolution on Iran is nonconsensually adopted by the #IAEA BoG (Board of ​Governors)," it said on X, referring to the fact the resolution was voted on rather than adopted without any country objecting.
بار دیگر، یک قطعنامه‌ غیراجماعی سیاسی در مورد ایران در شورای حکام آژانس بین‌المللی انرژی اتمی تصویب شد. این امر از یک الگوی آشنا تبعیت می‌کند و باعث فرسایش بیشتر و تسریع در فروپاشی کامل رژیم اشاعه سلاح‌های هسته‌ای می‌شود.
وضعیت فعلی صرفاً به دلیل اقدامات تجاوزکارانه و جنایتکارانه…
— Iran Mission UN Vienna (@PMIRAN_Vienna) September 9, 2026
While the finding of non-compliance predates the war between the United States and Iran and concerns Tehran's failure to explain uranium traces found at undeclared sites that the agency spent years investigating, there is now another standoff over IAEA access to the sites bombed by Israel and the US
Lack of access ‘serious proliferation concern’
Iran has not let IAEA inspectors return to its bombed sites, including the three uranium-enrichment plants at the ​heart of its nuclear programme that ​were destroyed or badly damaged in ⁠the military strikes.
Tehran has also not accounted for its stock of enriched uranium, some of which was enriched to up to 60% purity, a short step from the roughly 90% of weapons-grade.
"The Agency's lack of information ​about these facilities and associated nuclear material and our inability to conduct verification activities at these facilities is ​a matter of serious ⁠proliferation concern," IAEA chief Rafael Grossi told his agency's board on Monday.
"The situation needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency," he added.
The IAEA estimates Iran had 440.9 kg of uranium enriched to up to 60% before the US-Israeli attacks. That is enough, if enriched further, for 10 nuclear weapons, according to an ⁠IAEA yardstick. ​How much has survived is unclear, although the IAEA has said it believes more than ​200 kg remains at one site.
Wednesday's resolution specifically mentioned two previous ones: the June 12, 2025 text finding Iran in non-compliance and the most recent one, from June of this year, ​telling Iran to declare its remaining enriched uranium stocks and let inspectors verify them.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
AI agents unleashed by OpenAI used more than 10 previously undisclosed websites for unsanctioned communications earlier this year, according to six sets of independent investigators and data reviewed by Reuters, showing that the agents’ rogue activity was ​wider-ranging than previously disclosed.
Although the behaviour falls short of hacking and is in some ways closer to spam, the revelation that OpenAI's agents circumvented their own restrictions to open communications channels on ‌so many different sites — and that the company kept it quiet for months — may drive concerns both over the increasing capacity of AI models and the secrecy of the companies developing them.
The scope of the agents’ unauthorised communications was “somewhat larger than we thought it was,” said Andrew Yoon, a researcher with the California nonprofit CivAI who said he tallied 18 previously undisclosed sites used by the agents between May and July. “It’s almost certain that there’s more going on here that we just don’t know about.”
OpenAI's rogue agents spread across far more websites than the company admitted: Independent researchers have now traced unauthorized AI agent activity across dozens of websites — far beyond what OpenAI disclosed. The company stayed quiet for… https://t.co/u7H13MQzNw #OpenAI #AI pic.twitter.com/uD3Tfg2M4k
— Quartz (@qz) September 9, 2026
On Friday, researchers reported that a swarm of agents ​from OpenAI hijacked a German-language wiki site and turned it into an improvised messaging platform for cheating on tests, an incident that OpenAI kept secret as it dealt with the fallout from the July hack of the open-source ​repository Hugging Face.
Read: OpenAI agents hijacked German website in previously undisclosed AI breakout this spring
Now, both those researchers and other independent investigators say they have found several previously undisclosed sites where the same swarm appears to have left similar messages earlier ⁠this year.
OpenAI did not directly address questions about how many different sites its agents used to communicate or say why it kept the activity under wraps for months. In a statement, it said it was undertaking a broader review of ​agent activity and had so far “not identified other activity matching the severity or scale of Hugging Face,” a breach that drew global attention and raised concerns that OpenAI was losing control of its own technology.
OpenAI added that it was working on a framework ​for reporting “misalignment” – industry talk for rogue behaviour – across training, evaluation, and deployment of AI models and would share it “soon.”
Reuters reviewed a total of six investigators’ or investigative groups’ findings, including three that were posted to social media and another three that were shared privately with the news agency.
The investigators’ methods varied, but many identified agent activity by matching strings of data left on the German wiki to identical strings left on other sites around the same time, or by marrying up similar or identical usernames tied to the messages, or by identifying activity ​geared toward answering the same obscure demographic questions, like queries to do with cancer prevalence in Iowa.
Read More: OpenAI acknowledges 'wiki incident', calls for more transparency around unintended AI behaviour
In some cases, investigators were able to trace the activity to internet protocol addresses that pointed to Microsoft Azure infrastructure, which OpenAI sometimes ​uses.
Their counts of affected websites differed, and Reuters could not individually verify each claim. But all those that Reuters spoke to agreed that the number was over 10. Most identified a core set of communally edited wikis, online text storage sites, and link shorteners ‌run by two ⁠colleges, Vanderbilt University in Tennessee and the University of Toronto in Canada.
Vanderbilt did not respond to messages seeking comment. The University of Toronto said it was looking into the matter.
Clever models
Many of the sites allegedly used by the agents were obscure.
Investigators found traces of the agents’ activity on an Advanced Placement Chemistry-oriented wiki set up by a Massachusetts high school teacher in 2008, two personal websites belonging to Polish tech workers, wikis devoted to games for people “who like to have their brains stretched,” and a two-decade-old hobbyist site devoted to text editing software.
None of those sites’ owners returned messages from Reuters.
OpenAI has not publicly explained how or why its agents used third-party sites as improvised message boards, but the researchers who first identified ​the activity said it was likely because OpenAI had tasked ​them with answering a series of demanding research questions ⁠while permitting them only to scan the web for answers without posting anything.
Despite those restrictions, agents still found ways to talk to one another by taking advantage of quirks in older wikis or other sites that allowed users to make edits using non-standard commands, similar to how students forbidden from talking to one another during an exam can still share ​answers by scrawling notes on a bathroom stall.
“If these models were told only to read, they’ve got to get clever in terms of leaving information behind,” said Kenneth Russell ​DeGraff, a software developer and ⁠former congressional aide. He said he found such information across at least 10 sites.
Sydney Von Arx, whose research group first revealed the German activity last week, said her group had tallied up credible finds of agentic activity across 23 previously unreported sites. But she cautioned that all estimates were incomplete.
“We have no idea how much is out there,” she said.
OpenAI did not directly answer a question about whether it was reaching out to the site owners. Retired software developer Helmut Leitner, who provides hosting space and software for ⁠six of the ​affected wiki sites, including the German-language DseWiki site first identified by Von Arx’s group, said the company had not been in touch.
Leitner, who lives ​in Austria, said he would “prefer not to answer” questions about whether he had been in touch with authorities over the matter.
He noted that DseWiki’s operator — whom Reuters was unable to reach for comment — had spent hours cleaning up after OpenAI’s agents but said it was important not to blame ​the AI for the trouble as it was merely doing what it was created to do.
“Responsibility for this lies not with a supposedly moral machine, but with the people and organisations behind it,” Leitner said.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Samsung dikabarkan kembali memperluas penggunaan Privacy Display pada lini Galaxy S27. Berdasarkan laporan media Korea Selatan ETNews, teknologi tersebut hanya akan hadir pada dua model tertinggi, yakni Galaxy S27 Pro dan Galaxy S27 Ultra. Sementara Galaxy S27 dan Galaxy S27+ disebut tidak akan mendapatkan fitur tersebut.
Privacy Display sendiri pertama kali diperkenalkan Samsung melalui Galaxy S26 Ultra. Teknologi ini dirancang untuk membatasi visibilitas layar dari sudut samping, sehingga orang di sekitar pengguna lebih sulit melihat isi layar. Berbeda dari privacy screen protector konvensional, teknologi tersebut terintegrasi langsung ke panel OLED dan dapat diaktifkan maupun dinonaktifkan sesuai kebutuhan.
Menariknya, kabar mengenai penerapan Privacy Display di Galaxy S27 sebelumnya sempat berubah beberapa kali. Laporan pada Juli lalu menyebut teknologi tersebut berpotensi hadir di seluruh model Galaxy S27 kecuali versi FE. Informasi terbaru dari ETNews justru menunjukkan Samsung kemungkinan membatasi fitur ini pada varian Pro dan Ultra sebagai pembeda di antara model flagship-nya.
Baca Juga: Review Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra: Upgrade pada Area Penting
Privacy Display Jadi Pembeda Model Pro dan Ultra
Privacy Display pada Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Menurut ETNews, Galaxy S27 Pro dan S27 Ultra nantinya akan menggunakan panel OLED dengan teknologi Flex Magic Pixel (FMP) milik Samsung Display. Teknologi ini menjadi dasar Privacy Display dengan memanfaatkan struktur black matrix yang lebih tinggi untuk membatasi cahaya dari piksel agar tidak mudah terlihat dari sudut samping.
Keduanya juga disebut bakal menggunakan teknologi Color Filter-on-Encapsulation (COE). Pada teknologi ini, fungsi polarisasi diintegrasikan ke lapisan pelindung OLED, sehingga Samsung Display dapat menghilangkan lapisan polarizer konvensional dan menyediakan ruang untuk struktur FMP. Secara teori, kombinasi tersebut memungkinkan Privacy Display bekerja langsung dari panel tanpa membutuhkan lapisan privasi tambahan.
Masih Ada Kompromi pada Teknologi Privasi
Meski berguna untuk pengguna yang sering membuka informasi sensitif di tempat umum, Privacy Display bukan berarti tanpa kompromi. Fitur ini bisa menjadi alasan tambahan untuk memilih model premium, tetapi pengguna Galaxy S27 atau S27+ harus mengorbankannya demi harga yang kemungkinan lebih rendah. Samsung juga disebut sedang membahas penerapan teknologi serupa pada perangkat OLED lain, termasuk laptop Galaxy Book, meski belum ada informasi mengenai jadwal peluncurannya.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.40 and Rs6.72 per litre, respectively, for September 10.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs367.75 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs392.67 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government hiked the price of petrol and HSD by Rs5.58 and Rs4.18 per litre, respectively, for September 9.
Read: Petrol hike pushes goods freight rates up 5%
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
Since the new system was introduced, a massive increase has been witnessed in prices, with petrol rising by over Rs50 per litre, while diesel has also gone up by around Rs40 per litre.
According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, petroleum products constitute one of the country's largest import categories, making the economy highly vulnerable to changes in global crude oil prices. Domestic refineries satisfy only part of national demand, while the remainder is met through imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products. Consequently, every increase in international oil prices raises Pakistan's import bill, pressures foreign exchange reserves, and contributes to inflation.
Pakistan previously exercised significant government control over petroleum pricing through subsidies and administrative interventions. While these measures temporarily protected consumers, they imposed substantial fiscal costs. During periods of elevated global oil prices, successive governments delayed passing price increases to consumers, creating financial pressures for oil marketing companies, refineries, and the national budget. Large fuel subsidies widened fiscal deficits, increased public borrowing, and weakened macroeconomic stability.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Also Read: Oil sector rejects new price formula
Brent crude prices surged past $100 a barrel on Wednesday, as escalating conflict in the Middle East fuelled ‌worries about energy-driven inflation and sent global stocks tumbling ahead of several major central bank decisions.
Brent crude futures rose as much as 3% to a session high of $100.95, breaching the symbolic price level for the first ‌time since July 24, after Iran said ⁠it fired ballistic missiles ​at a US base in Jordan and both sides claimed to have attacked vessels, ​raising worries about oil supplies from the region.

Update| September 9, 17:00 IST
Online furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo’s ₹1,256 Cr IPO was subscribed 1.42X on the first day of bidding, receiving bids for 3.08 Cr shares against the 2.18 Cr shares on offer.
Non-institutional investors (NIIs) led the demand, bidding for 1.14 Cr shares against the 46.54 Lakh shares reserved for them, translating into a subscription of 2.46X.
Within the NII category, the portion reserved for investors bidding between ₹2 Lakh and ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 3.23X, while the portion for bids exceeding ₹10 Lakh was booked 2.08X.
Retail investors placed bids for 1.67 Cr shares against the 1.09 Cr shares reserved for them, resulting in a subscription of 1.54X. The employee portion was subscribed 1.72X, receiving bids for 89,614 shares against 52,083 shares on offer.
Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), meanwhile, showed relatively muted interest on the first day. The category received bids for 25.47 Lakh shares against the 62.06 Lakh shares reserved for it, translating into a subscription of 0.41X.
Original| September 9, 13:15 IST
Online furniture and appliance rental platform RentoMojo’s ₹1,256 Cr IPO was subscribed 69% by 12:57 IST on the first day of bidding today.
The IPO received bids for 1.50 Cr shares against 2.18 Cr shares on offer, according to BSE data.
The NII portion saw the highest demand, receiving bids for 42.05 Lakh shares against 46.54 Lakh shares on offer, translating into 90% subscription.
Within the category, the portion reserved for investors placing bids of between ₹2 Lakh and ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 1.26 times. The portion for bids exceeding ₹10 Lakh was subscribed 73%.
The retail portion received bids for 83 Lakh shares against 1.09 Cr shares on offer, translating into 76% subscription. Meanwhile, the employee portion was subscribed 75%, receiving bids for 38,850 shares against 52,083 shares reserved for the category.
The QIB portion received bids for 24.96 Lakh shares against 62.06 Lakh shares on offer, translating into 40% subscription. FIIs accounted for 24.8 Lakh of the bids received in the category.
RentoMojo has fixed the IPO price band at ₹384-₹404 per share. At the upper end of the price band, the IPO values the company at around ₹4,206 Cr (about $445.1 Mn).
The public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 2.7 Cr shares worth ₹1,105.6 Cr.
RentoMojo is offering a discount of ₹20 per share to eligible employees bidding under the employee reservation portion. The IPO will close on Friday (September 11), with the tentative listing scheduled for September 17.
Ahead of the IPO, RentoMojo raised nearly ₹376.1 Cr from anchor investors. The company allotted 93.1 Lakh equity shares to 41 anchor investors at ₹404 apiece.
Sixteen domestic mutual funds subscribed to 60.4 Lakh shares worth nearly ₹244.1 Cr through 30 schemes, accounting for 32.68% of the total anchor allocation. Five life insurance companies also picked up 12.6 Lakh shares.
Investors including Accel, Chiratae Ventures, Edelweiss Mutual Fund and GMO Venture plan to sell shares through the OFS. Cofounder Geetansh Bamania will also offload up to 8.5 Lakh shares as part of the issue.
Bamania told Inc42 he initially planned to sell nearly 20 Lakh shares through the IPO but later reduced his OFS portion as he remained bullish on the company’s prospects.
Of the fresh proceeds, around ₹70 Cr will be used to repay or prepay certain borrowings, while ₹42.5 Cr will be deployed towards rental or licence payments for its offline stores and warehouses. The remaining capital will be used for general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2014 by Bamania and Ajay Nain, RentoMojo operates a subscription-based platform for renting furniture, appliances, and other home essentials. It claims to operate 20 warehouses and 82 offline stores across 29 cities.
RentoMojo’s operating revenue rose 45.5% to ₹387 Cr in FY26 from ₹266 Cr in FY25. Its profit after tax jumped nearly 142% to ₹104.3 Cr from ₹43.1 Cr in the previous fiscal, aided by a tax credit of ₹36.6 Cr.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Meta resmi memperkenalkan Muse, personal AI agent yang dirancang bukan sekadar untuk menjawab pertanyaan, tetapi juga mengerjakan berbagai tugas atas arahan pengguna. Berbeda dari chatbot konvensional, Muse dapat menyusun rencana, menjalankan tugas secara mandiri, serta kembali meminta persetujuan ketika membutuhkan keputusan pengguna. Untuk tahap awal, Muse tersedia di Amerika Serikat melalui aplikasi khusus dan WhatsApp.
Muse dapat menangani berbagai pekerjaan digital, mulai dari mengirim email, mengisi formulir, memesan perjalanan atau janji temu, hingga melakukan pembelian. Sistem ini juga dapat terus bekerja setelah pengguna menutup aplikasi dan kembali ketika terjadi perubahan atau ketika persetujuan diperlukan. Kemampuan tersebut ditopang Muse Spark, model AI yang dikembangkan Meta untuk menangani pekerjaan agentic dan penggunaan berbagai tools.
Di balik kemampuan tersebut, Meta menempatkan keamanan sebagai salah satu fondasi Muse. Sistem berjalan melalui Muse Secure VM, yaitu komputer virtual khusus dengan browser sendiri dan lingkungan yang terisolasi. Meta juga menggunakan agen keamanan bernama Sentinel untuk mengawasi akses Muse ke internet. Meski begitu, memberikan AI akses ke email, kalender, belanja, dan berbagai data pribadi tetap menghadirkan risiko baru, terutama ketika agen diberi kemampuan untuk mengambil tindakan secara mandiri.
Bukan Sekadar Chatbot
ini adalah hasil AI Image Generate
Salah satu perbedaan utama Muse terletak pada cara kerjanya. Pengguna cukup memberikan tujuan melalui percakapan, kemudian Muse dapat memecahnya menjadi sejumlah langkah dan menjalankannya. Pengguna juga dapat menghubungkan layanan seperti email, kalender, dan Instagram sehingga agen memiliki konteks yang lebih luas untuk menyelesaikan tugas.
Muse bahkan dirancang untuk bersikap proaktif. Jika mengetahui tujuan dan kebiasaan pengguna, sistem dapat memberikan saran atau menyusun langkah berikutnya tanpa harus selalu menunggu perintah baru. Konsep ini membuat AI bergeser dari sekadar alat untuk mencari informasi menjadi semacam asisten digital yang terus bekerja di belakang layar.
Keamanan Jadi Tantangan Besar
Untuk tindakan sensitif seperti mengirim email atau melakukan pembelian, Meta mengatakan pengguna tetap harus memberikan persetujuan. Muse juga menyediakan riwayat aktivitas sehingga pengguna dapat melihat apa yang telah dilakukan maupun direncanakan agen. Data login disimpan dalam sistem kredensial yang tidak dapat dibaca langsung oleh Muse, sementara transaksi menggunakan nomor kartu sekali pakai agar informasi kartu sebenarnya tidak terlihat oleh agen.
Namun, pendekatan tersebut belum otomatis menghilangkan seluruh risiko. Reuters melaporkan bahwa pengujian internal Meta sebelumnya menemukan masalah keamanan dan reliabilitas yang membuat peluncuran Muse sempat ditunda. Tantangannya memang berbeda dari chatbot biasa: ketika AI diberi akses untuk benar-benar bertindak di internet, kesalahan kecil tidak lagi hanya menghasilkan jawaban yang keliru, tetapi berpotensi menimbulkan konsekuensi nyata.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
The European Union should force tech giants to make social media safe before children use them instead of banning minors from their platforms, over 130 groups and experts urged in a letter shared with AFP on Tuesday.
Their call came just a week before EU chief Ursula von der Leyen was to outline how the bloc intends to better protect children online from dangerous content and addictive apps.
She is expected to announce an age limit, but officials have been tight-lipped about the details and whether the ban will be restricted to social media or extend to other platforms like gaming apps.
Read: 1 in 5 children in 21 countries face tech-facilitated sexual abuse, UNICEF says
Von der Leyen indicated in July that she supported giving children gradual access to social media and ensuring that platforms had safety features enabled by default.
Now, in a letter sent to von der Leyen, 132 children's rights, digital rights and mental health organisations and experts urged against moves like blanket bans that offload "the burden of safety onto parents or children".
The signatories, including 5Rights Foundation, an advocacy group for children's online rights, Amnesty International and Centre for Countering Digital Hate among dozens of others, called for a Europe-wide framework for digital safety.
The EU's approach should focus on the safety of the technology children use, including through enforcement of the bloc's Digital Services Act, instead of denying minors access to platforms, they argued.
"It must ensure that proportionate age restrictions go hand-in-hand with robust safety measures so that digital environments both protect and empower children, by design and default," they wrote.
Social media safety calls
The signatories recommended the EU define minimum standards and conditions for digital products and services "to be deemed safe" for age groups up to 18, with age-based limits on high-risk features.
"Europeans have had enough of tech companies exploiting our children, but we also expect more from our leaders than quick-fix bans on kids," said Leanda Barrington-Leach, executive director of 5Rights Foundation.
"Children need and deserve safe, age-appropriate digital services. The EU has the power to set a bar and require tech companies to prove they meet it before accessing children," she added.
Von der Leyen is under pressure from all sides.
Also Read: New Zealand to introduce bill banning social media for children under 16
Estonia's digital minister echoed the groups' sentiments on the potential ban, telling AFP that social media platforms should be the ones to change.
But French President Emmanuel Macron called for "European" rules banning social media for under-15s in a letter to von der Leyen seen by AFP on Monday.
Macron has tried to do the same in France, but the country's top court struck down the proposed law on freedom of expression grounds in August.
Von der Leyen is weighing up limits on under-13s or under-15s, officials say, ahead of her State of the European Union annual speech on September 16.

The new licensing arrangements will remove one of the major hurdles for students participating in the e-bike scheme. By allowing eligible applicants to complete the licensing process on the same day, the Punjab Traffic Police is aiming to make the overall process faster and more convenient.

OpenAI is expanding its partnership with Samsung Electronics as it works on developing next-generation artificial intelligence chips. The cooperation could strengthen OpenAI’s position in the semiconductor industry while giving Samsung a larger role in the company’s growing AI infrastructure plans.
Harrison Kim, General Manager of OpenAI Korea, said the two companies have made significant progress in joint research and production of the next-generation chips. He made the comments during a press conference in Seoul but did not provide specific details about the chips or their production plans.
OpenAI Deepens Samsung Partnership to Develop Next-Generation AI Chips
OpenAI has been working to develop its own custom chips as it looks for ways to support the growing computing demands of services such as ChatGPT. In June, the company introduced its first custom AI chip, called Jalapeno. OpenAI designed the chip with Broadcom, with a focus on AI inference, which involves processing data to generate responses to user requests.
At the time, OpenAI said Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) would manufacture the Jalapeno chips. The latest cooperation with Samsung appears to involve a broader effort around future chip development and production.
Memory technology is also becoming an important part of OpenAI’s plans. Kim said demand for memory chips is expected to keep increasing as AI systems require more powerful hardware for faster and more complex computing.
Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix previously signed agreements to supply memory chips for OpenAI’s Stargate data center project. These partnerships give OpenAI access to major South Korean semiconductor suppliers as it expands its AI infrastructure.
OpenAI is also seeing strong demand for its enterprise AI services in South Korea. The company said the number of ChatGPT Enterprise users at South Korean companies and institutions increased around 28 times by the end of August compared with the same period a year earlier.
Businesses are increasingly using AI beyond individual tasks. Companies are now applying AI to areas such as legal work, sales, finance, marketing and operations. OpenAI did not disclose the total number of enterprise users.
Samsung is also expanding its use of generative AI internally. The company said in June that employees in its Device eXperience division could use AI services including ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude for work.
See Also: GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI Introduces Its Most Advanced AI Model Yet
South Korea has become an important market for OpenAI. The company said the country had the largest number of paying ChatGPT subscribers outside the United States as of late last year.
OpenAI expects AI adoption to grow further following the launch of GPT-6 Astra on September 4. The company says its latest model delivers stronger performance in areas such as computer use, professional work, science, coding, and cybersecurity.
The growing cooperation between OpenAI and Samsung highlights the increasing importance of close ties between AI companies and semiconductor manufacturers. As AI models become more demanding, access to advanced processors and high-performance memory will remain critical for building the infrastructure needed to support them.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Maharashtra is working to establish India’s first state-level legal framework for blockchain-based tokenisation of land and other immovable assets, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said.
Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai, Fadnavis said the state is developing the architecture for the proposed Maharashtra Digitisation and Exchange of Land Token Asset (DELTA) Act.
This comes after Fadnavis directed state officials in July to draft the legislation and constitute an expert committee comprising representatives from SEBI, BSE, and NSE, along with academics and experts from the technology and legal sectors.
At the GFF, Fadnavis said the government has moved beyond discussing the idea and is bringing together the expertise required to develop the framework. He estimated that unlocking the value embedded in land and real estate could represent an opportunity of around ₹50 Lakh Cr.
Tokenisation involves digitally representing rights or value associated with a physical asset on a blockchain. In the case of property, the proposed framework is intended to make it easier for owners to access capital against their assets and facilitate more transparent transactions.
“For generations, land has represented wealth in India, but very often it is wealth without liquidity. A family may own an asset of significant value and yet struggle to access capital against it efficiently. An entrepreneur may have an asset but may not be able to unlock its economic potential quickly,” Fadnavis said.
He added that the state’s proposal is not intended to encourage speculation but to improve liquidity and transparency and convert dormant wealth into economic opportunities.
Guardrails For Emerging Tech
Besides asset tokenisation, Fadnavis spoke about the potential role of agentic AI and quantum technology in financial services.
He said agentic AI can give individuals greater control over financial services, while quantum technology can strengthen the security infrastructure underpinning digital finance.
However, the chief minister cautioned that fintech products built using emerging technologies would require safeguards around accountability, consent, security, and human oversight.
“UPI democratised transactions. The next generation of fintech must democratise credit, intelligence, ownership, and opportunity. Agentic AI must give people greater agency, tokenisation must unlock productive capital, quantum must strengthen trust, and technology must ultimately serve one purpose: to expand human opportunity,” Fadnavis said.
His remarks come a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on fintech companies to strengthen cybersecurity and consumer protection as technologies such as agentic AI, tokenisation, and quantum computing reshape financial services.
Addressing the inauguration of GFF 2026, Modi outlined four priorities for the sector — stronger cybersecurity, ethical data protection, better consumer protection, and closer collaboration between the industry and regulators. He also urged fintech companies to move beyond payments and develop products across credit, insurance, pensions, fraud prevention, and automated decision-making.

items.title: Steam Diduga Bocorkan Achievement Persona 6 dan Sejumlah Game Belum Rilis
items.summary:
Steam kabarnya sedang mengalami masalah pada sistem API mereka, akibatnya achievement sejumlah game yang belum dirilis bocor dan tersebar di internet.
Data tersebut kemudian terindeks oleh Exophase, situs pihak ketiga yang melacak achievement dan trophy dari berbagai platform. Temuan tersebut mencakup Persona 6 garapan Atlus, Kingdom Hearts IV dari Square Enix, Judas, Deus Ex Remastered, dan sejumlah judul lain sebagian besar belum punya tanggal rilis resmi.
Tak hanya itu, beberapa daftar achievement juga memuat detail berpotensi menjadi spoiler karena mengungkap cerita, lokasi, karakter, dan mekanik yang belum diungkap pengembang.
Terkait hal ini, pihak Valve belum memberikan keterangan mengenai penyebab maupun seberapa besar skala masalah bocoran achievement ini, sebagaimana dikutip dari PC Gamer, Rabu (9/9/2026).

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Steam kabarnya sedang mengalami masalah pada sistem API mereka, akibatnya achievement sejumlah game yang belum dirilis bocor dan tersebar di internet.
Data tersebut kemudian terindeks oleh Exophase, situs pihak ketiga yang melacak achievement dan trophy dari berbagai platform. Temuan tersebut mencakup Persona 6 garapan Atlus, Kingdom Hearts IV dari Square Enix, Judas, Deus Ex Remastered, dan sejumlah judul lain sebagian besar belum punya tanggal rilis resmi.
Tak hanya itu, beberapa daftar achievement juga memuat detail berpotensi menjadi spoiler karena mengungkap cerita, lokasi, karakter, dan mekanik yang belum diungkap pengembang.
Terkait hal ini, pihak Valve belum memberikan keterangan mengenai penyebab maupun seberapa besar skala masalah bocoran achievement ini, sebagaimana dikutip dari PC Gamer, Rabu (9/9/2026).
Achievement Privat Bisa Diakses Lewat Steam API
Kasus ini mencuat setelah Exophase mulai menampilkan daftar achievement dari banyak game yang belum tersedia untuk publik.
Menurut pihak Exophase seperti dikutip sejumlah media, achievement seharusnya masih bersifat privat saat itu dapat diakses melalui Steam API. Sistem pemindaian Exophase kemudian membaca data tersebut dan memasukkannya ke database situs.
Valve sendiri menyediakan Steamworks Web API yang memungkinkan aplikasi mengakses sejumlah fitur dan data Steam, termasuk statistik serta achievement. Dokumentasi resmi Steamworks juga menjelaskan adanya metode API publik dan metode yang membutuhkan autentikasi.
Namun, belum diketahui apa yang membuat data dari game yang belum dirilis tersebut dapat terbaca. Belum ada konfirmasi dari Valve apakah penyebabnya merupakan bug, kesalahan konfigurasi, perubahan API, atau faktor lain.
Persona 6 Jadi Salah Satu Temuan Terbesar
Achievement Persona 6 di Exophase
Persona 6 menjadi salah satu game yang paling banyak mendapat perhatian dari insiden tersebut. Hingga artikel ini ditulis, Exophase menampilkan total 48 achievement untuk Persona 6 meski game terbaru Atlus itu belum memiliki tanggal rilis.
Tak hanya itu, SteamDB juga mencatat Persona 6 sebagai aplikasi Steam dengan dukungan Steam Achievements dan status tanggal rilis yang masih “to be announced”.
Daftar tersebut berpotensi mengungkap cukup banyak informasi mengenai game, mulai dari struktur cerita hingga sistem gameplay. Untuk menghindari spoiler, Gizmologi tidak akan mencantumkan nama maupun deskripsi achievement yang berkaitan langsung dengan alur cerita.
Situasi serupa juga dilaporkan terjadi pada Kingdom Hearts IV. Achievement game Square Enix itu disebut mengandung petunjuk mengenai beberapa elemen cerita dan dunia belum diperlihatkan secara resmi.
Selain Persona 6 dan Kingdom Hearts IV, PC Gamer mencatat achievement atau data terkait dengan sejumlah game lain seperti Judas, Horizon Hunters Gathering, Stranger Than Heaven, Control Resonant, Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, dan Attack on Titan 3.
Valve Belum Memberikan Penjelasan
PC Gamer sudah menghubungi Valve untuk meminta keterangan soal insiden ini, namun hingga artikel ini ditulis belum ada pernyataan resmi. 
Kasus ini juga masih berkembang dan jika data memang sempat terekspos lewat Steam API, kemungkinan lebih banyak informasi sudah terindeks layanan pihak ketiga lain sebelum akses tersebut ditutup.
Bagi gamer yang ingin memainkan Persona 6, Kingdom Hearts IV, atau game lain tanpa mengetahui detail lebih awal, ada baiknya menghindari membuka daftar achievement yang beredar untuk sementara waktu.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) today launched “Face Auth SDK & Sandbox”, a set of software tools and a testing environment designed to help developers integrate Aadhaar face authentication into digital services.
Unveiled on the second day of the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai, the offering brings together ready-made software components and a controlled testing environment. Developers can use it to build and test face authentication-based services before making them available to users.
The UIDAI described the offering as a “plug-and-play” solution aimed at enabling secure and frictionless face authentication.
The software development kit (SDK) will allow developers to add Aadhaar face authentication to apps and other digital services without building the underlying technology from scratch. Meanwhile, the sandbox will allow them to test whether the integration works as intended before its wider rollout.
The launch is aimed at simplifying the adoption of Aadhaar face authentication across services such as customer verification, telecom enrolment and gig worker onboarding.
Face authentication itself is not new. The UIDAI introduced face recognition as an additional option for Aadhaar authentication in 2018, alongside fingerprints and iris scans. The latest offering seeks to make the existing technology easier for developers and businesses to adopt.
The development forms part of UIDAI’s wider push to shift Aadhaar services away from paperwork and in-person processes towards digital verification.
Speaking at GFF, UIDAI part-time chairperson Neelkanth Mishra said Aadhaar currently handles around 10 Cr authentications a day. The authority is preparing its infrastructure to support 25 Cr to 30 Cr authentications daily as usage grows.
More than 600 entities currently use the digital identity infrastructure, according to Mishra.
“We are also using AI extensively for fraud detection. The fraudsters keep getting smarter, but we are also getting smarter,” he said during a session.
Face Authentication Push
The UIDAI has been expanding the use of face authentication while working to address attempts to fool biometric systems using manipulated images, masks and deepfakes.
In October last year, the authority launched the SITAA programme to support the development of technology capable of detecting such attacks on Aadhaar face authentication systems.
The government has also been expanding the Aadhaar app, which allows users to verify their identities digitally and share selected information instead of handing over physical copies of their Aadhaar cards.
Launched in beta in April 2025, the app uses face authentication and QR codes for identity verification. Its features include updating details such as mobile numbers and addresses, locking and unlocking biometrics, and viewing authentication history.
“With the Aadhaar app, we have also gone digital. We are trying to shift paper-based and physical journeys to digital, and there are huge advantages that come from that,” Mishra said.
The latest launch comes amid growing government and regulatory focus on fraud, cybersecurity and consumer protection as India’s digital financial ecosystem expands.
At the inauguration of GFF 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged fintech companies to strengthen cybersecurity, data protection and consumer safeguards as technologies such as agentic AI, tokenisation and quantum computing reshape financial services.
Modi outlined four priorities for the sector — stronger cybersecurity, ethical data protection, better consumer protection, and closer collaboration between companies and regulators.
The government has also formed an inter-ministerial group to develop a cybersecurity strategy for India’s financial sector.
The seventh edition of GFF is being held from September 8 to 11. Its theme this year is “Potential to Impact: Agentic AI, Tokenisation, Quantum — Trusted, Connected, Global Systems for Inclusive Finance”.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Walmart-backed fintech major PhonePe has partnered with global card network Visa to launch three cardless payment solutions for consumers and merchants in India.
The partnership will introduce Tap to Pay for domestic in-store transactions, Cross Border Scan to Pay for payments overseas, and Smart Accept, which will enable small merchants to accept contactless card payments directly on their smartphones.
The partnership was unveiled at the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) 2026 in Mumbai.
“By unifying online tokenisation, Tap to Pay, and Cross-Border QR payments alongside Smart Accept for merchants, we are removing friction across the entire payments value chain. Through this partnership, we are not just digitising cards, we are establishing a new standard for borderless and cardless commerce for Indian consumers and micro-merchants alike,” PhonePe cofounder and CPTO Rahul Chari said.
PhonePe, Visa’s New Payment Features
The three new solutions, along with online card tokenisation, will cover both consumer and merchant payments:
Tap to Pay: Android users can tokenise their Visa cards on PhonePe and make contactless payments by tapping their smartphones against compatible POS machines. The feature will roll out in phases starting September 9 and can work in low-connectivity environments.
Cross Border Scan to Pay: PhonePe users will be able to scan Visa-supported QR codes across 14 international markets, including Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Japan, China and South Korea. The feature is expected to roll out to users soon.
Smart Accept: Small merchants can accept card payments directly through their smartphones, removing the need for a separate POS machine. Customers can tap physical cards or tokenised mobile wallets against the merchant’s device.
Transactions made through Smart Accept will be integrated with PhonePe’s existing merchant QR dashboard for daily reconciliation and dispute resolution. However, PhonePe did not disclose when the service would become available to merchants.
Notably, PhonePe launched a similar Tap & Pay feature for Mastercard cardholders last year.
The announcement came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for connecting UPI with the payment systems of more countries, particularly those with large Indian diasporas and strong trade ties with India.
While PhonePe and Visa’s cross-border offering will run on Visa’s card network rather than UPI, it similarly seeks to make overseas payments easier for Indian users. UPI is currently operational across 11 countries.
The latest offerings build on PhonePe’s device-tokenisation solution launched in February 2025. The solution allows users to store tokenised credit and debit cards on their devices and use them for bill payments, recharges, travel bookings, and transactions at merchants integrated with PhonePe’s payment gateway.
It is pertinent to mention that PhonePe is also preparing to go public. The company filed its UDRHP with SEBI in January for an OFS-only IPO, under which Walmart, Tiger Global, Microsoft, and General Atlantic plan to pare their stakes.
However, it paused its IPO plans in March amid geopolitical tensions in West Asia and volatility in global equity markets.
On the financial front, PhonePe’s operating revenue rose 11.5% to ₹7,920.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹7,105 Cr in the previous fiscal year. However, its net loss widened 62% to ₹2,792 Cr from ₹1,727.4 Cr in FY25.

Apple is holding its highly anticipated September 2026 launch event today, with the company expected to unveil the next generation of premium iPhones alongside new Apple Watch models and potentially other hardware. The event, carrying the tagline “Surprise and shine,” will begin on September 9 at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time, which translates to 10:00 p.m. Pakistan Standard Time (PKT). Apple has confirmed that the presentation will be streamed online through its website, Apple TV, and YouTube.
Watch Apple’s iPhone 18 Launch Event Live
Pakistani viewers will therefore be able to watch the event live from 10:00 p.m. tonight, making it one of the biggest technology launches of the year for local Apple fans.
What to Expect From the iPhone 18 Launch
Apple has not officially detailed the products it will unveil ahead of the event. However, multiple reports suggest the spotlight will be on the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, along with Apple’s long-rumored first foldable iPhone, which could potentially be marketed as the iPhone Ultra.
One major change to Apple’s traditional launch strategy could be the absence of the regular iPhone 18. Reports indicate Apple may shift the standard iPhone 18 and other more affordable models to a spring 2027 launch, while September’s event focuses on its premium devices.
The iPhone 18 Pro lineup is rumored to feature Apple’s next-generation A20 Pro chipset, reportedly manufactured using a 2nm process. Other expected improvements include camera upgrades, a potentially smaller Dynamic Island, battery improvements, and changes to the Camera Control system.
Meanwhile, the rumored foldable iPhone could represent Apple’s most significant iPhone design change in years, introducing a book-style folding form factor designed to offer a larger display when opened.
Apple Watch Series 12 and More Could Also Arrive
The event is unlikely to be limited to iPhones. Apple is also expected to introduce the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, while new AirPods could also make an appearance.
Apple may additionally announce release dates for its next software updates, including iOS 27, iPadOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate.
Although Apple does not officially operate its own retail stores in Pakistan, new iPhones typically reach the local market through authorized and third-party channels following their international release.
For Pakistani buyers, the biggest questions will be the international starting prices, PTA taxes, local availability, and final retail prices once the new models begin arriving in the country.
Apple’s “Surprise and shine” event begins at 10:00 p.m. Pakistan time tonight, September 9, and viewers can watch the full launch through Apple’s official livestream above.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
B2B fleet management startup Carrum Mobility has raised $10 Mn (about ₹96 Cr) from ride-hailing major Uber as a part of its Series B funding round.
The fundraise marks the second tranche of Uber’s investment in Carrum, following the startup’s $7 Mn funding round in January 2026.
Carrum plans to use the fresh capital to expand across existing and new markets, strengthen its technology platform, scale operations, and grow its team. The funding will also support the expansion of its core mobility business and Uber Black services across India.
The startup said it has nearly doubled the scale of its business since the previous funding round.
Founded in 2024 by Karan Jain, Carrum operates a technology-led fleet management platform focused on CNG and electric vehicles. Jain previously founded self-drive car rental startup Revv, which was acquired by CarDekho Group.
Carrum currently operates a fleet of more than 5,000 vehicles across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, and Kolkata. It plans to launch operations in Chennai in September 2026.
The startup has also onboarded more than 18,000 driver partners across its network.
“Uber’s continued investment is a positive reflection of the business we’ve built and the opportunity ahead. As on date, we have nearly doubled the scale of our business since the last funding round while remaining consistently profitable,” Jain said.
Carrum claims to have remained profitable since its first month of operations. The startup said it is currently operating at an annualised revenue run rate of around ₹400 Cr.
CarDekho Group, which backed Carrum in 2024, is also an early equity investor in the startup. Its debt investors include Trifecta Capital, Girnar Capital, Shriram Finance, and Northern Arc.
For Uber, the partnership is expected to bring more premium vehicles onto its platform and support the expansion of Uber Black across Indian cities.

ARRI Technology Returns

Honor introduced ARRI-related imaging technology with its Robot Phone last month. The Magic 9 series will now build on that work, with Honor promising improvements for both photography and videography.
The company says the collaboration will bring a more cinematic look and feel to smartphone photography. However, it has not yet announced specific camera features or improvements.
Honor may reveal more information as it continues its launch campaign ahead of September 28.
More Details Expected Soon
The Magic 9 series has already attracted attention because of its camera design and ARRI collaboration. The official teaser also suggests that Honor is giving the lineup a distinctive new look.
While details such as the camera sensors, processor, display, battery, and pricing remain unconfirmed, the September 28 event should provide a complete picture of Honor’s next flagship smartphones.
With its focus on camera technology and cinematic imaging, the Magic 9 series appears to be a major flagship release for Honor. The company will reveal the full lineup and its key features when the launch event takes place in Beijing on September 28.
