items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has closed its antitrust probe into Google over its treatment of real money gaming (RMG) apps following the implementation of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.
The law prohibits online money games, their advertisements, and the facilitation of payments for such games.
The CCI said the legislation has made it impossible to grant the relief sought in the case, as directing Google to host or advertise RMG apps would be contrary to the law. It also clarified that closing the case did not amount to a finding on whether Google’s alleged conduct was anti-competitive.
What Was The Case About?
The case stemmed from a complaint by WinZO, which accused Google of abusing its dominant position by allowing Daily Fantasy Sports (DFS) and Rummy apps on the Play Store and Google Ads while excluding other RMG apps.
WinZO also challenged warnings displayed by Google Pay for payments made on its platform.
In November 2024, the CCI prima facie found Google dominant in three markets — licensable operating systems for smart mobile devices, app stores for Android devices, and online search advertising services in India.
The regulator said Google’s decision to allow only DFS and Rummy apps could create a “two-tier market” and put other RMG developers at a disadvantage. It subsequently directed its director general to investigate the allegations.
During the proceedings, Google proposed allowing legally permissible skill-based RMG apps on Google Play and Google Ads, subject to certification.
However, the legal framework changed after the Online Gaming Act came into force on May 1, 2026. The law banned online money games, their advertisements, and related payments without distinguishing between games of skill and games of chance.
Although the law is under challenge before the Supreme Court, the CCI said no stay on its operation is in place. It therefore held that there is no longer a lawful RMG market on Google’s platforms where some apps could be allowed while others were excluded.
The CCI also said the payment-warning issue could no longer be addressed, as the law prohibits facilitating payments for online money games.
Google discontinued its RMG pilot programme and stopped accepting RMG advertisements in January 2026, before the law came into force on May 1. It subsequently sought to submit a fresh commitment to formally close the pilot and prohibit such advertisements.
However, the CCI rejected the request, saying the proposed measures were now statutory requirements rather than voluntary remedies addressing competition concerns.
“Accepting such an offer may amount to treating mandatory statutory compliance as a negotiated competition remedy,” the regulator said.
WinZO sought to withdraw its complaint during a hearing on August 25, citing the change in law. However, the CCI said competition proceedings are conducted in the wider public interest and an informant cannot unilaterally determine whether a case should be closed.
Taking into account the change in law, the absence of an effective remedy, Google’s discontinuation of its RMG pilot and advertisements, and WinZO’s withdrawal request, the CCI concluded that continuing the investigation was unnecessary.
It recalled its November 28, 2024 order directing the investigation and closed the matter.
The regulator reserved the right to reconsider the allegations if the relevant provisions of the Online Gaming Act are stayed, struck down, repealed, or otherwise cease to operate. It said the decision is limited to the exceptional circumstances of the case.

items.title: Qualcomm Signs $60 Billion AI Chip Deal With Amazon – Why This Partnership Matters?
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Qualcomm is making a major push into the artificial intelligence market, and Amazon is becoming an important part of that strategy. The two companies have entered a long-term partnership that could see Amazon purchase up to $60 billion worth of Qualcomm AI data center chips and related products.
The deal is significant because Qualcomm is trying to build a much bigger business outside smartphones. The company has been known mainly for its mobile processors and connectivity technology, but it now wants a stronger position in the fast-growing AI infrastructure market.
Under the agreement, Qualcomm will develop custom chips for Amazon that are designed for AI inference. Inference is the process of running already-trained AI models to generate results. As more companies deploy AI services, the demand for hardware capable of handling these workloads is growing rapidly.
Qualcomm Signs $60 Billion AI Chip Deal With Amazon – Why
items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Qualcomm is making a major push into the artificial intelligence market, and Amazon is becoming an important part of that strategy. The two companies have entered a long-term partnership that could see Amazon purchase up to $60 billion worth of Qualcomm AI data center chips and related products.
The deal is significant because Qualcomm is trying to build a much bigger business outside smartphones. The company has been known mainly for its mobile processors and connectivity technology, but it now wants a stronger position in the fast-growing AI infrastructure market.
Under the agreement, Qualcomm will develop custom chips for Amazon that are designed for AI inference. Inference is the process of running already-trained AI models to generate results. As more companies deploy AI services, the demand for hardware capable of handling these workloads is growing rapidly.
Qualcomm Signs $60 Billion AI Chip Deal With Amazon – Why This Partnership Matters?
Amazon is one of the world’s largest cloud companies, and Amazon Web Services is investing heavily in AI infrastructure. Its custom chip business has also become an important growth area, with an annualized revenue run rate of more than $25 billion at the end of the June quarter.
For Qualcomm, working with Amazon provides an opportunity to become part of this expanding infrastructure. It also gives the company a major customer as it tries to compete in a market currently dominated by Nvidia.
Amazon is not the only major technology company Qualcomm is working with. Microsoft and Meta are also supporting Qualcomm’s efforts to expand into data center chips. Qualcomm expects its data center chip business to generate $15 billion in revenue by 2029.
The $4 Billion Stock Connection
The partnership also includes an unusual financial element. Qualcomm has granted Amazon warrants worth about $4 billion. The warrants will vest as Amazon purchases Qualcomm’s products and give Amazon the right to buy Qualcomm shares at $161.26 per share.
This structure connects Amazon’s future purchases directly with its potential ownership of Qualcomm stock. It also shows how closely technology companies are tying financing and long-term AI infrastructure partnerships together.
It’s Not Just About AI Chips
The deal goes beyond computing hardware. Qualcomm will also work with Amazon on optical communications technology for AI data centers.
The companies plan to develop high-speed optical connectivity solutions capable of supporting speeds of up to 1.6 terabits per second. This technology is aimed at handling the huge amounts of data that need to move between systems inside modern AI data centers.
That part of the agreement is important for Qualcomm because optical communications is a relatively new area for the company. Qualcomm entered the field more seriously after acquiring AlphaWave for $2.4 billion last year. AlphaWave CEO Tony Pialis later became Qualcomm’s data center chip chief.
By combining AI computing chips with optical connectivity, Qualcomm is positioning itself as a broader supplier of AI infrastructure rather than simply a chipmaker.
Qualcomm Also Gets AWS Support
The partnership will work in both directions. Qualcomm plans to expand its use of Amazon Web Services and its infrastructure for chip design workloads.
Using AWS services could help Qualcomm speed up parts of the chip development process and shorten development cycles. That could become increasingly important as semiconductor companies race to develop new AI hardware.
A Way Beyond Smartphones
The Amazon partnership comes at an important time for Qualcomm. The company faces an expected decline in revenue from its modem business with Apple as Apple continues moving toward developing more components internally. Qualcomm is also dealing with weaker smartphone demand and rising component costs.
That makes diversification especially important.
The Amazon agreement gives Qualcomm a major opportunity to build a new source of growth. It also shows that the company is serious about competing in AI infrastructure, where Nvidia currently has a dominant position.
For Amazon, the deal provides another source of custom AI hardware as it expands its cloud and AI operations. For Qualcomm, it could be one of the most important partnerships in its transition from a smartphone-focused chip company into a broader AI infrastructure supplier.
In short, the Qualcomm-Amazon deal is about much more than a chip order. It combines AI computing, optical connectivity, cloud infrastructure and a major financial commitment. If Qualcomm can deliver on its plans, the partnership could play a key role in determining how successfully the company moves into the next generation of AI data centers.

items.summary:

items.author: Ankush Das
items.content:
AI is all set to take centre stage at the Global Fintech Fest (GFF) in Mumbai this week, with product launches, live demos and industry conversations on how this emerging tech is reshaping financial services. But beyond the buzz, the bigger story is how deeply AI-powered systems are entering the Indian fintech stack, from customer onboarding and credit decisions to fraud detection, servicing and payments.
To understand where the industry stands and where it is headed, Inc42 spoke with senior executives from Zeta, HyperVerge, TruCommerce and RevRag AI, who are participating in the seventh edition of GFF.
The experts believe Indian fintechs have moved beyond the proof-of-concept phase: voice agents are handling customer interactions, AI is accelerating KYC and verification, fraud systems are becoming more sophisticated, and in-app assistants are beginning to execute tasks rather than simply answer questions. The next challenge is figuring out where these applications can deliver measurable value, and how far fintechs can take them without compromising trust, compliance and accountability.
So, where is AI delivering the most immediate value for fintechs today? Let’s unravel in this edition of The AI Shift…
Fintech’s First AI Moves Are Now Operational
Fintech companies are using AI to make existing processes faster and more efficient rather than letting it make financial decisions on its own. Kedar Parikh, the CPO of HyperVerge, an AI-powered identity verification and KYC platform, divides the sector’s adoption of AI into three broad phases.
Digital onboarding: This includes KYC, face matching and liveness checks. Customers across banking, financial services, insurance and telecom can now be onboarded in minutes instead of days
Fraud prevention: Faster onboarding also creates more opportunities for fake documents, synthetic identities and deepfakes to enter the financial system. This is pushing regulated entities to adopt AI for document forgery detection, biometric checks and deepfake prevention, although adoption remains a work in progress.
AI-assisted decision-making: This phase is still at an early stage. AI can collect data, spot patterns and present useful inferences, but lending, insurance and other high-value decisions continue to require human judgement.
This pattern is visible in customer service as well. According to Sivaram Kowta, the president of digital banking at Zeta India, a digital banking and card-issuing technology company, customer support, fraud management and underwriting are among the most active areas for AI adoption. Zeta’s AI agent resolves around 80% of customer-service calls for US-based subprime credit-card fintech Sparrow, Kowta said.
Ashutosh Prakash Singh, the cofounder and CEO of RevRag AI, an AI voice and chat agent startup focused on banking and financial services, said fintechs have moved from testing voice AI and in-app agents to scaling them and measuring their return on investment.
Singh said the next wave of deployment will go beyond contact centres, with fintechs, banks and non-banks such as PhonePe and Bajaj Financial Services exploring AI across in-app journeys, back-end workflows, branches, kiosks and other customer touchpoints. He expects these use cases to move from early deployments to broader scale across the BFSI sector by the end of this year and into next year.
AI As A Paper Pusher
The closer AI gets to a financial decision, the more difficult deployment becomes. In lending, for example, an AI system can collect customers’ financial history, classify information and apply existing rules but cannot become the final authority to approve a loan.
Kowta said the RBI has made it clear that regulated entities cannot shift responsibility for credit decisions to an AI model. A bank must understand the decision and remain accountable for it. As a result, banks and NBFCs are using AI in underwriting while retaining a human at the final decision point.
“AI is not doing something fundamentally new. It is a paper pusher, just an extremely capable or efficient paper pusher,” Kowta said.
If every other step in the lending process is automated but the final credit review remains manual, the overall process may become faster, but it does not become fully autonomous.
The compliance challenge is more complex. These constraints are not stopping adoption, but shaping the ecosystem. Currently, the main regulatory and compliance issues faced by Indian fintechs include:
The DPDP compliance: AI systems must account for consent, data use and the right to erase personal information under the Digital Personal Data Protection framework.
Data localisation: Banks and fintechs need clarity on whether financial information sent to overseas AI models remains in India.
User-level authentication: Agents need permissions linked to the authenticated customer, not broad access to an institution’s systems.
Payment authorisation: Agent-initiated payments in India require additional safeguards, including OTP-based authentication in several use cases.
Human accountability: Regulated entities remain responsible for lending, underwriting and other critical decisions, even when AI performs the supporting work.
According to Viren Inaniyan, cofounder and CEO of TruCommerce, a commerce infrastructure platform for AI agents, basic building blocks for agent-led commerce are already falling into place. These include AI platforms, commerce protocols, payment networks, gateways, merchant catalogues and checkout systems.
India’s payment ecosystem also has safeguards in place to make transactions more secure. For instance, card details need to be encrypted and cannot be exposed to or stored by an AI agent.
However, the bigger challenge is that very few people are using AI agents to make payments today. Agentic commerce accounts for an estimated 100 Mn transactions, or just 0.04% of UPI’s total transaction volume. This dataset is still too small for payment companies and merchants to understand how consumers behave when an AI agent is making purchases on their behalf.
The Shift From Features To Foundations
The conversations ahead of GFF point to a fintech ecosystem that is increasingly focused on scale, but not yet equally prepared for the cost of scaling. Kowta said less than 10% of bank budgets currently go towards AI, with spending often taking place project by project.
However, he expects the approach to change over the next one year. Smaller banks may slow down their AI plans, while larger banks could commit significantly bigger budgets, potentially investing ₹500 Cr to ₹1,000 Cr at one time to build shared infrastructure, governance and AI capabilities rather than funding disconnected projects.
For now, much of the industry is still in an AI computerisation phase. It is using the tech to perform existing tasks faster. The bigger change will come when banks redesign workflows around AI instead of adding an AI assistant to an old process.
The message from the ecosystem is not that AI adoption is slow. It is moving quickly in customer service, onboarding and fraud prevention. But the next jump, allowing AI to influence decisions involving money, will depend on whether Indian fintechs can build the compliance and accountability layers that make those systems trustworthy.
Top Stories From India & Around The World
KRAFTON To Invest $250 Mn In Indian Startups: The South Korean gaming giant is committing an additional $250 Mn (₹3,300 Cr) to Indian startups across AI, robotics and deeptech over the next three to four years, taking its total planned India investment to over $1 Bn. Chairman Byung Gyu Chang announced the plan after a meeting with PM Narendra Modi.
Navana.ai Raises ₹40 Cr: The Mumbai-based voice AI startup has raised ₹40 Cr ($4.2 Mn) in a Series A round led by existing investor and upGrad cofounder Ronnie Screwvala, with Antler India, Neysa.ai founder Sharad Sanghi and WestBridge’s Sandeep Singhal also participating. The company will deploy the capital to deepen its Indic-language speech models and AI contact centre.
OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Astra: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, with a 1 Mn-token context and a headline API price of $10-$50 per Mn tokens. Because it is the first OpenAI model rated critical on cybersecurity, the cyber-sensitive capabilities are gated behind a trusted-access programme, and it is rolling out to enterprise customers first before wider ChatGPT availability.
Nvidia’s PAIR Turns Idle PCs Into Personal AI Data Centres: Announced at IFA 2026, Nvidia’s free, open-source Personal AI Router (PAIR) pools idle laptops, desktops and Macs on a home network to run local AI models for agentic workloads, using existing Ollama or LM Studio installs. The tool routes agent subtask requests to whichever machine is free, letting developers run multi-agent setups locally without cloud fees or privacy trade-offs.
The Weekly Buzz: An Alien Mind
OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a striking essay titled “An Alien Mind,” warning that increasingly capable systems may develop goals misaligned with human values. He argues that no lab has solved alignment and monitoring well enough to continue scaling at maximum speed for much longer.
Pachocki calls for voluntary slowdowns, stronger third-party auditing, and international coordination, describing advanced AI as something that has ‘grown more than designed’.
The essay has intensified debate inside and outside the lab. Supporters see it as a rare moment of candour from a frontier institution; critics note the tension between the warning and OpenAI’s continued rapid deployment.
The contrast with Jensen Huang’s simultaneous “AGI has arrived” statement has only sharpened the discussion. Coming amid a week of cascading model releases, the essay reframes the central question of 2026: not only how capable the systems are becoming, but whether the institutions building them are prepared for the consequences of their own progress.
Startup In The Spotlight: Antimattr
Founded in 2025 by Sridipto Ghosh and Sirsho Chakraborty, Bengaluru-based Antimattr is building a voice-first computing system designed around memory and productivity. AI assistants are growing increasingly capable, but using them in the real world still means pulling out a phone or sitting in front of a screen.
The problem surfaced while the founders were building voice agents: the AI worked, but noisy environments such as cafés, airports and open offices made voice interactions unreliable.
Instead of putting a screen between the user and the machine, Antimattr pitches voice as the primary interface to AI. Its Project Mnemosyne combines a smart ring with a pair of voice-isolation earphones: the ring captures thoughts, records and summarises conversations and controls AI agents, while the earphones use six microphones and proprietary voice-isolation technology to enable clearer conversations and dictation even in noise.
The startup counts Y Combinator, Nikhil Kamath’s WTFund and gener8tor among its backers, with YC investing $500K.
Antimattr operates in India’s AI wearable market, projected to reach $19.1 Bn by 2033. As the company bets on a screenless AI future, its longer-term roadmap extends beyond Mnemosyne to a privacy-focused AI computer and, eventually, an AI-native vehicle.
Prompt Of The Week
What prompts and hacks are CTOs, CEOs and cofounders using these days to streamline their work?
Here’s the prompt Ram Khizamboor, COO at Indium, uses to run a pre-mortem on a client engagement, essentially forcing the AI to imagine failure:
“Assume it’s twelve months from now and this client engagement has failed. The contract wasn’t renewed, the relationship soured, and leadership is asking hard questions about what went wrong.
Write the post-mortem for it, answering these three questions in detail:
What were the three most likely causes of the failure
Which early signals did we ignore in the first 90 days of the engagement
What would the client’s CIO say, in hindsight, we should have seen coming
Be specific and unsparing. Don’t hedge or soften the findings just because this is a hypothetical exercise. Treat it the way a real post-mortem would be treated internally, with names, timelines, and decisions called out where relevant.“
Editor’s Note: Some prompts may need to be adjusted by users for best results or may not work as intended for certain users.
[Edited by Shishir Parasher]
[Creatives by Varshita Srivastava]

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan has spent two years and roughly $8 million building the foundation of a national digital public infrastructure system. The World Bank’s latest review shows that foundation is real, but almost nobody is using what’s been built on top of it yet. The Bank has flagged slow financial disbursement and a series of implementation gaps in the Digital Economy Enhancement Project (DEEP), a $69.16 million initiative meant to give the government the capacity to deliver digitally enabled public services to citizens and businesses. Just $8.36 million, or 12.09 percent, has been disbursed so far, leaving $60.80 million unspent more than two years after the project became effective in May 2024. It was approved in March 2024 and is scheduled to close in July 2028.
A Mixed Verdict, Not a Failing One
Despite the slow spending, the World Bank hasn’t downgraded DEEP into failure territory. It rated overall progress toward the project’s development objective and overall implementation progress as “Moderately Satisfactory”, with the project’s overall risk rating held at “Moderate”. That’s a project the Bank considers salvageable and partially working, not one it’s flagging for a fundamental rethink, at least not yet.
The project runs across four components: improving digital economy, governance, and service delivery capabilities, the largest piece at an estimated $58 million; development of the Pakistan Business Portal, at $15 million; and project management, at $5 million.
What’s Actually Been Built
Some of the underlying infrastructure has genuinely come together. NADRA has issued 2.3 million Digital IDs, and 6.5 million transactions have already been processed through the National Data Exchange Layer, the backbone system meant to let different government databases talk to each other securely. The PakID Vault, the digital credential-storage system, now supports 11 types of verifiable credentials. On the policy side, the Enterprise Architecture Framework has been completed, and the Data Governance Policy has been disclosed for public consultation, both foundational documents the rest of the system depends on.
Where the Numbers Get Harder to Defend
The gap between what’s been built and what’s actually being used is where this review turns pointed. Transactions through the National Data Exchange Layer stood at 650,000 in August 2026, against a closing-period target of 13.333 million, meaning current usage sits at under 5 percent of where the project needs to land by the time it closes. Only six entities have been integrated with the national data exchanger, against a target of 40 by November 2027, and private-sector integration is barely underway at all, with just one private-sector entity connected against a target of 13.
The credential vault tells a similar story on a smaller scale: 11 verifiable credentials are currently storable against a target of 40. The national citizen services portal is actually ahead on one metric, offering 18 services against a target of 20, one of the only areas where the project is close to its goal. The Pakistan Business Portal, by contrast, has processed zero Registration, Licenses, Certificates and Other (RLCO) transactions so far, against a target of 4,000 annual transactions by November 2027, and both B2G payments and RLCO services completed online remain at zero against a target of 50 percent.
The gender gap is arguably the most striking figure in the entire review. Women accounted for just 9.2 percent of users of digitally enabled services, against a closing-period target of 30 percent, a shortfall of more than two-thirds. Data on youth users wasn’t even available for the report, meaning the project can’t currently demonstrate progress on that front either way.
What the World Bank Wants Done Next
The Bank’s prescription is specific rather than general. It wants MoITT, operating under the institutional framework created by the Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025, to prepare a time-bound service prioritization and onboarding strategy in coordination with the newly formed Pakistan Digital Authority and both federal and provincial governments, covering concrete targets at six months, one year, and two years out. It also wants the Enterprise Architecture Framework published alongside a formal adoption roadmap, the Data Governance Policy and Interoperability Framework formally adopted and operationalized rather than left in consultation, and the completion of the feasibility study for the National Fiberization Plan, a requirement that’s been outstanding since the project’s early stages.
Why It Matters
DEEP isn’t an isolated initiative sitting quietly inside one ministry. It’s meant to serve as the federal backbone underneath Pakistan’s broader digital transformation agenda, including provincial programs like the $70 million Connected Punjab Programme, which was explicitly built to plug into DEEP’s national platforms and policies rather than duplicate them. When the foundational layer is running at under 5 percent of its usage target with two years still on the clock, every program depending on that foundation inherits the same uncertainty.
The infrastructure numbers, 2.3 million Digital IDs issued, 6.5 million transactions processed, and an Enterprise Architecture Framework completed, are not nothing. They represent real technical groundwork that a country doesn’t get to skip. But infrastructure that isn’t being adopted doesn’t deliver the outcome the project was funded for, and a Pakistan Business Portal that has processed zero transactions against a 4,000-transaction target is difficult to read as anything other than a system that exists on paper more than in practice. The 9.2 percent women’s participation rate, in particular, is the kind of gap that tends to widen rather than close on its own without a deliberate intervention, since digital access barriers by gender in Pakistan are well documented and don’t resolve simply because a service becomes technically available.
With roughly two years left before the July 2028 closing date, DEEP’s remaining runway isn’t short, but the World Bank’s own targets suggest the gap between what’s built and what’s actually used has to close far faster than it has so far. The project’s next review will show whether MoITT’s response to this one was a turning point or another entry in the same pattern: strong infrastructure, weak adoption, and targets that keep slipping further out of reach as the clock runs down.

According to an income tax circular issued by the FBR, a new Section 154B has been inserted into the tax framework. The provision requires banks and non-banking financial institutions to deduct tax when payments linked to social media revenues are credited to or received in an individual’s account.
The deduction will apply at the rate specified in Division IIIAB of Part III of the First Schedule, which has been fixed at 5%.

The measure applies to revenues received from social media platforms by individuals falling within the definitions of digital content creator or social media influencer.
The FBR has also formally defined the term “payment” for the purpose of the new section, making the deduction mechanism applicable at the point where such income reaches a recipient through a financial institution.
For resident taxpayers, the 5% deduction will be treated as minimum tax.
For non-resident individuals without a permanent establishment in Pakistan, the same deduction will be treated as a final tax.
The FBR has also made a consequential amendment to Section 169 to align the tax treatment with the new withholding provision.
The move marks a significant expansion of Pakistan’s tax net into the digital creator economy, as authorities seek to capture income generated through platforms such as video-sharing, social networking, and other online content services.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Islamabad Police just added 50 electric vehicles to its fleet, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was there in person to hand over the keys.
The vehicles were delivered as part of a push toward modern, safe, and environmentally friendly policing in the federal capital, with the prime minister handing the keys to Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Islamabad Inspector General of Police Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi at a ceremony this week.
A New Force, Built Around These Vehicles
The 50 EVs aren’t a general fleet upgrade; they’re purpose-built for the Capital Patrol force, a newly established 200-officer unit designed around Islamabad’s stated vision of becoming a “safe, smart, and green” capital. IGP Rizvi briefed the prime minister on how the force is structured: each patrol unit pairs one male and one female officer, and motorcycle-riding personnel will operate alongside the EVs to ensure faster response times and more effective coverage across different parts of the city. Every officer assigned to Capital Patrol will also be equipped with a body camera, a move officials framed as strengthening transparency, oversight, and accountability in day-to-day policing.
Why Electric, and Why Now?
Officials were specific about the financial case, not just the environmental one. The 50 EVs run entirely on electricity, and authorities project the switch will save roughly Rs 34 million a month in fuel costs, with each vehicle’s purchase cost recovered through those fuel savings in approximately 10.5 months. That payback framing suggests this was pitched and approved as much on operating economics as on emissions, a detail that matters for whether the program expands further.
This also isn’t Islamabad Police’s first move into electric vehicles. The rollout builds on an earlier, smaller batch of EVs introduced under the same “Capital Patrols Electric Vehicles” and “Go Green” push, with this delivery marking an expansion of that existing green fleet rather than a first-time pilot. The vehicles are supplied by BYD, the Chinese automaker that has been expanding its footprint in Pakistan through both direct dealerships and a local assembly partnership, and this deal adds a high-visibility government fleet contract to that expansion.
Why It Matters
A police EV fleet is a small line item against Pakistan’s broader energy and infrastructure challenges, but it’s a useful test case for whether electric vehicles work operationally in a demanding, always-on government use case, running patrols around the clock rather than sitting in a private garage overnight. If the projected fuel savings and 10.5-month payback period hold up in practice, it gives other provincial police forces and public-sector fleets a concrete, numbers-backed template to point to rather than an environmental talking point alone.
It also lands at a moment when Pakistan’s broader EV push, from BYD’s local assembly plans to federal EV policy targets, has been more aspiration than delivered infrastructure. A functioning, visible fleet of 50 electric police vehicles patrolling the capital daily does more to normalize EVs in the public imagination than a policy document ever could, and Shehbaz Sharif’s explicit framing of Islamabad Police as a “role model for other cities” signals the government wants this replicated elsewhere, not treated as a one-off capital-city showcase. Whether that happens will depend less on the ceremony and more on whether the fuel-saving numbers being cited today actually materialize once these vehicles are a year into daily patrol duty.

The Cost Of India’s Convenience Economy
Fuelled by massive capital and discounting wars, India’s instant service platforms are preparing for a mega festive season. But the gig workers are facing rigid targets and uncertain earnings.
The Invisible Cost: For an instant help worker, a booking is only one part of their shift. The rest can involve waiting near high-demand communities, staying logged in to remain eligible for assignments and finding an affordable way to reach the next home. While the platforms depend on this proximity to promise quick service, workers claim that the time spent being idle often produces no income.
Pay Promise Evolves: The instant help platforms initially marketed domestic work as a route to assured earnings. But gig workers now claim that compensation is increasingly linked to logged-in hours and tier-based performance. The issue is not merely linked to pay. Missed shifts, emergencies and a lack of bookings can make take-home income far less certain.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
The Cost Of India’s Convenience Economy
Fuelled by massive capital and discounting wars, India’s instant service platforms are preparing for a mega festive season. But the gig workers are facing rigid targets and uncertain earnings.
The Invisible Cost: For an instant help worker, a booking is only one part of their shift. The rest can involve waiting near high-demand communities, staying logged in to remain eligible for assignments and finding an affordable way to reach the next home. While the platforms depend on this proximity to promise quick service, workers claim that the time spent being idle often produces no income.
Pay Promise Evolves: The instant help platforms initially marketed domestic work as a route to assured earnings. But gig workers now claim that compensation is increasingly linked to logged-in hours and tier-based performance. The issue is not merely linked to pay. Missed shifts, emergencies and a lack of bookings can make take-home income far less certain.
Algorithmic Control: Ratings, availability and allocation systems also shape who gets the next booking. This pressures workers to accept jobs to avoid account suspensions or reduced payouts. Furthermore, workers also claim limited access to toilets, shaded waiting areas and secure resting places near customer clusters.
Safety Question: For women workers, rapid order allocation can mean accepting jobs in unfamiliar locations with little room to assess safety concerns. With ratings, incentives and account access tied to responsiveness, declining a booking may carry a cost. There is also a complete absence of welfare benefits like paid period leave or emergency medical support.
The Litmus Test: This festive season will test whether instant help platforms can build a business that values the workforce as much as customer convenience. Discounts may bring bookings, but retention will depend on fair pay and safety support. But as demand accelerates, will these platforms invest enough in the workers who make convenience possible? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Shiprocket’s Second Act
Shiprocket put up a healthy show in Q1 FY27. It managed to trim its losses while clocking a healthy jump in revenues. While the core shipping arm continued to scale, what stood out in its financials was the accelerating contribution of its newer commerce products.
Shiprocket’s emerging business grew 70% YoY to ₹180.4 Cr and improved its EBITDA margin during the quarter. This signals that the startup is betting its next growth story on monetising the merchant journey before, during and after every delivery.
The startup’s playbook is centred around monetising aggregated data to power its martech stack and extracting more value from its 2.2 Lakh merchant base. However, its next test will be scaling adoption and achieving profitability.
Global Fintech Fest Kicks Off
Prime Minister Narendra Modi yesterday kicked off the annual fintech extravaganza in Mumbai. In his speech, PM Modi called on fintech startups to strengthen cybersecurity and consumer protection amid the rise of agentic AI and quantum technologies.
Addressing the forum, the PM also outlined four broad priorities for the sector, namely stronger cybersecurity, ethical data protection, better consumer protection and closer collaboration between industry and regulators.
The Global Fintech Festival, which begins today, is expected to draw 1 Lakh visitors. The event will also see participation from over 5,000 companies, 700+ speakers, hundreds of investors and representation from 70+ countries.
RentoMojo’s ₹376 Cr Anchor Round
The furniture and appliance rental platform has raised nearly ₹376.1 Cr from anchor investors. The startup said that it allotted 93.1 Lakh equity shares to 41 anchor investors at ₹404 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band.
Sixteen domestic mutual funds lapped up 60.4 Lakh shares worth nearly ₹244.1 Cr via a total of 30 schemes. The round also saw participation from Edelweiss, Invesco, HDFC, Motlal Oswal, Bajaj Finserv and others.
RentoMojo’s public issue comprises a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹150 Cr and an offer for sale of up to 2.7 Cr shares. It has also set a price band of ₹384-₹404 apiece for its IPO, which values the startup at nearly ₹4,206 Cr at the upper end of the spectrum.
Bajaj Finance’s Latest AI Bet
The NBFC arm of Bajaj Finserv has acquired a 5% stake in the AI video generation platform for an undisclosed amount. The deal will enable Bajaj Finance to deploy TrueFan’s AI-led automation and personalisation tools across its ecosystem.
Founded in 2020, TrueFan initially operated a celebrity engagement platform before pivoting to AI in 2024. It now helps companies create personalised videos using celebrities and AI avatars. It caters to 100 enterprises and has raised $15 to date.
The investment is part of Bajaj Finserv’s broader strategy to ramp up presence in the AI space. In March, the company announced plans to invest up to ₹2,000 Cr over five years in early-stage startups across AI, cybersecurity, quantum technologies and fintech.
Circle To Acquire Tazapay
The US-based crypto platform has signed a deal to acquire the Singapore-based B2B cross-border payments startup. The transaction is said to be an all-stock deal valued at nearly $400 Mn.
The deal is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. With this, Circle will leverage Tazapay’s banking relationships, local payout rails and customer base to accelerate the adoption of its stablecoin product.
Founded in 2020, Tazapay offers B2B cross-border payment solutions for enterprises. It currently claims to clock $25 Bn in annualised payment volume, boasts 60+ banking partners and has built local payout rails in over 100 markets.
New CEO At Whatfix
Cofounder Vara Kumar Namburu has been appointed as the new chief executive of the SaaS unicorn, a week after the unfortunate demise of cofounder and CEO Khadim Batti.
An alumnus of Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Namburu cofounded Whatfix in 2013, and has been helming the research and development wing of the SaaS company.
Whatfix offers an AI-powered digital adoption platform that helps enterprises improve software adoption and get more value from their technology investments. It claims to cater to more than 650 enterprises globally and has raised over $260 Mn till date.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Inside Wippi’s Screen-Free AI Play for Kids
More and more children remain glued to their screens. But there are limited options that blend entertainment and learning without ads or visual overload. Wippi is betting that its screen-free AI companion can keep children curious through stories, music and games.
Wippi’s Interactive Play: Founded in 2024, Wippi builds voice-first products for children aged between four and ten. Its Wippi Player combines proprietary hardware, conversational AI and an audio-content library, allowing children to ask questions, interact with characters and navigate stories without looking at a screen.
For parents, Wippi offers a companion app to create profiles, set up the device and review listening patterns and AI interactions in more than 140 languages.
A Content Universe: The Wippi Player’s starter kit costs ₹6,499 and includes the device plus a playset. Additional physical character cards, illustrated storybooks, Wippi Radio and themed playsets create repeat-purchase opportunities, creating a business model beyond a one-time hardware sale.
The Next Chapter: Backed by 12 Flags, the startup now plans to strengthen voice-AI and engineering teams, broaden original content and characters, scale manufacturing in India and expand its D2C business. As it taps into AI and locally relevant storytelling, can Wippi turn a screen-free childhood into a scalable consumer tech category?

items.content:
Babak Knockout Stage FFWS SEA 2026 Fall telah selesai dengan empat tim esports Indonesia memastikan slot di babak Grand Finals. RRQ Kazu dan MBR Omega menjadi dua wakil terakhir yang lolos, menyusul Bigetron by Vitality dan Onic yang lebih dulu mengamankan tiket.
Rencananya, keempat tim dijadwalkan akan bertanding di Grand Finals FFWS SEA 2026 Fall berlangsung pada 19-29 September 2026 di Tunjungan Plaza Conventional Hall, Surabaya.
RRQ Kazu dan MBR Omega Lengkapi Wakil Indonesia
RRQ Kazu menutup fase terakhir Knockout Stage di posisi kelima dengan total 234 poin, di mana mereka sukses mengoleksi dua Booyah, 123 poin eliminasi, dan 111 poin placement.
Sepanjang tiga hari pertandingan pekan keempat, tim Free Fire ini mendapatkan 79 poin pada hari pertama, 85 poin di hari kedua, dan 70 poin saat terakhir. Dengan hasil tersebut, maka posisi mereka tetap berada di enam besar klasemen dan mengamankan tiket Grand Finals.
MBR Omega menyusul tepat di bawah RRQ dengan 231 poin. Jumlah tersebut terdiri dari dua Booyah, 123 poin eliminasi, dan 108 poin placement.
Perjalanan MBR justru ditentukan oleh performa di hari terakhir. Setelah meraih 68 dan 59 pin dalam dua hari pertama, MBR mengumupulkan 104 poin pada hari ketiga, termasuk dua Booyah.
Dengan hasil ini, empat wakil Indonesia akan bermain di Surabaya adalah: 
Bigetron by Vitality
ONIC
RRQ Kazu
MBR Omega
FFWS SEA 2026 Fall: Evos Divine Gagal ke Grand Finals
Di saat empat tim Indonesia melanjutkan perjalanan, Evos Divine harus berhenti di Knockout Stage. Tim esports ini finis di posisi ke-12 dengan 147 poin, terdiri dari 91 poin eliminasi dan 56 poin placement tanpa memperoleh Booyah.
Hasil ini cukup kontras mengingat Evos Divine merupakan juara Esports World Cup: Free Fire 2025. Garena menyebut tim tersebut harus kembali berjuang melalui kompetisi nasional pada musim berikutnya untuk mendapatkan kesempatan kembali ke level regional. 
Daftar Tim Grand Finals FFWS SEA 2026 Fall Berubah
Ada perkembangan lain setelah Knockout Stage selesai. Daftar awal yang disampaikan Garena masih mencantumkan Team Akkee dari Thailand sebagai peserta Grand Finals.
Free Fire Esports Global mengumumkan diskualifikasi Team Akkee pada 7 September 2026 karena persoalan administratif terkait dokumen perjalanan dan pengurusan visa. Secret WAG dari Vietnam, yang berada di peringkat ketujuh fase Last Chance, disebut mendapatkan slot pengganti.
Dengan perubahan tersebut, susunan Grand Finals menjadi empat tim dari Indonesia, empat Thailand, dan empat Vietnam.
Indonesia
Bigetron by Vitality
ONIC
RRQ Kazu
MBR Omega
Thailand
AG.AL
Buriram United Esports
Team Falcons
Twisted Minds
Vietnam
Team Flash
P Esports
GOW Esports
Secret WAG
Secret WAG sendiri bukan nama baru di persaingan regional. Tim asal Vietnam tersebut merupakan juara FFWS SEA 2026 Spring.
Grand Finals FFWS SEA 2026 Fall Digelar di Surabaya
Grand Finals FFWS SEA 2026 Fall akan berlangsung selama dua hari pada 19–20 September 2026 di Tunjungan Plaza Convention Hall, Surabaya. Kota tersebut sebelumnya juga menjadi tuan rumah FFWS SEA 2024 Fall.
Hari pertama akan mempertandingkan format Point Rush, sebelum kompetisi berlanjut ke penentuan juara menggunakan format Champion Rush pada hari kedua. Garena juga telah mengonfirmasi Surabaya sebagai lokasi Grand Finals sejak jadwal kompetisi diumumkan pada Agustus.
Dalam rilis yang diterima Gizmologi, tiket penonton dicantumkan dalam dua kategori. Tier A dibanderol Rp 50.000 dengan enam merchandise, sedangkan Tier B Rp 20.000 dengan lima merchandise. Penjualan dilakukan melalui Loket.com, dengan ketersediaan tiket mengikuti kondisi saat pemesanan.
Empat wakil Indonesia kini akan bertanding di hadapan publik sendiri untuk memperebutkan gelar FFWS SEA 2026 Fall. RRQ Kazu, MBR Omega, Bigetron by Vitality, dan ONIC memiliki waktu kurang dari dua pekan untuk mempersiapkan Grand Finals di Surabaya.
Intip Bocoran Patch Flame Arena di Free Fire
Garena umumkan hadirkan patch Flame Arena di Free Fire, jelang akan dimulainya kompetisi Free Fire World Series Global Finals (FFWS GF) Jakarta 2025. Patch update terbaru ini memberikan sesuatu yang baru untuk para pemain bermain dengan lebih seru.
FFWS GF 2025 Jakarta 2025 akan dimulai pada 31 Oktober mendatang, sementara patch Flame Arena akan hadir mulai 29 Oktober. Sebanyak 18 tim akan bertanding dalam gelaran kompetisi FFWS GF 2025 Jakarta dan kompetisi ini berhadiah total USD 1,150,000 atau sekitar Rp19 miliar.
Pada pembaruan kali ini, seluruh pemain akan merasakan sensasi kompetisi tingkat dunia dengan hadirnya berbagai hal menarik. Mulai dari sistem loadout baru, Flame Trophy & Flame Zone, hingga komentator yang membuat pertempuran semakin sengit.
Pada patch kali ini, Free Fire mengganti delapan loadout lama menjadi empat loadout baru yang terdiri dari Team Booster, Enhance Hammer, Tactical Market, dan Super Leg Pockets. Perubahan ini akan membuka strategi baru untuk memenangkan pertandingan baik di Battle Royale (BR) atau Clash Squad (CS).

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Evelyn Usman
One of the five persons who sustained bullet wounds during last week’s attack on Girkau community in Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State by suspected bandits is lying helpless at the Usman Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH), unable to afford the N190,000 required for a
Magnetic Resonance Imaging ,MRI and Computed Tomography CT scan , prescribed by doctors.
The victim, 30-year-old Jamilu Abubakar, was shot in the back by suspected bandits while returning from his farmland, where he had gone to harvest millet.
Abubakar, who spoke in an inaudible tone with the aid of an interpreter from his hospital bed, said he had lost sensation from his chest down to his lower limbs since he was shot.
His hope of raising the required amount is dim, as he revealed that his father is physically challenged and begs to feed his family.
According to him, “I cannot feel anything from my chest down to my lower limbs. Even if they pierced me with a sharp object, I cannot feel it. Doctors attending to me have requested a CT scan and MRI to determine the extent of the injury, but my family is unable to raise the amount required for the test. The Radiographer said it will cost N190,000, but we don’t have the money.”
Recounting how he was shot, Abubakar said he was returning from his farmland after harvesting millet when he sighted the armed men and attempted to flee.
“When I saw the armed men, I tried to run, but they shot me in the back. I was on the floor until they left. My father and other people who came out of hiding managed to rush me to the hospital. I have been given drips, but further treatment will depend on the outcome of the CT scan.
“My father is crippled. He begs to eat and uses the money he gets from begging to feed his children. Now, we don’t have money for my treatment,” he stated, appealing to well-meaning Nigerians to come to his aid.
Meanwhile, five persons have now been confirmed dead in the attack. Those killed were identified as Abubakar Zagu, popularly known as Dogon Attah; Abubakar Aliyu; Babangida Chali; and Adamu Dan Gashuwa Dukura.
The other injured victims were identified as Dahru Dantunba, Jamilu Madugu, Sani Danbuga, the community secretary, and Basiru Dansalah.
Meanwhile, the latest military operation has brought renewed hope to residents of some communities in Kebbe Local Government Area who had been living in fear after receiving threat letters from bandits.
Residents said the presence of troops and their incursion into the forests, where weapons, ammunition and motorcycles were recovered, had boosted their confidence and reassured them that the terrorists could be pushed back.
However, they appealed to the military not to withdraw from the area immediately, stressing that a sustained presence was necessary to prevent the criminals from regrouping and returning to the communities.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Rumor mengenai versi PC GTA VI kembali mencuat. Setelah Rockstar Games memastikan game ini akan hadir lebih dulu di PlayStation 5 dan Xbox Series X|S, banyak pemain memperkirakan versi PC bakal menyusul beberapa waktu kemudian. Pola tersebut memang bukan hal baru bagi Rockstar. Grand Theft Auto V, misalnya, baru mendapatkan versi PC sekitar dua tahun setelah pertama kali meluncur di konsol.
Namun, situasi pasar hardware saat ini disebut bisa membuat Rockstar mengubah strategi tersebut. Andy Robinson, jurnalis VGC, dalam VGC Podcast menyebut adanya pembicaraan bahwa Rockstar mungkin mempercepat kedatangan versi PC GTA VI. Menurutnya, tingginya permintaan hardware dan kondisi pasar gaming saat ini dapat menjadi salah satu alasan versi PC hadir lebih cepat dari perkiraan.
Meski demikian, pernyataan Robinson masih berada dalam ranah rumor dan belum menjadi informasi resmi dari Rockstar. Belum ada indikasi bahwa pengembangan versi PC benar-benar dipercepat, apalagi jadwal rilis resminya belum diumumkan. Karena itu, kemungkinan tersebut sebaiknya dipandang sebagai spekulasi berdasarkan kondisi pasar, bukan kepastian.
Baca Juga: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Tembus 1 Juta Kopi di Hari Pertama
Harga Konsol dan Krisis Hardware Jadi Faktor
Salah satu faktor yang mendukung spekulasi tersebut adalah kondisi harga dan ketersediaan hardware gaming. Peluncuran GTA VI diperkirakan bakal mendorong permintaan konsol PlayStation 5 dan Xbox Series X|S. Bahkan, stok PlayStation 5 Pro sempat dilaporkan menghilang dari sejumlah retailer dan kembali tersedia dengan kenaikan harga yang cukup signifikan.
Situasi ini juga tidak terlepas dari tekanan pasar komponen seperti DRAM yang mengalami peningkatan permintaan, salah satunya akibat kebutuhan infrastruktur data center. Sejumlah analis dan retailer bahkan memperkirakan stok konsol bisa semakin terbatas ketika GTA VI akhirnya meluncur.
Rilis GTA VI Versi PC Lebih Cepat Bisa Menguntungkan Rockstar
Fisik mobil yang lebih realistik ketika meledak di GTA 6 (Sumber: Rockstar Games/Netflix)
Jika kondisi tersebut berlanjut, versi PC yang hadir lebih cepat secara bisnis memang masuk akal. Rockstar dapat menjangkau basis pemain yang lebih luas sekaligus mengurangi ketergantungan terhadap ketersediaan konsol. Apalagi, PC gaming memiliki pasar yang besar dan pemain GTA di platform tersebut sudah terbukti cukup kuat.
Di sisi lain, mempercepat versi PC juga bukan keputusan sederhana. Rockstar selama ini dikenal membutuhkan waktu tambahan untuk mengoptimalkan game ke PC, terutama untuk judul sebesar GTA VI. Perusahaan juga berpotensi mendapatkan keuntungan besar dari penjualan konsol terlebih dahulu. Jadi, meskipun tekanan pasar bisa menjadi alasan untuk mempercepat port PC, belum ada bukti kuat bahwa Rockstar benar-benar akan mengubah pola rilisnya. Untuk saat ini, gamer PC masih perlu menunggu pengumuman resmi Rockstar.

The Zamfara State Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency (RUWATSAN) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) have strengthened cooperation to improve Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services across the state.
The Programme Manager of RUWATSAN, Dr. Abubakar Nasiru Galadima, announced this after receiving the Chief of the UNICEF Sokoto Field Office, Dr. Michael Juma, in his office.
He was accompanied by the UNICEF WASH Officer, Dr. Ebri Etang, and other members of the UNICEF team.
Dr. Galadima said the meeting has provided an opportunity for both organisations to have a fruitful and insightful discussion on ways to advance the WASH agenda across Zamfara State.
He said discussions focused on strengthening sustainable WASH systems, developing resilient infrastructure, improving operation and maintenance of WASH facilities, enhancing faecal sludge management, and strengthening water quality monitoring and surveillance.
He emphasised that the interventions were critical to accelerating progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 6 SDG, which seeks to ensure the availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.
Dr Galadima reaffirmed RUWATSAN’s readiness to work closely with UNICEF and other development partners to promote sustainable and resilient WASH systems that will contribute to achieving improved public health and the wellbeing of communities across the state.

The Zamfara State Government said it will strengthen public-private partnerships to attract investment and deepen sustainable economic growth in the state.
This was revealed by Governor Dauda Lawal at the 2026 Zamfara State Business Partnership and Economic Development Summit held in Gusau, the state capital.
The summit, organised by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism, was themed: “Strengthening Partnership Between the Zamfara Business Community and Government for Sustainable Economic Growth and Investment.”
Mr Lawal said the government would continue to explore appropriate public-private partnership arrangements in areas where private capital, expertise and operational capacity could complement government resources.
He identified industrial infrastructure, markets, logistics, renewable energy, tourism, skills development and other commercially viable sectors as areas where such partnerships could be explored.
He said the approach would be guided by transparency, due process, value for money, appropriate risk allocation and the long-term interests of the people of Zamfara State.
He urged investors from within Nigeria and beyond to explore opportunities in Zamfara, engage relevant government institutions and consider how their capital, expertise and innovation could align with the state’s development priorities.
The governor said Zamfara was endowed with significant economic potential, including agricultural resources, mineral deposits, livestock, human capital, entrepreneurial capacity, commercial activities and a rich cultural heritage.
He, however, noted that resources and opportunities alone could not guarantee prosperity, stressing that investment, technology, infrastructure, sound policies and effective institutions were required to transform them into sustainable economic value.

items.content:
— Experts raise alarm at Lagos food safety conference
By Olasunkanmi Akoni and Shekinah Ijile
LAGOS — At least 53,000 deaths associated with unsafe food are recorded annually in Nigeria, a food safety expert, Dr Adeniyi Odugbemi, has said.
Odugbemi, who attributed the figure to recent studies, urged stakeholders to move beyond identifying food safety challenges and adopt science-based solutions to prevent avoidable deaths.
The expert, Global Director of Quality and Food Safety at Archer Daniels Midland, ADM, stated this yesterday at the fourth Lagos State Food Safety Conference and Exhibition organised by the Lagos State Consumer Protection Agency, LASCOPA, at NECA House, Alausa, Lagos.
The one-day conference was themed, “From Burden to Solution: Safe Food Everywhere.”
Delivering the keynote address, Odugbemi described unsafe food as a major public health and economic challenge, saying Nigeria could no longer rely on faith alone to address foodborne illnesses.
He said, “We’ve sat too long on the problem. We’ve sat too long on the burden. We need to start working together, look at the complexity of this burden and begin to offer solutions.
“Food safety challenges, including biological, chemical and physical contamination, food fraud, adulteration, ineffective packaging, food loss and waste, require interventions based on science, empirical evidence and research.”
Odugbemi stressed the importance of food safety, saying, “If it is not safe, it is not food.”
He identified food security, food sustainability and food safety as major challenges across the food value chain, stressing that access to food should not expose consumers to illness or injury.
The expert also called for greater attention to Nigeria’s informal food sector, where many Nigerians obtain meals outside the home.
He urged stakeholders to support informal food vendors with the knowledge and resources required to maintain safe food-handling practices rather than simply criticising them.
Odugbemi further warned that food safety had economic implications for Nigeria, particularly as food exports could face rejection in international markets over safety concerns.
He said strengthening the country’s food safety system was essential to maximising the economic potential of its agricultural and food sectors.
Odugbemi called on government, industry, academia and consumers to take clearly defined responsibilities in ensuring food safety.
He urged government to develop science-based policies and regulations, industries to treat food safety as a competitive advantage, and academic institutions to focus research on practical challenges rather than solely on academic requirements.
For consumers, he advised vigilance, stressing that individuals had the right to reject food they considered unsafe.
Earlier, the General Manager of LASCOPA, Afolabi Solebo, said the agency was committed to strengthening food safety practices and protecting consumers from unsafe products.
Solebo said food safety was a shared responsibility involving farmers, processors, distributors, retailers and consumers, and not solely that of regulatory agencies.
He said LASCOPA had strengthened its enforcement mechanisms, expanded consumer education and deepened collaboration with the Lagos State Ministry of Health, Ministry of Agriculture, National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, and Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON.
Also speaking, a representative of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission, FCCPC, Mrs Odubunmi Olutoyin, described food safety as a consumer protection, public health, economic and trust issue.
She urged businesses to comply with food safety requirements and advised consumers to read product labels, check expiry dates, buy from reputable vendors and report unsafe practices.
NAFDAC, represented by Olubunmi Olugbenga, reaffirmed the agency’s commitment to strengthening regulatory oversight, promoting good manufacturing practices and collaborating with stakeholders to reduce food safety risks.
At the conference, Dr Nora Oseni, a food and cosmetic scientist and lecturer at Auchi Polytechnic, raised concerns over palm oil adulteration.
Speaking on “Palm Oil Adulteration: Emerging Risks, Detective Strategies and Regulatory Control,” Oseni warned that consumers’ reliance on the colour of palm oil, particularly the belief that “the redder, the better,” could contribute to adulteration.
She said some traders add oil-soluble dyes to palm oil to improve its appearance, while cheaper oils and recovered frying oils could also be used as substitutes or adulterants.
Oseni advised consumers to pay attention to the visual and organoleptic characteristics of palm oil, including its colour, layers and characteristic smell, and avoid oil that appears degraded or smells rancid.
She called for improved training of palm oil processors, stronger traceability and closer collaboration between researchers and industry.
During a panel session, industry representatives also highlighted the importance of traceability in protecting consumers.
Mrs Muyiwa-Salami Olanike of Chivita Limited said the company’s food safety management system enabled it to trace products from raw materials through production and distribution.
The panel also identified poor waste management as a major food safety concern in Lagos.
The conference called for a shift from merely discussing the burden of unsafe food to developing measurable and sustainable solutions capable of ensuring safe food for Nigerians.
The post Unsafe food kills 53,000 Nigerians yearly — Expert appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Quantum cybersecurity startup QNu Labs has raised ₹200 Cr (around $21 Mn) in its Series A1 funding round co-led by the state-backed National Quantum Mission and Speciale Invest, along with participation from Sony Innovation Fund, Gaja Capital and Artha Ventures, among others.
The Bengaluru-based startup plans to use the fresh capital across R&D, sales and go-to-market strategy, and forging partnerships. Cofounder and CEO Sunil Gupta told Inc42 that the startup will also invest in internal processes, IT and automation as it moves from a technology development phase into a “proof-of-scale” business.
The latest fundraise takes QNu Labs’ total capital raised to ₹375 Cr. Prior to this, QNu Labs raised ₹60 Cr in its Series A funding round.
The investment comes at a time when QNu Labs is expanding beyond its existing cybersecurity portfolio. The startup has built a new platform, QShield 2.0, focused on the discovery and assessment of cryptographic assets as enterprises begin preparing for quantum-safe migration.
It is also working on security solutions for drones and satellites, with its drone security technology already undergoing pilots. Gupta said QNu Labs expects the offering to cater to the defence sector.
Additionally, the fundraise will also help QNu Labs meet the matching requirement for its RDI project. After being awarded a ₹150 Cr project under the government’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund, QnU was required to raise a matching amount from its side.
The fresh capital will help it meet this requirement, with the startup saying it has already signed the final term sheet for the project.
Founded in 2016 by Gupta and Srinivasa Rao Aluri, QNu Labs is building cybersecurity products aimed at protecting data and communications against quantum computing-led threats. It currently offers solutions based on quantum random number generation (QRNG), quantum key distribution (QKD) and post-quantum cryptography (PQC).
It claims that its quantum-safe VPN is currently its most sought-after product. It has around 180 employees as of now.
Underlining the necessity of the fund raise, Gupta said quantum tech is moving closer to mainstream adoption, with India targeting 2029 for the transition.
“Now the common understanding across the globe is that this tech will become mainstream in the next 2 to 3 years,” he said.
The startup is also strengthening its international expansion, with a presence in Australia and the US and partnerships in other markets. While it sells hardware and software in India, its international business largely focuses on subscription-based platforms for enterprises across sectors such as banking and healthcare.

That compares with robust net purchases of ₹49,355 crore in June and July through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) that applies to FPIs.133946709"Global risk-free rates are rising and then there are AI-related flows which are being attracted by other countries. It is very difficult to see inflows amid high crude prices," said Abhishek Upadhyay, economist, fixed income strategy, ICICI Securities PD. "Additionally, some investors are also waiting on the sidelines to enter the market after there is a rate hike."The US 10-year treasury yield climbed to 4.81%, its highest level since November 2023 last week, while Japan's 10-year government bond yield moved above 3% for the first time since 1996. German 10-year bond yields, a key metric for euro zone borrowing, rose to the highest level since 2011.Read more: Goldman Sachs’ big warning! Oil prices could soar to $120 if attacks on shipping continue in Hormuz StraitHigher yields in the developed markets have narrowed the differential with Indian rates.Additionally, Indian bonds faced a major setback late July when Bloomberg Index Services deferred the inclusion of local debt in its flagship Global Aggregate Index, which is tracked by funds that collectively invest into about $70 trillion worth of debt worldwide."It is difficult to imagine that debt inflows could surge unless there is some let-up in high global rates. High rates globally have been a hurdle for portfolio flows, despite well behaved inflation and a stable currency," said Dhiraj Nim, economist and FX strategist, ANZ Bank.The rupee has stabilised in FY27 after having hit historic lows - in the vicinity of 97 to a dollar - late May.Market participants do not expect either a sharp surge in inflows or significant outflows, but rather a period of largely neutral flows. Any buying that does emerge is likely to come from global investors with dedicated India or broader Asia mandates, economists said.

By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR
CALABAR — The Chairman of the Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria, PFN, in Cross River State, Apostle Trinity Ogar, has urged residents to stop attributing recent flood, landslide and fire incidents in the state to spiritual causes.
Ogar, who is also the Acting Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, in the state, said the disasters should instead be viewed within the context of natural and environmental factors and existing early warning systems.
He spoke while responding to questions from journalists on the series of disasters recorded across the state in recent weeks.
His comments followed speculation among some residents linking the incidents to the alleged displeasure of an Efik marine deity, “Anansa,” said to be associated with traditional worshippers in the area.
The incidents include a fire outbreak at Spar Shopping Mall in Calabar, a landslide on Anansa Road which destroyed property, and another landslide at Ikot Awatim, which reportedly claimed four lives.
Several other deaths have also been reported in connection with flooding in parts of the state.
Some residents had called on the state government to engage the Efik traditional institution and the Obutung community, said to be associated with the deity’s shrine, to explore traditional measures to address what they believed was the cause of the disasters.
However, Ogar dismissed the attribution of the disasters to spiritual causes, saying government agencies had issued early warnings ahead of some of the incidents.
He expressed concern that residents often resorted to spiritual explanations for natural disasters instead of paying attention to scientific and environmental warnings.
According to him, greater attention should be paid to early warning systems and other preventive measures capable of reducing the impact of disasters on communities.
The PFN chairman also said sustained prayers had been offered across Calabar and other parts of Cross River State in response to the disasters.
He urged residents to take official warnings seriously and support measures aimed at preventing further loss of lives and property.

items.content:
— Lagos APC vows full mobilisation for Tinubu, Hamzat, candidates
By Olasunkanmi Akoni
LAGOS — Ahead of the 2027 general elections, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu of Lagos State, his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, and leaders of the All Progressives Congress, APC, have urged residents to shun violence and ensure peaceful conduct before, during and after the polls.
They made the call on Tuesday at an interdenominational prayer session for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, the election of Hamzat as Lagos State governor and other APC candidates, held at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Onikan, Lagos Island.
The prayer session, attended by party leaders, supporters and religious faithful, was organised to seek divine guidance, commit the party’s electoral aspirations to God and formally commence mobilisation for the 2027 elections.
Among those at the event were Senator Musiliu Obanikoro; Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; former Speaker of the House, Adeyemi Ikuforiji; Pa Tajudeen Olusi; Senator Ganiu Solomon; Jumoke Okoya-Thomas; Senator Idiat Adebule; Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Wale Edun; APC Lagos Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi; Fouad Oki; members of the National Assembly and state House of Assembly; members of Conference 57 comprising 20 local government chairmen and 37 Local Council Development Area chairmen, as well as traditional rulers and religious leaders.
Speaking at the event, Sanwo-Olu stressed the importance of laying a spiritual foundation ahead of political activities.
He said the party would combine prayer with grassroots mobilisation and engagement with voters across the state.
Sanwo-Olu said although the party was relying on prayer, its members were also conscious that “faith without work is dead.”
He said the APC would not take any voter, community or stakeholder for granted, adding that the party planned to take its campaign to communities across the 20 local government areas and 37 LCDAs of the state.
According to him, the party’s objectives include securing the re-election of President Tinubu and victory for its National Assembly and state-level candidates.

items.content:
By Steve Oko
For generations, the rhythmic clatter of wooden looms echoed through Akwete, a quiet riverine community in the Ukwa East Local Government Area of Abia State. Every woven thread told a story of ingenuity, resilience, and culture. The famous Akwete cloth was more than fabric; it was the people’s identity, painstakingly woven by women whose skills had been passed from one generation to the next.
Yet, behind the beauty of the colourful handwoven textile lay a painful reality. The women who kept the centuries-old tradition alive worked with little government support, obsolete equipment, limited access to finance and shrinking markets. Many younger people abandoned the craft in search of better opportunities, leaving fears that one of Nigeria’s oldest indigenous textile traditions could gradually fade into history.
That long season of neglect may now be drawing to a close. When Nigeria’s First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, arrived in Akwete on July 21, 2026, her visit was more than ceremonial. It was an acknowledgement that hidden within the modest weaving community is an economic asset capable of creating jobs, empowering women, and preserving Nigeria’s cultural identity.
The defining moment came when she announced a N2 billion intervention to establish and strengthen an Akwete production hub. For the women seated before her, it was more than a financial commitment. It was validation after decades of waiting for meaningful government intervention.
“I am donating N2 billion to the project,” the First Lady declared, while urging Nigerians, especially the South-East, to embrace Akwete cloth as a national fabric rather than merely a local cultural product.
Her words resonated deeply because they addressed one of the biggest challenges confronting the industry: visibility.
For decades, Akwete fabric has enjoyed admiration among cultural enthusiasts but has struggled to compete with more commercial indigenous textiles such as Aso Oke, despite possessing comparable historical and artistic value. The First Lady challenged Nigerians to change that narrative.
Her promise to wear Akwete fabric if President Bola Tinubu secures a second term was itself a powerful endorsement capable of projecting the fabric onto national and international fashion platforms.
However, Mrs Tinubu will not be the first high-profile Nigerian to proudly wear Akwete fabrics. In fact, Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra State is a brand Ambassador of Akwete textile. He has proudly adorned himself with different colours and designs of the prestigious local fabrics. Former Governor Okezie Ikpeazu of Abia State also did so well in promoting Akwete textile, just as the incumbent Gov. Otti is towing a similar line.
The diaspora Igbo community is scrambling for Akwete textile, as the women in the weaving industry confirmed to this Correspondent earlier that they were receiving orders for the Akwete fabric from different parts of the world. Beyond orders from the diaspora, some communities and women’s associations in Rivers, Bayelsa, and other neighbouring states have adopted Akwete textile as their uniform. The famous Arochukwu kingdom has been celebrating one of its traditional festivals with Akwete textile as the official attire. Some Government officials as well as patriotic individuals take pride in adorning themselves with Akwete fabrics.
Beyond symbolism, however, the N2 billion intervention has the potential to fundamentally transform the local economy. Experts have long argued that Akwete’s greatest challenge is not the absence of skilled artisans but the absence of investment. Most weavers still rely on manual production methods that limit output and income. Access to quality raw materials, modern finishing equipment, product packaging, branding, and organised marketing has remained poor.
A properly developed production hub could address many of these structural constraints. With adequate investment, hundreds of women could expand production, younger residents could acquire weaving skills as a viable means of livelihood, and the community could evolve into a major cultural and tourism destination.
For Abia State, which is increasingly positioning itself as Nigeria’s hub for small and medium-scale enterprises under Governor Alex Otti, the intervention fits neatly into the administration’s economic diversification agenda.
Governor Otti, while receiving the First Lady, acknowledged that his administration had recognised Akwete’s economic potential soon after assuming office in 2023 and pledged the state’s full cooperation in translating the intervention into tangible development.
He described the First Lady’s visit as timely and strategic, noting that the government was prepared to partner with her in building a modern production hub capable of unlocking the enormous commercial value embedded in the famous fabric.
The visit also demonstrated how development can transcend partisan politics. Although Governor Otti belongs to the Labour Party and the First Lady is a leading figure in the ruling APC, both emphasised collaboration rather than political differences. Their shared commitment underscored an important lesson: when livelihoods are at stake, governance should rise above party lines.
The significance of the visit was not lost on the people of Akwete. For perhaps the first time, they saw the First Lady of Nigeria walk through their weaving centre, inspect their looms, interact with the artisans and publicly commit substantial resources to their future.
The excitement reflected more than appreciation. It reflected renewed hope. If transparently implemented, the intervention could stimulate cottage industries supplying yarns, dyes and accessories, create employment across the value chain, attract fashion designers and textile entrepreneurs, encourage exports and improve household incomes across the community.
It could also inspire many young people to return to a profession their parents and grandparents once proudly practised but which declining returns had made unattractive. Perhaps the greatest significance of the intervention lies in its timing.
Across Nigeria, conversations about economic diversification increasingly focus on agriculture, technology and manufacturing. Yet, cultural industries remain one of the country’s least exploited economic frontiers.
Akwete represents what can happen when heritage becomes enterprise. Countries across Asia have transformed indigenous crafts into billion-dollar industries through strategic investments, branding and tourism. Nigeria possesses similar opportunities in communities like Akwete, where tradition and entrepreneurship naturally intersect.
The First Lady’s intervention therefore extends beyond charity. It represents an investment in culture, women, rural enterprise and economic inclusion.
Whether the N2 billion becomes a true game-changer will ultimately depend on transparent implementation, proper management and sustained institutional support from both the federal and Abia State governments. Some elder statesmen from the area, including former Senate President, Adolphus Wabara, and former Secretary General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo, Okey Emuchay, have, while lauding the gesture by the First Lady, called for transparency in the disbursement of the funds. It, therefore, becomes imperative that a corruption-free mechanism be put in place to checkmate abuse and the usual squandermania associated with ‘free money’.
For the women of Akwete, however, hope has returned to the looms. After decades of weaving history into every thread while waiting for government to notice them, they may finally be on the threshold of a new chapter—one in which their craft not only preserves the past but also secures the future. It is a challenge to the women and young girls in the area to double down and prove that, indeed, they can ‘do wonders’ with the necessary support.
Perhaps most importantly, the age-old myths that weaving in Akwete is exclusive of only the womenfold has to be broken. Similarly, there is a need for the trade to go beyond manual weaving and embrace technology for mass production. If the industry must break even and survive in this era of global competition, it must think about commercialisation and refuse to be limited by the ropes of tradition and myths.
The post How Remi Tinubu’s N2bn lifeline could revive Akwete’s dying weaving heritage appeared first on Vanguard News.
