items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
As the government has opened the gas sector to the private sector, Universal Gas Distribution Company (Private) Limited (UGDC) is set to woo foreign investors to tap potential investment opportunities in Pakistan's gas sector at the upcoming Gastech 2026.
The conference will take place in Bangkok, Thailand, where foreign oil and gas companies are expected to participate.
UGDC is the first private entity in Pakistan already engaged in the sales, marketing and distribution of gas. It will represent the country at Gastech 2026, the world's leading platform for natural gas, LNG, hydrogen, climate technologies and energy innovation.
UGDC's participation will place Pakistan's private gas sector alongside leading international energy companies, investors, policymakers, technology providers and industry experts.
Previously, state-run gas utilities dominated the sector, and oil and gas exploration companies were bound to allocate gas to these entities. However, the present government, particularly the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), has opened the gas market to the private sector by increasing gas allocation from 10% to 35%.
At present, circular debt in the gas sector has ballooned to Rs3.8 trillion, including principal and late payment surcharges. This has stalled work on new oil and gas exploration projects.
Oil and gas exploration companies have backed the government's decision to increase the private sector's share, aiming to secure better gas prices and reduce circular debt.
"UGDC is an example of a private entity currently working in the gas sector. We will engage foreign companies to attract investment in Pakistan, particularly in gas exploration, in light of the enabling environment created by the government," said Ghyas Paracha, CEO of UGDC, in a statement.
At Gastech, UGDC will focus on attracting international investment into Pakistan's upstream and midstream gas sectors, including indigenous gas exploration and development, gas processing, LNG infrastructure, pipelines, storage, trading and related energy projects.
The company will also explore strategic partnerships, LNG supply opportunities, technology collaborations and investment avenues to strengthen Pakistan's energy landscape.
UGDC will highlight the role of Third-Party Access (TPA) and private-sector participation in creating a more competitive and transparent gas market. It believes that increased investment in indigenous gas sourcing and infrastructure can reduce reliance on costly imports, improve utilisation of existing infrastructure and help address circular debt.
UGDC's participation reflects its commitment to facilitating international collaboration, investment, market liberalisation and the development of a competitive and sustainable gas sector in Pakistan.

items.author: SHAHRAM HAQ
items.content:
A committee of the Ministry of Industries and Production has suggested reducing sales tax on luxury vehicles after reviewing the automotive and auto parts manufacturing policy.
The Auto Parts Export Council (APEC), chaired by the Minister of Industries and Production and comprising the Secretary Industries, Secretary Commerce, Chairman of the Trade Development Authority of Pakistan (TDAP), CEO of the Engineering Development Board (EDB) and three industry representatives, reviewed the policy.
"The tax relief was recommended on luxury vehicles costing more than Rs10 million. This is just to benefit a few buyers in the high-end segment," said Abdul Rehman, former chairman of the Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts and Accessories Manufacturers (PAAPAM), adding that this would hurt the competitiveness of local production.
Rehman asked why this favour is being extended to the luxury segments at a time when the country remains under an International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme that has demanded difficult sacrifices from the wider population. "This has also raised questions over the priorities of the policymakers whether scarce fiscal space should be used to reduce the tax burden on luxury vehicles when millions of Pakistanis continue to absorb the cost of economic adjustment," he added.
Pakistan has been implementing tough economic reforms under its IMF programme. Reducing sales tax on hybrid and plug-in hybrid vehicles raises a fundamental policy question, Rehman said. The Finance Bill 2026 increased sales tax on hybrid and plug-in hybrid vehicles to 25% as part of efforts to strengthen revenues and meet fiscal commitments.
Rehman reasoned that luxury vehicles are well beyond the reach of most Pakistanis. This step by the Ministry of Industries and Production creates the perception that while ordinary citizens continue to shoulder higher taxes, inflation and reduced government support, tax relief is being extended to buyers of luxury vehicles.
It is pertinent to mention here that a locally manufactured Suzuki Alto, priced at around Rs3 million, carries approximately Rs550,000 in sales tax, federal excise duty and the New Energy Vehicle levy. In comparison, a Range Extended Electric Vehicle priced at nearly Rs10 million reportedly attracts sales tax of around Rs100,000, with no federal excise duty or NEV levy. "Such disparity has raised questions about whether government incentives are being distributed fairly. Vehicles such as Alto and Cultus serve as basic mobility options for middle-income families, yet receive no meaningful tax relief," Rehman added.

items.author: Our Correspondent

Gold prices in Pakistan declined on Monday, tracking losses in the international market after Friday's strong US jobs report strengthened expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month.
Investors are now waiting for key inflation readings for clearer clues on the policy path. In the local market, the 24-karat gold was quoted at Rs463,136 per tola after a drop of Rs2,400, according to rates issued by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association. Ten-gram gold was sold at Rs397,064, down Rs2,058. On Saturday, the per-tola rate had slipped by Rs3,600.
Spot gold was down 0.3% at $4,412.73 an ounce by 11:51 am ET (1551 GMT), according to Reuters. US gold futures for December delivery fell 0.4% to $4,458.70. Trading volumes were thin because US markets were closed for the Labour Day holiday.
Interactive Commodities Director Adnan Agar said the session was subdued. "Today (Monday) was a bank holiday in the US, so the market was pretty quiet. The high was $4,429, the low was $4,381, and the market was later standing at $4,414. Low volume is expected when there is a bank holiday. The market should open more normally tomorrow (Tuesday)."
He added that the US CPI inflation report, expected later in the current week, and next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting would keep prices volatile. "Fluctuations in gold will continue in the coming days. However, there are higher chances of it going upwards and fewer chances of it going downwards."
Traders are pricing in roughly a 60% chance of a Fed rate increase in the upcoming meeting. The US PPI and CPI data are due this week and will be closely watched for signs of persistent inflation. Geopolitical headlines also remained in the background after Iran said it would announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf.
Silver followed gold lower in the domestic market, declining Rs39 to Rs7,059 per tola.
Analysts say the combination of a firm dollar, higher rate-hike odds and holiday-thinned liquidity has pressured bullion in the near term. Attention now turns to this week's US inflation prints and the Fed's next policy decision, which will determine whether the recent pullback in both international and Pakistani gold prices extends or reverses.
The Pakistani rupee closed at 277.40 against the US dollar on Monday, gaining Rs0.01 compared to Friday's settlement at 277.41. Internationally, the dollar stayed shaky despite firmer US rate-hike bets, as Middle East tensions raised the risk of broader inflation that could push global central banks to tighten policy together.

items.content:
Regional Tax Office (RTO) Islamabad Chief Commissioner Yasmeen Fatima has urged retailers and small shopkeepers to register under the government's Simplified Income Tax Regime (Asaan Tajir Scheme) and file their returns by September 30, 2026, saying the initiative is designed to simplify taxation, encourage voluntary compliance and bring more businesses into the formal economy.
Speaking at an interactive session at the Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI) on Monday, she described the scheme as a friendly and positive gesture towards the business community and called for replacing the traditional fear and distance between taxpayers and tax officials with cooperation, facilitation and mutual trust.
Explaining the scheme, Yasmeen Fatima said traders with annual turnover of up to Rs200 million could opt for the simplified regime while keeping the option of filing normal tax returns. Under the simplified system, eligible traders will pay a minimum annual tax of Rs25,000, while those fulfilling the prescribed requirements will remain exempt from audit. She said the scheme offered small businesses greater certainty about their tax obligations and provided an opportunity for traders currently outside the tax net to enter the formal economy through a simpler and more manageable compliance mechanism.
She further elaborated that registration process had been made easier, with the relevant form available in Urdu to facilitate small traders. Traders could register through the Tax Asaan App, while those requiring assistance could approach the tax authorities directly.
The chief commissioner said the scheme also carried significant benefits for traders, including no audit and an amnesty provision, urging the business community to view the initiative positively and avail of the opportunity.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) succumbed to significant selling pressure on Monday as the benchmark KSE-100 index dropped 1,692.74 points, or 0.97%, over rising crude oil prices and escalating tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, which weighed on investor sentiment.
The index opened the week on a fragile note, falling 429.59 points, or 0.25%, at 9:39 am. It initially hit the high of 175,353.67, before selling intensified and dragged the index to the intra-day low of 173,603.75. Major sectors that came under pressure were oil marketing companies (OMCs), auto assemblers, cement, commercial banks and refineries.
In the international market, oil prices rose more than $1 a barrel as tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes involving vessels near Hormuz heightened fears of prolonged disruption to Middle Eastern supplies. Iran's planned restricted Gulf zone and a new shipping corridor added to supply fears. The developments sparked worries about the potential impact on Pakistan's import bill and external account, while increasing uncertainty for oil-sensitive sectors.
According to Arif Habib Limited (AHL), Monday saw 175k give way with the KSE-100 declining 0.97% to close at 173.6k and continuing to move towards July lows. Only 12 shares rose while 87 fell with Pakistan Services (+7.55%), Askari Bank (+1.54%), Adamjee Insurance (+3.23%) contributing the most to the index's gains. In contrast, UBL (2.69%) OGDC (2.48%) and Pakistan Petroleum (1.78%) were the biggest drags.
Pakistan Services rallied after media reports of an out-of-court settlement of a dispute that included the company's hotel properties and controlling vote in their operations. Thatta Cement and Fauji Foundation, which were involved in the row, signed a memorandum of understanding for the settlement, the Nukta website reported. However, in a bourse filing, Pakistan Services said it had no knowledge of the contents of the media report and cases relating to its shareholding were sub judice.
Meanwhile, Iran said a deal with Oman to manage shipping through Hormuz was just days away while oil prices continued to rise. AHL predicted that the July low of 170k was the near-term target for the KSE-100 index.
KTrade Securities noted that the trading session remained under pressure as broad-based selling dominated investor sentiment. Sector-wise, selling was evident across banks, oil & gas, cement, fertiliser and refineries. Individually, UBL, OGDC, PPL, MCB, Fauji Fertiliser, Lucky Cement, Bank AL Habib and Attock Refinery were among the major laggards, reflecting widespread profit-taking and risk aversion.
The weakness was further amplified by concerns surrounding elevated international oil prices. "Going forward, rising oil prices remain a key concern for the market, given their potential impact on Pakistan's inflation, external account and macroeconomic stability," it said.
"Investor sentiment is likely to remain cautious and headline-driven. Any moderation in crude prices could provide relief, while further escalation may keep the market under pressure."
Trading volumes decreased to 679.2 million shares versus Friday's tally of 874.3 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs23.7 billion.
In the ready market, shares of 495 companies were traded. Of these, 154 stocks closed higher, 311 fell and 30 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico Pk led the volume chart with trading in 82.5 million shares, losing Rs0.90 to close at Rs13.02. Foreign investors sold shares worth Rs122.5 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

items.title: Govt Launches Nationwide Hepatitis C Screening Drive
items.summary:
The federal government has decided to launch a nationwide hepatitis C screening drive as the number of patients in Pakistan has crossed 11 million.
Dr. Zia Dawar, Director of the Prime Minister’s Hepatitis Prevention Program, told Samaa that every citizen above the age of 12 will be screened under the initiative. The government has set a target of screening around 160 million people across the country.
The program will be carried out in three stages covering screening, testing, and treatment, with the government bearing the full cost of diagnosis and treatment.
According to Dr. Dawar, screening and testing are expected to cost around Rs. 7,500 per patient, while treatment expenses could reach up to Rs. 64,000 per patient.
Federal government employees will also be required to undergo hepatitis C testing, while authorities may recommend withholding the salaries of employees who refuse to be tested. Screening camps will be set up across federal ministries to facilitate the process.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
The federal government has decided to launch a nationwide hepatitis C screening drive as the number of patients in Pakistan has crossed 11 million.
Dr. Zia Dawar, Director of the Prime Minister’s Hepatitis Prevention Program, told Samaa that every citizen above the age of 12 will be screened under the initiative. The government has set a target of screening around 160 million people across the country.
The program will be carried out in three stages covering screening, testing, and treatment, with the government bearing the full cost of diagnosis and treatment.
According to Dr. Dawar, screening and testing are expected to cost around Rs. 7,500 per patient, while treatment expenses could reach up to Rs. 64,000 per patient.
Federal government employees will also be required to undergo hepatitis C testing, while authorities may recommend withholding the salaries of employees who refuse to be tested. Screening camps will be set up across federal ministries to facilitate the process.
The government also plans to screen passengers at airports for hepatitis C.
Screening and treatment facilities have already been established at 18 government hospitals, while authorities are also considering extending testing services to private hospitals.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
realme today officially launched the realme C100 Series in Pakistan, led by a massive 8000mAh Titan Long-Lasting Battery and designed for a generation whose lives are no longer defined by one role, one routine or one path.
For today’s Gen Z, a single day can move between study, work, gaming, content creation, sports and social life. Building on the insight behind realme’s The Ahead Generation initiative, the C100 Series brings the idea of Life Maxed to life through three core product strengths: long-lasting power, everyday durability and smooth performance.
At its heart is one simple promise: more freedom to choose what comes next, without battery getting in the way.
The realme C100 Series launches in three configurations:
realme C100x 6GB+128GB — PKR 64,999
realme C100x 8GB+128GB — PKR 74,999
realme C100 8GB+256GB — PKR 89,999
The realme C100 is available in Dream White, Frost Purple and Dark Coffee, featuring realme’s Blooming Design, while the realme C100x comes in Golden Coast and Deepblue Tides.
Power That Keeps Up
At the centre of the C100 Series is its 8000mAh Titan Long-Lasting Battery, giving users greater freedom to move through the day without constantly thinking about the next charge.
The battery is supported by 7-Year Battery Health and 45W fast charging, while Reverse Charging allows the phone to share power with compatible devices. The realme C100 supports 10W Reverse Charging, while the C100x supports up to 6W Reverse Charging.
From classes and freelance work to gaming, content and late-night conversations, the benefit is simple: less time worrying about battery, more freedom to keep going.
Ready for the Unexpected
A Life Maxed does not always go according to plan. That is why durability forms the second pillar of the C100 Series.
Both models feature 2m Drop Resistance, ArmorShell Protection, ArmorShell Glass and Rain Touch Mode, helping users stay protected against the drops, knocks and unpredictable conditions of everyday life.
The realme C100 takes protection further with IP69 Pro Water Resistance, tested up to 6m, while the realme C100x features IP64 dust and water resistance.
The result is a phone designed not only to last through a long day, but to keep up when that day takes an unexpected turn.
Smooth Through Every Switch
Life Maxed also means moving quickly between different parts of life — from work to entertainment, from scrolling to gaming, and from consuming content to creating it.
Both models feature a 120Hz Smooth Display for more fluid scrolling, navigation and gaming.
The realme C100 is powered by the MediaTek Helio G92 Max, supported by technologies including GT BOOST, Hyper Cooling and Flux Engine to deliver smoother gaming and everyday performance.
Both the realme C100 and C100x also feature a 50MP AI Camera, giving users more flexibility to capture and create throughout the day.
8000mAh. Life Maxed.
With an 8000mAh battery at its core, supported by stronger durability and smooth performance, the realme C100 Series is designed for a generation that wants more freedom to explore different sides of life.
Because Life Maxed is not simply about doing more. It is about having more possibilities — and the freedom to choose what comes next.
The realme C100 Series is now available in Pakistan, starting from PKR 64,999.

items.author: Arooj Fatima
items.content:
The Department of Specialised Healthcare and Medical Education, Punjab, has asked the Inter-Board Coordination Commission (IBCC) to review the equivalence criteria for Cambridge qualifications used in medical college admissions.
The department has written to the Executive Director of IBCC, highlighting concerns that the existing system may place O and A Level students at a disadvantage compared to those coming through the traditional Matriculation and FSc system.
Under the current admission criteria, merit for medical colleges is calculated by combining marks obtained in Matriculation/FSc or equivalent qualifications with the MDCAT score.
However, differences in the grading and equivalence systems can result in a significant gap between students who achieve exceptionally high grades in the Cambridge system and those who secure high marks in FSc.
As a result, even Cambridge students who obtain the highest possible grades in O and A Levels may find themselves at a comparative disadvantage in the highly competitive medical college admission process.
The Punjab government has therefore sought a review of the existing equivalence criteria to address concerns surrounding the treatment of Cambridge qualifications in medical admissions.

items.title: ECC Allows Donkey Exports from Gwadar Under Strict Conditions
items.summary:
The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the federal cabinet has approved the export of donkey meat and hides from the Gwadar Free Zone, subject to safeguards recommended by the Ministry of National Food Security and Research.
The decision was taken after the ECC reviewed recommendations from a committee formed to address issues related to the proposed exports.
ECC also approved continued gas supply to FatimaFert and Agritech until September 30, 2026, under the existing arrangement.
Separately, the committee approved Rs. 5 billion in seed money for the Daanish Schools Authority Fund through a technical supplementary grant, with the amount to be kept under an endowment framework.
The ECC also reviewed progress on the Pakistan Skills Impact Bond and set September 30, 2026, as the deadline for the Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training to submit substantive progress on the initiative.

items.author: Amiya Johar
items.content:
IT provider Tata Consultancy Services’ (TCS) subsidiary HyperVault is planning a 1GW AI data centre campus in the south Indian city of Hyderabad, with up to INR700 billion ($7.4 billion) earmarked for the project.
HyperVault, an AI data centre and infrastructure business, secured 264 acres for the development, which will be built in phases based on customer demand and technology requirements. Once fully built, the campus is expected to rank among India’s largest AI infrastructure facilities.
The site will target AI companies and hyperscalers, supporting high-density GPU deployments for AI training and inference. It will use liquid cooling and is designed to accommodate larger power requirements for advanced AI workloads. The company also plans to use green energy and water-neutral design principles.
HyperVault CEO and managing director Deepesh Nanda said the company is “building infrastructure for where AI is going: higher density, liquid cooling, larger power blocks and faster deployment”.
Meanwhile, TCS CEO K. Krithivasan noted: “Hyderabad offers the scale, talent and ecosystem to serve global customers,” adding the project combines “AI-ready infrastructure with our cloud, engineering, enterprise transformation and AI capabilities”.
The move forms part of TCS’ broader push into AI infrastructure. Last month, the IT services player struck a five-year partnership with Porsche worth €1.25 billion and agreed to acquire the company’s automotive and consulting unit MHP for €320 million.

items.author: Naeem Asghar
items.content:
The Senate Standing Committee on Interior on Monday approved a series of criminal law amendments, including a proposal to make acid attacks punishable by death, along with measures to criminalise the abuse of domestic workers, unauthorised liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) decanting and the wrongful detention of dead bodies by hospitals.
Chaired by Senator Faisal Saleem Rehman, the committee considered several private members’ bills concerning acid attacks, domestic workers, LPG safety, anti-rape legislation and consumer protection.
The bills were passed despite opposition from Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry, while Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) lawmakers also voted in favour.
The Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, moved by Senator Muhammad Abdul Qadir, seeking amendments to Section 336-B of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) concerning hurt caused by corrosive substances, was passed in the mover's absence.
The bill, citing the recent acid attack on a lady doctor in Quetta, said that despite an amendment made in 2011, acid attacks continued to cause lifelong disfigurement and trauma. It proposed punishment of “death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment of not less than 14 years and a fine of Rs2 million” as a strong deterrent against the crime.
Read: Suspect killed in encounter after acid attack on female doctor in Quetta
The committee also unanimously passed the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Bill moved by Senator Sarmad Ali, seeking to criminalise the abuse of domestic workers.
Its "Statement of Objects and Reasons" said domestic workers constituted one of the most vulnerable segments of society and were often subjected to physical violence, sexual abuse, forced labour and other forms of mistreatment by employers.
It said existing legal provisions did not specifically address abuse arising from the dependency and control inherent in domestic work settings.
The proposed provision covers physical violence, sexual harassment, threats, forced labour, wage theft, confiscation of identity documents, denial of food or medical care and humiliating treatment.
It proposes imprisonment for up to 10 years and a fine of up to Rs100,000, while offences resulting in serious injury or death would carry imprisonment for life and a fine of up to Rs500,000.
The bill would also make employers liable if members of their household committed abuse, unless they had taken reasonable steps to prevent such abuse.
Read More: Households continue to exploit child labour in Punjab
Schedule II of the Code of Criminal Procedure would also be amended to make the offence non-bailable and triable by a court of session.
The committee also approved the Criminal Laws (Amendment) Act moved by Senator Shahadat Awan, seeking to amend Sections 286 and 286-A of the PPC to criminalise the unauthorised transfer of LPG into smaller cylinders.
The bill noted that LPG decanting in residential areas and roadside setups without proper safety measures posed severe risks to public life and property.
It proposed increasing the punishment under Section 286 from six months to two years and raising the fine from Rs1,000 to Rs100,000. Under Section 286-A, the proposed punishment would increase from two to five years, while the fine would rise from Rs10,000 to Rs500,000.
The "Statement of Objects and Reasons" said the decanting of LPG from larger cylinders into smaller domestic cylinders without proper safety measures had become widespread in many parts of Pakistan. Such unauthorised operations, it added, were often conducted in residential areas, workshops and roadside setups without adherence to safety standards.
“The proposed amendments aim to deter negligent and reckless conduct in the handling of explosive and hazardous substances, ensuring greater public safety and accountability,” the statement said.
The committee unanimously passed another Criminal Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, proposing the insertion of a new Section 338CA to make the “wrongful detention of a dead body” a punishable offence.
Parliament’s responsibility is to turn the concerns of our people into meaningful legislation and action. Today, the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control took up important matters concerning public safety, justice, legislation and institutional… pic.twitter.com/tpxqssePts
— Samina Mumtaz Zehri (@SenatorMumtaz) September 7, 2026
The "Statement of Objects and Reasons" highlighted reports of private hospitals and clinics detaining the bodies of deceased patients until their families settled outstanding medical bills.
It cited instances in which hospitals allegedly demanded exorbitant advance deposits, sometimes as high as Rs2 million to Rs4 million, and withheld bodies even when outstanding dues were as low as Rs100,000.
The statement said such practices caused immense psychological harm to grieving families and denied the deceased the right to timely burial and dignified last rites, which it described as a fundamental religious obligation in Islam and other religions. It also maintained that the inviolability of human dignity did not cease upon death.
Also Read: Hospitals barred from retaining bodies over unpaid bills
The proposed provision carries a punishment of up to two years’ imprisonment and/or a fine of Rs500,000 for a first offence. A second offence, or detention of a body beyond 24 hours, would carry imprisonment of up to three years and/or a fine of Rs1 million. Exceptions have been provided for autopsies and police investigations, while the offence has been made compoundable by the legal heirs.
The Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) (Amendment) Bill, moved by Senator Bushra Anjum Butt, was also passed. The committee observed that legislation aimed at strengthening the legal framework against rape should receive appropriate government support.
On consumer protection, the committee passed the Islamabad Consumers Protection (Amendment) Bill, also moved by Senator Zehri, seeking to bring private healthcare under the ambit of the 1995 Act.
The proposed legislation targets undisclosed fees, non-itemised billing and demands for advance deposits before emergency treatment. It would also require hospitals to publicly display their fee schedules and provide itemised bills.
Separately, the committee expressed serious concern over reports that former parliamentarians were being required to obtain a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the Interior Ministry for the issuance of official passports and that the validity of such passports had been reduced from five years to one year.
Chaudhry told the committee that only the internal approval procedure had been changed.
The chairman directed that existing law must not be violated and that official passports should be issued with five-year validity in accordance with the law. Further deliberation on the matter was deferred.
The Interior Ministry also briefed the committee on concerns surrounding the unregulated use of social media by minors, saying that a high-powered committee was working on proposals to regulate children’s use of social media.

items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The government on Monday approved an increase of Rs0.5194 per unit in electricity tariffs, placing an additional burden of approximately Rs12.6 billion on power consumers.
The increase will apply to all consumer categories except lifeline consumers, units billed under the Incremental Consumption Package, and prepaid consumers.
The positive quarterly adjustment will be recovered over three months — September, October and November — at a uniform rate of Rs0.5194 per kWh.
During the hearing, it was suggested that the per-unit impact of the Rs33 billion quarterly adjustment requested by distribution companies (DISCOs) be spread over four months, from September to December 2026, instead of three months.
The authority, however, noted that Nepra had worked out an adjustment of around Rs12 billion, considerably lower than the amount sought by DISCOs. It therefore decided to retain the three-month recovery period.
The regulator also decided to extend the quarterly adjustment to K-Electric consumers for the same period. Accordingly, K-Electric consumers will also be charged Rs0.5194 per kWh, with the same exemptions for lifeline, Incremental Consumption Package and prepaid consumers.
Nepra directed all DISCOs to submit their quarterly adjustment requests immediately after the close of each quarter to ensure timely processing.
The distribution companies were also directed to provide category-wise details of increases or decreases in sales for each quarter compared with reference sales and actual sales during the corresponding period of the previous year.
For industrial consumers, the information must be provided separately for B1, B2, B3 and B4 categories.
The authority directed that future hearings include an analysis of sales and maximum demand indicator variances and their impact on quarterly adjustment amounts to provide a clearer understanding of the data.

The first round of negotiations between delegations from Jamaat-e-Islami (JI) and the federal government regarding the abolition of the petroleum levy and provision of relief to the public concluded on Monday in Islamabad, with the former submitting six key proposals to the government committee and agreeing to hold the next session on September 10.
The JI delegation was led by Vice Emir Liaqat Baloch, accompanied by Deputy Secretary Syed Farasat Shah, KP North Emir Inayatullah Khan, Lahore Emir Zia-ur-Rehman Ansari, Islamabad Emir Nasrullah Randhawa, Al-Khidmat CEO Karachi Naveed Ali Baig and Shahid Naeem. The government side was headed by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, alongside Adviser to the Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah Khan, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, and Minister of State for Finance Bilal Azhar Kayani.
Meet the Technical Team of Jamaat-e-Islami, who will be meeting with the Government team to negotiate how the Levy could be reduced. The 1st round of meetings is starting today in Islamabad.
The team consists of;
1. Liaquat Baloch - Seasoned Politician
2. Syed Firasat Shah - Ex… pic.twitter.com/2zC8lmys5h
— Jamaat e Islami Pakistan (@JIPOfficial) September 7, 2026
Speaking to journalists after the meeting, Baloch stated that they presented six detailed proposals to the premier’s designated team, emphasising that the direct 80-rupee petroleum levy per litre on petrol and diesel was severely impacting the national economy.
He clarified that peaceful sit-ins and protests across the country would continue while negotiations proceeded.
Read: Govt, JI agree to form technical committees to review petroleum levy
Baloch added that the primary objective remained providing immediate relief to the public, urging rulers to cut state expenditures as sufficient budgetary margin existed to accommodate tax relief. He also expressed concern over unfulfilled government commitments made during previous talks regarding independent power producers (IPP) protests and the Balochistan Long March, stating that daily petroleum pricing should be discontinued, further noting that current subsidy structures had failed.
پیچھے نہیں ہٹیں گے، ہمارے دھرنےاور احتجاج جاری رہیں گے۔
ایسی اسپیس موجود ہے جس سے عوا م کو ریلیف دیا جاسکتا ہے۔ہم نے 6 تجاویز حکومت کے سامنے رکھی ہیں۔ ہم توقع کرتے ہیں کہ 3 روز میں حکومت جائزہ لے گی اور عوام کو ریلیف ملے گا۔
لیاقت بلوچ، نائب امیر جماعت اسلامی پاکستان… pic.twitter.com/CIa5kurIJ2
— Jamaat e Islami Pakistan (@JIPOfficial) September 7, 2026
Iqbal stated that the government had invited JI for talks to seek their actionable suggestions, which had now been formally received. He noted that the relevant government institutions would review these recommendations and any impractical points would be discussed openly with JI during the upcoming session.
He mentioned that the government never desired to overburden citizens, but global economies had been disrupted by regional tensions, including the war in Iran, adding that petroleum prices would naturally ease once regional conflicts de-escalated.
On Sunday, JI chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman warned the government of expanding the party's protest movement if its demands were not accepted, saying the next phase could include wheel-jam and shutter-down strikes, closure of petrol stations and a long march towards Islamabad.

Addressing a press conference at the party's sit-in at Faisal Chowk on Mall Road, he accused the government of shifting the burden of its "incompetence, poor governance and failure to collect taxes" onto the public.

Rehman said the protest was not aimed at securing a political benefit for any party but at seeking relief for citizens facing rising costs. Inflation, he added, had made education, healthcare and other basic services increasingly unaffordable.
The JI chief criticised the petroleum levy, calling it a "jagga tax", and claimed that taxes of around Rs130 were included in the price of petroleum products, with the government directly collecting more than Rs105.
Rehman claimed that the government had collected more than Rs4 trillion through the petroleum levy and demanded that it explain where the money had been spent.
He also criticised the Federal Board of Revenue for failing to meet its tax targets and questioned capacity payments made to IPPs for electricity that, according to him, were neither generated nor supplied.
The JI chief said the government had reduced petrol and diesel prices following the protests but had failed to provide transparency in the mechanism used to determine petroleum prices.

items.author: Sports Desk
items.content:
Pakistan Women stormed into the semi-finals of the Women's Asia Cup with a commanding 72-run victory over Hong Kong Women on Monday, powered by a record-breaking spell from left-arm spinner Nashra Sandhu.
Chasing 144 for victory in the Group A encounter at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, Hong Kong were bowled out for 71 in 19 overs as Sandhu claimed 6-7 from her four overs, the best bowling figures by a Pakistani bowler in women's T20 international cricket.
The victory was Pakistan's second in three matches and secured their place in the knockout stage behind Group A champions India, who had already sealed top spot with three wins.
Pakistan will face Sri Lanka in the semi-finals on Friday.
Pakistan's comprehensive performance was set up by a measured batting display after they won the toss and elected to bat.
Shawaal Zulfiqar anchored the innings with a fluent 47 from 35 balls, striking six fours, while Ayesha Zafar added 26 from 19. Captain Fatima Sana provided the late impetus with an unbeaten 24 from 24 balls, including two sixes, to lift Pakistan to 143-8 from their 20 overs.
Tuba Hassan chipped in with a brisk 14 from 13 balls, while Sandhu finished unbeaten on three.
Hong Kong's Joyleen Kaur was the pick of their bowlers, taking 4-19 from four overs, but Pakistan's total proved far beyond Hong Kong's reach.
The chase unravelled almost immediately.
Fatima Sana removed Mariko Hill for a duck and Sadia Iqbal dismissed captain Natasha Miles for one as Hong Kong slipped to 1-1 and then 1-2 inside the second over.
Kary Chan offered resistance with a patient 30 from 47 balls, but once she was dismissed by Ayesha Zafar in the 16th over, Hong Kong's hopes of mounting a recovery disappeared. Sandhu then took control. The spinner removed Yasmin Daswani for 13 before running through Hong Kong's lower order, claiming the wickets of Marina Lamplough, Maryam Bibi, Shanzeen Shahzad, Alison Siu and Iqra Sahar.
Her figures of 4-0-7-6 surpassed the previous benchmark and represented the best bowling performance by a Pakistani player in women's T20I cricket.
Sandhu's extraordinary spell also earned her Player of the Match honours.
Hong Kong were eventually dismissed for 71, with Chan the only batter to pass 20. Pakistan's bowlers maintained relentless pressure throughout, conceding just four extras and restricting the Hong Kong innings to a run rate of 3.73.
In Group B, Sri Lanka have already booked their semi-final place. The second qualifier from that group will be decided by the match between the United Arab Emirates and Bangladesh.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Monday hiked the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs12.9 and Rs3.72 per litre, respectively, for September 8.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs358.77 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs381.77 per litre for September 8.
The latest revision comes after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs3.13, while increasing the price of HSD by Rs3.74 per litre from September 5 to September 7.
Read: Govt decreases petrol price by Rs3.13, increases HSD by Rs3.74 per litre till Sept 7
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, petroleum products constitute one of the country's largest import categories, making the economy highly vulnerable to changes in global crude oil prices. Domestic refineries satisfy only part of national demand, while the remainder is met through imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products. Consequently, every increase in international oil prices raises Pakistan's import bill, pressures foreign exchange reserves, and contributes to inflation.
Pakistan previously exercised significant government control over petroleum pricing through subsidies and administrative interventions. While these measures temporarily protected consumers, they imposed substantial fiscal costs. During periods of elevated global oil prices, successive governments delayed passing price increases to consumers, creating financial pressures for oil marketing companies, refineries, and the national budget. Large fuel subsidies widened fiscal deficits, increased public borrowing, and weakened macroeconomic stability.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices rose ​to a six-week high on Monday as Iran vowed to strike energy infrastructure across the Middle East in response to further ‌US attacks on its assets, the latest escalation in a conflict that has sharply reduced oil supply from the region.
Brent crude futures rose 85 cents, or 0.9%, to $97.13 a barrel by 12:38 pm EDT (1638 GMT), after hitting their highest point since July 24 at $98.06.
"Commercial tankers are now being deliberately used as instruments of reciprocal ​economic pressure, substantially weakening the previous distinction between military confrontation and commercial shipping," maritime intelligence firm Marisks said.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Deepinder Goyal’s wearable startup Temple has released its first validation study, with researchers finding that its proprietary brain flow metric broadly tracked changes in cerebral blood-flow velocity recorded using transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasound.
However, the study, published as a preprint, involved only 23 healthy adults and has been submitted for peer review.
TCD is a non-invasive ultrasound technique used to measure the speed and direction of blood flow in the brain’s major arteries. The study compared Temple’s metric with blood-flow velocity in the middle cerebral artery rather than directly measuring total or absolute cerebral blood flow.
Researchers compared Temple’s wearable with TCD during two activities designed to produce changes in cerebral blood flow – stationary cycling and a shift from standing to lying down. Data from 20 participants was analysed under each protocol.
Temple’s brain flow metric registered a median within-subject correlation of about 0.8 with middle cerebral artery blood-flow velocity across both activities, according to the paper.
Goyal said in a post on X that the result demonstrated that Temple could track changes in brain blood flow that conventional heart-rate measurements might miss.
During the postural test, participants’ heart rates declined when they lay down, while cerebral blood-flow velocity increased. Temple’s metric moved in the same direction as the Doppler reading despite the opposing change in heart rate, the researchers found.
“Any device that only measures heart rate would have gotten this completely wrong,” Goyal said.
The findings suggest that Temple’s wearable can follow the direction and pattern of short-term changes in cerebral blood-flow velocity under controlled conditions. They do not establish that the device can accurately measure absolute cerebral blood flow or diagnose medical conditions.
The paper also said further studies involving other measurement techniques and cerebrovascular challenges would be needed to determine whether Temple’s brain flow metric specifically reflects cerebral activity and to establish potential clinical applications.
Goyal acknowledged the limited scope of the research, saying it involved one study, two interventions, and healthy adults. He added that further validation studies of Brain Flow and Temple’s other proprietary metric, Entropy, were under way.
The startup is also offering to loan its devices to qualified researchers seeking to independently test its metrics, Goyal added.
Temple’s Wearable Bet
Temple is developing a wearable device intended to continuously track signals associated with cerebral blood flow. It describes its device as a product that will measure “brain flow” – the blood flow to the brain.
Unlike conventional consumer wearables that primarily monitor metrics such as heart rate, blood oxygen levels, and sleep, Temple is betting on measurements taken from the side of the head.
Temple raised around ₹493 Cr earlier this year from investors including Peak XV Partners, Steadview Capital, NK Squared, and Goyal. The round reportedly valued the startup at about ₹1,700 Cr (about $204 Mn).
Its valuation subsequently nearly doubled to $375 Mn as part of an ESOP liquidity programme for early employees.
Last month, Goyal said Temple had reduced the size of the wearable to less than half that of the earlier version. The startup is preparing to open preorders and expects to begin shipping the device before the end of 2026.
Temple also recently acquired London-based longevity medicine practice Longevous for an undisclosed amount, adding clinical and scientific expertise ahead of the wearable’s launch.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Swiggy’s subsidiary, Swiggy Networks Ltd, has entered a share acquisition agreement with B2B ecommerce unicorn Udaan to acquire Swiggy-owned retail distribution platform LYNK in a share-swap transaction valuing the business at ₹500 Cr.
Under the deal, Swiggy Networks will transfer its entire shareholding in Lynks Logistics Ltd to Trustroot Internet Pvt Ltd (TIPL), Udaan’s Singapore-based parent entity.
In return, TIPL will issue 1.67 Lakh Series R CCPS to Swiggy Networks at an issue price of $314.40 apiece. The shares, worth $52.37 Mn, will give Swiggy a roughly 2.8% stake in Udaan.
Swiggy will further invest ₹75 Cr in primary capital in Udaan for an additional 0.4% stake, taking its total shareholding to about 3.2%.
The acquisition is expected to be completed by October 22, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
How The Deal Is Structured
In an exchange filing, Swiggy said Lynks Logistics reported nil standalone revenue in FY26 and had a negative net worth of ₹11 Lakh as of March 31, 2026.
However, the B2B authorised distribution business is currently operated by Swiggy Networks. Before the sale, Swiggy Networks will transfer this business to Lynks Logistics under a business transfer agreement.
“During the financial year ended March 31, 2026, the said business contributed revenue of ₹668 Cr, representing 2.90% of the consolidated revenue of the company. The net assets attributable to the said business were ₹500 Cr as at March 31, 2026, representing 2.73% of the consolidated net worth of the company,” Swiggy said.
Following the transfer of the business, Swiggy Networks will sell its entire shareholding in Lynks Logistics to Udaan’s parent entity.
LYNK’s operations are concentrated in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Kolkata, which together account for about 75% of its revenue. Udaan expects the acquisition to expand its retail distribution network and strengthen its relationships with consumer brands.
Swiggy Exits B2B Distribution
Founded in 2015 by Abinav Raja and Shekhar Bhende, Chennai-based LYNK operates a technology-led distribution platform connecting FMCG brands with retailers.
Swiggy acquired LYNK in 2023 to enter the food and grocery retail segment. LYNK cofounder Bhende joined Swiggy as a vice president post the acquisition to lead the FMCG retail distribution business under the foodtech company.
Bhende exited Swiggy in June 2025 and is currently building an AI-led business in stealth.
Swiggy CFO Rahul Bothra said combining LYNK with Udaan would bring together the former’s distribution capabilities and the latter’s scale and technology platform.
The divestment will allow Swiggy to retain exposure to the B2B distribution opportunity through its minority stake in Udaan, while transferring the business to a larger, specialised operator.
For Udaan, the transaction comes after it completed a $160 Mn recapitalisation exercise comprising fresh equity, new debt, and conversion of existing debt into equity following the initiation of insolvency proceedings by its creditors.
The B2B ecommerce unicorn said the recapitalisation helped it strengthen its balance sheet and enhance its financial flexibility.
“The acquisition of LYNK further strengthens our business and expands our presence across some of India’s most important consumption markets. Together, these developments position Udaan strongly for its next phase of growth and our ambition to build a technology-led distribution network for India’s retail ecosystem,” Udaan cofounder and CEO Vaibahav Gupta said.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
At the World Humanoid Robot Games in China last month, robots jumped, boxed and danced. Some fleet-footed bots ran faster than Usain Bolt over 100 meters. Spectators cheered the machines’ improving capabilities and their meme-worthy stumbles. .
Two days after the Games ended, the People's Liberation Army's official newspaper drew its own conclusions from the show. The PLA Daily called for researchers to accelerate the transfer of cutting-edge technologies from laboratories to military training grounds for robotic “combatants.”
China's defense establishment ​is accelerating research into humanoids’ military uses and planning for their eventual wartime deployment, according to a Reuters review of more than 100 Chinese military procurement notices, academic studies, patents, official publications, government records and defense-company materials.
Military institutions are testing humanoids against battlefield requirements, seeking ‌to acquire robots and technologies to train them, and studying how they might function alongside troops, the previously unreported records show. The work gained momentum in 2025 and 2026, focusing on robot perception, manipulation, and training data.
Chinese manufacturers accounted for about 95% of global humanoid shipments in 2025, according to BofA Global Research. That commercial dominance gives the PLA access to an expanding industry while developing its own military applications.
China’s robot defense research underscores how rapidly military technologies are evolving globally. In the Russia-Ukraine war, semiautonomous drones that use artificial intelligence for navigation and targeting have transformed reconnaissance and attack, while robots carry supplies and retrieve casualties. Reuters has previously documented the Chinese military’s efforts to learn from Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II.
That evolution is driving worldwide military interest ​in autonomous systems.
“Going where we don’t want humans to go is one of the most compelling reasons to develop robots in the first place,” said Dennis Hong, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at UCLA. “If losing a robot means avoiding the loss of a human life, then the robot ​can become expendable.”
An Honor humanoid robot falls apart next to Tiangong humanoid robots during a 100m large size group semifinals, at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games at the National Speed Skating Oval in Beijing, China, on August 25, 2026. REUTERS
China's defense ministry and the National University of Defense Technology (NUDT), the PLA’s premier research institution, didn’t respond to requests for comment about humanoid robots’ military applications.
Reuters found no evidence that China has deployed an armed humanoid with an operational ⁠PLA unit. The robots remain energy-intensive and unreliable outside controlled demonstrations. Battlefield environments pose many variables and challenge robots’ abilities in unpredictable ways, said Aaron Johnson, a professor of mechanical engineering at Carnegie Mellon University.
Urban assault force
Already, China has a vision for humanoid robots in urban warfare.
Six “combat robots” – humanoids, robot dogs or unmanned vehicles – would be ​split up between two assault teams. Working with ground troops, the robots would clear an enemy-occupied building, floor-by-floor and room-by-room.
That scenario was described in an August 2025 paper by researchers at NUDT’s test center in Xi’an. The study modeled an urban assault force using equipment the authors projected could be available within five to 10 years. ​It didn’t specify the robots’ rules of engagement, the weapons they would carry, nor how they would handle civilian encounters.
Improvements in balance, perception and endurance could make humanoids useful in places including buildings, tunnels and ship interiors, said Juo-Min Chou, a researcher at Taiwan's Institute for National Defense and Security Research. “Their two hands and two feet could, in theory, combine mobility, climbing and manipulation,” she said.
For simpler reconnaissance or logistics missions, however, quadruped, tracked or wheeled robots would generally be cheaper and easier to deploy at scale, Chou added.
Chinese military commentary envisions an expanding range of roles for humanoids. A July 2025 article in PLA Daily argued that humanoid missions could eventually evolve "from supporting combat toward primary combat" and discussed how robots might be authorized to fire on ​a living target that had been verified by a human.
In December, the PLA Eastern Theater Command released an AI-generated montage that showed military robots, including humanoids and quadrupeds, overwhelming Taiwan's defenses in a hypothetical future conflict.
China isn’t alone in exploring battlefield uses for humanoids. Last year, the US Army launched a competition to develop “militarized humanoid ​capabilities” that could eventually work alongside soldiers. The Army said potential roles included reconnaissance, security, obstacle clearing, hazardous-material operations and offensive and defensive missions in urban terrain. Up to 10 finalists were due to test their systems with U.S. military experts this year, with as much as $1.25 million available for follow-on contracts.
The US robotics industry, however, trails far behind China ‌in developing two-legged and ⁠four-legged machines. Reuters reported last month that China’s Unitree robots – among the world’s leading producers of humanoids and quadrupeds – based designs for its best-selling robot dogs on innovations financed by the U.S. military.
The Pentagon and the US Army didn’t comment for this story.
A humanoid robot traffic police officer developed by SUPCON stands on duty on a street in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province, China, July 21, 2026. REUTERS
Infiltrating enemy lines
Chinese interest in humanoid robots’ military applications began to pick up in 2024. That year, NUDT and China’s Academy of Military Sciences hosted a defense-technology forum that included a session on military applications for humanoid systems, according to NUDT’s website. Neither institution responded to Reuters’ questions.
A year later, NUDT explicitly framed humanoid robots as battlefield tools. A university competition in June 2025 featured an event that simulated “infiltration behind enemy lines,” requiring robots to enter an area, map it and locate targets, according to its website. Another envisioned robots conducting identity checks, discipline inspections and security patrols at military bases.
The military-research university described the competition in part as a proving ground for humanoids to eventually "move toward the battlefield."
Procurement records around that time reflected that ultimate goal.
In May 2025, the ​PLA issued a tender to purchase a humanoid robot, including installation and technical ​training. Four months later, a procurement notice that listed an NUDT email ⁠as its contact address sought an “embodied humanoid robot intelligent perception and dexterous operation system.”
The records contained few specifics. Reuters couldn’t determine whether the tenders were filled, and if so, which companies won or which robot models were supplied.
In June this year, the PLA budgeted about $300,000 for a system to collect and label camera, radar and motion data for humanoids, including information about terrain they could traverse, according to another military procurement document.
The specifications show Chinese military interest is extending from robot bodies into the ​perception, manipulation and training systems that defense scholars say are essential for humanoids to move beyond controlled demonstrations.
Remote operations
By 2026, humanoid development had spread beyond military academia into China's defense industry.
The Fuxi robot made by Norinco, a state-owned defense ​conglomerate, is one example. Company materials published in ⁠August described the full-size humanoid as capable of sentry duty, all-weather reconnaissance, intelligent patrol and fulfilling dangerous roles.
A Lightning humanoid robot by Honor crosses the finish line of the second Beijing E-Town Half Marathon and Humanoid Robot Half Marathon in Beijing, China April 19, 2026.
Fuxi can be paired with Norinco’s teleoperation system, which allows a human operator to control a humanoid remotely, according to the company. Removing the need for a robot to make all decisions autonomously would address what many robotics experts say is the biggest challenge with humanoids.
Norinco didn’t respond to a request for comment.
Malcolm Davis, a senior analyst at the Australian Strategic Policy Institute, said he didn’t see humanoid robots as practical battlefield systems at present. "But in five to 10 years,” he said, “they could very well be."
Even if remotely operated today, humanoid systems designed for autonomous deployment would eventually need to navigate ethical ⁠dilemmas. The laws of ​war require forces to distinguish combatants from civilians and to refrain from attacking wounded or surrendering fighters.
The International Committee of the Red Cross has cautioned that autonomous weapons may struggle to interpret signs of ​surrender reliably because such judgments can depend on context, conduct and intent.
The US military requires autonomous weapons to undergo legal review and realistic testing and for commanders and operators to exercise appropriate judgment over the use of force. China’s defense ministry said in March that AI-powered weapons should remain under human control.
Those concerns haven’t deterred China's exploration of humanoids’ military uses.
Wang Yonghua, a researcher at China’s Academy of ​Military Sciences, wrote in a November commentary that humanoids face unresolved problems in movement, perception and intelligence. Technical breakthroughs, lower manufacturing costs and industrial-scale production would be needed for humanoids to become widespread military systems.
If those conditions are met, Wang wrote, "humanoid robots will stream onto the battlefield."

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan concluded its participation at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh with a series of investment, cybersecurity, and technology partnership outcomes, as the country sought to strengthen its presence in the regional digital economy.
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja wrapped up her visit to the four-day event, held from August 31 to September 3, where Pakistan participated under the Tech Destination Pakistan banner.
The national pavilion featured 25 startups and more than 50 Pakistani technology companies, showcasing solutions in artificial intelligence, automation, and digital services while engaging with investors, government representatives, and technology firms from across the region.
Cybersecurity Cooperation With Saudi Arabia
One of the key outcomes of the visit was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding between Pakistan’s Ministry of IT and Telecommunication and Saudi Arabia’s National Cybersecurity Authority.
The agreement is aimed at strengthening cooperation on cybersecurity through the exchange of expertise and best practices, with a focus on addressing emerging digital threats.
During the conference, Khawaja also held bilateral meetings with senior officials from Saudi Arabia, South Korea, and Algeria, as well as representatives of the Digital Cooperation Organization and major Saudi technology institutions.
She also delivered a keynote titled “How We Built a Digital Nation,” highlighting Pakistan’s Digital Nation Pakistan Act, recent connectivity investments, the 5G spectrum auction, and reforms intended to attract technology investment.
Pakistani Startups Secure Investment and Regional Deals
LEAP 2026 also delivered tangible outcomes for Pakistani startups.
Edversity, an Ignite-supported startup, secured a $400,000 investment from Rapidev Group to support its international expansion and scale its AI-powered education platform.
Meanwhile, OfficeFlow AI signed an incubation partnership with Dhahran Techno Valley to expand its AI-powered business automation platform in the region. The startup also reached a deal with MIS Arabia, a Saudi technology services company serving major enterprise clients.
In addition, eight Pakistani startups graduated from the first cohort of AstroLabs LEAP, a 12-week soft-landing accelerator delivered through BridgeStart Pakistan, Ignite, and AstroLabs.
Pakistan’s participation in Riyadh was focused on attracting foreign investment, creating business-to-business partnerships, and expanding global market access for the country’s technology sector.
With LEAP 2026 now concluded, the agreements and investments secured during the event are expected to support deeper technology cooperation between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia while opening new regional opportunities for Pakistani startups and digital companies.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
United States President Donald Trump has shared a map on his Truth Social account that appears to depict much of North America and surrounding territories under the US flag, in the latest in a series of provocative posts involving geography and territorial claims.
The image shows the American flag covering the US as well as large parts of Canada, Greenland and Mexico, while US-style imagery also appears across other areas of the region. The post did not include an explanation from Trump.
The image comes a day after Trump shared another graphic that appeared to rename the US state of New Mexico as New America, with the word Mexico crossed out and replaced by America. The White House has not announced any formal effort to change the state's name.
Alongside the North America map, Trump posted several other similar images after the New Mexico graphic drew criticism from state officials.
New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham said on X that the state’s name “isn’t up for debate”, accusing Trump of “colouring on maps” while working families face rising fuel costs.
Senator Martin Heinrich said on X: “Three things I will always call by their actual names … The Gulf of Mexico, Lake Ontario, New Mexico.”
Three things I will always call by their actual names...
The Gulf of Mexico
Lake Ontario
New Mexico
— Martin Heinrich (@SenatorHeinrich) September 6, 2026
Representative Melanie Stansbury also rejected the idea, saying: “We’re New Mexicans. Period.”
Rep Gabe Vasquez said Trump could not “erase New Mexico”, its history or culture.
Trump has increasingly used geographic renaming and maps as part of his political messaging. In January 2025, he ordered the Gulf of Mexico to be referred to by the US government as the “Gulf of America”. On August 27, he signed an executive order directing federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario “Lake America”, a move that came amid sharply deteriorating relations with Canada.
The Trump administration has also pursued claims over Greenland, a self-governing territory of Denmark, prompting diplomatic tensions.
Washington's pressure on Cuba has also intensified, with the US imposing sanctions and maintaining a broader economic pressure campaign against Havana.

TECNO has expanded its CAMON lineup with the CAMON Slim 5G, adding faster connectivity, a larger battery, and upgraded camera hardware while retaining the ultra-thin 6.39 mm profile of the original CAMON Slim.
The biggest change is under the hood. TECNO has replaced the Helio G200 Ultimate used in the 4G version with MediaTek’s Dimensity 7300e, bringing 5G connectivity and improved performance.
Despite the slim design, the phone houses a 6000 mAh battery with 45 W fast charging. The regular CAMON Slim carries a smaller 5600mAh battery but supports faster 60W charging.
The CAMON Slim 5G features a 6.78-inch 1.5K AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate. Unlike the curved screen of the 4G model, TECNO has opted for a flat panel on the new version.
Upgraded Sony Camera and Rugged Protection
Photography also receives a notable upgrade. The CAMON Slim 5G uses Sony’s LYT-700C 1/1.56-inch main sensor, replacing the smaller LYT-600 sensor found on the 4G model. It supports 24mm, 35 mm, and 50mm portrait focal lengths, along with TECNO’s Super-Zoom FlashSnap feature. A 32MP camera handles selfies.
TECNO has also equipped the phone with IP66, IP68, IP69, and IP69K dust and water resistance. The device has undergone MIL-STD-810 testing and carries TÜV SÜD certification for long-term performance stability.
The CAMON Slim 5G runs HiOS 16 based on Android 16, with TECNO promising three major Android upgrades and five years of security updates.
Expected Price and Release Timeline in Pakistan
TECNO has not yet announced official Pakistan pricing or availability. However, based on its positioning within the CAMON lineup, the CAMON Slim 5G could arrive in the Rs. 68,999 to Rs. 84,999 range, depending on the memory configuration.
A Pakistan launch in late September or October 2026 appears plausible, although TECNO has yet to confirm a local release date.
In selected markets, the phone will also come with a three-month Google AI Plus subscription with 2TB of storage at no additional cost.

Huawei said the new chip design delivers greater computing power while using less electricity. The architecture, called LogicFolding, is part of ​the "Tau Scaling Law" principle unveiled in May as Huawei seeks to overcome US restrictions on access to advanced technology.
Xiaomi takes aim at Apple
At a separate launch event, Xiaomi unveiled its most premium phone to date, the Xiaomi 18 Fold. The device uses what Xiaomi calls a "medium-fold solution", remaining ​passport-sized when closed while supporting three apps side by side when opened.
The HarmonyOS operating system running on a Huawei Mate XT2 foldable smartphone displayed at a Huawei store in Beijing, China September 7, 2026. REUTERS
Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun said the device had several advantages ​over Apple products. Weighing 219 grams and measuring 5.02 mm thick when unfolded, the phone is lighter than Apple's iPhone Pro Max, he ‌said.
The handset ⁠runs Xiaomi's in-house XRing O3 AI processor, which Lei said outperforms Apple's A19 Pro in responsiveness. It also uses DRAM memory chips supplied by Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT .
The Xiaomi 18 Fold is priced from 10,999 yuan ($1,540) to 14,999 yuan ($2,100).
Read More: Musk pushes regulatory limits with Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi service
"Nowadays, memory is very, very expensive. We don't say it is cheap, but it is value for money," Lei said.
Samsung remains top foldable vendor
The launches come ​ahead of Apple's unveiling of its ​latest iPhone series on Wednesday, ⁠with expectations high that it could also introduce a foldable phone.
Huawei is currently the only major brand selling a so-called tri-fold phone. The Chinese tech giant is barred from selling products in ​the US, where Washington has deemed it a national security risk.
South Korea's Samsung Electronics (005930.KS), opens new tab, the ​world's biggest foldable ⁠smartphone vendor, launched a tri-fold device in December but reportedly discontinued sales after three months. In July, it expanded its foldable lineup to include a passport-sized foldable phone.
Huawei led China's smartphone market with a 22.6% share in the second quarter, ahead of Apple's 18.1%, according ⁠to consultancy ​IDC. Xiaomi held a 12.4% share.
Huawei was even more dominant in folding ​phones, accounting for 68% of shipments in China in the second quarter, according to US-based research company Smart Analytics Global.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday urged the people of Sindh to join the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf's September 27 protest, calling for a week-long shutdown of Karachi.
“I am inviting you to the September 27 protest. But you have to sit with us. You don't have to come to D-Chowk. Come with us to Karachi. For a week, Karachi should be closed. They will hold your feet. I am writing it down for you,” Afridi said while addressing lawyers at a convention held in Karachi under the Sindh High Court Bar Association.
Afridi’s convoy reached Karachi in the early hours of Monday after a journey of more than six hours. The PTI rally in Karachi was thrown into uncertainty on Sunday after authorities blocked several key arteries, causing massive traffic disruption across the city and delaying his arrival. However, Afridi vowed to reach Karachi and launch a street movement, saying he would not leave Sindh until the objective was achieved.
Afridi, along with PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, Karachi Bar Association President Aamir Nawaz and other leaders, addressed the convention. Lawyers were also present on the occasion.
Also Read: Sharjeel Memon lambasts 'Form 47' federal ministers over new provinces
Addressing the gathering, Afridi said the “tyrants” who considered themselves above the law would continue to prevail unless people stood up against them.
“But we have won only once. We have to try once. We have to stand up for ourselves and our children,” he said.
Afridi then spoke about PTI founder Imran Khan, saying there was no need to worry about him as he could be released within half an hour.
“Imran can sit in power. He can leave the country. His popularity is so high that no one can win elections against Imran. He can come back as prime minister. But he is not making a deal because he knows that leaders are born once in a century,” he said.
The K-P chief minister said Pakistan had never had a leader like Imran, adding that the PTI founder was not giving up despite the “cruel regime”.
“It is our duty to stand up for ourselves, for our children, for our Pakistan and for the people of Pakistan. On September 27, you will see the revolution of the people. You will see a sea,” Afridi said.
“ستائیس ستمبر کی کال پر آپ ہمارے ساتھ لبیک کہیں ڈی چوک آنے کی ضرورت نہیں کراچی میں نکلیں ،ایک ہفتے کے لیے کراچی بند ہو صرف ایک ہفتے کے لیے ،میں لکھ کے دیتا ہوں یہ آپ کے پاؤں پکڑیں گے ۔مسئلہ یہ ہے ہم ظلم سہتے جارہے ہیں اور یہ کرتے جارہے ہیں جس دن آپ نے ان کا ہاتھ پکڑا یہ آپ کے… pic.twitter.com/vFxbbBl56d
— PTI (@PTIofficial) September 7, 2026
He said people from across Pakistan would come out on September 27, claiming that no one would be able to win an election against PTI in Sindh for the next 30 years.
“The passion of the people that I have just seen in Sindh was not in K-P before 2013. This is something else. These are the scenes of the revolution. God willing, the time has come to change the history and destiny of Sindh,” he said.
Afridi further added that the “thieves” would run away from Sindh and that “only Imran will rule Sindh.”
The chief minister said the people of Sindh were brave, courageous and sincere, but were unfortunate to be ruled by what he described as “this kind of shamelessness”.
He said that while Bilawal Bhutto Zardari had welcomed him in a post on X, pits had allegedly been dug along the route and containers placed to block his way.
Afridi said Bilawal, as chairman of the party, perhaps had authority over Sindh’s ministers, but questioned how his directives could be ignored by those serving under him.
“Workers are being arrested. Our mothers and sisters are being disrespected here. Either there is someone else’s government in Sindh, or yours is not,” he said.
Read More: PTI's Barrister Gohar warns against dividing provinces without broad public consensus
The chief minister also said he had witnessed resentment among the people of Sindh over what he called the province’s “division”.
“So, I announce from here that I will stand with the people of Sindh, God willing. And a young tribal man also promises you that if blood has to be shed for the rights of Sindh, then the sea of Karachi will first taste the drop of blood of Sohail Afridi,” he said.
Afridi continued his criticism, saying that the two political families were “untouchable”.
“First the grandfather, then the daughter, then the husband, then the son, then the daughter, then the sister. Maybe there is something else, I don't know. You know better. First the brother, then his brother, then Nawaz Sharif, then Shehbaz Sharif, then Hamza Shehbaz, then Maryam Nawaz, and now their children,” Afridi said.
The chief minister contrasted this with K-P, saying that the province had an Imran-led government and that he himself had no political background.
“Who am I? I have no political background. I am middle class, like you, an ordinary young man who used to attend gatherings, travel in taxis, buses and rickshaws. I have come up through these roads, from the grassroots level of my political struggle. I am not even a relative of Imran,” Afridi said.
