items.author: Hasnaat Malik
items.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s remarks that the creation of new provinces or administrative units could ultimately be decided through public opinion have triggered a debate over whether a referendum can constitutionally be used to create new provinces.
Article 48(6) of the Constitution provides that if the prime minister considers it necessary to hold a referendum on any matter of national importance, he may refer the matter to a joint sitting of Parliament.
If approved by a joint sitting, the prime minister may cause the matter to be referred to a referendum in the form of a question capable of being answered by either “Yes” or “No.”
It has been learnt that a proposed constitutional amendment is under serious consideration, with around two dozen constitutional articles likely to be amended as part of a broader restructuring of the system.
Following strong resistance from the PPP to any division of Sindh and to proposals involving reconsideration of provincial autonomy, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday said the people would ultimately decide on the creation of provinces or new administrative units.
Constitutional experts believe Naqvi may be referring to a referendum as a means of ascertaining public opinion. However, they say a referendum itself cannot constitutionally create a new province, although a public vote could provide strong moral and democratic backing for such a move.
Advocate Abdul Moiz Jaferii said Article 239(4), by its very language, establishes a constitutional requirement that any amendment altering the limits of a province must first be passed by a two-thirds majority of the relevant provincial assembly before being presented for presidential assent.
“This procedure contains within it a second implied command: that this is the only way to alter the limits of a province,” he said. Jaferii further argued that where a specific constitutional provision exists, a general provision such as the power to hold a referendum cannot be used as a substitute for the prescribed constitutional procedure.
Read More: ‘Sindh is one, shall remain one’: Assembly passes resolution against division of province
“Also, when the federation can achieve its desired goal of more effective and localised administration through the empowerment of local government through adding flesh to the already existing Article 140A, it is hard to understand what they’re actually after here,” he said.
Jaferii said the division of Sindh would be a “minefield” that even the sturdiest of boots would find difficult to cross. “The PPP will be the least of their problems. It is the people of Sindh that reject the division of a boundary more ancient than our country, and one they look upon with pride and familial belonging. You disrespect this at your own peril,” he added.
Barrister Tariq Mahmood Khokhar pointed out that the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to alter the country’s internal geography, with affected states having no veto power.
“In Pakistan, Parliament alone cannot alter provincial boundaries. It is Parliament and the affected provincial assembly. The affected states have veto power,” he said.
Khokhar said there was no constitutional requirement for a national referendum on the creation of new provinces. However, he added that referenda could provide democratic legitimacy if conducted transparently, freely and fairly.
“We have a history of farcical referenda under General Zia and General Musharraf. A replication of the same may escalate Pakistan’s existential crisis,” he warned.
Khokhar further argued that the federal and provincial legislatures are products of Form 47, and their constitutional and democratic legitimacy is contested within Pakistan and abroad.
“Crucially, the proposed constitutional amendment through the existing assemblies will be seen as a coerced parliamentary fig leaf. In my opinion, the issue of more provinces be deferred to future legislative assemblies, elected by the people of Pakistan in free and fair elections,” he said.
Former federal minister Fawad Chaudhry said Mohsin Naqvi’s speech was “confused, vague, and riddled with contradictions.” He said Naqvi was criticising a political and administrative system of which he himself is a part, but has offered no clear plan or objective.
Chaudhry questioned how Naqvi could propose a referendum when, according to him, no major political party appeared willing to own the proposal.
“Citing examples of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and London Mayor Mohammad Sadiq, both products of local government, further obscures whether he supports empowered local government or new provinces,” he added.
Advocate Hafiz Ahsaan Ahmad Khokhar said Pakistan’s debate over new provinces should primarily be approached as a question of governance reform.
“Before initiating a proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment, Parliament and the prime minister could consider a referendum to ascertain the public pulse on additional provinces, stronger units and local governments. The people’s will provides moral authority,” he said. However, Khokhar stressed that a referendum could not replace the constitutionally prescribed procedure.
“Articles 238 and 239 prescribe constitutional amendment procedures, while Article 239(5) requires approval by not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the relevant Provincial Assembly where an amendment alters provincial limits.
Also Read: Naqvi vows not to back down from demand for new provinces, says decision must reflect public will
“Article 239(4) regulates the process. Accordingly, a public mandate under Article 48(6) would strengthen legitimacy, while creation of provinces must comply with Article 239. The people’s will provides authority for reform,” he said.
Khokhar said restructuring should not merely result in the creation of additional provincial capitals. Instead, its objective should be decentralisation through a strong federation, manageable provinces, empowered regions and effective local governments.
He noted that Article 140A requires provinces to establish local government systems and devolve political, administrative and financial responsibility and authority to elected representatives.
“Articles 141 and 142 regulate legislative competence; Articles 153 and 154 establish the Council of Common Interests framework; Article 160 provides for the National Finance Commission; and Articles 162 to 164 contain further financial and legislative provisions.
“These arrangements should be revisited to improve governance and service delivery,” he said.
Ahmad said new provinces could be justified in the public interest on the basis of population, geography, accessibility, viability, equitable development, identity and representation.
“Before triggering a 28th Amendment, consultation should ascertain the people’s will. The broader agenda must address justice, administration, accountability and service delivery.
“Outdated centralised arrangements can delay decisions and distance government from citizens. Public demand for change should be recognised,” he said.
He said the objective should be a governance compact combining new provinces, strong regions, empowered local governments, justice reform and modernised institutions.
Such reforms, he said, should strengthen Pakistan’s unity and constitutional integrity.
Political analyst Tahir Malik said remarks by PML-N leader Khawaja Saad Rafique reflected the view that the failure to allow the parliamentary system and the Constitution to function was one of the biggest reasons behind the system’s failure.
“Mohsin Naqvi has remained consistent with his earlier narrative that the system is not delivering and that it has failed, and he has identified all the factors contributing to this failure. This time, however, he appears to have gone a little more defensive in his speech,” Malik said.
He said there appeared to be a hint that the matter was moving towards a referendum.
“When they talk about the people, they also know that creating new provinces under the Constitution is a difficult process. Perhaps the intention is to seek the people’s opinion on the matter, and a referendum could be the means to do that,” Malik added.

Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy A18 4G has appeared in a new leak revealing its colors, storage options and several expected specifications.
Reliable tipster Roland Quandt says the phone will be available in light blue, black and silver, with 128GB and 256GB storage options. The full RAM lineup remains unknown, although a 4GB version has already appeared in testing.
Samsung Galaxy A18 4G128/256GBLight BlueBlackSilver
— Roland Quandt (@rquandt.bsky.social) 2026-09-02T13:17:13.599Z
Design and Display
CAD-based measurements put the Galaxy A18 4G at approximately 164.4 x 77.8 x 7.84mm, increasing to around 9.74mm when the rear camera bump is included.
That would make it about 0.34mm thicker than the Galaxy A17, while keeping almost the same overall dimensions.
The phone is expected to retain a 6.7-inch Super AMOLED display with a 90Hz refresh rate.
Samsung also appears to be keeping the familiar Infinity-U waterdrop notch for the front camera.
The rear triple-camera module closely resembles the Galaxy A17, although the pill-shaped camera housing appears to sit slightly more flush with the back panel.
Internals and Software
The Galaxy A18 4G is expected to use MediaTek’s 6nm Helio G99 chipset, continuing Samsung’s use of the processor in affordable A-series 4G phones.
Samsung moved to the Helio G99 after previously using the 12nm Helio G80 in the Galaxy A14.
A Geekbench listing showed the Galaxy A18 4G with an octa-core processor featuring two cores clocked at 2.2GHz and six cores at 2.0GHz, paired with 4GB of RAM.
The device reportedly scored around 744 points in Geekbench’s single-core test and 2,064 points in the multi-core test, putting performance close to the Galaxy A17 4G.
The same listing showed the phone running Android 17 with One UI 9.
Storage options are expected to include 128GB and 256GB, while additional RAM configurations have not yet been confirmed.
Cameras
The Galaxy A18 4G is expected to use a triple-camera system similar to its predecessor.
Current speculation points to a 50MP main camera, a 5MP ultrawide camera and a 2MP macro camera.
A 13MP front camera is also expected.
If accurate, the camera hardware would remain largely unchanged from the previous generation.
Battery and Pricing
The Galaxy A18 4G is widely expected to come with a 5,000mAh battery.
Samsung has not yet announced pricing, with official details expected in the coming weeks.
A separate Galaxy A18 5G is also expected to arrive later. That model may switch to a Qualcomm processor, replacing the Exynos 1330 used in the Galaxy A17 5G.
The 4G version appears likely to launch first and focus on basic smartphone use such as video streaming, social media, web browsing and online payments rather than major performance improvements.

items.author: Shazia Tasneem Farooqi
items.content:
Pakistan's rising cost of living is giving an old habit a new economic meaning: repair it rather than replace it.
From mobile phones and laptops to air-conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, and other household appliances, consumers are increasingly paying technicians to extend the lives of products once discarded or replaced.
For thousands of technicians, workshop owners and spare-parts dealers, this has created a business built on a simple proposition: when buying new is expensive, keeping the old one working makes better economic sense. But the activity is becoming more than a collection of small repair shops. It is overlapping with refurbishment, used-device trading, component recovery and e-waste recycling.
A 2026 study by 6Wresearch on Pakistan's e-waste recycling market provides a useful picture of this wider value chain. Its publicly available framework tracks component refurbishing alongside precious-metal recovery, plastics separation and battery processing. It covers IT and telecom equipment, consumer devices, appliances and EV components as waste sources.
The report is significant because it places refurbishment between conventional repair and recycling. An ageing device does not necessarily move directly from a consumer's home to a scrap dealer. It can pass through repair, parts replacement, refurbishment, resale and eventual recovery of its remaining materials.
Mobile phones get second life
A mobile technician may replace a damaged screen and return a phone to its owner. Another trader may buy a damaged handset, replace components and sell it as a refurbished device. Spare parts removed from one phone can become useful for another, while phones that cannot be economically repaired may still have value for their components.
The same principle applies to computers and appliances. A laptop with a faulty motherboard, a refrigerator with a damaged compressor or an air-conditioner requiring an expensive component does not become worthless. Technicians can recover usable parts, while traders buy non-working equipment for dismantling and resale.
"Users come to us with all kinds of problems, from slow charging and blank screens to storage issues, broken screens, faulty buttons and damaged charging ports," said Furqan Alvi, a mobile repair shop operator who also sells new devices.
For consumers, a repair bill may be a fraction of the price of a new appliance, particularly when the problem involves a replaceable component rather than the complete product.
Keeping computers alive
The repair market has adapted to changing consumer behaviour. Independent technicians increasingly operate through small workshops, home-based setups and social media pages, using messaging platforms to receive complaints, send repair estimates and arrange doorstep services.
A large number of home-based technicians operate across Karachi. Arshad Awan, who repairs desktop PCs and laptops, communicates with customers through WhatsApp and social media groups.
"People insist on getting their computers repaired for two basic reasons. One is to save their data and, most importantly, to avoid the cost of buying a new machine. They are even reluctant to buy a new adapter for smoother charging," Awan said. He said he could repair PCs and laptops of almost all brands and models. "I communicate through social media groups to find work, and people contact me. Sometimes work comes easily, while at other times I may have to wait for even a month."
Repair, trade and resell
The spare-parts trade forms another layer of this informal economy. Dealers stock new, used and salvaged components, while technicians depend on networks of suppliers to find parts for models no longer supported by manufacturers.
Another growing practice is the exchange of old mobile phones for new ones, with customers paying a relatively small amount to upgrade. The used phones are then resold, allowing older devices to move from one owner to another rather than entering the waste stream. This creates an ecosystem where the value of an old product is not determined only by whether it still works. Its screen, battery, motherboard, compressor, motor or power supply may each have a separate resale value.
For some businesses, the next step is refurbishment
Recently, Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan said Samsung had proposed establishing certified mobile-phone refurbishment facilities in Pakistan. The government said a regulated refurbishment ecosystem could strengthen local industry, create employment, build technical expertise and generate opportunities to export refurbished devices.
Samsung also proposed replacing commercial imports of used phones with certified refurbished devices produced through authorised facilities and backed by quality assurance and warranties. The proposal gives a formal-industry dimension to a trade largely developed outside organised manufacturing.
If certified refurbishment facilities emerge, Pakistan could move from importing and repairing used electronics towards repairing and refurbishing devices locally, adding value before resale or export.
The environmental case is equally important
Pakistan's Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination has warned that the country lacks comprehensive baseline data on the scale, sources and handling of e-waste. The ministry said in 2025 that roughly 500,000 tonnes of e-waste are generated annually and that much of it is handled through informal and unsafe channels. It has called for formal collection and recycling systemsand a national framework for e-waste management. The ministry has also noted that discarded mobile phones, computers, televisions and household appliances are often dumped, burned or dismantled informally. At the same time, many products can be reused, refurbished or recycled.
This creates a difficult paradox. The informal repair economy keeps products in use for longer and prevents some equipment from becoming waste, but the same informal system can become environmentally hazardous when products reach the end of their useful lives and are dismantled without proper safeguards.
The opportunity is not simply to formalise every neighbourhood repair shop. It is to connect the different parts of the chain.
A more organised system could allow consumers to hand over unwanted devices, technicians to recover usable components, refurbishers to restore working products and authorised recyclers to recover materials from equipment that can no longer be repaired.
For Pakistan's small businesses, this could turn an activity traditionally viewed as low-end informal work into a more structured service industry. For consumers, it means a broken product can remain useful for longer. For manufacturers, refurbishment could create a new channel for devices that would otherwise enter the used market without quality controls. And for the environment, every additional year that a repairable product remains in use delays its journey into the waste stream.
The 6Wresearch study forecasts Pakistan's e-waste recycling market through 2032, covering component refurbishing, recycling and recovery activities as the sector develops into a broader commercial value chain. The repair economy may therefore be telling a bigger story about Pakistan's consumption pattern: as replacement becomes harder to afford, the country is learning to extract more value from the products it already owns.
What began as a neighbourhood technician fixing a broken phone or appliance could eventually become part of a larger circular economy – one in which the first business is repair, the next is refurbishment, and the final value lies in recovering whatever remains.

items.title: Geopolitical tensions drag stocks down
items.summary:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its losing streak during the outgoing week, with the KSE-100 Index shedding 1.3% week-on-week to close at 175,329 points, as renewed US-Iran tensions and higher crude oil prices kept investors on the defensive.
The index remained under pressure despite intermittent support from corporate earnings and local buying, recording declines in the first half of the week before recovering modestly in the final two sessions.

On Tuesday, the bourse kicked off September and saw investors walking on a tightrope. The index fell 508.69 points, or 0.29%, to settle at 176,466.99.

Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) extended its losing streak during the outgoing week, with the KSE-100 Index shedding 1.3% week-on-week to close at 175,329 points, as renewed US-Iran tensions and higher crude oil prices kept investors on the defensive.
The index remained under pressure despite intermittent support from corporate earnings and local buying, recording declines in the first half of the week before recovering modestly in the final two sessions.
On a day-on-day basis, the PSX commenced trading week with a consolidation session, where the KSE-100 declined 721 points (-0.41%) to close at 176,976. On Tuesday, the bourse kicked off September and saw investors walking on a tightrope. The index fell 508.69 points, or 0.29%, to settle at 176,466.99.
Geopolitics weighed on market sentiment on Wednesday. The PSX registered a negative session, declining 1,690 points (-0.96%) to close at 174,777. Thursday was a flattish day, when the index edged higher by 153 points (+0.09%) to 174,930. Friday marked modest gains as the KSE-100 rose 399 points (+0.23%) to close the week at 175,329.
Arif Habib Limited (AHL), in its report, noted that the KSE-100 consolidated its position amid renewed US-Iran tensions, with support from corporate earnings partly offsetting a cautious investor stance. The index closed at 175,329 points, down 1.3% week-on-week.
Among major economic developments, AHL mentioned, the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) collected Rs902 billion in August 2026 (+2% year-on-year), falling Rs28 billion short of the Rs930 billion target, while 2MFY27 collection stood at Rs1,722 billion (+5% YoY), Rs12 billion above the Rs1,710 billion target.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for August clocked in at 11.15% YoY compared to 9.2% in July. Fitch Ratings assigned Pakistan's proposed US dollar bond and MTN programme a 'B' rating with an 'RR4' recovery rating, indicating average recovery prospects.
Oil marketing companies' (OMC) sales declined 3% YoY to 1.26 million tons in August 2026, driven by high-speed diesel (+32%) and motor spirit (-9%) demand amid higher fuel prices. Month-on-month, sales fell 16%. Refinery supplies surged 32.2% YoY to 964k tons in August, driven by strong MS, HSD and furnace oil demand, but declined 15.7% MoM due to lower OMC purchases amid higher domestic prices. For 2MFY27, refinery sales rose 40.2% YoY to 2,107k tons.
Naya Nazimabad Apartments REIT saw an exceptional 8x oversubscription, achieving the upper price ceiling of Rs23 and raising Rs1 billion in equity, said AHL. T-bill auction yields declined across most tenors, with the government raising Rs680.1 billion against the target of Rs800 billion, mainly through the three-month tenor at Rs387.8 billion.
Pakistan posted a $3.2 billion trade deficit in August, with exports up 3.8% YoY to $2.5 billion and imports up 7.4% YoY to $5.7 billion. Urea offtake declined 14% YoY in August to 701k tons, with Engro Fertilisers the only player posting growth (+18% YoY), while 8MCY26 offtake remained broadly flat at 3.79 million tons. Cement dispatches rose 3% YoY in 2MFY27, despite August sales declining by 1% YoY to 4.04 million tons amid softer domestic demand, as per AHL.
Topline Securities, in its weekly review, noted that continuing its downward momentum, the KSE-100 index dipped by 1% WoW, primarily driven by escalating US-Iran tensions and higher crude oil prices. Major developments during the outgoing week were Pakistan's CPI for August 2026 clocking in at 11.1% compared with July CPI of 9.2%, trade deficit for August coming in at $3.2 billion (up 10% YoY but down 20% MoM) and the government raising $3 billion through dual-tranche Eurobond for five- and 10-year tenors at 7.5% and 7.9%, respectively.
Individuals and local companies were largely buyers in the market as they purchased net equities worth $15 million and $5.7 million, respectively, as of Friday's close, whereas mutual funds and foreign corporates were major sellers, as they sold net equities worth $15 million and $10.2 million, respectively. Average daily traded volume and value during the week stood at 767 million shares and Rs33 billion, respectively, Topline said.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) President Atif Ikram Sheikh has called for revamping and effectively implementing the ECO Trade Agreement (ECOTA) to enhance intra-regional trade and transform the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) region into a more integrated and competitive economic bloc, a statement said on Saturday.
The ECO region currently accounts for only around 4% of global trade, while intra-regional trade stands at approximately 8.75%, significantly below its actual potential, Sheikh said.
The region possesses enormous economic advantages, including vast hydrocarbon and mineral resources, a young and skilled population, strategic road and rail connectivity linking Asia with Europe, and proximity to major markets such as China, India and Russia. However, high tariffs and non-tariff barriers, limited product diversification, difficulties in trade-related payments and regulatory differences continue to constrain regional trade.
Sheikh recalled that ECOTA was signed in 2003 and entered into force in April 2008 with the objective of establishing an ECO Free Trade Area. However, differences in tariff structures, incomplete product lists and concerns regarding equitable benefits have hindered its effective implementation.
"ECOTA should not remain merely an agreement on paper. We need to address the outstanding issues through sustained negotiations and develop a framework that provides balanced and equitable benefits to all member states," the ECO CCI president stated.
He proposed a balanced approach to tariff reductions, greater product diversification and investment to enhance regional competitiveness, and stronger mechanisms for trade-related payments. He also emphasised reducing transaction costs, improving regulatory transparency, facilitating e-commerce and digital trade, and developing regional transport and logistics infrastructure.
Sheikh further suggested utilising the resources of the ECO Trade and Development Bank to support trade finance and regional infrastructure projects.
He stressed that Pakistan, as an active member of ECO and ECO CCI, would continue supporting initiatives aimed at strengthening regional economic integration. "The ECO region has all the ingredients of a powerful economic bloc. What we need is stronger commitment, practical trade facilitation and a modernised ECOTA to convert our vast resources and strategic location into greater trade, investment and shared economic prosperity," he said.

Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI) President Sardar Tahir Mehmood has called on the business community, philanthropists and overseas Pakistanis to join hands in expanding quality education and skills development for children in Balochistan, stressing that investing in the province's youth is investment in a stronger and more prosperous Pakistan.
Speaking at a programme organised under the auspices of the ICCI, in collaboration with Al Hijrah Schools Trust and Win Win Marketing, Mehmood said Balochistan was a critically important matter for Pakistan and for the development of the province, society must go "two steps further" in extending its fullest support.
The ICCI president also said that Pakistan, with a population of around 250 million, offered enormous opportunities for investment and economic partnerships. Referring to his recent visit to Turkiye, he revealed that foreign investors were showing growing interest in Pakistan because of its large consumer market, workforce, tariff concessions and comparatively lower operating costs.
He expressed hope that the business community, overseas Pakistanis and philanthropists would come forward to strengthen the Trust's educational mission, particularly in Balochistan.
Al Hijrah Founder Abdul Kareem Saqib highlighted the Trust's journey from its establishment in Birmingham, UK, in 1988 to its expansion into Pakistan. Al Hijrah was initially established to provide Muslim children living abroad with an educational environment combining Islamic values with modern learning.
He said the Trust subsequently came to Pakistan and in 2001 entered into an agreement with the government of Balochistan to establish its educational project in the province.

How Much Will Students Pay?
The total cost of each electric bike is listed at PKR 199,000, while the cost payable by the student is PKR 109,000.
Students will pay this amount through a 36-month installment plan, with the monthly installment set at PKR 3,028. The government will cover the insurance, mark-up and registration costs, reducing the overall financial burden on students.

Students can submit their applications through the official CM Punjab Electric Bike Scheme portal:
bikes.punjab.gov.pk

Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Saturday said the peace, prosperity and well-being of the people of Balochistan were core to the state’s efforts, according to the military’s media wing.
The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said Field Marshal Munir visited Quetta Garrison and interacted with commanders and commanding officers of field formations.
He reaffirmed that the peace, prosperity and well-being of the people of Balochistan remained central to the state’s efforts.
“ A stable and secure environment would continue to facilitate development initiatives, economic opportunities and improved prospects for the people of the province,” he said.
During the visit, he was given a comprehensive briefing on the prevailing security situation, operational preparedness and measures being taken to maintain peace and stability across the province.
Read: 48 terrorists killed in IBOs across Balochistan over 72 hours: ISPR
Matters relating to institutional coordination and support for the socio-economic development of Balochistan were also reviewed, the statement said.
The army chief appreciated the professionalism, operational readiness and selfless commitment of the troops.
He underscored the importance of continued coordination among law enforcement agencies and other state institutions to consolidate peace and maintain an environment conducive to sustained economic activity and development.
Field Marshal Munir also paid tribute to the sacrifices of the martyrs and appreciated the dedication of officers and troops in the discharge of their duties.
He was received earlier on arrival by the Quetta Corps commander.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022, and over the same period, TTP attacks increased more than sevenfold to 838 from 118.
Although Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
The forces continued operations across the provinces against what the state describes as Indian-sponsored terrorists and their proxies, but despite these efforts, the groups have continued to target civilian and defence installations.
In one such operation earlier this week, security forces killed 48 "Indian sponsored terrorists" in intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan.
In another operation, security forces killed 21 terrorists in a series of operations in Balochistan’s Chagai and Pishin districts and at Ziarat Cross. Six security personnel, including two officers, and a Customs official were also martyred during the engagements.

items.summary:
India Women demolished Pakistan by seven wickets in their Group A match of the Women's Asia Cup at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium thanks to Shree Charani’s devastating spell.
Charani returned figures of 3-7 from four overs as Pakistan, after choosing to bat, collapsed from 27-1 to 35-6 and were eventually dismissed for just 55 in 18.1 overs.
India needed only 8.4 overs to overhaul the modest target, reaching 57-3 with Harmanpreet Kaur unbeaten on 18 and Deepti Sharma on 12.
Pakistan made a reasonable start before their innings unravelled dramatically. Muneeba Ali struck 13 from 15 balls and Shawaal Zulfiqar made run-a-ball 14, but neither could build a substantial partnership.
Charani broke through when she trapped Zulfiqar lbw, and the spinner struck again in the same over when Gull Feroza was caught for a duck.
Ayesha Zafar fell to Charani soon afterwards, leaving Pakistan at 29-4 after 5.6 overs.

items.content:
India Women demolished Pakistan by seven wickets in their Group A match of the Women's Asia Cup at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium thanks to Shree Charani’s devastating spell.
Charani returned figures of 3-7 from four overs as Pakistan, after choosing to bat, collapsed from 27-1 to 35-6 and were eventually dismissed for just 55 in 18.1 overs.
India needed only 8.4 overs to overhaul the modest target, reaching 57-3 with Harmanpreet Kaur unbeaten on 18 and Deepti Sharma on 12.
Pakistan made a reasonable start before their innings unravelled dramatically. Muneeba Ali struck 13 from 15 balls and Shawaal Zulfiqar made run-a-ball 14, but neither could build a substantial partnership.
Charani broke through when she trapped Zulfiqar lbw, and the spinner struck again in the same over when Gull Feroza was caught for a duck.
Ayesha Zafar fell to Charani soon afterwards, leaving Pakistan at 29-4 after 5.6 overs.
The pressure intensified as India's bowlers attacked relentlessly. Prema Rawat claimed three wickets for nine runs, while Deepti Sharma took two for five. Shafali Verma also chipped in with the wicket of Muneeba.
Pakistan's lower order offered little resistance. Fatima Sana was trapped lbw by Deepti without scoring, while Eyman Fatima was run out for five.
By the time Umm-e-Hani and Nashra Sandhu departed, Pakistan were 54-9. Tuba Hassan's dismissal for nine ended the innings at 55.
Charani's four-over spell was particularly economical, conceding fewer than two runs an over while accounting for three of Pakistan's top-order batters.
India's chase began explosively but briefly threatened to become interesting when captain Fatima Sana removed Shafali Verma and then struck twice more.
Shafali smashed 12 from just six balls, including a four and a six, before being caught and bowled for the first wicket.
Pratika Rawal followed for four and Smriti Mandhana was dismissed for nine, leaving India 29-3 after 3.6 overs.
Pakistan, however, could not sustain the pressure.
Kaur steadied the innings with an unbeaten 18 from 18 balls, including a four and a six, while Deepti provided calm support with an unbeaten 12 from 14.
The pair saw India home without further damage, sealing victory with 68 balls to spare.

items.summary:
The Pakistan Airports Authority has formally approved minimum wages for outsourced employees, according to ARY News.
The authority has fixed the minimum pay for outsourced staff at Rs40,700, with the new wage structure applicable from July 1 after the federal government’s wage increase of Rs3,700.
PAA has directed outsourced contractors to ensure the revised salary is paid to all concerned employees.
All outsourced workers, including security personnel, will now receive a monthly salary of Rs40,700.
The new wage will be mandatory for all existing and extended outsourcing agreements.
Contractors have also been instructed to ensure EOBI and social security payments are made for the employees.
Separately, the Civil Aviation Authority and the Pakistan Airports Authority are set to be shifted from Karachi to Islamabad.
Their headquarters will move from Karachi Airport to Islamabad Airport, while a temporary headquarters will be set up at Islamabad Airport for the immediate transfer process.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Motorola is reportedly preparing to launch a wide foldable smartphone later this year, joining Samsung, Huawei and Xiaomi in the growing wide-screen foldable category.
Samsung introduced its first wide foldable, the Galaxy Z Fold8, in July, while Huawei followed with the Pura X View in August. Xiaomi is also preparing to unveil the Xiaomi 18 Fold on September 7.
Android Headlines now reports that Motorola will enter the same category with a new wide foldable expected to arrive “in the coming months.”
The publication has not revealed the phone’s name but shared several design sketches showing what the device could look like.
Two Possible Designs
The leaked sketches show two slightly different versions of Motorola’s upcoming foldable.
Both designs feature a horizontally positioned rear camera island with three circular cutouts. One version places one of the cutouts outside the camera island, while the other keeps all three inside.
The back panel is expected to use 3D glass, while the camera module features what the sketches describe as metal decoration.
Motorola branding is also visible on the hinge.
Slim Body and Creaseless Display
The sketches describe the phone as having a bezel-less design, an “easy-open profile,” an “ultra-slim housing,” and a “creaseless display.”
The main folding display includes a selfie camera in the top-right corner.
The outer display also has a selfie camera, positioned inside a centered punch-hole.
Camera Layout Still Unclear
The rear of the phone features three circular openings, but it is not yet clear whether all three are camera sensors.
One of the cutouts could instead house an LED flash or another type of sensor.
No additional information about the camera specifications has been revealed.
What We Know About the Hardware
The report does not provide details about the chipset, RAM, storage, battery, or software.
Motorola already offers the Razr Fold, its first book-style smartphone with a horizontally folding design, but the upcoming device would use the wider form factor shown in the leaked sketches.
Expected Launch
Android Headlines’ source says Motorola’s wide foldable will arrive “in the coming months,” although no specific launch date has been provided.
For comparison, Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8 starts at $1,899.99 for the 12GB RAM and 256GB storage model, while the 12GB RAM and 512GB version costs $2,099.99.
More details about Motorola’s upcoming wide foldable are expected closer to its launch.

items.author: Anadolu Agency
items.content:
Israeli officials, with the support of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, are obstructing the implementation of US President Donald Trump’s plan to end the war on the Gaza Strip, according to Israeli daily Haaretz.
In a report headlined “The Gaza deal is stuck. For those involved, the reasons are clear: Netanyahu and the elections,” the newspaper said on Friday that Israeli security officials are refusing to cooperate with Trump’s Board of Peace.
“The gap between the American vision for the Gaza Strip and the results on the ground has never been clearer than it is now, and neither has the gap between the US and Israel,” it said.
The Gaza agreement remains “stuck” nearly a year after a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas was announced, with less than two months remaining before elections in Israel and US midterm elections, the daily added.
Haaretz, citing an unnamed source familiar with the issue, said there was “mutual frustration between the Board of Peace and the Israeli establishment”.
Israeli officials, including members of the National Security Council and the Defense Ministry as well as officers in the army’s Southern Command, are openly refusing to cooperate with the board, according to the source.
“They are not even trying to hide it anymore. They say: We will not cooperate with you because you threw us under the bus,” the source said.
The statement referred to a 15-point document issued by the Board of Peace on July 30, which calls for the disarmament of Hamas and other Palestinian factions, the transfer of Gaza’s administration to a national Palestinian committee and a phased Israeli withdrawal.
Netanyahu rejected the roadmap on Aug 9, insisting that the factions be fully disarmed before any Israeli withdrawal.
Israeli officials told US diplomats that Washington had taken them “for granted”, the source said.
They also criticised the roadmap and expressed concern that its implementation would make the government appear as though it was “selling out Israel”, according to Haaretz.
Netanyahu’s support
The source described Israel’s obstruction of Trump’s plan as an established “approach", saying the Board of Peace understands that it is linked to the approaching Israeli elections and is supported at the highest level by Netanyahu.
Israel is scheduled to hold elections for the Knesset, or parliament, on Oct 27, amid declining poll numbers for Netanyahu and his Likud party.
Haaretz said another element of this approach was Israel’s obstruction of the departure of thousands of Gazans recruited by the technocratic committee tasked with managing Gaza to serve in a new police force in the enclave.
Israel has prevented the recruits from leaving Gaza for training in Egypt, according to the report.
The Board of Peace also fears that even if they are allowed to leave, Israel could prevent them from returning after completing their training, citing security concerns, the source said.
The technocratic body, formally known as the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, was established in January under Palestinian official Ali Shaath to oversee civilian affairs, security and essential services during the transitional period.
Trump-Netanyahu relations
A second unnamed source told Haaretz that relations between Trump and Netanyahu were “extremely poor”, adding that very little remained of their previously close relationship.
Read More: Israeli ministers call for Gaza expulsion
Trump announced a 20-point plan to end the Gaza war on Sept 29, 2025. It included the release of Israeli captives, the disarmament of Hamas, a partial Israeli withdrawal, the formation of a technocratic administration and the deployment of an international stabilisation force.
The first phase of the plan took effect on Oct 10, 2025.
While Hamas fulfilled the requirements of the first phase, Israel reneged on its commitments and continued its attacks.
Despite Israel’s failure to honour the agreement, Trump announced in mid-January the start of the plan’s second phase, which is backed by UN Security Council Resolution 2803, adopted on Nov 17, 2025.
The second phase calls for a broader Israeli military withdrawal, reconstruction and the start of the disarmament process.
Israel, however, continues to occupy about 70% of the Gaza Strip and insists that Palestinian factions must disarm before it withdraws.
The agreement followed two years of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, which began on Oct 8, 2023, and has since continued in various forms.
The Israeli offensive has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians, injured over 174,000 others and caused widespread destruction affecting about 90% of Gaza’s civilian infrastructure.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz came under fire on Saturday after her remarks that Punjab faced a greater security threat from other provinces than neighbouring countries triggered widespread criticism and concerns over the widening provincial divide.
The remarks, made at the e-launching ceremony of the Artificial Intelligence Hub in Lahore, triggered criticism, particularly from opposition figures, who accused the chief minister of targeting Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa and undermining provincial harmony.
The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI), the main opposition party, hit out at the chief minister, alleging that her remarks reflected an intention to “break Pakistan apart”.
In a post on X, the party said: “Love for India always wells up from the hearts of the Sharif family, while harboring hatred for their own smaller provinces.”
شریف خاندان کے دلوں سے ہمیشہ بھارت کے لیے پیار ابھر کر نکلتا ہے اور اپنے ہی چھوٹے صوبوں کے لیے نفرت۔ پنجاب کی جعلی وزیراعلی آج کھل کر اس بات کا اظہار کررہی ہے کہ اس کو انڈیا سے نہیں اپنے پڑوسی صوبوں سے خطرہ ہے ۔ ان کی نیت ایک بار پھر پاکستان کو توڑنے کی ہے۔
پاکستان کا اصل دشمن… pic.twitter.com/vjCeuppBPj
— PTI (@PTIofficial) September 5, 2026
The PTI said it was “extremely regrettable and irresponsible” for a provincial leader to describe neighbouring provinces within Pakistan as a threat.
“When a provincial leader, instead of fostering unity and solidarity with their own compatriots, fuels hatred and division against them, it shakes the foundations of the federation,” it said.
The party also criticised what it described as the Sharif family’s approach towards India and alleged that their policies had raised questions about their attitude towards the country’s smaller provinces.
It said that if the provinces and people of one’s own country began appearing as “enemies and threats”, the issue lay “not in the neighboring provinces, but in your own mindset and priorities”.
The party also questioned how threats to Pakistan were being defined, alleging that the country’s “real enemy” was being determined according to the preferences of what it called “power-hungry individuals”.
The PTI argued that the appearance of Pakistan’s own provinces and people as “enemies and threats” should prompt a reassessment of the government’s priorities.
“If the units of your own country and your own people start appearing as enemies and threats to you, then the problem lies not in the neighboring provinces, but in your own mindset and priorities,” it said.
Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Ayeen-e-Pakistan (TTAP) Punjab Chief Organiser Ammar Ali Jan and Information Secretary Shayan Bashir condemned the remarks they said blamed Pakistan’s own provinces for terrorism, calling the statement “not merely regrettable but dangerous”.
They said the chief minister had told a public gathering in Lahore that the threat to Punjab came less from across the border than from the provinces alongside it.
Jan said alienation among young people in the smaller provinces was already deepening due to years of political deprivation and injustice. He said linking entire provinces to terrorism would fan hatred and prejudice.
He added that such remarks could play into the hands of elements seeking to destabilise Pakistan.
Bashir said it was “a particular arrogance” for a chief minister whom he described as having been installed on a disputed mandate to cast suspicion on provinces where, he claimed, the people’s verdict was respected.
He alleged that the PML-N leadership was trying to divide people along provincial lines to revive what he called “dying politics”, adding that people would no longer be misled by attempts to stoke hatred.
The TTAP leaders said Punjab’s leadership had a particular responsibility not to speak about smaller provinces in a language of suspicion and demanded that the chief minister withdraw her remarks.
“This country is held together by the Constitution and by equal citizenship, not by sorting provinces into the trusted and the suspected,” they said.
Qaiser calls remarks ‘insulting’
Former National Assembly speaker and senior PTI leader Asad Qaiser also condemned CM Maryam's remarks, describing them as insulting towards K-P.
“Maryam Nawaz’s insulting and sarcastic statement regarding Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is extremely shameful and reprehensible,” Qaiser wrote in a post on X.
He said K-P had been confronting terrorism for several decades and that its people had paid the heaviest price in the war against terrorism.
مریم نواز کا خیبر پختونخوا کے حوالے سے توہین آمیز اور طنزیہ بیان انتہائی شرمناک اور قابلِ مذمت ہے۔ خیبر پختونخوا گزشتہ کئی دہائیوں سے دہشت گردی کے عفریت کا سامنا کر رہا ہے اور اس جنگ کی سب سے بھاری قیمت اسی صوبے کے عوام نے ادا کی ہے۔ آپ کے چچا کی موجودہ وفاقی حکومت اور میاں نواز…
— Asad Qaiser (@AsadQaiserPTI) September 5, 2026
He criticised successive federal governments for what he described as flawed and failed policies, arguing that the people of K-P continued to suffer the consequences of decisions taken by successive administrations.
“Thousands of families were uprooted, millions of people were displaced, businesses were destroyed, and an entire generation spent their lives in fear, unrest and insecurity,” Qaiser said.
He recalled the mass displacement caused by military operations in areas including Waziristan, Bajaur, Swat, Buner, Lower Dir and Shangla, saying millions of people had been forced to leave their homes during periods of conflict while also highlighting the sacrifices of the K-P Police in the fight against terrorism.
“Instead of acknowledging these countless sacrifices and providing solace to the wounds of the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the families of martyrs and the police personnel, mocking and ridiculing their hardships not only demonstrates political insensitivity but is also an extremely lamentable stance at the national level,” Qaiser said.
He urged CM Maryam to recognise the contribution of K-P residents and law-enforcement personnel to the country’s fight against terrorism and to show greater sensitivity towards families affected by the conflict.
“Maryam Nawaz should, instead of taunting the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, acknowledge their sacrifices, pay tribute to the martyrs and ghazis of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police, and respect the affected families,” he said.
‘Divisive and derogatory’
Former PML-N senator Mushahid Hussain Sayed also criticised the statement, describing it as divisive and derogatory towards K-P.

— Mushahid Hussain Sayed (@Mushahid) September 5, 2026
In a post on X, he called it a “shockingly chauvinistic statement” that was “highly divisive and derogatory” and reflected “ignorance and arrogance”.
He argued that the people of K-P were among the biggest victims of terrorism, while, in his view, India had been “conveniently exonerated”.
PPP's Raisani questions CM’s thinking
Pakistan Peoples Party leader and National Assembly member from Balochistan Jamal Khan Raisani also questioned the chief minister’s assessment of the threat.
“Punjab is not threatened by neighboring provinces or the people living there. It is threatened by your thinking,” he wrote on X.
He urged the Punjab government to improve border management instead of “profiling” people coming from other provinces.
پنجاب کو پڑوسی صوبوں اور وہاں بسنے والے لوگوں سے نہیں۔ آپ کی سوچ سے خطرہ ہے۔ دیگر صوبوں سے آنے والے لوگوں کی غیر ضروری پروفائلنگ کرنے کے بجائے صوبے کے بارڈر منیجمنٹ کو بہترکریں۔ سی پیک کے اعلان کے بعد نواز شریف نے بلوچستان کے طلبا کیلیے اسکالرشپس کا اعلان کیا جو اب نصف سے بھی کم… pic.twitter.com/SMdbOGHbUc
— Nawabzada Jamal Khan Raisani (@JamalRaisani) September 5, 2026
Raisani also raised the issue of scholarships for students from Balochistan, saying that after the announcement of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, former prime minister Nawaz Sharif had announced scholarships for Balochistan students, but that these had subsequently been reduced.
He further alleged that, during a meeting, a response involving wheat had placed students from Balochistan “in the ranks of terrorists”.
Zulfi Bukhari calls remarks ‘beyond politics’
PTI leader Zulfi Bukhari also condemned the statement, describing it as going beyond political differences and alleging that it was an attempt to divide the country.
In a post on X, he said the “latest venom is beyond politics; it is an attempt to divide and tear the country apart”.
He argued that progress and prosperity required a “complete vision for the country as a whole”, rather than divisive politics.
Father and daughter have always gone to extraordinary lengths to defend India backed terrorism even at the cost of pitting one Pakistani province against another. But this latest venom is beyond politics; it is an attempt to divide and tear the country apart.
At a time when… https://t.co/SbMbJHl8ib

Shameful to blame #Pakhtunkhwa, victim of terrorism, for terrorism in #Punjab while deliberately shutting eyes to the death, destruction & mass displacement inflicted on the province by the State’s anti-#Pashtun… https://t.co/Wn5TTUOaNI

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Saturday said the province faced a greater security threat from “neighbouring provinces than from neighbouring countries”, stressing that terrorism entered Punjab through its provincial borders and calling for greater coordination, intelligence sharing, and the use of modern technology to address it.
Addressing the e-launching ceremony of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Hub in Lahore, the chief minister said Punjab was facing a rapidly evolving security situation and vulnerabilities across several areas, including terrorism, ethnic and religious conflicts and organised crime.
“As you can see, I am from a tri-border area. I am sorry to say that the threat is less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces. Terrorism comes from there to Punjab. Everyone has an eye on Punjab,” she said.
She, however, described Punjab as a safe province and said the provincial government had invested billions of rupees in technology to strengthen security.
“I am happy to share that Punjab is now the most AI-enabled province and not only the most AI-enabled province, it is the most technology-enabled province,” she said.
The chief minister said the AI hub would facilitate intelligence fusion, real-time information-sharing, threat anticipation and the study of emerging patterns, allowing the provincial government and law enforcement agencies to respond to potential threats before they developed into incidents.
“There is a rapidly evolving security situation in Pakistan, and there are a lot of vulnerabilities in many areas,” she said, adding that the province faced not only terrorism but also ethnic and religious conflicts, organised crime and the spread of drugs.
She said federal and provincial law enforcement and intelligence agencies had worked as “one unit” in challenging situations, stressing that Punjab had consistently demonstrated a unified response.
“Whenever there is such a situation in Punjab which demands unity, which demands coordination, which demands support across the departments, Punjab has always been the only province which has a very unified response, which has a government of one unit, and all the other departments work together,” she said.
Maryam said the government had strengthened checkposts and joint checkposts in the tri-border areas through technology and fortification.
“When I became the Chief Minister, I saw that the most technologically advanced terrorists had night-vision cameras. They used to come with a lot of planning. Now, thanks to Allah, we have that system,” she said.
She said cameras had been bulletproofed, and thermal cameras and drones had also been deployed.
“We have spent money on fortifying our check-posts and joint check-posts so that our people are safe,” she said, adding that while attacks still occurred, casualties had been reduced, according to her, because of investment in technology and fortification.
The chief minister recalled that checkposts had previously lacked adequate protection, saying security personnel had been sitting behind makeshift barriers. She said they now had high walls and safe rooms where personnel could take shelter during attacks.
She also highlighted the government’s actions in the Kaccha areas, which she described as having previously been a hub of terror and crime, with kidnapping for ransom a daily occurrence.
“Thanks to Allah, we have received support from the military, the Punjab government, and the Sindh government. Kaccha is now a crime-free area,” she said, adding that the writ of the state had been established in the area.
The chief minister said organised crime, including murder, theft, robbery, street crime, vehicle snatching and motorcycle snatching, had posed a major challenge when she assumed office.
She claimed there had been a 70 per cent reduction in crime, while acknowledging that serious challenges remained, particularly child abuse and rape.
“Providing a safe and secure environment is a very difficult task, not an easy task, but a difficult decision. I have made that decision by putting myself at risk,” she said.
She said development projects would have little meaning if citizens remained unsafe.
“If we build roads, if we build metros, if we plant diamonds and pearls, if someone's house, if someone's animal is stolen, if someone's car is stolen after saving money in instalments, then it means that all my investments are in vain,” she said.
Maryam also announced a renewed focus on corruption within government departments and law enforcement agencies.
She said a helpline had been established for members of the public to report demands for bribes and allegations of corruption.
“I request that the public report on that helpline, and we will advertise it as well. And there will be instant action. As soon as we get the evidence, we will arrest them,” she said.
She claimed that hundreds of people had been arrested since the previous day and said she had issued written instructions to civil administration and police officials, including commissioners, deputy commissioners, RPOs and DPOs, to take action against corrupt elements.
The chief minister also said body cameras had been provided to personnel to monitor their conduct during duty.
“I got them to wear body cams only so that I know what they are doing in their eight to 10 hours of duty. And they also know that we are being watched,” she said.
She directed departments to “purge” their ranks and files of corrupt elements, warning that those failing to do so would face strict action.
Maryam said the AI hub would help the province move from responding to incidents after they occurred to anticipating and preventing threats.
“Punjab will get a lot of support in coordination, assessment, and timely action. And this will lead to a very synchronized and coordinated response,” she said.
She said timely intervention could reduce the need for damage control and firefighting after an incident.
“After that, there will be damage control. After that, there will be firefighting. If we can control before that, then it will be a great blessing from Allah,” she said.
The chief minister thanked the Home Department, home minister, IT staff, Special Branch and intelligence agencies for their role in establishing the AI hub and expressed hope that the project would strengthen coordination between federal security departments and provincial authorities.

items.content:
A new study from China has found that men and women age in strikingly different ways -- and the clues lie hidden in the results of everyday blood tests and health check-ups.
The study, recently published in the journal Nature Aging, was jointly conducted by researchers from the China National Center for Bioinformation (CNCB), under the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), the Institute of Zoology of CAS, Xuanwu Hospital of Capital Medical University and other institutes.
Researchers looked at health data from more than 104,000 adults across China, aged 18 to 98. They focused on 172 common measurements, such as weight, cholesterol and blood sugar. From this, they built special "ageing clocks" to show when human bodies go through the biggest changes over time.
They found that for men, the most important turning point came between ages 35 and 45. During this decade, their metabolism shifted noticeably -- body mass index went up, along with triglycerides and cholesterol. For women, the big change happened later, between 55 and 65, around the time of menopause. At that stage, women experienced strong hormonal changes, along with rising fat and cholesterol levels. Yet despite these distinct ageing trajectories, the physical differences between men and women tended to diminish as they grew older.
Read More: 1 dead, 11 missing after mudslide in eastern China
The study also showed that certain substances in our blood -- including glucose, lipids, uric acid and two tumour-related markers called CEA and HE4 -- build up as we age and are linked to faster biological ageing. To test this, the scientists exposed human blood vessel cells to higher levels of these substances in the lab. The cells began to show clear signs of senescence, suggesting that these factors are not just markers of ageing but may actually help cause it.
But there is some encouraging news. The researchers found that some ageing effects might be reversible. For example, a common diabetes drug called metformin helped protect cells from the ageing damage caused by high glucose levels. In another experiment, mice that were switched from a high-fat diet back to a normal diet showed clear improvements in liver ageing.
"This suggests that lowering metabolic stress -- by improving diet or controlling blood glucose -- could be a potential strategy to slow down ageing," said Xiong Muzhao, a researcher from CNCB.
The findings suggest that reducing age-related metabolic burden may be a promising strategy for promoting healthy ageing. They also highlight the importance of sex-specific assessment and intervention throughout the lifespan, said Li Jiaming, a researcher from CNCB.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Nintendo secara resmi mengumumkan dua presentasi Direct yang akan berlangsung berturut-turut pada 8-9 September 2026. Pertama, The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct pada 8 September dengan durasi sekitar 30 menit. Direct ini memang khusus dihelat untuk memperingati hadirnya salah satu franchise terbesar Nintendo.
Sehari setelahnya, Nintendo Direct 9.9.2026 akan berlangsung pada jam yang sama, durasi 45 menit, berfokus pada game Nintendo Switch 2 yang rilis musim dingin 2026. Strategi tayangan kali ini menjadi hal yang tidak biasa dari Nintendo, menunjukkan bahwa perusahaan ingin memberikan ruang khusus untuk perayaan Zelda tanpa bersaing dengan announcements judul lain.
Perayaan 40 tahun The Legend of Zelda adalah momentum besar bagi Nintendo, menandai empat dekade franchise yang telah menjadi simbol identitas perusahaan sejak diluncurkan di NES pada 1986. Perusahaan telah mengisyaratkan selama berbulan-bulan bahwa perayaan ini akan berlangsung, dan kini akhirnya format dan durasi spesifiknya terkonfirmasi. Direct spesial ini dikabarkan memuat informasi terbaru tentang perkembangan Zelda di masa mendatang.
Selain itu, setelah Direct kedua selesai pada 9 September, Nintendo Treehouse: Live akan melanjutkan dengan sesi gameplay sepanjang 110 menit dari game-game yang ditampilkan di Direct. Ini memberikan kesempatan bagi fans untuk melihat action langsung dari judul-judul upcoming tanpa perlu menunggu review dari outlet gaming eksternal. Struktur tiga sesi ini adalah salah satu yang paling ambisius Nintendo dalam beberapa tahun, mencerminkan betapa besar skala software slate yang mereka siapkan untuk akhir 2026 ini.
Data bisnis dari perusahaan menunjukkan bahwa Switch 2 sudah terjual 23,68 juta unit terjual dan 58,17 juta software units per 30 Juni 2026. Dengan momentum itu, Nintendo menjelang musim liburan paling kompetitif sejak Switch 2 diluncurkan, dan showcase dua hari ini dapat dikatakan sebagai strategi untuk membangun excitement maksimal sebelum musim belanja dimulai.

Proyeksi Game yang Hadir dalam Nintendo Direct 9 September
Yang paling ditunggu dalam Zelda Direct adalah informasi soal Ocarina of Time Remake. Nama tersebut pertama kali kali diumumkan pada Juni 2026 dengan artwork konsep, namun belum menampilkan gameplay substansial. Fans sudah berbulan-bulan berinspeksi terkait detail remake ini, apakah ini sekadar visual update atau perubahan gameplay yang lebih mendalam, dan 30 menit Zelda Direct memberikan ruang ideal untuk menunjukkan first real gameplay footage.
Kemungkinan lain yang beredar adalah first trailer untuk The Legend of Zelda live-action movie yang akan debut 30 April 2027. Perusahaan belum menunjukkan apa pun dari proyek sinematik ini, dan Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct adalah venue sempurna untuk mengumumkan dan menampilkan footage pertama. Ini akan menjadi moment besar untuk franchise, mengintegrasikan gaming dan film dalam satu perayaan yang koheren.
Spekulasi komunitas juga menyebut kemungkinan re-release atau remaster dari game Zelda klasik lainnya. Beberapa fan mengharap Satella ver. dari original Legend of Zelda, atau remaster dari Majora’s Mask, Twilight Princess, atau game Zelda lainnya yang belum ada di Switch 2. Nintendo belum mengkonfirmasi apa pun, tapi 30 menit adalah durasi yang cukup panjang untuk mengumumkan lebih dari sekadar Ocarina of Time.
Untuk sesi Direct 9 September, spekulasi menunjuk ke Luigi’s Mansion 4 sebagai kemungkinan besar, mengingat franchise ini tidur selama 7-8 tahun sejak Luigi’s Mansion 3 di 2019. 3D Mario game baru juga sering menjadi subject spekulasi, dengan fans menunjukkan bahwa hampir 10 tahun sudah berlalu sejak Super Mario Odyssey. Dua judul ini adalah franchise yang biasanya menjadi tentpole launch atau holiday release Nintendo, jadi timing ini cukup cocok. Third-party releases besar untuk Switch 2 juga kemungkinan besar akan diumumkan di Nintendo Direct standard.
Streams akan tersedia di Nintendo of America YouTube channel dan regional variants-nya. Untuk fans Indonesia, waktu broadcast akan jatuh pada 9 September malam untuk Zelda Direct, dan 10 September pagi untuk Nintendo Direct dan Treehouse.

OpenAI said on Saturday that its agents had appropriated wiki sites as impromptu message boards, adding that more transparency was needed around such incidents.
The statement follows a Reuters report that a swarm of OpenAI agents had hijacked a communally edited German site earlier this year and used it as a springboard for cheating during tests and other rogue behaviour.
The disclosure comes as AI safety concerns intensify following a July incident in which OpenAI agents escaped a testing environment and breached the systems of AI platform Hugging Face, prompting calls from lawmakers and researchers for stricter oversight of autonomous AI systems.
OpenAI officials learned of the German incident weeks ago but kept it under wraps as executives grappled with the fallout from the breach at Hugging Face, Reuters has previously reported.
OpenAI did not immediately return a message seeking further details on what the company knew about what it described as the "wiki incident", or why it waited until after the Reuters story to discuss it publicly.
Read More: OpenAI agents hijacked German website in previously undisclosed AI breakout this spring
In a statement posted to the social media site X, OpenAI said that it, and others, needed to be more transparent about incidents of unintended behaviour by AI — typically referred to in the industry as "misalignment".
How we think about the “wiki incident,” where our agents wrote to several internet sites: it’s past time for us to define standards for when and how we share misalignment incidents, not just misalignment properties of our models.
Historically, we have treated misalignment… pic.twitter.com/NNTbfSxVWn
— OpenAI (@OpenAI) September 5, 2026
"Our misalignment disclosure practices need to expand for this new phase of model capabilities," OpenAI said, adding that the industry did "not yet have a clear standard for how to report misalignment that shows up during training, evaluation, and deployment."
OpenAI said that it was "working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on these issues."

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Preparing to take the stage representing Ethiopia at the Miss World pageant, Ruth Yirgalem Weldesilasie thinks of her sister, who was abducted and murdered ahead of the contest.
"I'm going to change my pain to my purpose," the 25-year-old told AFP in Vietnam's coastal Nha Trang city, as 111 contestants gathered for the Saturday night pageant finale.
This summer, Ruth's 29-year-old elder sister, Kidusan Yirgalem Weldesilasie, was kidnapped for ransom, disappearing from her side as she prepared for the global beauty contest. Kidusan was discovered dead, her remains split between two suitcases, in late July. Ruth's ex-boyfriend and her sister's partner are among 10 arrested suspects, according to local media reports.
Violence against women and girls is endemic in Ethiopia's deeply patriarchal society. Ruth hopes that by defying her grief to travel to Vietnam, she has found a platform to highlight its wrongs. "I've been wanting to do this for a lifetime," she said. Ahead of her departure, Ruth said she thought to herself that while she could not bring her sister back, "if I go, there are things that I will do".
Saturday's event will be the 75th anniversary edition of the world's oldest beauty pageant.
The industry has in the past been criticised for reducing women to objects of glamour, undermining the feminist cause. But in more recent decades, contests have focused on the charity and activist work of contenders while still staging all-colourful theatrical performances.
Dignity
On a break from rehearsals outside a hotel where she lodges with fellow competitors, Ruth told AFP of the stark issues she hopes her presence will highlight.
Her social impact projects focus on children's mental well-being and maternal health. When you heal a woman, "you give her dignity back", she said. "You give her another life." But travelling in Ethiopia, she has seen many other women's issues requiring advocacy.
UN data shows that nearly 20 million women in a country of 130 million people were married or in a union before the age of 18. Female genital mutilation rates, though declining, are nearly 50 per cent for women between the ages of 15 and 49. A petition calling on the government to declare violence against women a "national crisis" has been signed by nearly 170,000 people.
Decades of instability and a 2020-2022 war in the country's north have worsened the lives of legions of women. The root cause of all the problems is the same: women are treated as objects.
Putting a price on women's lives
When the kidnappers of Ruth's sister called to demand their ransom, the point hit home. "Imagine the person that you care for most has a price; one day you're being asked for a price", Ruth told AFP. "It was hard, very hard."
Ruth will be mourning in the spotlight, a counterintuitive choice that she battled her emotional instincts to make. "I know when I go back home tomorrow, I'm going to sit on my couch and try to process everything and cry my eyes out," she said. But she is motivated by the memory of her sister.
As a child, her family would tell her: "You are the one for your sister. You are the one who is going to protect her." She sees taking the stage in Vietnam as a way to serve the larger sisterhood of women, even if her own sibling is lost. "I want women to think beyond what they are going through," she said.
"I want to show the world that even when the world is being hard on you, you can also make it."

Ahead of its Thursday 10 September launch, TECNO has detailed the power system inside the SPARK 50 Pro, a power system led by 60W Super Charge paired with a long-lasting 6000mAh battery, and framed it around a moment most people know well: the point in the afternoon when the battery drops into single digits and the rest of the day suddenly becomes a negotiation.
Meet the Fifteen-Minute Reset
Fifteen minutes is roughly a chai break. A wait between meetings. The time it takes to get ready before heading out. Plugged in for just 15 minutes, the SPARK 50 Pro’s 60W Super Charge delivers enough charge, giving users a meaningful boost to get back to what they were doing, without the phone becoming something they have to constantly manage.
For always-connected users, the day rarely follows a fixed schedule, moving between work and daily responsibilities, social media, gaming, entertainment and staying connected. The 15-minute reset is designed for those moments when there simply isn’t time to wait around for a phone to charge.
With a combination of a long-lasting battery and super charging, the SPARK 50 Pro is designed to support the way users move through their day, from work and daily responsibilities to entertainment, gaming and social connections, helping ensure that a low battery does not become the reason they have to miss a plan.
60W Super Charge — Power Up in No Time
The SPARK 50 Pro’s 60W Super Charge is built for moments when there’s no time to wait. Its 15-minute reset gives users a quick top-up to get back to work, gaming, entertainment or staying connected without slowing down their day.
6000mAh Long-Lasting Beast
With a 6000mAh battery, the SPARK 50 Pro is designed to keep pace with busy days that move between work, social media, gaming and entertainment. It delivers the endurance users need to stay connected without constantly searching for a charger.
6 Years Strong, Battery Health Locked In
TECNO rates the SPARK 50 Pro’s battery at more than 1,900 charge cycles while retaining over 80% of its original capacity, equivalent to approximately six years of normal use. AI Charging Protection and dedicated charging modes further support long-term battery health.
Supporting the battery system are multiple charging modes, including Super Charge for quick top-ups, Smart Charge for everyday use and Low-Temp Charge for extended gaming sessions, along with AI Charging Protection to help preserve long-term battery health. The complete SPARK 50 Pro specification, pricing and availability will be announced on Thursday 10 September.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday began talks in Moscow with US special envoy Steve Witkoff and President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner on efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war.
Citing the Kremlin, Russian state news agency RIA reported that presidential aide Yury Ushakov and presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev were also taking part in the meeting.
Speaking at the beginning of negotiations, Putin said the situation they must address during their talks is "certainly complex", expressing that Trump continues his efforts to resolve the ongoing war despite entering a "difficult situation".
"Today, we will discuss all its components, all aspects, and we, for our part, are ready to inform you of our view of the situation," Putin said in remarks that were aired by Russian state media.
"As you informed us, I know that after Moscow, you are planning to travel to (Ukraine's capital) Kyiv. In any case, no matter what happens there, contacts of this kind are certainly always beneficial," he added.
For their part, Witkoff thanked the Russian president for agreeing to a three-day ceasefire while he and Kushner visit both Moscow and the Ukrainian capital over the weekend.
Witkoff also conveyed the gratitude of former US Marine Robert Gilman's family to Putin for the help in his return. Gilman, who was imprisoned in Russia since 2022, was released by Moscow last month.
The pair landed in Moscow earlier today for talks on how to end the ‌war in Ukraine, where they were met by Dmitriev.
A motorcade, carrying Witkoff, Kushner and Dmitriev, left Moscow's governmental airport and headed towards the city, a Reuters witness said.
US President Donald Trump suggested on Friday that the ​US had a fresh concrete proposal aimed at ending the war, which is now in its fifth year. He did not, however, elaborate on ​what that proposal would be.
Read: Russia torments Kyiv with seventh day of strikes
Russian envoy Dmitriev, who told Reuters in June that he had remained in contact with the US negotiators ⁠during a pause in their visits to Russia, took part in all their previous meetings with Putin alongside Putin's foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov.
He also played a ​role in negotiating US sanction waivers for Russian oil this year.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday that the two men would fly to Ukraine on Sunday after visiting ​Moscow. In an X post on Saturday, Zelensky said Russia hit two Ukrainian airports ahead of US envoys' visit to Kyiv.
Last night, the Russians struck a civilian enterprise in Kamianske, in the Dnipro region, killing four people and injuring five others. My condolences to their families and loved ones. Ordinary residential buildings were damaged in many regions – in Kherson, Boryspil, and the… pic.twitter.com/e9W8OvFA2Q
— Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) September 5, 2026
Peskov said in a statement posted on the Kremlin's channel in Max Messenger that Putin had ordered the military not to strike Kyiv for three days, starting at midnight on Saturday, in connection with Witkoff and Kushner's visit to the Ukrainian capital.
​A vast gulf in positions
The Russian Defence Ministry reported 53 Ukrainian drones in Russian airspace on Saturday, significantly fewer than the average seen in recent months. ​Moscow is celebrating City Day on Saturday, with hundreds of thousands of people taking part in open-air festivities across the city.
A vast gulf remains between Russia and Ukraine on how ‌to end ⁠the 4-1/2-year-old war, the deadliest in Europe since World War Two.
A source close to the Kremlin, speaking before reports emerged of a possible trip by President Trump's envoys, said Putin was still intent on capturing more territory.
"There is no chance of reaching an agreement regarding the front line until Putin finishes securing the remaining part of the Donetsk region," the source told Reuters, adding that the Kremlin leader was confident — based on reports from his commanders — that this would happen by the ​end of the year.
Kremlin's position 'unshakeable'
Western ​military analysts see such a possibility ⁠as remote, given Moscow's slow rate of progress. Ukraine refuses to surrender land that it has successfully defended at huge cost, and rejects such terms as tantamount to surrender.
The Kremlin said on Friday the position that Putin set out in a ​speech two years ago - that Ukraine should cede the entire territory of four regions claimed by Russia and abandon ​its plan to join ⁠NATO — was "unshakeable".
Since the last peace talks in February, each side has intensified long-range air attacks deep inside the other's territory, while the war at sea has also escalated.
Read more: US approves possible $5b weapons sale to Saudi Arabia amid Middle East tensions
On the ground, the front lines have remained largely static, with Russia making only gradual gains in its attempt to take the whole of Ukraine's Donbas region.
Ukraine's drone strikes on ⁠Russian oil ​refineries have led to a summer of fuel shortages and rising prices for Russian motorists, while some ​30 attacks on giant warehouses belonging mostly to Wildberries, the country's biggest online retailer, have affected the consumer economy.
A Russian drone attack hit the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service in Kyiv on Friday — the 10th ​consecutive day of heavy attacks on the capital — and Zelensky vowed to retaliate.
Four days earlier, the US move to welcome Russia back to a meeting of G20 countries while denying some journalists access to the gathering dismayed some finance leaders. The two-day meeting in Asheville, North Carolina, came as the global economy was being buffeted by an energy shock triggered by the US-Iran war, faced rising tensions over China's huge goods trade surplus and was braced for how an investment surge in AI would ultimately play out.
As US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent opened the meeting, some ministers were surprised and dismayed to see Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov sitting at the G20 table, the first time they had attended the forum in person since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.
