items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Governor Uba Sani has said that youth empowerment is central to his administration’s philosophy and not just a mere slogan which is chanted at events.
He noted that Kaduna State Government recognises ‘’that a society cannot secure prosperity by marginalising the generation that will inherit its institutions, its economy and its responsibilities.’’
Governor Sani who made this known at the International Youth Day Conference on Friday, also supported outstanding youths from Kaduna State who have made their marks in science and technology, with N3 million each.
The beneficiaries include a group of Computer Engineering students from Ahmadu Bello University(ABU) Zaria who produced the Innovative Walking Aid, which helps the visually impaired.
Another beneficiary was Fauziyya Muhammad Auwal of Kaduna State University, the first female astronaut candidate with Titans Space Industries, Nigeria’s first female analog astronaut for the 2026 LunAres Research Station Poland and founder of ASTHERA, an initiative focused on space technology.
Others are the eight-member Microchip Designers who were selected for specialised training under the Kaduna State Human Capital Development initiative.
The rest are Al Amin Mohammed Idris and Shamsudeen Jibril, winners of the National Board for Technology Incubation(NBTI) NEXTGEN challenge
Speaking at the event, the Governor further said that Kaduna State is committed to moving beyond promises and symbolism towards investment that empower the youth.
‘’We will continue to expand skills acquisition and vocational training, because every young person deserves the opportunity to leave school with not only a certificate, but also a skill with which to earn a dignified living.
‘’We will deepen digital literacy and technological innovation, because Kaduna’s youth must not merely consume the products of the digital economy; you must design, build and own them,’’ he said.
The Governor also promised to strengthen ‘’entrepreneurship and access to finance, because too many promising ideas have been abandoned not for lack of talent, but for lack of opportunity and capital.’’
The Governor also pointed out that empowerment must ultimately include power, especially the power to participate and to influence decisions as well as to lead.
‘’We must create credible pathways through which young people can enter public service, governance and civic leadership. Not as a favour granted by older generations,’’ he advised.
Governor Sani maintained that creating such pathways is a recognition of reality because youths are already leading in ‘’businesses, communities, schools, families, creative enterprises and social movements.’’
He noted that government cannot accomplish this alone because ‘’the transformation we seek requires an ecosystem of government, private enterprise, civil society, development partners, educational institutions and, most importantly, young people themselves.’’
The Governor therefore called on ‘’development partners, civil society organisations and institutions whose resources, expertise and commitment continue to expand opportunities for the youth of Kaduna.’’
He counseled the youth not to allow their local government, language, faith, gender, economic circumstance or disability to determine the limits of their ambition.
‘’Build relationships beyond the boundaries you inherited. Learn from people whose experiences differ from yours. Create enterprises, ideas and institutions that solve real problems. And, above all, refuse to surrender your imagination to the difficulties of the present,” he advised.
In her welcome address, the Commissioner of Youth Development, Barrister Gloria Ibrahim, said that the theme of the International Youth Day Conference 2026, is “Different Contexts, Common Aspirations.’’
‘’Across Kaduna State, our young people come from different worlds — the busy tech hubs and corporate spaces of Kaduna metropolis, the agricultural heartlands of Sabon Gari and Birnin Gwari, the trading posts of southern Kaduna, and the classrooms, workshops, and start-ups scattered across our 23 Local Government Areas,’’ she said.
According to the Commissioner, ‘’our contexts differ, but our aspirations converge: good jobs, real opportunity, a peaceful and secure state, and a genuine seat at the table where decisions about our future are made.’’
Describing Governor Uba Sani as a leader that delivers on his promise, Barrister Ibrahim pointed out that his commitment to young people is not measured in words but in what has done.
‘’In 2025, His Excellency created the Kaduna State Ministry of Youth Development — a dedicated institution to coordinate policy, programmes, and partnerships for young people, so that youth development is no longer an afterthought but a central pillar of governance in our State,’’ she recalled.
The Governor has also been investing on youth empowerment, especially with the establishment of three modern skills and vocational centres in Rigachikun, Zango Kataf, and Soba, she added.
‘’Beyond vocational trades, His Excellency has also prioritised the future of work by driving Digital and Tech Skills Empowerment programmes across the State, equipping our young people with the ICT, digital literacy, and technology skills they need to compete not just locally, but globally,’’ she disclosed.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
NVIDIA has agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, with plans to scale the platform, strengthen its infrastructure, and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide.
Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the broader AI ecosystem after the acquisition. Developers will continue to choose the models, frameworks, cloud providers, inference services, and computing platforms they want to use.
NVIDIA compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.
Hugging Face Will Remain Open
Hugging Face will continue supporting open-source and open-weight models from developers across the AI industry.
The platform will also maintain multi-cloud and multi-accelerator support, allowing developers to choose the hardware and infrastructure that best fit their needs.
Hugging Face has grown into a major platform for the open-model community over the past decade.
More than 18 million developers, researchers and creators use the platform to share more than 3 million models, 500,000 datasets and 1 million applications.
More than 200,000 companies also use Hugging Face to discover, evaluate, customize, and deploy AI models.
NVIDIA Highlights Importance of Open Models
NVIDIA said open-weight models can expand access to AI by enabling startups, businesses, universities, and public institutions to use advanced capabilities without training each model from scratch.
The company said open models also allow organizations to select the most suitable model for different tasks while supporting innovation, cybersecurity, sovereignty, and broader AI adoption across sectors including factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms, and small businesses.
NVIDIA has also backed an open letter supporting the role of open weights in the AI economy.
The company said open weights can help distribute AI leadership across companies, institutions, and communities rather than concentrating access to advanced models.
NVIDIA’s Existing Contributions to Hugging Face
NVIDIA said it has invested in open-weight models and open-source platforms, including Hugging Face, for several years.
The company describes itself as the largest contributor of open models and data to Hugging Face.
NVIDIA has released more than 500 models and more than 250 open datasets on the platform.
It also develops its own models, libraries, and tools openly so developers can use, modify, and build on them.
What Changes After the Acquisition
NVIDIA plans to use its infrastructure, engineering resources, and global reach to improve Hugging Face’s platform reliability, safety, model evaluation, inference, and deployment capabilities.
At the same time, the company says it intends to preserve the open ecosystem that helped make Hugging Face a major platform for AI developers.
The Hugging Face team will join NVIDIA, while the Hugging Face brand will remain in place.
NVIDIA said the acquisition is intended to help Hugging Face serve the global AI community at a larger scale while keeping the platform open to different models, hardware providers, cloud services, and development tools.

items.summary:
Motorola unveiled several new products at its IFA 2026 keynote, including the Edge 70 Plus smartphone, Watch Ultra, a Swarovski edition of the Razr 70, and a new Snap magnetic wireless charger.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Motorola unveiled several new products at its IFA 2026 keynote, including the Edge 70 Plus smartphone, Watch Ultra, a Swarovski edition of the Razr 70, and a new Snap magnetic wireless charger.
Motorola Edge 70 Plus
The Motorola Edge 70 Plus comes in four Pantone-certified colors: Gray Lilac, Milky Blue, Mountain View, and Sage.
Each finish has a different texture and inspiration. Mountain View uses a silk-like finish and a green shade inspired by ancient forests. Gray Lilac combines mauve and grey with an acetate finish.
Milky Blue takes inspiration from early morning skies and uses a soft-luxe texture, while Sage is a muted green inspired by eucalyptus after rain and also has a soft-luxe finish.
The phone has a quad-curved design on both the front and back. Motorola says the rounded shape removes sharp edges and makes the device more comfortable to hold.
It features a 6.78-inch Pantone-validated AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate. Two Hi-Res-certified stereo speakers accompany the display.
Inside, the Edge 70 Plus uses the Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 chipset with 8GB of LPDDR5X RAM and either 128GB or 256GB of storage.
The phone has a 200MP main camera with optical image stabilization, up to 10x digital zoom, and 4K video recording. Motorola says this is the highest-resolution camera it has used on one of its phones.
The camera is also Pantone-validated for colors and skin tones. The phone additionally includes a dedicated macro camera and a 32MP selfie camera.
A 6,500mAh battery powers the device, with support for 45W charging and bypass charging for gaming.
The Motorola Edge 70 Plus will become available in selected European and Middle Eastern countries in the coming weeks, with prices starting at approximately $697.
Motorola Watch Ultra
Motorola also introduced the Watch Ultra, a 46mm smartwatch with IP68 and 5ATM water resistance.
The watch runs Wear OS by Google and uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon W5+ Gen 1 chipset.
It features a 1.5-inch OLED display capable of reaching up to 2,700 nits of brightness. Motorola claims up to two days of active use.
Motorola partnered with Polar to expand the watch’s fitness and health-tracking features.
The Watch Ultra includes a breathing exercise mode called Setene, along with Nightly Recharge, Sleep Plus Stages, a personalized sleep score, and a Running Coach.
Additional Polar-powered features include Activity Goal, Activity Score, Active Intensity Zone, Inactivity Alert, Smart Calories and Energy Sources.
The watch supports dual-band GPS and includes built-in LTE, marking the first Motorola smartwatch capable of cellular connectivity. This allows it to operate without a connected phone.
Google Pay is also supported.
Motorola offers the stainless steel Watch Ultra in silver and black. Users can choose from standard 22mm straps, including breathable silicone straps in Pantone Black Beauty and Mountain View, as well as genuine leather straps in Pantone Black Beauty and Nuthatch.
The Motorola Watch Ultra will launch in selected markets across Europe, the Middle East, Latin America, North America and Asia Pacific in the coming weeks.
It will cost approximately $499.
Motorola Razr 70 With Crystals by Swarovski
Motorola also expanded its Brilliant Collection with a special edition of the Razr 70, known as the Razr 2026 in the US.
The Motorola Razr 70 with Crystals by Swarovski comes exclusively in Pantone Meteorite with a quilted soft-touch finish.
Motorola has decorated the phone with 35 hand-positioned Swarovski Crystals in Silver Night. A larger 32-facet Swarovski Crystal is also built into the hinge.
A transparent protective case is included so the crystal-covered design remains visible.
Underneath the special finish, the phone retains the standard Razr 70 hardware.
It features a 3.6-inch cover display and a 6.9-inch Extreme AMOLED folding display.
The phone has a dual rear camera system led by a 50MP main camera, along with AI features and a 4,800mAh battery.
Motorola claims the battery can provide more than 36 hours of use.
The Swarovski edition will be sold as a limited edition in most markets worldwide and will cost $900 in the US.
Motorola Snap
Motorola also unveiled the Snap, a magnetic wireless charger supporting the Qi2.2 standard.
The charger delivers up to 25W through Qi2.2 and uses strong magnetic alignment to keep compatible devices in position.
It also works with compatible magnetic cases and includes protection against overheating and overcharging.
Motorola says the charger consumes no power while in standby mode.
Compatible Motorola smartphones can charge at up to 30W using the company’s proprietary charging protocol.
A 1.5-meter braided USB-C cable is included in the box.
In Europe, Motorola will also offer the Snap in a bundle with an adjustable aluminum stand featuring a silicone-lined holder and an Alcantara base.
The Snap will launch in Europe, the Middle East, Latin America, North America, and other supported regions in the coming weeks.
It will cost approximately $46.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
SaaS startup Meritto’s parent NoPaperForms has filed its updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) with Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for its initial public issue (IPO).
The startup’s proposed public offering will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth ₹375 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) component of up to 3.8 Cr equity shares.
As reported earlier, only investor Info Edge will participate in the OFS. As per the UDRHP, the venture capital giant, via Startup Investments (Holding) Ltd, will offload 3.8 Cr shares.
Around ₹148 Cr of the fresh proceeds will be utilised to bolster its tech stack and cloud infrastructure, while ₹96 Cr will be deployed for customer acquisition and retention. A chunk of the capital will also be used for general corporate purposes and fueling inorganic growth via acquisitions.
This nearly a year after the enterprise tech startup first filed its DRHP with the market regulator via the confidential route in November 2025. It then received SEBI’s nod to float its IPO in March this year.
Founded in 2017 by Naveen Goyal and Suraj Sapra, NoPaperForms offers two products: Meritto and Collexo. The former offers SaaS-based enrolment automation and CRM tools for educational institutions, helping them manage student recruitment, admissions and fee collection.
Under Collexo, it offers fee-collection and payments-related solutions for educational institutions. Its Pixi brand, under Collexo, also sells co-branded cards to students. The startup also enables educational organisations to deploy AI agents across student-facing and institutional workflows with its Mio AI suite.
The startup claimed to have catered to 1,183 customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026, including 104 overseas clients. India accounted for 91.2% of its total revenue in FY26, while international operations contributed the remaining 8.8%.
NoPaperForms processed invoices worth ₹124.6 Cr in FY26 and ₹39.9 Cr in Q1 FY27. Meanwhile, average revenue per customer improved to ₹9.8 Lakhs in the fiscal year ended March 2026 as against ₹9.2 Lakh in FY25.
On the financial front, NoPaperForms reported an operating revenue of ₹115.6 Cr in FY26, up 25.2% from ₹92.3 Cr in the year ago fiscal. Meanwhile, the startup’s profits surged 534% to ₹11.9 Cr in the fiscal under review as against ₹1.9 Cr in FY25.
The startup also posted an operating revenue of ₹44.8 Cr in Q1 FY27 against a net profit of ₹6 Cr in the quarter under review.

items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has notified higher wellhead gas prices of up to 16 percent for the second half of 2026, with prices for fields operating under the Petroleum Policy 2012 rising by around 10 percent on average, according to Topline Securities.
The revised prices are effective for the second half of 2026 and reflect the annual price adjustment mechanism, which is based on the average oil price during the preceding six months. Arab Light crude averaged $92.2 per barrel from January to June 2026, compared with $68.4 per barrel from July to December 2025, representing a 35 percent increase.
Topline said a 35 percent rise in oil prices would translate into an estimated 10 percent to 11 percent increase in gas prices for companies operating under the Petroleum Policy 2012, reflecting the sliding benefit mechanism under the policy. OGRA has issued notifications for some fields, while revised prices for the remaining fields are expected to follow.
The wellhead price for Chachar increased 15.8 percent to $2.02 per MMBtu from $1.75, while prices for Bhit and Badhra rose 15.4 percent to $4.45 per MMBtu from $3.86. Prices for Fazl X1, Rayan 1, Shahdadpur and Dhok Sultan increased by about 9.8 percent.
The price for Rizq rose 6.7 percent to $6.32 per MMBtu from $5.92. Rehman field prices increased by 6.7 percent for both production categories, while the price for Adam X1 Well edged up 0.4 percent to $2.74 per MMBtu from $2.73.
Topline said the revision represents an average increase of 8 percent to 10 percent. Although the impact has already been incorporated into its forecasts, the brokerage said it viewed the revision as positive for exploration and production sector earnings.

The funeral prayer was held at the palace of the late monarch in Gumel Emirate in the afternoon of Friday, September 4, 2026, following his death in Cairo, Egypt, on Thursday, September 3, after a period of illness.
The late Emir, who was born in 1942, spent decades serving as a traditional leader and custodian of the culture, history and values of the Gumel Emirate.
The funeral attracted prominent personalities, including Nigeria’s Vice President, Kashim Shettima, who led a delegation from the Presidency, as well as Jigawa State Governor, Malam Umar Namadi.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Acer has expanded its Windows gaming handheld lineup with the Predator Atlas 7, a smaller 7-inch alternative to the 8-inch Predator Atlas 8 announced earlier this year.
The company introduced the new handheld at its IFA press conference in Berlin. Acer also showed a concept device called Project DualPlay Mini, which combines a handheld gaming system with a small productivity laptop design.
Design and Display
The Predator Atlas 7 features a 7-inch 1080p IPS touchscreen with a 120Hz refresh rate.
The panel reaches up to 500 nits of brightness and supports variable refresh rate.
Acer has included Hall-effect analog triggers, while buyers can also choose TMR joysticks designed to reduce the risk of stick drift.
The handheld weighs 750 grams with the larger 80Wh battery. Acer will also offer a 60Wh version weighing just under 700 grams.
Hardware and Storage
The Predator Atlas 7 uses Intel’s latest mobile hardware and can be configured with up to an Intel Arc G3 Extreme processor and Intel Arc B390 graphics.
It supports up to 24GB of RAM.
For storage, Acer uses a standard M.2 2280 slot with support for up to 1TB. The standard format should also make replacing the storage drive with a larger one easier.
Acer uses a dual-fan cooling system consisting of a thin metal fan and a conventional plastic fan to cool the internal hardware.
Connectivity
The Predator Atlas 7 includes two Thunderbolt 4 ports and a UHS-II microSD card slot.
It also supports Wi-Fi 7.
A fingerprint reader is integrated into the power button for biometric authentication.
Battery
Acer has fitted the handheld with an 80Wh battery, which is unusually large for a 7-inch gaming device.
A smaller 60Wh battery configuration will also be available for users who prefer a lighter device.
Project DualPlay Mini
Acer also showed Project DualPlay Mini, an 8-inch concept gaming handheld with a flip-and-swivel display.
Opening and rotating the screen reveals a built-in backlit keyboard.
The design allows users to operate the device as a conventional controller-based handheld or rotate the screen to use the keyboard for first-person shooters and productivity tasks.
Acer has not announced any plans to release Project DualPlay Mini commercially.
The company also placed a Morse code message on the back of the concept device to mark Acer’s 50th anniversary.
Pricing and Availability
The Acer Predator Atlas 7 will launch in North America in the fourth quarter of 2026.
It will arrive in EMEA in November.
Acer has not announced pricing for the Predator Atlas 7 yet.
The larger Predator Atlas 8 remains scheduled to launch in September.

Monthly Stipend and Internship Duration
Selected interns will receive Rs. 60,000 per month throughout the three-month program.
The stipend will provide financial support while participants complete their learning activities, field assignments and capstone projects.
The department has not mentioned whether interns will receive any additional accommodation, travel or food allowance. Candidates should check the terms and conditions on the application portal before submitting their forms.
Automatic Merit-Based Selection
The Punjab government will use an automatic merit-based system to select candidates.
Applicants must enter accurate academic and personal information because the online system will use these details during the selection process. Any incorrect or incomplete information may affect an application.
Candidates should upload clear and valid documents and carefully review every section of the form before final submission.
Learning Management System
Participants will receive access to a modern Learning Management System for structured training and professional development.
The platform will allow interns to complete learning modules and access material related to climate change, environmental protection, sustainable development and climate leadership.
The program also includes district-wise learning opportunities, enabling participants to gain experience connected to environmental issues in different areas of Punjab.
UNFCCC Certification
UNFCCC certification will form an integral part of the internship program.
This component will introduce participants to international climate frameworks and strengthen their understanding of global efforts to address climate change.
Candidates should review the official portal for details about the certification process, course requirements and completion conditions.
Exposure to EPA Field Offices
Interns will gain practical exposure through Environmental Protection Agency field offices.
This experience will allow them to observe environmental monitoring, regulatory work and other departmental activities.
It may also help participants understand how government agencies address pollution and climate-related problems at the district level.
Experience in EPCCD Units
The program will provide exposure to EPCCD’s strategic, development, communications and climate policy units.
Interns will learn how the department plans environmental initiatives, develops climate policies, manages public communication and coordinates projects.
This combination of field and office experience is intended to help participants understand both the practical and policy sides of environmental governance.
Capstone Projects and Expert Mentorship
Participants will complete capstone projects as part of the internship.
These projects will allow interns to apply their learning to environmental or climate-related issues. Experts will guide participants during the program and provide mentorship for their professional development.
The announcement does not specify the topics, assessment method or team structure for these projects. The department may share further instructions with selected candidates.
Seats Reserved for Female Candidates
The Punjab government has reserved 50 percent of the internship seats for female candidates.
The quota aims to increase women’s participation in environmental leadership, climate policy and public-sector initiatives.
The program also includes a special quota for graduates who have completed their qualifications from foreign institutions.
Eligibility Criteria
Interested candidates should check the eligibility rules and terms available on the official application portal. Applicants should apply only if they meet all requirements mentioned by EPCCD.
They should also prepare their CNIC, recent photograph, academic records and other documents requested by the online system.
How to Apply for Punjab Climate Internships
Candidates can apply through the officialPunjab Climate Internship portal.
Applicants should open the portal and create an account if required. They must then complete their personal and academic profile and provide the requested information.
Candidates should upload clear copies of all required documents, select the relevant program and review the application carefully.
After checking the information, applicants should submit the form and save a screenshot or copy of the completed application for their records.

Xiaomi has announced the Smart Band 11 in China, bringing a slimmer design, improved health tracking, and longer battery life compared with its predecessor.
Reservations are already open ahead of the fitness tracker’s sale through Xiaomi’s channels and major Chinese e-commerce platforms.
Design and Display
The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 features a 1.72-inch AMOLED display with up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a narrow 2mm bezel.
The tracker has a curved body measuring 9.99mm thick and weighs as little as 15.58 grams.
Xiaomi offers several strap options, including metal and ceramic versions. The wearable also carries a 5ATM water-resistance rating.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Xiaomi has announced the Smart Band 11 in China, bringing a slimmer design, improved health tracking, and longer battery life compared with its predecessor.
Reservations are already open ahead of the fitness tracker’s sale through Xiaomi’s channels and major Chinese e-commerce platforms.
Design and Display
The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 features a 1.72-inch AMOLED display with up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness and a narrow 2mm bezel.
The tracker has a curved body measuring 9.99mm thick and weighs as little as 15.58 grams.
Xiaomi offers several strap options, including metal and ceramic versions. The wearable also carries a 5ATM water-resistance rating.
Health and Fitness Tracking
The Smart Band 11 can track heart rate, blood oxygen levels, and stress.
It also includes dedicated female health features.
Xiaomi has added professional sleep management with HRV monitoring and AI-based sleep insights.
The fitness tracker supports more than 150 sports modes covering a wide range of indoor and outdoor activities.
Battery and Software
The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 offers up to 21 days of battery life.
It also includes NFC support for functions such as contactless payments and smart access cards.
The wearable runs HyperOS 4 and works with both Android and iOS devices.
Other features include smartphone notifications, music controls, and customizable watch faces.
Pricing and Availability
The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 starts at $43 in China.
The NFC version costs around $50, while the ceramic and metal editions are priced at approximately $60.
Reservations are currently open through Xiaomi’s official channels and major Chinese e-commerce platforms.
Xiaomi has not yet confirmed international availability.

items.content: A stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs report has put a September interest-rate hike back firmly on the table, leaving Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh facing a difficult choice as President Donald Trump intensifies his demands for lower borrowing costs, Reuters reported.U.S. employers added 162,000 jobs in August, nearly three times what economists had expected, while the labor force participation rate rose to 61.6%. More people moved from the sidelines directly into jobs, helping keep the unemployment rate at 4.1% even as the pool of available workers expanded.The report strengthens the argument for the Fed to raise rates at its Sept. 15-16 meeting, particularly after Warsh last week said he needed confidence that inflation was moving back toward the central bank's 2% target "clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do."But the stronger labor market data arrives as Trump steps up pressure on the central bank."The Fed Board, with its great new leader, must ​get smart - BE PATRIOTS for a change," Trump said in a Truth Social post Friday after the jobs data were released.He also renewed his criticism of high interest rates, saying: "High interest rates put the U.S.A. ​at a very unfair disadvantage, and I won't allow that to happen!"Trump then tied his demand for lower rates to U.S. trade policy, threatening to halt trade with countries running a deficit with the United States."We should have ​the LOWEST RATE of any country in the World ... LOWER THE RATE OR I'LL STOP TRADING WITH COUNTRIES WITH WHICH WE HAVE A DEFICIT," Trump said.The threat adds another layer of uncertainty for the Fed, which is already navigating inflation that has remained above its 2% target for more than five years. Trump's tariffs, along with higher energy prices linked to the escalation in the U.S.-Iran conflict and strong investment in artificial intelligence, have added to price pressures and pushed up longer-term Treasury yields.For now, however, the jobs report itself does not settle the Fed's decision.Wage growth was 3.1% in August, a pace broadly consistent with the Fed's inflation goal, while the increase in labor-force participation suggests the steady unemployment rate was driven by more people working or looking for work rather than a deterioration in labor-market conditions."The upshot of today's numbers is that the September FOMC meeting remains finely balanced," Pantheon Macro economists wrote. "FOMC members have uniformly signaled that inflation data will determine their next ​policy steps."That makes next week's consumer price index and producer price index reports crucial. Fed Governor Christopher Waller told Reuters NEXT on Thursday that he would support keeping rates in the 3.50%-3.75% range if inflation data continued to moderate.Markets nevertheless moved toward pricing a hike after Friday's report, with interest-rate futures implying about a 62% chance of an increase this month, up from roughly 55% before the data."While Fed officials have communicated that they are squarely focused on the inflation readings, today's strong employment report also provides additional support for rate hikes this year," Nationwide Chief Economist Kathy Bostjancic wrote."We now see two, 25 basis-point rate hikes by year-end, lifting the fed funds rate to 4-4.25%." (Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: SUGAR Cosmetics Raises ₹145 Cr From A91 At A Near 80% Valuation Cut
items.summary:
D2C beauty and personal brand SUGAR Cosmetics has raised ₹144.47 Cr ($15.3 Mn) in a fresh equity round from VC firm A91 Partners, as per the startup’s MCA filings accessed by Inc42.
It allotted 1.12 Lakh Series D7 CCPS to A91’s entity A91 Emerging Fund III at an issue price of ₹12,871. The CCPS will compulsorily convert into equity shares upon listing of the startup or one day prior to the expiry of 20 years from issue date. The startup’s board of directors passed the resolution at its meeting held on September 1.
The startup has raised the fresh capital at a significant valuation cut. Its post-money valuation with the round, which seems to be its Series D equity round, is in the range of ₹550-600 Cr ($58-64 Mn), as per Inc42’s calculations.
This implies a hefty 75-80% cut from the ₹2,600-2,700 Cr valuation it commanded back when it had raised funds in November 2024. The startup’s pre-money valuation for the round stood at ₹433.6 Cr. SUGAR’s peak valuation was about ₹3,000 Cr ($500 Mn)
items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
D2C beauty and personal brand SUGAR Cosmetics has raised ₹144.47 Cr ($15.3 Mn) in a fresh equity round from VC firm A91 Partners, as per the startup’s MCA filings accessed by Inc42.
It allotted 1.12 Lakh Series D7 CCPS to A91’s entity A91 Emerging Fund III at an issue price of ₹12,871. The CCPS will compulsorily convert into equity shares upon listing of the startup or one day prior to the expiry of 20 years from issue date. The startup’s board of directors passed the resolution at its meeting held on September 1.
The startup has raised the fresh capital at a significant valuation cut. Its post-money valuation with the round, which seems to be its Series D equity round, is in the range of ₹550-600 Cr ($58-64 Mn), as per Inc42’s calculations.
This implies a hefty 75-80% cut from the ₹2,600-2,700 Cr valuation it commanded back when it had raised funds in November 2024. The startup’s pre-money valuation for the round stood at ₹433.6 Cr. SUGAR’s peak valuation was about ₹3,000 Cr ($500 Mn) back in 2022.
Inc42 has reached out to the startup for their response on the development. The story would be updated in case they respond.
Notably, SUGAR’s net loss for the fiscal year FY25 nearly doubled to ₹135 Cr from ₹68.4 Cr. Its operating revenue also plunged by about 20% to ₹404.4 Cr in FY25, compared to ₹505.1 Cr in FY24.
At the same time, its EBITDA losses more than doubled to ₹116 Cr in FY25 as against ₹48.5 Cr in FY24.
To note, SUGAR is yet to report its financial performance for the fiscal year FY26.
“The company has demonstrated a sustained and worsening pattern of financial deterioration over the past two financial years,” wrote Sayali Deshkar, the registered valuer, in a valuation report attached with the filings dated June 30, 2026.
SUGAR’s economics were impacted mainly by its aggressive offline expansion. As per an ET report, the startup had to shut 30-40% of the physical stores that it opened due to the losses incurred per store.
Inc42 has reached out to the company with questions and the story will be updated with their response.
Founded in 2015 by the husband-wife duo of Vineeta Singh and Kaushik Mukherjee, Mumbai-based SUGAR sells beauty and personal care products on its own website, in physical stores, and through ecommerce platforms.
To date, the startup has raised $90 Mn from investors like Elevation Capital, A91 Partners, Anicut Capital, and IndiaQuotient.
SUGAR operates four brands – SUGAR, POP, ENN, and Quench Botanics – and competes with listed companies like Nykaa and Mamaearth as well as the likes of Renee Cosmetics.
The stakes are high with India entering the D2C 3.0 era where D2C brands are expected to command more than two-thirds of the overall gross merchandise value (GMV) across ecommerce by 2031.
Beauty and personal care is one of the most funded segments within the D2C ecosystem, with this space drawing over $1.1 Bn in funding across 201 deals between 2015 and Q1 FY26.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Two Israeli ministers floated proposals this week for the mass removal of Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, resurfacing an idea voiced repeatedly by right-wing politicians over the past three years as they seek to rally supporters ahead of an election.
The calls by two of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political allies have revived Palestinian fears that Israel ultimately aims to forcibly expel them from Gaza despite US-led diplomatic efforts to end the conflict there.
Far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir laid out a seven-year plan for removing Gaza's population through "voluntary emigration" during a press conference on Thursday night. He said he would seek the creation of a "ministry in charge of emigration" in the next government.
Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party said in a statement on Thursday that Turkey, Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of Congo were being considered as potential destinations.
Ismail Al-Thawabta, director of Gaza's government media office, said, "The Palestinian people are deeply rooted in their land and will not be intimidated by such threats."
Israel is due to hold a general election on October 27. It will be the first since an Israeli military campaign starting October 7, 2023 laid waste to Gaza, which has a population of more than two million.
An October 2025, US-backed, ceasefire halted large-scale fighting, but it has not ended Israeli strikes or produced progress on a plan for permanent peace.
Ben-Gvir's comments followed those of Defence Minister Israel Katz, from Netanyahu's Likud party, who said on Wednesday there was "no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration".
"We are fully prepared to move them out if it becomes possible by sea, by air, by every way possible. Egypt is not willing, so it won't be through them," he said during an online conference hosted by Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper.
Netanyahu's office did not immediately provide comment.
Polls suggest Netanyahu, who has led the most right-wing coalition in Israeli history, could lose power next month, his security credentials still shaken by the 2023 attack though analysts say he can't be written off.
Israel's defence ministry in 2025 established an office tasked with overseeing voluntary emigration from Gaza, after comments by US President Donald Trump suggesting Gazans could be permanently displaced.
Trump later backed away from the idea, which faced strong resistance from Arab states and was widely rejected internationally. Israel reportedly sounded out several African countries as potential resettlement sites.
Netanyahu has said he supports what his government has described as "voluntary emigration" from Gaza, but that far-right ministers goals of re-establishing Jewish settlements in the territory are unrealistic. Israeli officials have denied intending to transfer Gaza's population out by force.
Calls for resettlement of Gazans have prompted fears among Palestinians of a new "Nakba", the name given to the displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinians who fled or were driven from their homes in the wake of the 1948 war that accompanied the founding of the state of Israel.
The Gaza Strip is central to Palestinian hopes of statehood in territory captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Israel has killed more than 73,000 Palestinians since October 2023, according to Gaza health authorities.
A UN inquiry determined that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, arguing that its killings, siege and destruction were carried out with the intent to destroy Palestinian life in the enclave.
Israel, which is fighting a genocide case at the International Court of Justice, rejects genocide allegations as politically motivated and claims that its military campaign targets Hamas, not Gaza's civilian population.
This week, Ben-Gvir posted an AI-generated video depicting dozens of Palestinian prisoners on a conveyor belt, entering a prison facility. They emerge from the other side emaciated, distressed and in tears.
Ben-Gvir later deleted the video, after it had amassed millions of views on X. His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In a crowded Gaza City displacement camp, some Palestinians said that they believed the latest Israeli calls were an election ploy.
They also said Gaza was their land and they would never leave it.
"We will die on the land of Gaza," said one resident, 52-year-old Mohammed Abu Al-Qumbuz.
"We were born on it, our children grew up on it, so it is very difficult to think of leaving."

items.content:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) leader Syed Naveed Qamar said on Friday that his party would not support the government in its legislative affairs until progress was made on its grievances, including those concerning the Azad Jammu and Kashmir elections and appointment of judges.
Speaking to the media at Parliament House, Qamar said the PPP was not a complete ally of the government, although it had continued to support it. He stressed that such support could not be taken for granted. "It takes two hands to clap."
Qamar said a problem persisted when a political party had reservations that had not been addressed.
"We have conveyed some complaints to the government," he said, adding that if the government expected the PPP to support it, its grievances should also be addressed.
"Our complaints relate to the Kashmir elections, the appointment of judges and other issues," Qamar said, adding that the government had so far assured the PPP that it would look into its complaints, but no progress had been made from the government's side.
Qamar said the PPP had therefore decided that until there was progress from the government, it would not support the government in its legislative business.
The decision could complicate the government's efforts to push through legislation, particularly on bills where it requires the PPP's support. Bilawal had earlier said the PPP would withhold support for government legislation until its outstanding concerns were addressed.
Referring to parliamentary proceedings, Qamar said an attempt had been made on the previous day to bulldoze a bill through the Senate Standing Committee on Interior.
He said the PPP should not support the Islamabad local government bill in any case, adding that his party had submitted a dissenting note on the legislation.
"The government should resolve these issues and take steps in this regard," he said.
Referring to Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, Qamar said the minister was currently not in the country.
"I do not know where he is active," he added.
The latest disagreement comes after weeks of friction between the PPP and PML-N over the conduct of the AJK elections and the appointment of judges. The dispute over judicial appointments followed the acrimony generated by the AJK polls as the coalition partners also found themselves at odds over other political issues.
The PPP has maintained that its concerns over the AJK elections were not adequately addressed despite being raised before the election commission, Parliament and other constitutional forums.
Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has also alleged that political and administrative machinery was used during the AJK election process and that commitments made to the PPP before the formation of the federal government were not honoured.
It is pertinent to note that earlier this week, AJK PPP leader and former prime minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore accused the PML-N of prioritising political power over the interests of the state. He called for doubling AJK's budget and ensuring a level playing field for all political parties in the region.
Rathore said unrest in AJK could not be treated as a purely regional matter, stressing that the region's stability had direct political, economic and social implications for Pakistan.
He said the situation in AJK over the past three months had caused serious concern among the people of the region as well as the wider Pakistani public. The issues confronting AJK, he added, could not be ignored because the relationship between Pakistan and Kashmir was rooted in shared history, ideology and emotion.

items.content:
An explosion that ripped through a wedding celebration in southern Iran on Tuesday, killing four people and injuring at least 68 others, likely resulted from a direct hit by a US munition and not a ricochet off another target, according to an analysis by weapons experts who reviewed images and video verified by Reuters.
The incident in the small town of Kuhestak has reignited concerns about the civilian toll in the US war with Iran and marks the most dramatic case since a missile struck an Iranian primary school in February, killing scores of children and teachers inside.
The US Central Command had announced its forces carried out multiple strikes across Iran's south on September 1, targeting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps air defence sites, radar systems, and communications facilities. The barrage came in retaliation for earlier Iranian attacks on US military assets around the Gulf.
On Thursday, US President JD Vance said the United States was investigating the strike. "We're investigating it because obviously we care. We want to know," Vance said during a White House press briefing.
The US military said it was aware of reports and was looking into them.
Iran's delegation to the United Nations did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
On the night of the attacks, dozens of residents had gathered in a home in Kuhestak for a wedding ceremony, according to eyewitnesses. During the party, a munition likely struck the building's roof.
Reuters shared video and images of the incident with four military weapons experts who said the damage was consistent with a direct hit, as opposed to secondary damage from a munition ricocheting off a separate target.
Three of the experts said the munition was likely a US weapon, rather than an errant Iranian air defence missile.
After the strike, bloody shoes lay amid the rubble, and wedding decorations that are common in that part of Iran were strewn about, the images show.
One eyewitness sent a voice note to Reuters moments after the strike, saying: "Kuhestak is destroyed. Four, five, ten houses were destroyed. Many people are under the rubble. God help us."
Local residents spoke on condition of anonymity.
Two US officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that the US military had carried out strikes in the area of Kuhestak on September 1, specifically targeting the town's telecommunications tower.
That tower is roughly 135 meters from the site of the wedding celebration, according to satellite imagery. The tower was hit at approximately 9:30pm local time, according to Iranian media.
The count of four deaths and 68 injuries came from Balochestan Human Rights Documentation Network and Haalvsh, which monitor and document human rights abuses.
Three of the people killed were guests of the wedding – Kolsoom Mollahi Najhandania, 43; Zarkhatoon Taheri, 50; and four-year-old Amir Mohammad Karimi – according to the groups. The fourth person, 16-year-old Mohammad Mallahi, was killed while riding his motorcycle near the communications tower.
The names have also been confirmed in Iranian media.
The incident comes more than six months after a missile destroyed a primary school in Minab on February 28, hours after the start of the US and Israeli attacks on Iran that launched the current conflict. That hit killed more than 175 children and teachers, according to Iranian officials.
Meanwhile, US Donald Trump has slammed the American left and the Democrats in a post on Truth Social, claiming they would "rather have us lose the war in Iran than have President Donald J Trump win the war for America".
"These are very sick people who suffer from serious TDS, sometimes referred to as Trump Derangement Syndrome," he adds.
Separately, Anadolu reports that the US' Strategic Petroleum Reserve has fallen to 286.6 million barrels - its lowest level since 1982.
Since the US launched its war on Iran, 30 per cent of the 415m barrel stockpile have been lost.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Security forces killed 48 "Indian sponsored terrorists" in intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan over the last 72 hours, the military's media wing said on Friday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the anti-terrorist operations were carried out in Mastung, Quetta, Kalat and Sibi districts against "Indian proxies, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij".
"During comprehensive anti-terrorist operations with increased tempo in Balochistan, in last twelve – twenty-four hours, security forces have conducted multiple Intelligence based operations in Mastung, Quetta, Kalat and Sibi District of Balochistan, against Indian proxies, Fitna al Hindustan & Fitna al Khwarij sending to hell thirty six Indian sponsored terrorists," ISPR said.
The military's media wing noted that on September 4 2026, during the conduct of an operation in Mastung, the movement of terrorists was "identified and engaged" by security forces, further adding that the intense exchange of fire resulted in the killing of six "Indian sponsored terrorists".
The statement also added that a cache of ammunition and improvised explosive devices was also destroyed on-site.
ISPR stated that "in another engagement, an intelligence-based operation was conducted in the general area of Shaban, district Quetta. During the conduct of the operation, own troops identified four Khwarij hideouts and, after an ensuing fire exchange, neutralised twenty-six Khwarij".
The statement further added that another IBO was conducted in Kalat, stating that during the conduct of the operation, security forces raided a terrorist hideout and killed two Indian sponsored terrorists.
"In Bhag area of district Sibi, swift response by security forces in conjunction with local population foiled terrorist attempt to raid police station, Bhag. During the fire exchange, two Indian sponsored terrorists were sent to hell," ISPR said.
The statement noted that in the "last forty-eight to seventy-two hours, 48 terrorists belonging to Indian proxies, Fitna al Hindustan & Fitna al Khwarij have been neutralised across Balochistan".
ISPR said that "sanitisation operations were being conducted to eliminate any other Indian sponsored terrorist found in the area", noting that the relentless counter terrorism campaign under vision "Azm e Istehkam" (as approved by Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan) by security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan would continue at "full pace" to wipe out menace of "foreign-sponsored" and supported terrorism from the country.
In an earlier statement in the day, the military's media wing said that security forces had killed 12 terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al-Hindustan, in an IBO in Balochistan's Kalat district.
According to a statement issued by the ISPR, the operation was conducted on September 2 following reports of the presence of terrorists in the area.
"During the conduct of the operation, terrorists' hideout was identified, monitored and busted through prompt surgical action by own forces," ISPR said. It said the action had killed "all twelve Indian sponsored terrorists".
"Cache of ammunition and improvised explosive devices were also destroyed on-site," the ISPR said. Sanitisation operations were under way in the area to search for and eliminate "any other Indian sponsored terrorist."
"The relentless counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of Azm-e-Istehkam (as approved by the Federal Apex Committee under the National Action Plan) by the security forces and law enforcement agencies of Pakistan will continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country," the statement concluded.
Separately, security forces foiled a terrorist attack in Bhag, Kachhi district, Radio Pakistan reported on Friday.
During the effective action by security forces, multiple terrorists were killed. A clearance operation by security forces was under way in the area to eliminate any remaining terrorists.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif paid tribute to the security forces for eliminating terrorists.
In separate statements, the president and the prime minister expressed their resolve to completely eradicate the menace of terrorism from the country.
They said the entire nation stood firmly with the armed forces in their unwavering resolve to safeguard the country.
"The continuous operations by law enforcement agencies and security forces are aimed at completely eliminating terrorism being patronized by external elements," the president remarked.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said officers and personnel of the security forces were conducting effective operations against terrorists attempting to undermine peace in the country.
He said the government will never allow terrorists to succeed in their nefarious designs to disrupt peace in Balochistan.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The price of a fertilizer bag could increase by up to Rs700 following a proposed amendment to the Gas Infrastructure Development Cess (GIDC) law, officials told the Senate Standing Committee on Petroleum on Friday.
The committee, which met under the chairmanship of Syed Mustafa Mahmood, was considering the Natural Gas Development Surcharge Amendment Bill and the Gas Infrastructure Development Cess Amendment Bill.
PPP leader Syed Naveed Qamar called for both bills to be deferred, saying his party had decided not to participate in any legislation. Qamar said the party had also decided not to support legislation in any committee and called for the bills to be postponed.
The committee chairman said the bills would first be discussed and members would be briefed on them before any decision was taken on their passage.
Officials of the Ministry of Petroleum Products said the proposed legislation sought to amend the GIDC law and expand the scope of where the collected cess could be utilised within the gas sector.
According to officials, the cess was originally meant to be spent on the TAPI and Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline projects. The authorities said Rs294 billion collected under the cess was to be spent within six months in accordance with a Supreme Court order.
Under the proposed amendment, however, the funds could be utilised for infrastructure anywhere in the gas sector. Officials said the fertilizer sector was currently receiving gas from Mari and new pipelines costing $500 million were being laid to supply Mari gas to fertilizer factories.
The Mari gas field is Pakistan's second-largest natural gas reservoir, located in District Ghotki, Sindh, and operated by Mari Energies Limited.
They said the cost of laying gas pipelines for the fertilizer sector would be passed on through a cess imposed on fertilizer bags, potentially increasing the price of a bag by up to Rs700.
Qamar strongly opposed the proposal, saying the entire burden would ultimately fall on the public. He also objected to passing the cost of companies purchasing ships on to consumers and farmers.
He said fertilizer prices should be determined by the market and the government should not fix them. He warned that other sectors could also make similar demands in the future.
"Tomorrow, power companies will say that we have built infrastructure, now give us the money," he said, adding that he could not support the proposal under any circumstances. Petroleum Secretary Hamid Yaqoob said the proposed amendment would also cover other infrastructure in the gas sector.
He told the committee that collection of the gas cess had remained suspended since 2021 following a court order. A representative of the Fertilizer Manufacturers Advisory Council said the fertilizer industry had itself developed the infrastructure in question and that its benefits would ultimately go to farmers.
He said the cost of the infrastructure would have to be passed on.
The representative also complained that the gas being supplied to the fertilizer sector was of poor quality and that the industry was receiving no subsidy.
At the conclusion of the discussion, the committee chairman said the bills would not be taken up, citing the PPP's decision. The committee subsequently deferred both bills.

items.title: NY Muslims reclaim their city after 9/11 backlash
items.summary:
Asad Dandia was eight when he
watched the September 11, 2001 attacks on television at his Pakistani-immigrant
parents' home in New York.
Then came the backlash -- years of Islamophobia as Americans processed attacks that had killed nearly 3,000 people.
There was anger, suspicion and worse.
At 19, Dandia experienced a police informant posing as a friend to infiltrate his family home, part of a now-disgraced surveillance effort purportedly seeking to detect Islamic extremism.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Asad Dandia was eight when he
watched the September 11, 2001 attacks on television at his Pakistani-immigrant
parents' home in New York.
Then came the backlash -- years of Islamophobia as Americans processed attacks that had killed nearly 3,000 people.
There was anger, suspicion and worse.
At 19, Dandia experienced a police informant posing as a friend to infiltrate his family home, part of a now-disgraced surveillance effort purportedly seeking to detect Islamic extremism.
Today, though, the 33-year-old
historian finds a New York transformed:
one with its first Muslim mayor, public prayers in Times Square and new mosques rising across the city.
"Twenty-five years after 9/11, we mourn and we grieve what happened, and at the same time, we recognize that I am not responsible for what happened," he told AFP.
"I don't deserve to be targeted for what happened, and I am as much of a New Yorker as anybody else in that respect," said Dandia, who leads walking tours centered on the city's Muslim communities.
Islamophobia surged in the United States after the 2001 attacks in which militants hijacked airliners and flew them into Manhattan's World Trade Center and
the Pentagon outside Washington.
A fourth plane crashed into a Pennsylvania field after a passenger revolt.
Muslims reported increased public assaults and harassment, and some stopped wearing visual markers such as hijabs in a bid to conceal their religion.
Meanwhile, US authorities monitored Muslims by requiring thousands of men and boys to register with the government, leading to many being deported from the country.
"Everyone was in such fear," said Mohammed Razvi, a native Pakistani who founded the Council of Peoples Organization nonprofit to support Muslims in New York after 9/11.
"We had gunshots fired in our neighborhood by individuals who felt that we were responsible," he added.
Razvi said he started introducing himself as "Mo" after 9/11 to avoid the stigma he encountered when saying "Mohammad."
"Muslims trying to live the American dream were being blamed for something they had nothing to do with or even control," he said.
In New York, police began surveilling hundreds of Muslims as part of their counterterrorism strategy, often targeting people without evidence of wrongdoing.
Dandia experienced this as a 19-year-old college student, when a young Bangladeshi man joined a mutual aid charity he had started.
The pair grew close: sharing meals, playing sports and even sleeping at Dandia's home. But seven months later, the man revealed that he was an NYPD informant sent to monitor Dandia and his community.
"It was heartbreaking, but it was also terrifying," he recalled. "My relationship with the world around me shifted underneath my feet."
After his ordeal, Dandia and rights groups won a landmark legal settlement that restricted the NYPD from launching similar surveillance programs and established a watchdog to monitor the force.
For Gadier Abbas, an attorney with the Council on American-Islamic Relations, the NYPD program was the prime example of the "anti-Muslim hysteria" that followed 9/11.
But today, Abbas said, "there is a lot
of hope."
"You see American Muslims in every single walk of life, almost at every single level, and that's a testament to the vibrancy of the community."
New York will soon boast the largest mosque in the state -- one of more than 100 added since 2001 in New York -- while Muslims are a rising cultural and political force.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who took his oath of office on a Quran, has become the new face of American leftist politics.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
realme is set to launch the realme C100 Series in Pakistan on September 7, introducing a new smartphone lineup built around one of the clearest changes in how young people live today: life no longer happens one role at a time.
realme’s recent The Ahead Generation research points to a shift away from the traditional “study first, work later” path. Students are entering work earlier, young people are exploring ambitions beyond a single career path, and learning, work, entertainment and social life increasingly overlap.
For this generation, a smartphone is expected to stay reliable across all of those different parts of life — without forcing users to constantly think about where the next charge is coming from.
At the center of the upcoming C100 Series is an 8000mAh Titan Long-Lasting Battery, designed to give users more freedom to move between the different sides of their day with fewer interruptions.
8000mAh. Life, Maxed.
A student’s day may start with university, move into freelance work or a client call, continue with content creation or sport, and end with gaming or time with friends.
In this kind of lifestyle, battery life is no longer just a specification. It can determine whether the phone continues to keep up as the user moves from one role to the next.
With support for Fup to 40 hours of heavy usage on a single charge, the realme C100 Series is designed to stay with users through longer days and multiple parts of their lives.
For realme, Life Maxed is not simply about fitting more into a day. It is about having the freedom to live more sides of your life without your battery becoming the reason you have to stop, compromise or choose one over another.
That is the idea behind the campaign message:
8000mAh. Life, Maxed.
One Big Battery Story, Two Choices
The C100 Series will arrive in Pakistan in two models:
realme C100 — 8GB + 256GB
realme C100x — 6GB + 128GB / 8GB + 128GB
Both models are built around the same core 8000mAh battery experience, while offering different configurations for users.
Battery utility also goes beyond the phone itself. The realme C100 supports 10W Reverse Charging, while the realme C100x supports 6W Reverse Charging, allowing users to share power with another device when needed.
The series will also bring added durability and a smooth viewing experience to complement its long-lasting battery, with further details to be revealed at launch.
Built for More Sides of Life
As younger consumers take greater control over their careers, ambitions and everyday choices, they increasingly need technology that can remain dependable across different parts of their lives.
The realme C100 Series brings that idea together through a simple promise:
More freedom to live every side of your life. Powered by 8000mAh.
The realme C100 Series will officially launch in Pakistan on September 7, when realme will reveal complete specifications, pricing and availability.
8000mAh. Life, Maxed.

items.content:
Abstract
Enterprise resource planning (ERP) is a critical part of the digital transformation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), especially when cloud ERP systems are available to organizations with limited internal IT resources. However, the process of implementing ERP is more than just a technical one; it involves significant transformation of organization, roles, information and habits. This paper aims to thoroughly investigate the impact of change-management practices on ERP implementation success on the part of UK SMEs with a focus on user adoption, project delivery and operational efficiency. This paper builds on existing ERP and organizational-change literature, suggesting that the success of ERP implementation depends heavily on the ability of the organization to prepare employees, communicate the need for change, control the risks of the ERP implementation and ensure ongoing support following deployment.
The analysis will be based on three interrelated areas of change management: stakeholder engagement and organization readiness; training, user adoption and behavioural change; and risk management, after go-live support and operational improvement. Best practices that have been published at this time have consistently shown that top-management commitment, communication, user involvement, training and change management are important factors that influence ERP outcomes (Nah, Lau, & Kuang, 2001; Umble, Haft, & Umble, 2003; Somers & Nelson, 2001). In SMEs, these things are even more relevant as limited capital, resources, and human resources can increase the impact of the opposition, insufficient preparation, and disruptions of the implementation process. Cloud ERP can overcome certain technical limitations, but it does not reduce the organizational problems of adjusting well-established routines and decision-making procedures.
The paper concludes that the project governance of ERP must include change management as part of the process rather than as a post-technical implementation process. The effective involvement of stakeholders with a formal engagement process, structured training, risk registers, communication and post-go-live support can help improve user acceptance and mitigate implementation disruption. In the case of UK SMEs whose management skills and specialist resources may be limited, a pro rata, integrated and change management strategy may therefore enhance the chances of ERP investment delivering operational value beyond simply the successful software implementation.
Keywords: Enterprise Resource Planning, ERP, Change Management, SMEs, Cloud ERP, User Adoption
Introduction
1.1 Transforming Data Sharing and Functioning
ERP systems play a vital role for organizations to link financial management, human resources, procurement, supply-chain activities, customer information and operational data together. ERP systems do not just change the way information is created within the business; they also transform how that information is shared and how various business and organizational functions use them. This means that implementation involves both technology investment and organizational change. Previous studies on the implementation of ERP have shown that, on its own, the technical use of an ERP system does not guarantee successful implementation, as organisational, managerial, and human factors can influence whether the system delivers its intended benefits (Somers & Nelson, 2001; Nah et al., 2001; Umble et al., 2003). So, the success of ERP implementation should be interpreted in a broader sense than the mere fact that software is installed to the specifications. This is especially important for SMEs. SMEs typically have less access to financial resources, lower levels of specialist IT support and rely on key workers and external vendors more than larger organizations. These traits can increase the impacts of the major technology projects, while at the same time decreasing the capacity of the organization to deal with implementation issues. Meanwhile, cloud computing has alleviated some of the infrastructure and maintenance pressures that are often a part of ERP systems, opening up the door for smaller companies to gain access to enterprise-level technologies. However, cloud deployment cannot solve the challenge of redesigning processes, determining new responsibilities and building employee competency. There are still changes to organizational practices and user behaviour when implementing enterprise systems (Esteves-Sousa & Pastor-Collado, 2000). Change management is then placed at the crossroads of technology and organization. User involvement, communication, training, and leadership support and organizational readiness are recurring critical success factors cited in literature of ERP projects (Aladwani, 2001; Nah et al., 2001; Somers & Nelson, 2001). The theory of change management also focuses on how to get ready for the change, how to get them to accept the desired state and how to reinforce the new behaviour or mindset once the change has taken place (Armenakis & Harris, 2009). With this view, it is paramount to recognize that employee resistance to ERP doesn’t necessarily mean they are not interested in innovation. It may, however, be due to a lack of clarity about the role one has at work, lack of understanding of the technology, lack of involvement in decision making or concern about the implications of organizational change.
In this context, this paper investigates the following research question: How does the adoption of change-management practices affect user adoption, project delivery and operational efficiency in the context of cloud-based ERP implementation in UK SMEs? The analysis focuses on areas of relevance for implementation outcomes, such as: stakeholder engagement and organizational readiness; training of employees and user uptake; and risk management, post-go-live support and efficiency. The primary thesis is that change management is not a project management on its own. Instead, it is a component of the governance framework that links technological change to organizational performance.
Stakeholder Engagement and Organizational Readiness
2.1 Requiring Sound System
One of the most consistent factors that have been identified as a determinant of ERP implementation success is stakeholder engagement. ERP projects comprises various groups of people in the organization, such as a senior management team, operational staff, finance staff, IT staff and external implementation partners. They might have different expectations and requirements. Therefore, developing a technically sound system requires the involvement of key stakeholders in defining its requirements; conversely, the resulting system may be technically functional but fail to reflect actual operational needs (Nah et al., 2001; Umble et al., 2003).
2.2 Users Involvement and ERP Systems
User involvement is critical because ERP systems often standardize processes that were previously managed or performed differently by individual users. According to Aladwani (2001), resistance can be minimized if organizations explain the reason and outcome of the technological change lucidly and take the participation of the users into the process of change. Likewise, user involvement and top management support are among the critical factors that are linked with ERP success, as described by Somers and Nelson (2001). Senior-management involvement can have a particularly strong impact in SMEs, where organizational structures are often less hierarchical and key decisions around the use of technology can have an immediate impact on the entire organization.
Organisational preparation is, therefore, more than technical readiness. It encompasses leadership support, employee awareness, the availability of resources to facilitate new procedures, and employees’ preparedness for change. Armenakis and Harris (2009) define readiness for change as a state of people within an organization where they have a knowledge of the need for change and think that the organization and members are likely to succeed in change. In the context of ERP, this implies that individuals should develop a clear change story to present before implementation, map out the stakeholders involved, convey anticipated advantages and constraints, and set up systems for feedback from staff members. Good stakeholder engagement can then enhance the quality of requirements and minimize misunderstandings and resistance when implementing the requirements themselves.
Training, User Adoption and Behavioural Change
3.1 Meeting Technical Requirements
Whether the employees use the ERP effectively or not is the key to the successful implementation of ERP. Even when technical requirements are met, a system may fail to create organisational value if employees do not use it effectively, do not use it at all, or enter inaccurate information. Therefore, user acceptance and user satisfaction are crucial factors of information-system success (DeLone & McLean, 2003; Wu & Wang, 2007). Training is one of the main tools which can transform the technical implementation into successful user adoption.
It is not enough to simply teach software functionality when it comes to ERP training. It is paramount that personnel maintain clear visibility regarding adjustments to their operational mandates, processes and working relationships with other areas and understand the impact of the new system. Education and training are continuous critical success factors as users need to learn enough to use the system and adjust to new business processes (Nah et al., 2001; Umble et al., 2003). A more recent ERP study also shows that training is crucial during the implementation and post-implementation stages as the organizations improve their use of the system after a successful implementation.
3.2 System Adoption and Systems Training
The relationship between training and system adoption is also consistent with technology-acceptance research. Venkatesh et al. (2003) emphasise that perception of usefulness, ease of use, social influence and facilitating conditions can influence the adoption of a technology. In the context of an ERP system, these factors mean that staff members are more inclined to embrace new systems because they know their real-world benefits and can count on the right resources to help them. Hence, for the successful implementation of the project, SMEs can avail of role-specific training, establishing super user arrangements, and demonstrations and feedback mechanisms other than one-shot training before implementation.
Additionally, change management needs to understand that adoption is a gradual process. Employees may understand how to handle a system but struggle to use it effectively when under pressure in real-world situations. Accessible support and continuous learning can then help mitigate any momentary implementation problems into permanent resistance. The results indicate that there is a need for the training to be linked to communication, user involvement, and other aspects of organizational change. Consequently, it will be a purely technical activity (Aladwani, 2001; Esteves-Sousa & Pastor-Collado, 2000).
Risk Management, Post-Go-Live Support and Operational Efficiency
4.1 A Look at EPR Implementation
There is profound vulnerability associated with the implementation of ERP. Challenges can include lack of requirements, overly aggressive schedules, poor data quality, reliance on vendors, lack of resources, integration issues and employee resistance. While scope, cost and schedule are often the primary focus of traditional project management, ERP implementation also needs to take into account organizational and behavioural risks. Project management, change management and communication and organizational support have been shown through critical-success-factor research to be in a close relationship (Somers & Nelson, 2001; Nah et al., 2001).
For SMEs, it is possible to identify and keep track of these risks with a relatively simple formal risk register. A risk register can attribute responsibility, provide a way to plan for mitigating risks and set up escalation plans for issues that are affecting project delivery. When considering change-related risks, these should be integrated into the technical risks. For instance, albeit the technology is operating correctly, low participation rates in training may indicate problems later in the implementation process, as can user acceptance issues or stakeholder involvement. Embedding these risks within project governance helps project managers take action before they turn into operational problems.
4.2 Post-go-live As Vital Tool in ERP
Post-go-live is also vital. ERP implementation does not end with system deployment; users, processes, and organisational needs continue to evolve and change over time. Post-implementation studies reveal that continuous support, system enhancement, knowledge sharing and user involvement are vital areas for ensuring ERP’s long-term success (Butarbutar et al., 2023). Post-go-live support can cover help-desk arrangements, corrective actions, system enhancements, refresher training, performance monitoring and structured feedback. These methods enable organizations to detect defects and usability issues before employees become comfortable with the new system. Once installed, the ultimate success of ERP is measured by operational value, not installation. The effective implementation should help to improve the quality of information, integration of processes, decision-making and organizational efficiency. DeLone and McLean (2003) highlight that the three factors of system quality, information quality and service quality lead to use, user satisfaction and to eventual organization benefits. Therefore, UK SMEs need to consider factors like user adoption, process-cycle times, error rates, reporting quality, task completion and operational productivity when assessing ERP projects. The benefits of change management are all about connecting the dots between system availability and the actual realized organizational benefits.
Conclusion
5.1 Organizational Change in UK-SMEs
It is important to recognize that ERP in UK-SMEs is not just a software installation project, but a programme of organization change supported by technology. Stakeholder involvement, leadership commitment, training, effective communication, and continued support are consistently identified in the literature as contributing to the success of ERP implementation. (Nah et al., 2001; Somers & Nelson, 2001; Umble et al., 2003). While cloud ERP can help to make enterprise systems more accessible for SMEs, it cannot overcome behavioural and organizational issues that result from the adoption of new systems and processes.
Based on the evidence presented in this paper, change management can impact successful ERP in three interrelated ways. Firstly, stakeholder commitment and organizational readiness contribute to the understanding, quality of requirements, and acceptance of the transformation. Second, formal training and ongoing user assistance increase adoption and minimize workarounds and suboptimal system use. Third, embedding change-related risks in project governance and continuing to support organizations after go-live can help make projects more resilient and can help organizations to translate technological investments into benefits gained in operations.
For UK SMEs, the implication for practice is that change management should be integral to the project initiation phase and continue through to post-implementation rather than be introduced upon the identification of resistance. A lean and balanced approach such as stakeholder mapping (identification and prioritization of stakeholders), communication, user participation, training, risk monitoring, and post-go-live evaluation can give smaller organizations an enabling concept for complex ERP transformation. In the end, the success of ERP implementation is not determined by whether an organization implements an efficient information system, but by whether its employees, processes, and management approach are able to successfully transform to leverage that system in order to deliver long-lasting value to the organization.
Author’s Profile
Ogheneruona Ajuyasono is a professional technology expert and IT Project Manager with extensive years of delivering software, systems implementation and business transformation enabled by technology.
