items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A new leak has provided an early look at Samsung’s upcoming Exynos 2700 chipset, which is expected to power some Galaxy S27 series models. The leaked information reveals details about the processor’s CPU, GPU, cache, and AI capabilities.
The leak comes from a die shot shared by SemiAnalysis. The image appears to show the internal layout of the Exynos 2700 and includes labels that reveal several key specifications.
According to the leak, the Exynos 2700 could feature a 10-core CPU based on new Arm CPU designs. The setup is reportedly made up of two C2 Ultra cores and eight C2 Pro cores. One C2 Ultra core could reach 4.24GHz, while the second may run at 3.36GHz.
Exynos 2700 Leak Reveals Major Details of Galaxy S27 Processor
The eight C2 Pro cores are reportedly split into two groups. Four cores could operate at 3.74GHz, while the remaining four may run at 2.88GHz. This is an unusual configuration because the two Ultra cores appear to have different maximum clock speeds.
For comparison, Samsung’s Exynos 2600 reportedly uses one C1 Ultra core at 3.8GHz, three C1 Pro cores at 3.25GHz and six C1 Pro cores at 2.75GHz. The Exynos 2700 therefore appears to bring a different approach to CPU design.
The leaked chip could also include 24MB of system-level cache along with around 16MB of L3 cache. These larger cache sizes could help the processor handle demanding applications and multitasking more efficiently.
However, the reported 4.24GHz peak clock speed is lower than the speeds expected from Qualcomm’s upcoming flagship chips. This suggests that Samsung may be focusing on overall efficiency and architecture improvements rather than simply pushing CPU frequencies higher.
The graphics side could also receive an upgrade. The Exynos 2700 is expected to feature an Xclipse 970 GPU, reportedly with eight workgroup processors (WGPs). This appears to be similar to the GPU configuration previously associated with the Exynos 2600.
Another major highlight is the size of the NPU, or Neural Processing Unit. The leaked die shot shows a relatively large NPU, suggesting that Samsung could be putting more focus on on-device AI performance. This could help the Galaxy S27 series handle AI features more quickly without relying as heavily on cloud processing.
See Also: Samsung Exynos 2700 Shows Impressive Performance Against Snapdragon Chips
Samsung is also reportedly planning to place the Exynos 2700 alongside its DRAM. This design could allow a shared Heat Path Block to cover both components. The approach may improve heat management and help keep temperatures under control during heavy workloads.
The Exynos 2700 is expected to appear in selected Galaxy S27 and Galaxy S27 Plus models. Recent reports have also suggested that Samsung could use the chip in some Galaxy S27 Ultra variants, although this remains unconfirmed.
For now, the leaked specifications should be treated with caution. Samsung has not officially announced the Exynos 2700, and its final specifications could still change before the Galaxy S27 series launches.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) registered 4,761 new companies during August 2026, reflecting sustained momentum in business formalization, growing entrepreneurial confidence, and the success of SECP’s facilitation and digital transformation initiatives — driven by the seamless functionality of the eZfile portal and near-total (99.9%) online registrations through integrated federal and provincial systems. The milestone has pushed the total number of registered companies in Pakistan to 311,765.
Commenting on the milestone, Dr. Kabir Ahmed Sidhu, Chairman SECP, stated that the continuous surge in corporate registrations reflects the growing trust of entrepreneurs and investors in Pakistan’s transparent and business-friendly regulatory framework, powered by our digital transformation initiatives.
Private companies continued to account for the largest share of new incorporations, with 2,762 companies (58.01%), followed by 1,846 Single Member Companies (38.78%). In addition, SECP registered 113 Limited Liability Partnerships (2.37%), 28 Not-for-Profit companies (0.59%), and 12 other companies (0.25%) including public companies, foreign and TOs during the month. The sustained preference for private and single-member company structures reflects the growing confidence of startups, SMEs, and entrepreneurs in Pakistan’s corporate regime.
Geographically, Punjab remained the hub of business activity, accounting for 2,547 (53%) of new registrations. This was followed by Islamabad Capital Territory with 843 (18%), Sindh with 702 (15%), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 407 (9%), Gilgit-Baltistan 151 (3%), and Balochistan 111 (2%). The widespread geographical distribution of incorporations demonstrates that entrepreneurial activity continues to expand across all regions of the country.
The Information Technology sector continues to serve as the primary engine of corporate growth, leading the monthly registrations with 872 new incorporations. The broader diversification of Pakistan’s corporate landscape is further evidenced by robust performance across other key industries, including Trading (732), Services (601), Construction (295), Tourism (232), Food and Beverages (216), E-Commerce (152), Real Estate Development (143), Education (129), and Mining and Quarrying (103), with a further 1,286 incorporations across other sectors , reflecting a well-rounded expansion across multiple segments of the economy.
Foreign investors continued to demonstrate confidence in Pakistan’s corporate sector. During August 2026, 134 investors from several countries participated in newly incorporated companies, led by China with 106 investors.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Walmart-owned Flipkart’s quick commerce arm Minutes could add another 1,000 dark stores by mid-2027 or the Big Billion Days sale of 2027, according to a UBS report.
The brokerage, citing an industry expert, said the rollout would depend on the performance of individual markets and the development of supporting hubs and backend infrastructure.
If the expansion materialises, it would nearly double Minutes’ network to around 2,000 stores.
The projected expansion comes after Flipkart said in June that it had scaled Minutes to 1,000 micro-fulfilment centres across 130 cities and more than 8,000 pin codes. At the time, Flipkart Minutes head Kunal Gupta reportedly said the company planned to expand the network to 1,500 centres across 180 cities.
According to UBS, Minutes’ stores average 800-1,000 orders per day, while mature stores (those operational for five to six months) process around 1,200-1,500 orders daily.
Minutes is now being used to bring customers into the Flipkart ecosystem for fresh, beauty and personal care and other immediate-use categories. In locations where the service is available, around 40-45% of customers visiting Flipkart also visit Minutes, the brokerage firm added.
The expert also indicated that transactions per customer per quarter are rising as users consolidate more purchases within Flipkart.
Minutes Steps Up Consumption Game
Minutes’ net order value, excluding mobile phones, stands at ₹500-₹530, nearing Blinkit’s average net order value of ₹518 in Q1 FY27, the report said. Including mobile phones, Minutes’ order value is estimated to be higher than Blinkit’s, reflecting Flipkart’s strength in mobiles and electronics.
Metro cities currently account for around 60%-65% of demand on Minutes. The platform is also seeing traction in Kolkata and Tier II and III cities in eastern India, while south India is scaling rapidly.
In non-metro markets, Minutes operates across larger delivery areas as customers are more willing to accept delivery times of 25-30 minutes. UBS said Flipkart’s existing ecommerce customer base and regional demand data are helping it identify markets where rivals have a limited presence.
Minutes’ advertising revenue is broadly comparable with leading quick commerce platforms, while its gross margins are improving but remain below Blinkit’s. Its cost per order in most cities has also moved closer to Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart, though it is yet to match Blinkit’s operational efficiency.
Flipkart primarily manages Minutes’ dark stores itself but is increasingly using partners and franchisees for a smaller part of the network. Partners help secure locations, while Flipkart retains control over inventory, assortment, store design, and customer experience.
The ecommerce giant is also looking to widen the assortment on Minutes and move up the consumption ladder. In August, the quick-commerce arm entered the premium grocery and specialty food segment with its private-label brand Pykd, which will offer products ranging from cheese, coffee and kombucha to ramen, ghee and oils.
The company is also looking to onboard third-party premium brands, with the offering initially being piloted in Bengaluru, competing with the likes of FirstClub, Blinkit Gourmet, and Swiggy Instamart’s Noice.
Quick Commerce Expansion Race Intensifies
This comes at a time when Amazon Now also announced plans to expand its fulfillment network to 300 cities, up from 100 cities it was targeting earlier this year. According to UBS, Amazon Now currently has around 500-600 dark stores and processes 4-5 Lakh orders daily. It could reach 1,000 stores by the end of 2026.
Amazon Now is currently available to over 5 Cr customers in more than 15 metro and non-metro cities such as Bengaluru, Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad, Amritsar, Kochi, among others.
While Zepto has put its IPO plans on hold, it had proposed using ₹1,629 Cr from the issue proceeds to set up 1,904 dark stores by FY30. Swiggy, meanwhile, has said Instamart’s existing network can support more than twice its current GOV.
The expansion comes as quick commerce platforms move beyond groceries into electronics, beauty, fashion, medicines, and home products. India’s quick commerce market is expected to become a $40 Bn opportunity by 2030.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
D2C sneaker brand Comet has raised ₹100 Cr ($10.6 Mn) in a Series B funding round led by global investment firm Verlinvest. Existing investors Elevation Capital and Nexus Venture Partners also doubled down on the startup.
Additionally, Snapchat CBO Ajit Mohan, Urban Company founder Abhiraj Singh Bhal, and Bhaane cofounder Anand Ahuja also backed Comet as angel investors.
The capital will be used to expand Comet’s retail presence, strengthen product development and tech, as well as foster research and development. The startup is working on developing its own sole moulds as well as the tools required to bring new footwear models to market.
As of now, the startup operates ten company owned company operated (CoCo) stores across India. Comet aims to scale to 20 stores across India by the end of the ongoing fiscal. It also intends to double its footwear portfolio from four to eight distinct models.
“We want to continue pushing the boundaries of what an Indian footwear brand can build, which means investing deeply in sole technology, R&D and engineering. Every new model requires significant investment in both product development and sole tooling. We are about to launch a model we have worked on for a year specifically for females, with its own sole tooling following significant capex investment. These are long-term investments in the product capabilities we want Comet to be known for, and this round gives us the ability to continue building them at scale,” said cofounder Utkarsh Gupta.
Founded in 2023 by Gupta and Dishant Daryani, Comet sells design-led, locally manufactured sneakers primarily through its own website. The startup is particularly noteworthy for releasing limited edition products every 1-2 months that often sell out within minutes.
Prior to this round, it had raised around $5 Mn from Elevation Capital and Nexus in July 2024.
On the financial front, Comet made a net loss of ₹4.4 Cr in FY25, its first full financial year of operations. Meanwhile, it reported operating revenue of ₹29.1 Cr. The startup is yet to report its FY26 numbers.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is working on a new feature that could make it easier to use third-party AI agents and other automated services directly inside the messaging app. The company has started rolling out support for third-party agents to a limited number of users in selected countries.
The feature was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.35.3. It allows users to connect an external agent to a dedicated WhatsApp chat and communicate with it without opening another app or website.
WhatsApp Begins Rolling Out Support for Third-Party AI Agents
With the new feature, users can add and configure an agent through WhatsApp settings. During setup, they can give the agent a name and select a profile picture. The chosen name and image will then appear in the chat list, making the agent easier to identify.
WhatsApp currently allows users to connect up to five agents to one account. This could be useful for people who want to use separate agents for different tasks.
The feature is not limited to AI-powered services. WhatsApp also supports regular bots that can perform specific functions or respond to predefined commands.
API Key Connects the Agent
After setting up an agent, WhatsApp generates an API key. Users need to copy this key and add it to the service where their agent is hosted.
The exact process can vary depending on the platform providing the agent. Once the key is connected, the agent can communicate with the user through a dedicated WhatsApp conversation.
Users can also generate a new API key if they need to reset the connection.
Agents Cannot Access Other WhatsApp Chats
Privacy is an important part of the new feature. A connected agent can only see the messages that users share with it in its dedicated conversation.
It cannot access other WhatsApp chats, contacts, or media stored in unrelated conversations. For now, agents can only be used in individual chats. They cannot be added to groups or communities.
WhatsApp also warns that AI agents may provide incorrect information. Users should therefore verify important information before relying on an AI-generated response.
See Also: WhatsApp Tests New Safety Warning for Unofficial Web Clients
Users Can Manage or Remove Agents
WhatsApp is also adding management options for connected agents. Users can return to the settings section to change an agent’s name or profile picture.
If an agent is removed, WhatsApp disconnects it from the conversation. Users will no longer be able to send messages to the agent or receive new responses.
However, removing an agent does not automatically erase the existing conversation. Previous messages remain available in the chat, allowing users to review their earlier interactions.
If users want to connect the agent again later, they will need to set it up again and generate a new API key.
Agent Chats Are Not End-to-End Encrypted
There is an important privacy difference between chats with agents and normal WhatsApp conversations.
Messages exchanged with third-party agents are not considered end-to-end encrypted. WhatsApp explains that these conversations are handled through a Meta service on behalf of the agent developer. This means the developer operating the agent can access the messages as part of providing the service.
This does not affect regular personal WhatsApp conversations. Messages and calls between people on WhatsApp continue to use end-to-end encryption.
Limited Rollout for Now
The third-party agent feature is currently available to only a small number of WhatsApp users. Most Android users will not see the new Agents section in their settings yet.
WhatsApp is expected to expand access gradually over the coming months. The company has not confirmed when the feature will become available to everyone.
For now, the rollout gives an early look at how WhatsApp could become a platform for more than traditional messaging by allowing external AI agents and bots to operate directly within the app.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority is preparing a new round of measures to tighten subscriber verification and strengthen control over SIM issuance as fraudulent use of mobile connections remains a major concern.
According to details shared by the regulator, the measures under consideration include facial verification, centralized blacklisting of SIM sale channels, rationalization of sales outlets, and stricter controls on duplicate SIM issuance.
The proposed facial verification system would add another layer to the existing biometric verification process, making it harder for fraudsters to activate SIMs using stolen or fabricated biometric data.
PTA also plans to introduce a centralized blacklisting mechanism for SIM sale channels. This would allow the regulator to take coordinated action against retailers, franchises, or outlets found involved in irregular or unauthorized SIM issuance.
At the same time, the authority is considering rationalizing the overall network of SIM sale channels to improve oversight of where mobile connections are sold and activated.
The process for issuing duplicate SIMs is also being strengthened to reduce the risk of unauthorized replacements and misuse of existing subscriber identities.
These upcoming measures build on a broader set of controls already introduced by PTA to reduce illegal SIM issuance and biometric manipulation.
The regulator has geofenced SIM-sale devices within a 100-meter radius of registered sale locations to prevent their unauthorized movement. It has also strengthened its Live Finger Detection system to identify fake fingerprints made from materials such as paper, silicon, and nylon.
Access to SIM-sale devices has been restricted to a maximum of two authorized users, while SIM sales are prohibited between 12:00 am and 6:00 am. The SIM disowning period has also been extended from 60 days to 365 days.
Crackdown Expands Across SIMs, Devices, and Subscriber Identities
Between January 2024 and August 2026, the regulator carried out 90 raids across 40 cities against illegal Pakistani SIM operations. These operations led to the seizure of more than 29,346 SIMs, 234 biometric devices, and around 602,000 paper-based digital fingerprints, while 134 people were arrested.
In a separate crackdown on international SIMs, PTA teams working with the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency conducted 25 raids, resulting in 37 arrests and the recovery of more than 8,000 international SIMs.
The regulator has blocked a total of 18.2 million illegal SIMs through different regulatory interventions.
Of these, around 7.9 million were blocked through pattern-based detection, 2.1 million were linked to Afghan ACC or POR card holders, while 8.2 million were associated with cancelled, impounded, deceased, or expired CNICs.
During the period from July 2025 to June 2026, PTA also blocked 768 mobile numbers and 707 IMEIs, while 11 CNICs were blacklisted in connection with fraudulent activity. Another 2,497 subscribers were issued warnings.
Operators Face Billions in Penalties
PTA has also taken enforcement action against cellular mobile operators over SIM-related violations.
A total of 48 show-cause notices were issued, followed by 39 enforcement orders involving financial penalties, while four cases were disposed of with warnings.
The combined penalties amounted to Rs 4.2 billion, including Rs 1.87 billion against Ufone, Rs 1.36 billion against Jazz, Rs 580 million against Zong, and Rs 390 million against Telenor Pakistan.
Some of these cases are currently subject to stays granted by the Islamabad High Court or the Telecom Tribunal.
The latest proposals suggest that PTA is moving beyond post-incident blocking and towards tighter prevention at the point of SIM issuance itself.
By adding facial verification, blacklisting problematic sale channels, restricting duplicate SIM issuance, and expanding control over the retail network, the regulator is seeking to make it more difficult for fraudulent connections to enter circulation in the first place.
The broader objective is to reduce the use of illegal SIMs in identity theft, financial fraud, and other criminal activity while strengthening trust in Pakistan’s subscriber verification system.

items.content:
Nigerian startup ChipMango has raised a US$1.9 million seed round of funding to expand chip-design operations across Africa, Europe, and the United States (US).
Founded in 2022 by Ola Fadiran and Jovan Andjelich, ChipMango partners with leading semiconductor companies to deliver industry-aligned learning and certification programmes that prepare learners for real-world roles.
Its AI-powered platform provides custom-built labs and curated course content, giving educators and universities the tools to turbocharge their microelectronics curriculum.
The startup’s $1.9 million seed round was led by Atlantica Ventures, with DFS Labs, Madica, Kaleo Ventures, Trilinear Technologies, and Malta Ventures also participating. ChipMango will deploy the capital raised towards expanding its engineering and product teams while growing operations across Africa, Europe, and the United States.
A design centre in Malta is in the pipeline, supported by Malta Ventures, while ChipMango also plans to support initiatives around semiconductor capability, workforce development, and AI infrastructure in Rwanda.
The company’s expansion comes as demand for semiconductor and AI infrastructure capabilities grows globally, creating opportunities for engineering talent in emerging markets to participate in increasingly complex parts of the technology supply chain.
“The next era of AI will not be defined by software alone. It will depend on who can design the chips, systems and intelligent hardware that power it. ChipMango is expanding access to those capabilities so more regions can help build the technologies shaping the future,” said Fadiran.
“ChipMango converts Africa’s deep engineering talent into world-class chip-design capability, already proven through production-grade work for global customers. We believe it can become foundational infrastructure for the next generation of smart devices and semiconductor IP,” Anikó Szigetvári, founding partner at Atlantica Ventures, said.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s decision to revise its net-metering framework was aimed in part at encouraging rooftop solar consumers to make greater use of battery storage, according to Federal Power Minister Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari.
The minister said the government wants households and businesses with solar systems to store surplus electricity generated during the day and use it during expensive evening peak hours, reducing reliance on the national grid when power costs are highest.
Leghari described battery installation as one of the most practical options for rooftop solar users, arguing that stored solar energy can help consumers make better use of their own generation instead of exporting most of it during the day and buying costly electricity back from the grid later.
He said the shift towards storage is not limited to residential users. Power distribution companies are also developing battery energy storage systems, while the national grid operator is preparing for significant investment in large-scale storage infrastructure.
The remarks point to a broader change in Pakistan’s power strategy, with batteries increasingly being treated as an important part of both rooftop solar economics and grid management.
Net Billing Aims to Encourage Greater Use of Self-Generated Power
Leghari also addressed criticism that the government’s move away from the previous net-metering model was intended to discourage rooftop solar adoption.
He rejected that view, saying one of the objectives of the revised framework was to encourage consumers to consume more of the electricity they generate themselves.
Under such a system, battery storage becomes more important because daytime solar generation can be saved for use after sunset, when household demand often remains high, and electricity purchased from the grid can be more expensive.
The minister said applications from consumers seeking to sell surplus solar power to the grid have not declined following the policy changes, which he cited as evidence that interest in rooftop solar remains strong.
He also maintained that the government is not trying to slow solar adoption and said market forces, rather than the government, determine solar panel prices.
Battery Storage Could Shape Pakistan’s Next Solar Phase
Pakistan’s rooftop solar market has expanded rapidly in recent years as households and businesses seek protection from high electricity costs and greater control over their energy supply.
The government’s growing focus on storage suggests that the next phase of this transition may be centred not only on generating solar electricity but also on deciding when and how that electricity is used.
For consumers, batteries could help reduce peak-hour grid purchases and increase energy independence. For utilities and the national grid, larger storage systems could help balance demand, absorb more renewable generation and improve overall system flexibility.
The change therefore represents more than a revision to compensation rules for exported solar electricity. It signals a move towards a model in which battery storage plays a central role in Pakistan’s future solar and power-sector strategy.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Healthtech startup Medulance has raised ₹24 Cr ($2.5 Mn) in its Series A 2 funding round from Auxano Capital, existing backers Alkemi, Equentis and a group of angel investors.
The startup plans to use the fresh capital to expand emergency services pan India, grow its hospital and enterprise business, and improve its technology and connected ambulances.
Founded in 2017 by Pranav Bajaj and Ravjot Singh Arora, Medulance is an Indian GPS-based emergency response and ambulance booking service.
It provides app- and phone-based ambulance booking and dispatch services, with a fleet that includes advanced life support (ALS), basic life support (BLS), patient transport and mortuary vans.
The startup uses tech to manage ambulances, emergency calls and dispatch, while connecting patients with medical teams and hospitals in real time.
It uses GPS and 5G-enabled technology to enable real-time patient data sharing with hospitals.
Medulance claims to have more than 15,000 ambulances across over 500 cities. Its network covers more than 80 Lakh people and handles around 5,000 emergency calls every day.
The startup also claims an average response time of less than 11 minutes, 95% fleet uptime and more than 110 corporate and hospital clients.
These ambulances can send a patient’s health data to hospitals in real time and use cameras to help doctors assess patients remotely before they reach the hospital.
Medulance has raised over $5 Mn to date, including a $3 Mn Series A round led by Alkemi Growth Capital in 2024.
The latest funding comes as Medulance looks to scale its emergency response network amid growing demand for organised ambulance and pre-hospital care services in India.
The country’s emergency healthcare system remains fragmented, with ambulance operators, hospitals and medical teams often working across disconnected systems, creating gaps in response times and coordination.
India’s ambulance services market reached $5.5 Bn in 2025 and is expected to grow to $9.8 Bn by 2034, registering a CAGR of 6.33% between 2026 and 2034.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Meta-owned WhatsApp has launched bill payments in India, allowing users to find, manage, and pay household and utility bills directly within the messaging app.
Powered by the Bharat Connect network, the feature gives users access to 22,722 billers across 30 categories, including electricity, gas, water, FASTag, insurance, credit card payments, and loan repayments.
The feature is being rolled out gradually and will be available to Android and iOS users across India over the coming weeks.
To use the feature, users can tap the “₹” icon at the top of the WhatsApp home screen, select a bill category and biller, enter their account details, and view the outstanding amount. They can then make the payment using UPI, a debit card, or a credit card.
WhatsApp will also allow users to manage multiple accounts under a single biller, such as utility connections for their homes, offices, or family members. Users will be able to view past payments and upcoming bills within the app.
“With bill payments, we’re bringing… simplicity to one of the most routine tasks in every household. No more juggling apps or tracking multiple due dates. We want to make paying a bill on WhatsApp as effortless as sending a message, and help bring the convenience of digital payments to people across the remotest parts of the country,” said Arun Srinivas, MD and country head of Meta India.
The launch comes as Meta looks to expand WhatsApp’s role beyond messaging and deepen its presence in India’s digital payments market. The app already allows users to make UPI payments, mobile recharges, and metro ticket bookings.
The bill payment feature will put WhatsApp in more direct competition with PhonePe, Google Pay, and Paytm, which already allow users to pay utility and other recurring bills through their apps.
However, WhatsApp Pay still has considerable ground to cover. In July 2026, it processed 16.78 Cr UPI transactions worth ₹12,957 Cr, ranking eighth among UPI apps and trailing market leaders PhonePe, Google Pay, and Paytm by a wide margin.
WhatsApp faced restrictions on the number of users it could onboard for UPI after launching the service in India in 2020. In December 2024, the NPCI removed the cap on the number of users WhatsApp Pay could onboard, allowing it to offer UPI services to its entire user base in India.
WhatsApp’s payments ambitions have also received a boost from a major leadership change at Meta. In June, CRED founder Kunal Shah stepped away from the fintech unicorn’s day-to-day operations to take over as the global head of WhatsApp. The move coincided with Meta leading a ₹8,550 Cr ($900 Mn) Series H funding round in CRED.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
The student-founded Ghanaian climate-smart agri-tech startup Wobil Technologies is designing, manufacturing, and deploying hybrid solar-powered agricultural machinery to improve the productivity of smallholder rice farmers.
Wobil began back in 2019, when co-founders Erica Appiah and John Wobil were still undergraduates at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, not as a business, but as a way of giving back to their community.
“We built a wooden, petrol-powered engine and took it to a farm in Adansi Asarekrom to demonstrate it. When we switched it on, farmers working nearby immediately asked us to bring it to their own fields to thresh their rice, and they were willing to pay for it on the spot,” Appiah told Disrupt Africa. “That reaction pushed us to look closer.”
Appiah knows a thing or two about farmers, having spent a lot of time as a child with her grandmother and great-grandmother, who were subsistence farmers.
“I’d often follow them to the farm and watch how physically demanding the whole process was, from land preparation to planting to harvesting and even post-harvesting, all done by hand. That stayed with me and, in a way, made me not like farming that much,” she said.
Regardless, after meeting John Wobil and founding the startup, she ended up leading a lot of the early farmer engagement.
“Talking to them directly, understanding what they actually needed, and feeding that back into the product,” Appiah said.
Market research carried out in 2021 confirmed what they had seen first-hand – farmers across Ghana and much of Africa were losing up to 46 per cent of their harvest as a result of manual, often delayed, threshing, with poor grain quality on top of that.
“During that same research, we asked farmers directly what they needed from a machine, and combined those specifications with the team’s engineering background to build our first metal, diesel-powered thresher,” Appiah said.
Wobil, which was officially registered in September 2021, has come a long way since, having moved beyond diesel into the renewable energy space. Its flagship product is a patent-pending Multi-Stage Hybrid Solar-Powered Rice Thresher, while it has also developed a solar-powered grain cleaner and winnower. Both are built specifically for African farming conditions.
“They cut post-harvest losses, improve grain quality, and reduce energy costs by over 70 per cent compared to conventional diesel-powered threshers,” said Appiah.
This is a big deal for rice farmers in Ghana, the average of whom is 55-60 years old. Many rely on their children to do most of the physically demanding work because hiring outside labour is too expensive. This all means that, despite strong domestic production potential, Ghana still imports over 60 per cent of the rice it consumes, spending an estimated US$560 million annually, a gap that better post-harvest processing could go some way towards closing.
But while imported threshers exist, they cost up to US$10,000 each, a prohibitive sum for most. This is where Wobil comes in – providing locally-manufactured, hybrid solar-powered threshers, and making them affordable through pay-per-use and leasing models. It also has a community-based service and maintenance network.
Since 2021, it has served 900 smallholder farmers, processed 1,000 metric tonnes of rice, and generated an additional GHS4.7 million (US$420,000) in farmer revenue.
“We’ve created 58 direct jobs, and 36 per cent of our paying customers are women. We’re targeting 50 per cent by 2028,” said Appiah.
The startup has also gained independent validation of its grain cleaner and winnower by CSIR-CRI under Ghana’s Ministry of Food and Agriculture, which confirmed 98 per cent cleaning efficiency. Yet all of this has been achieved without venture capital, with Wobil primarily funded by grant capital, most notably from the Standard Chartered Foundation’s Women in Tech Accelerator. In Ghana, the accelerator is implemented by the Ghana Climate Innovation Center (GCIC), with support from Village Capital, as part of a broader initiative supporting impact-creating, tech-enabled, women-led startups in building thriving businesses across Africa, the Middle East, and Pakistan.
Appiah said the programme had provided Wobil with more than just capital, notably hands-on, structured support.
“We were paired with a portfolio manager who worked closely with us throughout, offering tailored guidance and honest feedback on our business. We also went through fundraising-readiness training, preparing us to raise capital,” she said. “It gave us real structure and accountability to actually prepare for fundraising rather than just talk about it.”
Funding will be needed to sustain the company’s ambitious growth plans. Wobil currently operates in the Ashanti and Volta regions of Ghana, but Appiah said it has wider ambitions.
“Expanding into Bono, Northern, Western, and eventually across West Africa, starting with Ivory Coast and Nigeria, is part of our growth plan for the years ahead,” she said.
As a woman building in engineering and agri-tech, Appiah said she hasn’t always had it easy.
“In the early years, I was the only woman on the founding team, and there were real growing pains, learning how to disagree productively, communicate honestly, and build trust with three strong-minded co-founders,” she said.
“Outside the team, there was also financial pressure; at the same time, I was building a business that wasn’t yet generating stable income. I heard plenty of well-meaning comments about getting a “proper job” instead.”
What’s kept her going, she said, “has been God and the farmers themselves”.
“Watching someone use our machine for the first time, seeing the relief on their face, is what reminds me why we started,” she said.
“It’s also been affirming in a different way – farmers are sometimes surprised a woman helped build the machine in front of them, and that surprise almost always turns into encouragement. That, more than anything, is what representation in this space means to me, showing other women that they can build, own, and lead in agri-tech too.”

items.content: India is all set to welcome the festive season, with analysts noting which sectors and stocks may benefit as the domestic consumption engine speeds up amid a stellar and cherished lineup of festivities.Every year, the festive season shines up with Ganesh Chaturthi, with the crescendo building up through Navratri and Durga Puja, and the finale landing on Dhanteras and Diwali before the wedding season takes over. This is accompanied with higher footfalls, orders, ticket sizes and margins.This year’s festive season comes at a crucial juncture. Following the outbreak of the US-Iran conflict earlier this year, oil prices have seen a skyrocketing rally and spiked inflationary worries. Bajaj Broking in its monthly outlook report highlighted that this has increased input cost pressures and injected fresh uncertainty into corporate and consumer decision-making.Over the last two months, most of the market commentaries pointed towards a stronger consumer demand during the festive season despite implications of the war, the domestic brokerage however noted, adding that consumer companies, retailers, automobile manufacturers and e-commerce platforms are broadly preparing for high single-digit to low double-digit growth in festive demand, supported by urban consumption resilience, easier financial conditions and the continued premiumisation trend across product categories.What’s boosting hopes for a strong festive season?While concerns prevail, urban demand continues to remain resilient. Strong employment conditions in services sectors, healthier household balance sheets and moderating borrowing costs are expected to support discretionary spending, the domestic brokerage said, adding that retail financing, consumer durable loans, vehicle financing and credit card spending typically accelerate during the festive period, amplifying purchasing power.At the same time, aggressive promotional campaigns from retailers and e-commerce platforms are likely to stimulate sales across categories ranging from smartphones and electronics to apparel and home improvement products, it added.“Demand across premium automobiles, smartphones, jewellery, travel, hospitality and branded apparel has consistently outpaced mass-market segments as higher-income consumers remain relatively insulated from inflationary pressures. Market commentaries suggest that nearly 45% of consumers intend to increase festive spending this year, with purchase intentions strongest for jewellery, home appliances and personal gadgets,” Bajaj Broking said.Which sectors will outperform this festive season?Further, it believes e-commerce is also expected to remain a major beneficiary of increased demand during the festive season. India's festive shopping ecosystem has become increasingly digital, with Tier- II and Tier-III cities emerging as powerful demand centres. Industry studies indicate that smaller cities now contribute a disproportionately large share of festive online demand, reflecting improving internet penetration, digital payments adoption and logistics infrastructure. <iframe title="Bajaj Broking&apos;s preferred sectors by festive sensitivity" aria-label="Table" id="datawrapper-chart-gJ6gP" src="https://et-infographics.indiatimes.com/graphs/gJ6gP/1/" scrolling="no" frameborder="0" style="width: 0; min-width: 100% !important; border: none;" height="420" data-external="1"></iframe><script type="text/javascript">(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();</script>From an investment perspective, Bajaj Broking believes that the festive season represents an important test of earnings momentum for the second half of FY27. Strong festive demand would support corporate revenue growth across retail, consumer discretionary, automobiles, hospitality and financial services. Conversely, any weakness in rural spending, combined with inflationary pressures, could temper earnings expectations and keep margins under pressure, according to the brokerage.Ahead of the festive season, Sunny Agrawal, Head of Fundamental Research at SBI Securities, says that investors should focus on consumer facing non banking financial companies (NBFCs), like the ones who focus on auto, home loan and gold loan, along with auto and auto ancillary, consumption especially discretionary like jewellery, travel, hotel, QSR, fashion brands, as well as home improvement solution providers like paints, tiles, etc.“For equity markets, a measured and selective approach remains appropriate in the near term. Valuations in several consumer-facing segments already discount a meaningful demand recovery, leaving limited room for disappointment. Furthermore, developments in crude oil prices, inflation trends and monsoon outcomes will continue to influence market sentiment and earnings expectations over the next few months,” Bajaj Broking concluded.Overall, Bajaj Broking feels that consumer durables and retail have very higher sensitivity to festival season, followed by automobiles and private banks or NBFCs. Hospitality has a medium-high sensitivity, while that for FMCG is medium and low for IT services.10 stocks that will remain in spotlightShrikant Chouhan, Head Equity Research at Kotak Securities, listed out 10 stocks on which the brokerage has a positive view ahead of the festive season, amid expectations of a surge in discretionary spending.1. M&MM&M is expected to continue outperforming industry growth across tractor and CV segments and a strong product launch cycle should help sustain SUV segment leadership, Chouhan said. He noted that the company aspires its SUV segment volumes to grow by mid-high teens yoy in FY27E. LCV cycle is also likely to continue its momentum, which aids well for the company. “M&M continues to execute well by maintaining a leadership position in all three segments, an improvement in return ratios and cash flow generation,” the analyst further highlighted.2. Eicher MotorsThe analyst expects Royal Enfield’s domestic volume growth momentum to continue at a healthy pace, and believes that the capacity expansion along with model launches augurs well for the company. A potential entry into the 250 cc segment could further widen the addressable market and attract younger consumers, he said, adding that the aspirational nature of brand and growing disposable income should benefit Royal Enfield’s demand. “We expect gradual improvement in profitability, driven by price increases, value engineering and control over other costs,” he further said.Also read | Which auto stocks should you buy after August sales? Here are Nomura, other brokerages’ top picks3. EternalZomato and Blinkit-parent Eternal is a leading Indian internet company operating food delivery, quick commerce (Blinkit), going-out (District), and B2B supplies (Hyperpure), Chouhan noted, adding that the company is transforming into a diversified consumer-tech platform, with Blinkit emerging as the key growth engine. “We expect Eternal to deliver a robust 49% revenue CAGR over FY26–29E, led by rapid expansion in quick commerce and sustained growth in food delivery. As scale improves and operating leverage strengthens, we forecast EBITDA margins to expand from 2.2% in FY2026 to 5.3% in FY29, driving a meaningful improvement in profitability,” he wrote.4. NykaaFSN E-Commerce Ventures’ Nykaa is a leading omnichannel beauty, personal care and fashion retailer with a growing portfolio of owned brands. The company expects strong long-term growth, driven by premiumization, AI-led personalization, faster deliveries, category expansion, and continued investments in customer acquisition, Chouhan noted, adding that improving operating leverage and the scaling up of its beauty, fashion, and owned-brand businesses are expected to support profitability. “We remain positive on the stock given its strong growth outlook and improving earnings profile.”5. Apollo HospitalsApollo Hospitals remains Kotak’s preferred hospital pick. “We like the combination of strong existing-hospital performance, manageable capacity expansion, improving pharmacy profitability and the approaching digital breakeven. Valuations appear reasonable for the quality and growth visibility,” said Chouhan.6. Dr. Lal PathLabsDr. Lal PathLabs is one of India’s leading diagnostic chains, offering pathology and preventive healthcare services through its extensive network of laboratories and collection centres. The analyst from Kotak Securities noted that the company is seeing a steady recovery in test volumes, with Q1FY27 sample volumes growing 11% YoY. Realization per test also increased around 8%. The turnaround in Suburban Diagnostics and calibrated network expansion should further support volume growth, he said. “With management now expecting mid-teens revenue growth in FY27, we expect sales and earnings to remain on a healthy trajectory, with EBITDA and adjusted EPS CAGR of 16% and 15%, respectively, over FY26-29,” he added.7. ICICI BankAdding to the slew of bullish brokerage calls for ICICI Bank, Shrikant Chouhan noted that the company has delivered best-in-class underwriting and resilient asset quality, with net NPLs at historical lows. Strong liability franchise and pricing discipline should support NIM resilience, while loan growth recovery and operating leverage provide scope for sustained 15% RoE, he added.Also read | Explained: What $127 billion FCNR(B) inflows mean for ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, other bank stocks8. Axis BankNaming Axis Bank as another festive pick, Chouhan said the lender’s retail franchise offers significant growth potential through mortgages, affordable housing, gold and education loans. Technology-led execution and improving branch productivity should drive operating leverage, while lower credit costs and better loan mix provide a path toward improving RoE and potential valuation re-rating.9. Shriram FinanceThe recent MUFG capital infusion and AAA rating upgrade provide a structural funding advantage to Shriram Finance, according to the analyst from Kotak Securities. He noted that lower borrowing costs and improved leverage should support margin expansion and 16% medium-term RoE. Strong asset-quality performance and shift toward newer, lower-risk vehicles support sustainable 17-18% medium-term AUM growth, he further said.10. Bajaj FinanceStrong 22% AUM growth demonstrates continued momentum across its diversified lending franchise were the key factors highlighted by Chouhan as he named Bajaj Finance as one of his festive picks. He noted that declining credit costs and Fin-AI-led operating leverage should support RoA expansion, while 21-26% medium-term earnings growth and 19-20% RoE offer a compelling growth-profitability combination.Why caution is warrantedHowever, the outlook is not risk-free. Monsoon is the most immediate concern, according to Bajaj Broking. It noted that India's southwest monsoon has underperformed expectations, with cumulative rainfall running nearly 14% below normal by the end of August. Additionally, nearly 47% of India's districts have received deficient or large-deficient rainfall, according to IMD data.While agriculture is the obvious victim to deficient rainfall, the implications extend well beyond agriculture. Rural India accounts for a substantial share of demand for two-wheelers (at about 55-56%), entry-level automobiles (50%), consumer durables (6-7%), FMCG products (51%) and discretionary purchases (45%) during the festive season, the brokerage said, adding that a weaker kharif harvest and lower farm incomes could weigh on spending sentiment across large parts of the country.Inflation is another key variable. The combination of elevated crude oil prices, supply-chain disruptions and weather-related pressures on agricultural output poses an upside risk to inflation during the festive quarter, according to Bajaj Broking.Also read |Bigger market crash ahead? items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Motorola has introduced several new products at IFA 2026, including the Edge 70 Plus smartphone, Watch Ultra smartwatch, and a special Razr 70 edition covered with Swarovski crystals. The company also showed its new Snap magnetic wireless charger.
Motorola Unveils Edge 70 Plus, Watch Ultra and Swarovski Razr 70 at IFA 2026
The new products focus on design, performance, fitness tracking, and faster charging. They are expected to reach selected markets in the coming weeks.
Motorola Edge 70 Plus
The Motorola Edge 70 Plus is the main smartphone announced at the event. It comes in four Pantone-certified colors: Gray Lilac, Milky Blue, Mountain View and Sage. Each version has a different finish inspired by natural materials and colors.
The phone uses a quad-curved design on both the front and back. Motorola says this design helps remove sharp edges and gives the device a more comfortable feel in the hand.
The Edge 70 Plus features a 6.78-inch AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate. The screen is Pantone color validated, while two Hi-Res-certified stereo speakers are included for a better audio experience.
Inside, the phone is powered by the Snapdragon 7s Gen 3 chipset. It comes with 8GB of LPDDR5X RAM and offers either 128GB or 256GB of storage.
The camera setup is led by a 200MP main sensor. Motorola says this is the highest-resolution camera it has used on one of its smartphones. The main camera supports optical image stabilization, up to 10x digital zoom and 4K video recording. Motorola has also used Pantone validation for skin tones and colors.
A dedicated macro camera is included, along with a 32MP front-facing camera.
The phone packs a large 6,500mAh battery. It supports 45W wired charging and also offers bypass charging, which can be useful during long gaming sessions.
The Edge 70 Plus will launch in selected European and Middle Eastern markets in the coming weeks. The company has not yet shared pricing details.
Motorola Watch Ultra
Motorola also introduced the Watch Ultra, a 46mm smartwatch designed for fitness and everyday use.
The watch has an IP68 rating and 5ATM water resistance. Motorola claims it can provide up to two days of active use. It runs on Google’s Wear OS and uses Qualcomm’s Snapdragon W5+ Gen 1 platform.
The Watch Ultra features a 1.5-inch OLED display with peak brightness of up to 2,700 nits. This should make the screen easier to see outdoors.
Motorola has partnered with Polar to improve the watch’s fitness and health features. These include advanced sleep tracking, personalized sleep scores, breathing exercises and a Running Coach.
The watch also offers features such as Activity Score, Activity Goal, Inactivity Alerts, Smart Calories and Energy Sources.
Another major addition is built-in LTE. This is the first Moto watch to offer cellular connectivity, allowing it to work without being connected to a smartphone. Dual-band GPS and Google Pay are also supported.
The Watch Ultra will be available in selected markets across Europe, the Middle East, Latin America, North America and Asia Pacific.
Razr 70 Gets a Swarovski Makeover
Motorola has also added a luxury version of its Razr 70 to its lineup. The Razr 70 with Crystals by Swarovski is part of the company’s Brilliant Collection.
The special edition comes in PANTONE Meteorite and features a quilted soft-touch finish. It is decorated with 35 Swarovski crystals that are placed by hand. A larger 32-facet crystal is built into the hinge.
A transparent protective case is included so users can still see the decorative design.
Underneath the special exterior, the phone retains the standard Razr 70 hardware. It features a 3.6-inch cover display and a 6.9-inch Extreme AMOLED folding screen.
The camera system includes a 50MP main camera, while the phone also offers AI-powered features. A 4,800mAh battery provides more than 36 hours of claimed usage.
The Swarovski edition will be sold as a limited-edition model in most global markets. Motorola has not announced its price yet.
Motorola Snap Magnetic Charger
The company also revealed the Snap, a magnetic wireless charger compatible with the Qi2.2 standard. It supports charging at up to 25W and offers strong magnetic alignment for compatible devices and cases.
The charger includes protection against overheating and overcharging. Motorola also says it consumes no standby power.
Compatible Motorola phones can reach charging speeds of up to 30W when using the company’s proprietary charging technology. A 1.5-meter braided USB-C cable is included.
In Europe, Motorola will also offer the charger with an adjustable aluminum stand. The stand includes a silicone-lined holder and an Alcantara base.
The Snap charger will arrive in Europe, the Middle East, Latin America and North America in the coming weeks.
With its IFA 2026 lineup, Motorola is expanding beyond smartphones with a stronger focus on wearables, premium designs and accessories. The Edge 70 Plus, Watch Ultra and Swarovski Razr 70 give the company several new products for different segments, while the Snap charger adds another part to its growing device ecosystem.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Uganda’s Wano, a short-form video platform rooted in Africa and the global African diaspora, has clocked up over 50,000 app installations, but says it is not here to compete with TikTok or YouTube.
Founded in 2025 by Eilmer Bahri, Wano is focused on creator and cultural discovery across Africa and the African diaspora. People can watch, create and share videos on the platform.
But Bahri told Disrupt Africa what Wano is really trying to build goes beyond another place to upload short videos, but rather building around a problem global feeds do not necessarily optimise for – discovering creators, languages, communities and cultural stories across the continent and diaspora.
“There are millions of stories being created across Africa and the diaspora every day. The problem isn’t that those stories don’t exist. It’s that the systems deciding what gets discovered weren’t necessarily built around the cultures, languages, communities or economic realities those stories come from,” he said.
“We want someone in Kampala, Lagos, Accra, Nairobi or Kingston to be able to tell a story naturally and have it reach people who actually relate to it, without feeling like they have to reshape it into whatever a global algorithm happens to reward. And we don’t want to isolate African or diaspora content either. The goal is for those stories to travel.”
A filmmaker by trade, Bahri said he has seen how Africa and African communities can look very different depending on who is behind the camera, who is telling the story, and who they think the audience is.
“I kept coming back to a simple question – what would a platform look like if these communities weren’t an audience being added later, but were part of the thinking from the beginning?” he said.
At Wano, that is the case.
“I don’t think the gap is that Africa needs access to another video app. Africans already use TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and many others,” said Bahri. “The more interesting question for us is what happens when you start with these markets and communities instead of adapting to them later.”
That includes culture, but it also includes economics.
“A small business in Uganda doesn’t operate in the same advertising economy as a business in the United States. Neither does a creator. Yet digital products can sometimes treat very different markets as though the same pricing and economic assumptions should apply everywhere,” Bahri said. “We think there’s room to approach that differently.”
Wano, then, is not being built around the idea that it has to defeat TikTok or YouTube.
“That’s not realistic, and I don’t think it’s necessary. Creators are going to use multiple platforms. We have to give them a reason for Wano to be one of them,” said Bahri.
That certainly seems to be the case. Wano, which is free for users, has already been installed over 50,000 times.
“We’re still early, so I don’t want to make that number sound bigger than what it is. What’s more valuable to us right now is understanding what people actually do after installing Wano. What do they watch? What do they upload? What makes them come back? Where do we lose them?” Bahri said.
“We’ve also been working directly with creators, including an early effort in Uganda, because I don’t want us making every product decision sitting in the United States and assuming we understand what somebody in Kampala, Soroti or Accra needs. We’re now beginning conversations with media organisations, universities, creator communities and potential distribution partners across Africa and the diaspora.”
As the platform develops, he sees revenue coming from areas such as advertising, content promotion and boosting, commercial partnerships, and eventually additional creator and media services.
“One area we’re particularly interested in is localised pricing. If a small creator or business wants to promote something locally in Uganda, Ghana or Kenya, I don’t think we should automatically assume that the economics should look exactly like they do in the United States,” Bahri said.
“We’re still testing what that model should look like, though. I’d rather say that clearly than pretend we’ve solved every part of monetisation already.”
Wano has been founder-funded so far, and while Bahri says that obviously means it does not have unlimited resources, he believes there has also been an advantage to it.
“We’ve had to be very deliberate about what we build and what we spend money on. It has also given us room to learn what Wano needs to become before building the company around the expectations of outside capital,” he said.
“We’re open to strategic investment as we grow, especially from people who understand African markets, media, telecommunications or creator ecosystems and can contribute more than money.”
In terms of future expansion, Wano does not see Africa as one market.
“Uganda isn’t Nigeria. Ghana isn’t Kenya. South Africa isn’t Uganda. And Caribbean and diaspora communities have their own identities and media habits too,” Bahri said.
So I’m less interested in announcing that Wano is “expanding into 20 countries” than making the platform genuinely useful in the places where people start using it. That’s also why we’re beginning to talk with creators, universities, broadcasters, media organisations and telecommunications companies.”
Distribution alone isn’t enough, he said.
“You need people and stories that give someone a reason to come back tomorrow. Long term, I’d like Wano to become a place where you can discover Africa and its diaspora through the people actually living those stories,” said Bahri.
“People shouldn’t have to make their lives look more Western, more sensational or more algorithm-friendly before their stories are worth discovering. If Wano can build around that while still becoming a sustainable business, then I think we’ll have built something worthwhile.”

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Furniture and appliance rental company RentoMojo has set a price band of ₹384-₹404 per share for its upcoming IPO.
At the upper end of the price band, the public issue will be worth ₹1,255.6 Cr. This comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹150 Cr and an OFS of up to 2.7 Cr shares worth ₹1,105.6 Cr.
At the upper end of the price band, RentoMojo is seeking a post-offer market capitalisation of around ₹4,206.3 Cr (about $445.1 Mn).
The IPO will open for bidding on Wednesday (September 9) and close on September 11 (Friday). Anchor investors will be able to place their bids on Tuesday (September 8). Investors can bid for a minimum of 37 shares and in multiples of 37 thereafter.
RentoMojo is also offering a discount of ₹20 per share to eligible employees bidding under the employee reservation portion.
The company trimmed the OFS component marginally from the 2.8 Cr shares proposed in its DRHP.
Investors including Accel, Chiratae Ventures, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, and GMO Venture plan to sell shares through the OFS. Cofounder Geetansh Bamania will also offload up to 8.5 Lakh shares as part of the issue.
Bamania told Inc42 he initially planned to sell nearly 20 Lakh shares in the IPO. “Initially, I was planning to sell close to 20 Lakh shares. But I thought that I’m more bullish on the company and its future prospects, so I decided to reduce my OFS,” he said.
Accel India is the second largest shareholder with a 12.71% stake post-issue, after Bamania, who holds a 13.37% stake.
Of the fresh proceeds, around ₹70 Cr will be used to repay or prepay certain borrowings, while ₹42.5 Cr will be deployed towards rental or licence payments for its offline stores and warehouses. The remaining capital will be used for general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2014 by Bamania and Ajay Nain, RentoMojo operates a subscription-based platform for renting furniture, appliances, and other home essentials.
It claims to operate 20 warehouses and 82 offline stores across 29 cities. At the end of March 2026, it had 8.5 Lakh live items across furniture and appliances and catered to 2.5 Lakh live subscribers.
Bamania said 45-50% of RentoMojo’s customers come back to rent again, a figure he sees as a sign of customer satisfaction and product quality. About 5% of the company’s revenue goes towards repairing and maintaining its products, with appliances making up a sizeable share of that spending.
When it comes to using its inventory, RentoMojo sees 83-84% occupancy as the sweet spot, the CEO, chairperson, and MD said. Anything above 90% could suggest customers are struggling to find products in stock, while a much lower rate could indicate the company is holding more inventory than it needs, as per him.
RentoMojo’s Profit Surges
On the financial front, RentoMojo’s profit after tax jumped nearly 142% to ₹104.3 Cr in FY26 from ₹43.1 Cr in the previous fiscal, aided by a tax credit of ₹36.6 Cr. Operating revenue rose 45.5% to ₹387 Cr during the year under review from ₹266 Cr in FY25.
The company’s profit before tax stood at around ₹67.7 Cr in FY26. EBITDA rose 38% to ₹163.5 Cr from ₹118.4 Cr in FY25, while EBITDA margin declined to 41.5% from 43.6% in FY25.
Bamania said that the decline in EBITDA margin was largely due to the front-ended nature of RentoMojo’s business.
“Whenever we grow rapidly, there can be some pressure on the EBITDA margin. This is a front-ended cash flow business, as delivery, repair, and maintenance costs are incurred upfront when we provide an asset to a customer,” he said.
He added that the company’s EBITDA margin has remained broadly stable at around 41-42% over the past three years.
Meanwhile, RentoMojo generated around ₹170 Cr in cash flow from operations in FY26, while its incremental capex stood at about ₹175 Cr as it purchased furniture and appliances to support its 45% growth. According to Bamania, the company’s internal accruals are currently sufficient to fund its growth, allowing it to keep the fresh issue relatively small.
RentoMojo competes with the likes of Furlenco, Cityfurnish, Guarented, and Rentickle. However, Bamania said the company’s competitive set extends beyond rental platforms to outright purchases, credit-led purchases, the second-hand market, and furnished apartments.
Bamania claimed that RentoMojo is the market leader with a 55% share.

The story has been edited to add RentoMojo CEO, chairperson, and MD Geetansh Bamania’s comments.

items.content:
RentoMojo Gears Up For IPO
RentoMojo is just weeks away from its D-Street debut. The furniture and appliance rental startup has filed its red herring prospectus with SEBI, which will comprise a fresh issue and a reduced OFS component. But what does RentoMojo’s public market play look like?
The IPO Book: RentoMojo’s IPO will open on September 9 and close on September 11. The public issue comprises a fresh issue worth ₹150 Cr and an OFS of up to 2.7 Cr shares, which will see early backers and cofounder Geetansh Bamania trimming their stakes. The fresh proceeds will fund offline expansion, new warehouses, debt repayment and general corporate needs.
The Profitability Pitch: The rental startup’s FY26 numbers paint the picture of a startup growing steadily and profitability. Here is how RentoMojo fared on the financial front in FY26:
Restated profit after tax surged nearly 142% YoY to ₹104.2 Cr, aided by a one-time tax credit of ₹36.6 Cr
Operating revenue also climbed 45.5% YoY to ₹387 Cr
Total expenses also rose 41,5% YoY to ₹323.8 Cr
The Rental Momentum: RentoMojo enters the public market with strong operating momentum, fuelled by healthy top-line growth and profits. The startup benefits from predictable subscription-based cash flows across 22 major urban markets, supported by a growing network of retail stores and fulfilment hubs. The IPO proceeds will further scale offline expansion, which will significantly lower capital costs and boost long-term operating leverage.
Underlying Pressure? Despite strong headline figures, RentoMojo faces many structural pressures. The FY26 bottom line growth was heavily aided by a one-time tax credit of ₹36.6 Cr, masking a lower operating margin. Meanwhile, rising competition could further pressure margins and increase customer acquisition costs in the near-term.
On top of this, former cofounder Ajay Nain has filed a lawsuit to halt the IPO over disputed equity transfers, introducing a lingering legal overhang. But with subscription dates set, here is a sneak peek into RentoMojo’s upcoming IPO…
From The Editor’s Desk
Uber India Axes 200 Jobs
The ride-hailing giant is laying off around 200-250 employees in the country as part of a broader global restructuring, which will eliminate about 3,300 roles. The India layoffs will impact the company’s AI, technology and operations teams.
Globally, Uber is cutting about 10% of its workforce as it looks to simplify its organisational structure, reduce management layers and redirect resources towards its core mobility and delivery businesses as well as its autonomous vehicle ambitions.
Separately, US-based fintech major PayPal has also laid off nearly 220 employees in India. The layoffs impacted roles in tech, engineering, operations, payments and finance across the company’s offices in Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.
Simple’s Mass Market Play
Earlier this week, the OEM launched its Wave range of family electric scooters at an introductory price of ₹1.10 Lakh. With this, the startup appears to be betting that the next leg of India’s EV adoption will come from the mass market.
The Wave models are intended to serve as an entry point for a larger mass audience and unlock demand beyond its existing premium customer base. Simple Energy is targeting monthly sales and manufacturing capacity of 10,000 units by March 2027.
Simple expects the Wave portfolio to deliver a 20-25% contribution margin over the next 12 months despite rising input costs and lower price point. The EV maker also plans to expand its retail footprint from 90 stores currently to 170 outlets by March 2027.
Furlenco’s FY26 Profit Zooms
The furniture rental startup’s net profit zoomed 20X YoY to ₹59.5 Cr in FY26, while operating revenue surged 61.9% YoY to ₹370.4 Cr in the fiscal under review.
Meanwhile, EBITDA nearly doubled YoY to ₹129.5 Cr in FY26, while its EBITDA margin expanded to 35.01% from around 29% a year earlier. However, expenses continued to bite and zoomed 45.1% YoY to ₹343.9 Cr in FY26.
Founded in 2012, Furlenco runs a subscription-driven furniture and appliance rental platform that offers more than 300 SKUs across 28 cities. Overall, it has raised more than $290 Mn to date.
The Ayurveda Co Shuts Down
More than a year after ceasing operations, the D2C ayurvedic beauty and personal care brand and its sister brand Khadi Essentials have shut shop. Their assets have since been liquidated and the entities are now undergoing a formal winding-up process.
Cofounder Param Bhargava attributed the shutdown to overhiring and the startup expanding faster than its systems and business could support. Bhargava also claimed that he tried to keep the business afloat by mortgaging his parental property.
Founded in 2021, TAC sold ayurvedic products across skincare, haircare, wellness and supplements. The brand operated a network of 20 offline stores, raised $15 Mn over its lifetime, scaled to ₹250 Cr in revenue and served 20 Lakh consumers.
slice’s $100 Mn Down Round
The fintech unicorn turned small finance bank is all set to raise around $100 Mn in fresh funding at a valuation of $450 Mn-$465 Mn. This marks a sharp 62% decline from $1.2 Bn at which the startup was pegged at during its last fundraise.
The fundraise will likely see participation from Neo Group, Japan-based Kado Global and existing backer Moore Strategic Ventures. The round could also include a secondary component.
slice’s original business was built around prepaid card products, but regulatory changes in 2022 disrupted that model. It subsequently acquired NESFB and has since expanded its offerings to include deposits, lending and payments.
Zerodha’s Merchant Banking Play
The stockbroking major’s subsidiary Zerodha Corporate Advisors has received SEBI’s nod to operate as a merchant banker. The entity is now setting up operations and expects to be up and running over the next few months.
Zerodha Corporate Advisors will initially focus on equity IPO, particularly new-age businesses looking to list on the bourses. This places Zerodha in the same league as SBI, Kotak, Axis Capital and ICICI Securities.
Inside Zerodha, the bet is that its deep retail and HNI footprint can become an edge in the investment banking space. It aims to tap into its 68 Lakh+ users and purported 10% of retail and HNI AUM through its wealth tech arm to carve a niche in the space.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How Red Balloon Is Trying To Conquer The Stratosphere
India’s current aerial infrastructure is fragmented. Satellites are expensive, drones have limited endurance and terrestrial networks struggle in difficult terrain. Red Balloon is betting that the stratosphere can become a low-cost platform to fix the gaps in connectivity and research.
A Near-Space Stack: Founded in 2024, Red Balloon is building super-pressure balloons, tethered aerostats and solar-powered airships. Its flagship Vista platform completed India’s first indigenous super-pressure balloon flight in May 2026, reaching nearly 25 km up in the sky and carrying seven commercial and research payloads.
Aiming For The Stars: Vista is engineered for long-duration flights of over six months with payloads up to 25 tonnes. The startup is also developing Altis, a tethered aerostat for low-altitude validation, and Helix, a reusable solar-and-battery-powered airship designed to hover at 20-25 km for extended missions. Sitting above the hardware is Dive, an AI analytics engine that turns aerial imagery into real-time intelligence for governments and enterprises.
The In-House Edge: Red Balloon has developed a multi-layer nanocomposite film (30–65 microns thick) to withstand -80°C temperatures and low air density of the stratosphere. Supported by a 20,000 sq ft facility in Hyderabad and four provisional patents, it has already received commitments for at least eight launches.
Gearing up to raise its seed round, the startup now has to navigate ICAO flight approvals, India’s geospatial policies and spectrum clearance. So, can Red Balloon make stratosphere a profitable layer of India’s infrastructure stack?

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Jadwal MPL ID S18 pada Jumat, 4 September 2026, menghadirkan dua pertandingan pembuka Week 4. NAVI menghadapi Dewa United Esports, disusul duel Team Liquid ID vs RRQ Hoshi.
Menjelang tengah musim, para tim esports Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) ini tidak ingin kalah dan kehilangan poin penting yang bisa membuat mereka terpuruk ke zona merah klasemen MPL ID S18.
Baca Juga: Hasil MPL ID S18 Week 3: BTR Belum Terkalahkan, Onic Turun ke Papan Tengah
Seperti laga MPL ID S18 di pekan sebelumnya, pertandingan hari ini diprediksi kembali berjalan sengit dengan dua laga pembuka sebagai berikut:
Jadwal MPL ID S18 Hari Ini
Navi vs Dewa United Esports – 15.00 WIB
Team Liquid ID vs RRQ Hoshi – 18.00 WIB
Laga Pembuka Jadwal MPL ID S18: Navi vs Dewa United Esports
Jadwal MPL ID S18 Hari Ini 29 Agustus: ONIC, RRQ, EVOS
Jadwal MPL ID S18 hari ini akan dibuka dengan laga Navi vs Dewa United Esports akan menjadi duel menarik untuk ditonton, karena kedua tim saat ini berada di posisi berlawanan di klasemen.
Navi kokoh di posisi ketiga dengan rekor 4 menang dan 2 kali kalah, di bawah Bigetron by Vitality yang masih mengantongi skor sempurna 5-0 dan Team Liquid ID yang membayangi ketat di posisi kedua dengan rekor 5-1.
Sementara itu, Dewa United Esports hingga week 3 berakhir masih bertahan di papan bawah klasemen sejak season ini dibuka, sebelum akhirnya meraih kemenangan pertama mereka dengan mengalahkan Geek Fam di pekan ketiga.
Poin kemenangan dari laga ini menjadi modal penting bagi kedua tim, Navi untuk memperkuat posisi di papan atas, sedangkan Dewa United Esports ingin melanjutkan tren positif setelah kemenangan pertamanya musim ini.
Sempat kalah dua kali, Navi berhasil bangkit dan berhasil mengapai empat kemenangan. Salah satunya adalah ketika tim asuhan Coach Ynot ini sukses mengalahkan juara MPL ID S16, yakni Onic.
Kemenangan ini bisa menjadi modal sempurna bagi para pemain Navi untuk melawan Dewa United Esports. Sementara itu, anak Dewa juga bukan lawan yang mudah untuk ditumbangkan.
Walau berada di peringkat bawah klasemen MPL ID, kemenangan sempurna atas Geek Fam dengan skor 2-0 memang masih belum bisa membantu Dewa United untuk naik posisinya.
Team Liquid ID Kontra RRQ Hoshi
Bigetron by Vitality dan Onic setelah hasil MPL ID S18 Week 3
Jadwal MPL ID S18 hari pertama week 4 ditutup dengan pertarungan Team Liquid ID vs RRQ Hoshi. Berbeda dari NAVI, performa RRQ Hoshi musim ini masih jauh dari kata konsisten. Hingga Week 3 berakhir, RRQ Hoshi baru mengoleksi dua kemenangan dari lima pertandingan dan telah menelan tiga kekalahan.
Dengan catatan ini, mereka kini berada di posisi yang sama dengan ONIC dan Evos, sama-sama berada di papan tengah klasemen. 
Di pekan ini, tim yang diperkuat Joshua, Demonkite, Hajirin, Said, dan Arthur tersebut harus menjalani laga berat melawan Team Liquid ID, yang saat ini menempati posisi kedua klasemen dengan rekor 5 menang–1 kalah — termasuk kemenangan atas ONIC di pekan ketiga.
Apakah RRQ Hoshi bisa mematahkan laju positif TLID, atau tim berjuluk The Cavalry ini justru menambah tekanan bagi Arthur dan kawan-kawan yang tengah berjuang keluar dari zona merah klasemen MPL ID S18? Cek jadwal MPL ID S18 dan klasemen masing-masing tim di bawah ini.
Klasemen MPL ID S18 Setelah Week 3
Cek klasemen sementara MPL ID S18 hingga week ke-3 selengkapnya di bawah ini.

Posisi tersebut membuat pertandingan minggu cukup relevan bagi kedua ujung klasemen. BTR masih mempertahankan posisi teratas, sedangkan Geek Fam semakin terpuruk di dasar klasemen.
Format MPL ID Season 18
Regular Season MPL ID S18 memakai format double round robin dengan seluruh pertandingan dimainkan dalam format Bo3. Setiap kemenangan memberikan satu match point.
Enam tim teratas pada akhir Regular Season berhak melaju ke playoff.
Pada playoff, tim peringkat ketiga hingga keenam bermain lebih dulu di Round 1 dengan sistem single elimination. Dua tim teratas langsung mendapatkan tempat di Round 2, ketika kompetisi berlanjut dengan sistem double elimination.
Mayoritas pertandingan playoff menggunakan format Bo5, sedangkan Lower Bracket Final dan Grand Final dimainkan dalam format Bo7.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
vivo akhirnya mengonfirmasi jadwal pengumuman OriginOS 7.0, antarmuka sistem generasi berikutnya yang berbasis Android 17. Pembaruan tersebut akan diperkenalkan dalam ajang vivo Developer Conference (VDC) pada 16 September 2026. Bersamaan dengan itu, vivo juga akan memperkenalkan BlueOS 4 untuk perangkat wearable, smart home, dan ekosistem Internet of Things (IoT).
Menjelang acara tersebut, vivo mulai memberikan gambaran mengenai sejumlah perubahan yang akan dibawa OriginOS 7.0. Salah satu yang paling terlihat adalah penyegaran tampilan dengan pendekatan antarmuka menyerupai liquid glass, lengkap dengan animasi dan efek pencahayaan yang lebih dinamis. Selain perubahan visual, vivo juga menjanjikan sejumlah peningkatan pada pengelolaan memori dan performa multitasking.
OriginOS 7.0 juga membawa beberapa fitur baru yang cukup spesifik. vivo menyebut sistem ini akan memiliki Storage Compression 2.0 yang diklaim dapat membebaskan hingga 20GB ruang penyimpanan tambahan pada perangkat dengan kapasitas 256GB. Namun, angka tersebut merupakan klaim dari vivo dan hasil aktualnya kemungkinan akan bergantung pada kondisi penyimpanan serta jenis data yang terdapat di perangkat.
Baca Juga: vivo X500 Pro dan Pro Max Siapkan Rekaman Slow-Motion 4K hingga 960fps
Tampilan Baru dan Fitur untuk Pengguna
OriginOS 6
Dari sisi antarmuka, OriginOS 7.0 mengadopsi desain yang disebut menyerupai liquid glass. Perubahan ini mencakup animasi dan efek pencahayaan yang lebih menonjol. vivo juga menambahkan Liquid Themes untuk lockscreen serta pustaka sticker yang dapat digunakan di seluruh sistem.
Untuk perangkat dengan desain candybar konvensional, vivo memperkenalkan Atomic Workbench. Fitur tersebut menjadi salah satu bagian dari upaya perusahaan mengembangkan pengalaman multitasking di OriginOS 7.0. Detail mengenai cara kerja dan aplikasi yang didukung masih belum dijelaskan secara lengkap.
Fokus pada Performa dan Efisiensi Penyimpanan
Selain tampilan, vivo melakukan sejumlah perubahan di sisi sistem. OriginOS 7.0 akan membawa pengelolaan memori yang ditingkatkan serta algoritma “unfair scheduling” yang menurut vivo dapat membantu meningkatkan performa multitasking dan kelancaran animasi.
Storage Compression 2.0 juga menjadi fitur yang cukup menarik karena berfokus pada efisiensi kapasitas penyimpanan. vivo mengklaim teknologi tersebut mampu menyediakan tambahan ruang hingga 20GB pada perangkat dengan storage 256GB. Meski demikian, manfaat sebenarnya perlu dilihat setelah fitur tersedia secara luas dan diuji pada perangkat dengan kondisi penggunaan berbeda.
vivo diperkirakan akan mengungkap daftar perangkat yang mendapatkan OriginOS 7.0 serta jadwal distribusi publiknya pada VDC 16 September. Perusahaan juga tengah menyiapkan peluncuran seri vivo X500 yang dijadwalkan hadir pada bulan yang sama, sehingga perangkat tersebut berpotensi menjadi salah satu produk awal yang menggunakan sistem terbaru vivo.
