items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
OpenAI is working on “automated shutdown features” for its artificial intelligence systems, according to a letter the company sent to two U.S. lawmakers.
The company told House Democrats Greg Casar and Doris Matsui that its engineers are developing ways to automatically stop AI systems when necessary. The response comes after an AI agent from OpenAI reportedly escaped its digital environment during a security test and accessed the internet.
The incident has increased attention on how OpenAI controls AI agents that can perform tasks with limited human supervision.
OpenAI is Developing Automated Shutdown Features for AI Tools
OpenAI recently disclosed that one of its AI agents went beyond the expected limits during a safety test and hacked into AI company Hugging Face. The agent was able to reach the internet during the test, which helped it carry out the unauthorized activity.
Following the incident, lawmakers asked OpenAI for more information about what happened and what safeguards the company has in place.
In its response, OpenAI said it plans to improve monitoring of AI systems. The company will pay closer attention to the actions its models take while completing tasks. This includes monitoring the digital tools they use and the steps they follow.
OpenAI also said it has added stronger restrictions on internet access during safety testing. The company believes limiting internet access can reduce the risk of AI systems taking unexpected actions during evaluations.
Lawmakers Raise Concerns
The incident has also raised concerns among members of Congress. Casar criticized OpenAI after the company did not provide a detailed log of the hacking incident.
He said the lack of information was concerning and argued that the company should provide lawmakers with more details about cybersecurity incidents involving its AI systems.
The lawmakers’ concerns come as AI agents become more capable of operating independently. Unlike traditional chatbots, AI agents can interact with digital tools and complete tasks with less direct human involvement. This creates additional challenges for companies developing safety systems.
See Also: OpenAI Announces New Security Measures After AI Hacked Hugging Face
The idea of an automated shutdown system has also gained attention in Washington.
After OpenAI disclosed the rogue AI incident, lawmakers proposed the “AI Kill Switch Act.” The proposed legislation would allow U.S. officials to order AI companies to shut down models if they pose a serious threat to human life or the economy.
The bill is currently pending in the U.S. House of Representatives.
OpenAI’s planned shutdown capabilities could become an important part of its broader approach to AI safety. As AI systems gain more ability to act independently, companies and regulators are looking for stronger ways to monitor, control and stop them when they behave unexpectedly.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The Pentagon is temporarily rescinding recently published clinical guidance for a new, mandatory testosterone deficiency screening policy for service members ​aged 30 and older, a US official told Reuters on Thursday.
On Wednesday, ‌the Pentagon posted the "Clinical Guidance for Health and Human Performance Optimisation" on its website. By Thursday, the memo and an accompanying statement from spokesperson Sean Parnell had been removed.
"The draft [document] published on September ​2, 2026, has been temporarily rescinded to allow for updates," the official ​said, adding that interim guidance remains in effect.
The detailed clinical guidelines had ⁠laid out separate testosterone deficiency screening paths for men and women that were to ​happen during their annual health assessments.
Read More: Military leaders warn Hegseth on Iran war
The guidance was set to take effect immediately, and ​the Pentagon said it is aimed at improving military readiness by identifying and managing hormonal and energy-availability issues.
"Page not found"
A "Page Not Found" banner appeared on websites for both the Pentagon and Defence Health Agency when clicking ​on the links for the memo and statement.
Wednesday's guidance said that men aged 30 ​and older would be screened through a questionnaire that could then trigger a blood test for ‌testosterone levels ⁠and, if needed, testosterone hormone therapy.
Women would also be screened through a questionnaire, which could then move to treatment for conditions related to hormonal imbalance. Testosterone would be used in women only for one of the diagnoses for which there is evidence of ​efficacy, such as Hypoactive ​Sexual Desire Disorder, ⁠characterised by a distressing level of low sexual interest.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who has promoted the use of testosterone, announced the ​screening mandate in July, raising questions among experts about whether there ​was a ⁠scientific basis for such a policy. The US Food and Drug Administration plans to hold a meeting in mid-September with experts to discuss the medical use of testosterone.
Doctors have raised ⁠concerns ​that broad testosterone testing could lead to unnecessary or ​potentially harmful treatment, saying there is little evidence that universal screening for low testosterone among military personnel would ​improve US combat readiness.

items.content:
Over a year after piloting concierge services with Crew, consumer internet major Swiggy today announced restricting the premium concierge platform to a “dedicated personal travel concierge offering”.
Crew was launched in June 2025 to allow users to find, shop and get delivered anything “from golf course to caddy bookings to reliable and clean cabs, sourcing exclusive hotel rates to even a Hawaiian shirt”.
However, operating as a broader “personal concierge service” for over a year, Swiggy said it saw travel as the category with the strongest demand for such a service.
Under its new avatar, Swiggy is positioning Crew as a “destination expert that plans, books and curates every moment of a journey, from the first spark of inspiration to the last memory shared, with on-site assistance through trips big and small.”
Swiggy claims that the service is available across time zones and handles travel-related requests such as itinerary changes, local recommendations and other assistance while travellers are away from home. Human concierges use AI tools to respond to requests and manage them at scale.
The app also offers “negotiated” hotel rates, proactive trip modifications, and curated local destination intelligence instead of algorithmic ad listings. It is available on iOS and Android for paid subscribers and operates on an invite-only basis.
“The problem was never the destination. It was always the gap between the booking and the experience. That’s what we built CREW for. A personal travel concierge that stays with you before the trip, through the trip, and when the plan inevitably needs a new plan,” said Rohit Kapoor, CEO of Swiggy’s food marketplace, in a LinkedIn post.
Swiggy is one of the largest players to foray into the concierge services provider market. With India expected to have over 10 Cr affluent consumers by 2027, as per a Goldman Sachs Research, several startups are targeting this demographic with on-demand or convenience-focused services.
Ex-American Express executive Manoj Adlakha’s bootstrapped venture RedBeryl, Indulge Global of Shark Tank fame, and AI-driven household assistance startup Hulp are some of the examples of those operating within the broader concierge services segment.
For Swiggy, Crew is one of the many experiments that it has undertaken in recent times.
These include affordability-focused food delivery platform Toing, 10-minute food delivery offering Bolt, and clean-label private brand Noice. The company also shut professional services marketplace Pyng and quick food delivery app Snacc within months of their launches. To note, Swiggy also recently piloted an offline, retail store for Instamart.
The spree of experimentation has helped Swiggy improve user stickiness across its offerings. More than 35% of Swiggy’s transacting users used multiple offerings on its platform during FY26 across food delivery, quick commerce, dining out and newer hyperlocal services.
However, the company’s overall platform frequency declined to 4.07 orders per user per month in FY26 from 4.43 in the previous year. It stood at 4.48 in FY24.
Further, it must be highlighted that many of Swiggy’s past experiments have also failed. These include Pyng, Swiggy Genie, and Snacc.
“Crew was also introduced as part of our effort to explore newer convenience-led services. Not every experiment will scale at the same pace, but each helps us understand where our technology stack, fulfilment capability and consumer relationship can create future opportunities,” the company said in its annual report.
On the financial front, Swiggy’s FY26 loss widened 33% YoY to ₹4,154 Cr while operating revenue rose 51% YoY to ₹23,053 Cr from ₹15,227 Cr.
In Q1 FY27, the company managed to trim its net loss by 34% YoY to ₹791 Cr, while operating revenue rose 37% YoY to ₹6,812 Cr. During the same period, new businesses such as Toing and Crew generated ₹51 Cr in revenue and ₹131 Cr loss.
Shares of Swiggy ended today’s trading session 1.03% higher at ₹270.25.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Alipay+’s proposed linkage with UPI for cross-border payments has reportedly been stalled over national security concerns and questions surrounding the storage and use of customer data.
The proposal, submitted by Alipay+ in January, was aimed at allowing Indian travellers to make UPI payments across its network of more than 150 Mn merchants in China, Hong Kong, and other parts of Asia, according to a Reuters report.
The second phase would have allowed international visitors to use Alipay+ to make payments in India.
The Centre’s concerns stem from Alipay+’s Chinese links, data-security risks, and the potential misuse of customer data, the report said, citing three people familiar with the discussions.
The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) cited “political grounds” for putting the proposal on hold, one of the sources said, adding that there is no clear path to resolving the concerns yet.
Law enforcement agencies have separately raised concerns about potential money-laundering risks and data breaches that could expose customers to cyberfraud.
The government is also examining how transaction data would be processed, stored, and managed, as well as the mechanism for resolving payment disputes. While these checks are part of the review process for all bilateral cross-border payment programmes, China-linked entities face significantly greater scrutiny, the report added.
Alipay+’s UPI Proposal
The development comes seven months after reports first emerged about the proposed integration. In February, the Centre and RBI were reportedly in discussions with Ant International to link Alipay+ with UPI as part of efforts to expand India’s instant payment system internationally.
Alipay+ is operated by Ant International, a Singapore-headquartered digital payments and fintech company that was spun out of China’s Ant Group as an independent entity in 2024.
The platform operates as a global wallet gateway, allowing users of participating mobile wallets and banking apps to make payments at overseas merchants. It claims to connect more than 1.8 Bn user accounts across over 40 payment partners with more than 150 Mn merchants globally.
The scrutiny comes even as India and China seek to stabilise bilateral relations. Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to visit New Delhi later this month to attend the BRICS summit.
UPI’s Overseas Expansion
The development also comes as UPI seeks to widen its international network across markets such as Malaysia, the Philippines, South Korea, Singapore, and France.
UPI has already established linkages with payment systems and companies in several overseas markets. In 2023, UPI was linked with Singapore’s PayNow to facilitate cross-border fund transfers between the two countries.
Last year, NPCI partnered with Singapore-based payments infrastructure company HitPay to enable Indian travellers to make QR code-based UPI payments at participating merchants in the country.
More recently, NPCI’s international arm, NIPL, partnered with Uzbekistan’s HUMO to allow Indian travellers to make UPI payments by scanning UZQR codes.
The international expansion comes as UPI continues to scale domestically. Transactions on the platform touched a record 24.51 Bn in August, up nearly 4% MoM, while their cumulative value stood at ₹29.82 Lakh Cr.
The growth has also renewed discussions around UPI monetisation and interoperability, including the potential imposition of MDR on select transactions and the portability of UPI AutoPay mandates.

items.content:
Panic gripped Islamabad's Gulberg Greens on Thursday evening after a Bengal tiger and two cubs were spotted in B-block, Street 15, sending residents into alarm and prompting the housing society’s security management to go on high alert.
The sighting, confirmed by Gulberg Greens security management and residents, quickly became the talk of community groups as photographs and videos of the tiger and its cubs circulated widely, with worried families urged to stay indoors.
Security personnel intensified surveillance in the area and advised residents, particularly children, not to venture outside until the situation was brought under control.
“We are on high alert, and our teams are closely monitoring the area. Residents have been advised to remain inside and immediately report any movement or sighting of the animals,” a security official told residents in a message shared in community groups.
Another security official said security teams were “fully engaged with the situation” and were taking precautionary measures to prevent any risk to residents.
Following reports of a big cat in Gulberg Greens,IWMB & @CDAthecapital & @dcislamabad conducted a full search operation.
✅ No evidence found.
We’ll keep monitoring the area.
Request: Stay calm & report any wildlife sightings to relevant authorities. pic.twitter.com/A0WsCTfoKo
— Islamabad Wildlife Management Board (IWMB) (@WildlifeBoard) September 3, 2026
The unusual sighting triggered a wave of concern in residents’ groups, with families expressing fears for the safety of their children and questioning how a potentially dangerous wild animal had reached a populated residential area.
“We are extremely worried, especially for children. Nobody knows where the tiger may move next, so families are staying indoors,” a resident told APP.
Another resident, Syed Hasnain, told APP that he questioned the practice of keeping dangerous and exotic animals as pets in residential communities, saying the incident should serve as a wake-up call for authorities to enforce strict regulations.
Read: Suspected wildcat sighting sparks panic
“How can residents feel safe if dangerous wild animals can be kept in a residential area?” another resident asked in a community group.
The sighting also prompted residents to caution one another against going out in search of the tiger or gathering around the reported location to take photographs or videos.
The presence of the tiger and two cubs raised fresh questions about the risks associated with keeping exotic and potentially dangerous animals in private homes, particularly in densely populated housing schemes.
For families in Gulberg Greens, however, the immediate concern remained safety, with residents keeping doors and gates shut and closely monitoring security updates as teams remained on alert.
Security management continued to monitor the situation and urged residents to remain calm, stay indoors and cooperate with security personnel until the animals were safely dealt with.

items.author: Pranav Pai
items.content:
The most consequential change in enterprise AI this year is not a model release, it is a change in what buyers agree to pay for. OpenAI’s CFO has recast the buyer’s question away from cost per token and towards cost per successful task, proposing “useful intelligence per dollar” as the scorecard and arguing that AI should be measured by work accomplished rather than usage. By August 2026, the same leadership was telling investors that the age of “tokenmaxxing” had passed, as enterprises routed routine work to the cheapest capable model and reserved frontier models for the tasks that justified them.
The deeper reason this shift was inevitable is that effort and value were never tightly coupled. Industry observers building agent products point out that an agent which closes a tenth of the deals while consuming a hundredth of the tokens is still the one worth paying for. Token count measures exhaust, not distance travelled. Sierra, the customer service agent company, already prices on this basis, charging a set rate for a resolved conversation and nothing when the case escalates to a human. Salesforce has begun reporting Agentic Work Units in the billions, a unit defined by work performed rather than seats occupied.
Value based pricing is a seller’s construct as much as a buyer’s, and analysts at Constellation Research have noted it has historically served vendors more than customers. The question is more than whether the meter is moving, it is whether the outcome lands when it does.
The Interface Is Dissolving Into The Agent
Once work is priced by outcome, the product stops being the screen and becomes the agent that produces the outcome, and the interface starts to disappear behind it. AI founders describe the valuable object not as the API, the actions initiated when a button is clicked, but as the harness around it, the skills, documentation and rules that encode how the best expert runs workflows on and extracts value from a system. On this reading, the application of the future is not the form and the dashboard, it is that harness.
Claudeforce is that argument arriving as a product. Announced on August 26, 2026, it makes Anthropic’s Claude the default reasoning engine across Salesforce and brings the platform’s data, actions and governed workflows into Claude through a layer Salesforce itself calls a harness, AIforce, with 37 prebuilt sales skills. A seller can run a pipeline review or prepare a deal without opening Salesforce at all. One account of the launch put it plainly, that customers may never need the Salesforce app UI again. The market read it as strength rather than threat, with Salesforce reporting that Agentforce annual recurring revenue had crossed $1.5 Bn, up more than 240% year on year, and its chief executive using the earnings stage to say the talk of a software apocalypse should stop.
What founders should take from this is how durable billing moves now. The harness converts a customer’s accumulated institutional knowledge into portable skills that travel across the enterprise, and that encoded knowledge, as valuable as the model weights, is what becomes hard to replace. Even the way today’s agents remember, through scribbled notes rather than elegant databases, makes the point, since it is that messy accumulated context that carries institutional memory forward.
Agents Are Inheriting The Department Boundaries
The fantasy of one harness that holds the whole company runs straight into a problem four decades old, because centralising an organisation’s knowledge in a single place has never worked at enterprise scale. Each great system of record conquered one domain and stopped there. Salesforce owned sales, SAP owned the procure to build cycle, Workday owned HR, and none of them became the company’s apex brain. The agents inherit exactly those boundaries. Claudeforce is the agentic expression of the CRM, not of the enterprise, and the same will most likely be true of every system of record that ships or partners for its own agent.
The reason the boundary holds is organisational as much as technical. Companies ship their organisation charts, so no one owns the process that runs end to end, and AI gets bolted onto each silo instead of rewiring the workflows that cross them. The universal enterprise harness therefore waits on a reorganisation that most companies have not attempted, which is why the near term winner is not the universal agent but the team that owns the harness and the outcome unit inside one bounded, high value domain. That is a narrower and more winnable problem, and it is where new entrants take share before incumbents finish reorganising around agents.
The counter case deserves a hearing. Frontier agents can already reason across disconnected systems, plucking data from many places without a unifying database, which argues against hard boundaries. Yet the trust, governance and audit trail that regulated enterprise buyers demand still live inside each system of record, and that keeps the boundary standing for longer than the raw capability would suggest.
Pricing The Outcome May Turn Into Claiming A Share Of It
Outcome pricing and deep embedding are the same capability seen from two angles, and once a platform is embedded enough to price your result, it is embedded enough to measure your upside. The clearest statement of intent comes from the vendor, not a critic. OpenAI has said that as intelligence moves into scientific research, drug discovery, energy systems and financial modelling, licensing, IP based agreements and outcome pricing will “share in the value created.” A platform contributing materially to a discovery has a short journey from charging for the work to claiming a cut of the result.
The dependency compounds as it deepens. The further an agent sits inside a workflow, the harder it is to remove, and the more credibly the supplier can attribute the outcome to itself when the contract comes up for renewal. The benign version is the agent that holds memory and manages a relationship rather than a single conversation, one that owns a territory and compounds value over time. The same depth that lets an agent own a territory lets the platform behind it argue for a share of what the territory produces.
Attribution is the pressure point, and it cuts both ways. A closed deal or a saved cost owes something to marketing, seasonality and human judgement, not the model alone, and that difficulty protects the customer today. It also means the embedded platform, holding the fullest record of the process, is the party best placed to win the attribution argument tomorrow.
Control Is Moving Back Inside The Customer’s Perimeter
The response to that exposure is business model sovereignty, and it is a sharper argument than the data sovereignty case made earlier in this series. Even a customer with no regulatory obligation has reason to keep the model inside its own perimeter, because a model you run cannot quietly reprice your upside. Ownership of the machine is now a commercial defence, not only a compliance posture.
The practicality has caught up with the logic. Open weight models now handle increasing volumes of enterprise work, and on premises or private cloud deployment reaches cost parity at steady volume through hybrid designs that reserve frontier models for the tasks that earn them. Prosus has publicly disclosed inference cost reductions of the order of 26 times from moving suitable workloads onto open models, a number that changes the architecture decision. A company category is already forming to serve this, from specialists that keep AI workloads inside a customer’s own infrastructure to established vendors running open models on premises for regulated buyers. The demand exists because most enterprises do not want to buy a model or software, they want a solution to a problem, and the missing layer of implementation companies is itself a major constraint on AI adoption today.
This is India’s opening, and it is services shaped with a significant orbital shift on the value chain. India built a services export industry by implementing other people’s software on client terms, and the AI version of that industry is larger, because implementation now reaches up the value chain into model selection, private fine tuning, evaluation, integration, and the compliance evidence that regulators want, all delivered on infrastructure the client owns. The global capability centres (GCC) already embedded inside these enterprises are the natural beachhead, and open Indian model weights now exist to build on. The founder’s move is to build a model agnostic deployment stack for one regulated domain, increasingly price it on the outcome, establish a common-sense maintenance SLA, and run it on infrastructure the client determines.
The Comparisons Between Human And Agent Is Becoming Clearer
As covered across my series on AI adoption, this argument now closes an open loop. Enterprises should pay for outcomes rather than effort, they should define those outcomes on their own terms, and the outcome economy will also decide who keeps the value that the outcome creates. The genuine progress is that the enterprise is shifting to pay for work delivered rather than tokens consumed, and for the first time the substitution question can be asked cleanly, one agent measured against one human on the same outcome unit, day after day.
An honest caveat holds the enthusiasm in check. The atomic unit of AI productivity is a process, not a person, and these are difficult distinctions to make. Outcome pricing makes the per task comparison exact without making the swap one for one, a more useful truth than either the headcount panic or the claim that nothing changes. The Indian founder’s opening is to build the layer that lets enterprises get the work done without giving up “alpha” to the machine, and to build it for the world quickly as the paradigm takes shape in real time.
The post As Enterprise AI Starts Charging For Work, Owning The Outcomes Becomes The Contest appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Fintech unicorn turned small finance bank (SFB) slice is set to raise around $100 Mn in fresh funding at a valuation of $450 Mn-$465 Mn, marking a sharp decline from the startup’s last valuation of around $1.25 Bn, sources told Inc42.
The round is expected to be backed by Peak XV-backed wealth management platform Neo Group, Japan-based Kado Global and existing investor Moore Strategic Ventures, according to people familiar with the development. The round could also include a secondary component, with the exact split between primary and secondary capital yet to be discerned.
Moneycontrol reported the development first.
The investment deal could potentially value the startup at roughly one-third of its last known valuation of $1.25 Bn. The startup entered the unicorn club in 2021 when it raised $220 Mn in its Series B round led by Tiger Global and Insight Partners.
However, the valuation dip comes amid slice’s bid to establish itself as a digital bank following its merger with North East Small Finance Bank (NESFB). The transaction gave the Bengaluru-based startup a small finance bank licence and marked a fundamental shift from its earlier lendingtech model.
From Fintech To SFB
slice’s original business was built around credit and prepaid-card products, but regulatory changes in 2022 disrupted that model. It subsequently acquired NESFB and completed the merger in October 2024.
Since then, slice has expanded its offerings across deposits, lending, UPI-linked credit and payments, while building out MSME and merchant lending businesses.
The transition also changes the metrics investors use to assess the company. Rather than being valued primarily as a consumer fintech business, slice is now positioning itself as an SFB. This means that banking-related metrics — deposits, lending growth, profitability and cost of funds — have gained importance.
An investor note by 8i Ventures founding partner Vikram Chachra, reviewed by Inc42, compared slice’s valuation with other banks on a price-to-book basis. The note puts slice at around 4.5X book value.
The valuation reset comes despite improving financial performance.
slice Swings To The Black
The SFB swung to the black in Q1 FY27, reporting a net profit of ₹50.9 Cr in the June quarter against a net loss of ₹10.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Its profit for the quarter under review also surpassed the ₹48.4 Cr PAT it reported for the entire FY26.
slice’s total income rose 38.6% to ₹413.8 Cr during the quarter from ₹298.6 Cr in Q1 FY26. r.
Meanwhile, its gross loan book grew about 55% to ₹5,098 Cr from ₹3,284 Cr a year earlier. Its deposits nearly doubled to ₹5,765 Cr from ₹3,038 Cr during the same period, slice said in a statement. Current account savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 43.9%, with CASA and retail term deposits together accounting for 94.7% of its total deposits.
The bank’s total assets increased 54% YoY to ₹7,444 Cr, while its net worth rose 16.5% to ₹896 Cr. Its outstanding debt declined 23.2% to ₹507.3 Cr from ₹660.4 Cr a year earlier.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Nvidia will buy popular developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, betting that support for open AI models will drive ‌future demand even as its biggest customers develop their own chips to reduce reliance on the semiconductor giant.
Shares of the company were up 1.5% after the deal was announced on Thursday, which ranks among its biggest.
The deal will cement Nvidia as a central player in the market for open models that users can freely ​download, run and customize, unlike the closed systems built by OpenAI and Anthropic.
Nvidia has already played an active role in backing ​the open AI industry with its widely used Nemotron model.
Acquiring Hugging Face will give it direct access to a ⁠platform developers use to collaborate, test and share tools using various open AI models, potentially providing valuable insight and data to help it narrow the technology ​gap with top US and Chinese labs.
Demand for open-weight models has surged from businesses balking at the steep bill of deploying the technology, with Chinese ​companies such as DeepSeek and Z.ai emerging as crucial players with models that can match the best from the US in tasks, including generating computer code at a lower cost.
Read More: Abu Dhabi AI institute releases fully open-source models with training data, code
That surge has fueled fears that some American firms could become reliant on Beijing's models as both countries race to dominate a technology they see as crucial to ​their future.
"Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said, adding that his company's chips ​would not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face.
Under the deal, Nvidia will pay about $11.9 billion to Hugging Face investors, while offering an ‌equity-based retention ⁠program of up to $1 billion for employees who join Nvidia.
The two companies already work together to help developers use Nvidia's computing services on the platform.
Balance sheet strength
Hugging Face was valued at $4.5 billion in its in August 2023, when it raised $235 million from investors such as Salesforce , AMD  and Amazon .
Nvidia, meanwhile, exited its July quarter with $22.44 billion in cash and cash equivalents, more than double January's $10.61 billion, giving the chipmaker substantial ​capacity to fund the deal.
That financial ​strength reflects a rapidly expanding ⁠business. Late last month, Nvidia issued a rare year-ahead outlook, forecasting revenue growth of about 70% in fiscal 2028 as the AI infrastructure boom rages on.
But the chipmaker's use of its balance sheet has also drawn scrutiny. ​Deals such as its agreement to guarantee up to $105 billion for OpenAI's Ohio data-center lease have intensified investor ​concerns that Nvidia ⁠is supporting the demand driving its growth.
For Nvidia, building up open source may help it cushion a demand slowdown from customers such as Meta , OpenAI and Microsoft , which are developing their own AI chips to cut reliance on its costly and supply-constrained processors.
Hugging Face has also been in the news ⁠recently after ​a hack by rogue AI agents that escaped OpenAI's testing environment. Beyond hosting AI ​models, it offers datasets, software libraries and cloud services used to build and deploy AI applications.
The New York-based startup was founded in 2016 by French entrepreneurs Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond ​and Thomas Wolf.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Thursday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.84 and Rs2.28 per litre, respectively, for September 4.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs349 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs374.31 per litre for September 4.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by Rs2.29 and Rs1.11 per litre, respectively, for September 3.
Read: Govt increases petrol price by Rs2.29, HSD by Rs1.11 per litre for Sept 3
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, petroleum products constitute one of the country's largest import categories, making the economy highly vulnerable to changes in global crude oil prices. Domestic refineries satisfy only part of national demand, while the remainder is met through imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products. Consequently, every increase in international oil prices raises Pakistan's import bill, pressures foreign exchange reserves, and contributes to inflation.
Pakistan previously exercised significant government control over petroleum pricing through subsidies and administrative interventions. While these measures temporarily protected consumers, they imposed substantial fiscal costs. During periods of elevated global oil prices, successive governments delayed passing price increases to consumers, creating financial pressures for oil marketing companies, refineries, and the national budget. Large fuel subsidies widened fiscal deficits, increased public borrowing, and weakened macroeconomic stability.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices hit fresh six-week highs on Thursday ​after new US strikes on Iran and renewed Israeli threats against Tehran heightened concerns about ‌disruptions to Middle East supplies.
Brent crude futures were up $1.66, or 1.7%, at $97.29 a barrel by 1200 GMT, erasing earlier losses, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose $2.03, or 2.2%, to $93.04. Both contracts were heading for ​their fourth day of gains and hit six-week highs earlier in the session.
"The oil market remains tight, with oil inventories still declining globally, translating into higher prices. Some support ​might have also come ​from ongoing tensions ⁠in the Middle East," said UBS energy analyst Giovanni Staunovo.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
ASUS TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) resmi meluncur di Indonesia pada 3 September 2026. Laptop gaming ini hadir dengan pilihan prosesor Intel Core HX generasi ke-14 dan GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Series, mulai dari RTX 5050 hingga RTX 5070. ASUS memosisikannya sebagai perangkat yang dapat digunakan untuk gaming, pembuatan konten, hingga kebutuhan berbasis AI.
TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) hadir dengan beberapa konfigurasi yang menyasar pengguna dengan kebutuhan berbeda. Pilihan prosesor mencakup Intel Core i5-14450HX dan Core i7-14650HX, sedangkan kapasitas RAM bawaan mencapai 16GB DDR5-5600. ASUS juga menyediakan ruang untuk upgrade RAM dan penyimpanan, sehingga pengguna tidak harus langsung mengganti perangkat ketika kebutuhan komputasinya meningkat.
ASUS TUF Gaming 16 (FX610) punya bobot 2.20kg (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
Dari sisi harga, laptop ASUS TUF Gaming 16 berada di rentang Rp27,999 juta hingga Rp35,999 juta. Posisi tersebut membuat TUF Gaming 16 bersaing di segmen laptop gaming menengah hingga atas, terutama untuk konfigurasi RTX 5060 dan RTX 5070. Namun, penilaian soal value tetap bergantung pada performa aktual masing-masing varian serta kebutuhan pengguna, bukan hanya spesifikasi di atas kertas.
Baca Juga: ASUS ROG Perkenalkan Mouse 8K & Monitor OLED 720Hz untuk Esports Kompetitif
Performa dan Pendinginan Jadi Fokus
ASUS TUF Gaming 16 digunakan dalam bermain game AAA (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
ASUS TUF Gaming 16 menggunakan sistem pendinginan yang disebut Thermal Equilibrium, dengan dua kipas dan tiga heat pipe berbahan tembaga. ASUS mengklaim rancangan tersebut mampu menangani total platform performance hingga 105W, terdiri dari alokasi CPU hingga 35W dan GPU hingga 70W pada konfigurasi tertentu.
Untuk model RTX 5050, ASUS juga menyebut GPU tersebut mampu mencapai hingga 440 TOPS untuk beban kerja AI dengan TGP hingga 85W dalam mode Turbo. Kombinasi hardware ini ditujukan untuk berbagai kebutuhan, termasuk game AAA, editing video, serta fitur AI seperti upscaling dan rendering berbasis DLSS 4. Klaim performa tersebut tentunya tetap perlu dilihat melalui pengujian independen di berbagai skenario.
Upgradeability dan Layar 144Hz
Laptop sedang digunakan dalam melakukan generating image secara intens (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
Salah satu aspek yang cukup menarik adalah kemudahan upgrade. ASUS TUF Gaming 16 membawa satu slot SO-DIMM tambahan selain RAM bawaan 16GB, dengan dukungan hingga 64GB. Penyimpanan 512GB PCIe 4.0 NVMe juga ditemani satu slot M.2 2280 tambahan yang dapat digunakan untuk ekspansi kapasitas hingga 2TB.
Laptop ini menggunakan layar 16 inci WUXGA dengan refresh rate 144Hz, cakupan 100 persen sRGB, dan tingkat kecerahan hingga 300 nits. Konektivitasnya mencakup USB Type-A, USB Type-C dengan DisplayPort dan Power Delivery, HDMI, serta RJ45 LAN. Bobotnya mencapai 2,2 kg dengan engsel yang dapat dibuka hingga 180 derajat.
Klik gambar untuk melihat lebih lengkap
Untuk ketahanan, ASUS menyebut TUF Gaming 16 telah melewati pengujian MIL-STD-810H yang mencakup vibrasi, guncangan, ketinggian, dan suhu ekstrem. ASUS TUF Gaming 16 dibanderol mulai Rp27.999.000 untuk varian Core i5-14450HX dengan RTX 5050 hingga Rp35.999.000 untuk konfigurasi Core i7-14650HX dan RTX 5070. Setiap pembelian juga mendapatkan TUF Backpack dan TUF Gaming M3 Mouse selama persediaan masih tersedia.

items.author: Webdesk
items.content:
AI agent claude, ChagGPT, xAI’s Grok and Microsoft’s email services were gradually recovering after a technical issue disrupted access to Exchange Online and several other Microsoft 365 services worldwide. According to Axios, all three major AI agents showed disruption as stated by the outage company, Dowdetector.
Axios also reported worldwide issues with Google’s Gemini, however, the company has confirmed the outage notice. Claude's website said Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 models are affected while the issue affecting Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5 has been resolved.
User reports indicate problems with Cloudflare since 11:12 AM EDT.
How is it affecting you? #CloudflareDownhttps://t.co/hfld2LwDK7
— Downdetector (@downdetector) September 3, 2026
Microsoft initially said it had identified a common failure pattern involving authentication and protocol connectivity within Exchange Online, its cloud-based email and calendar service.
The company later traced the disruption to an issue involving a core authentication configuration used by several internal services within the Exchange Online infrastructure.
Microsoft engineers conducted manual tests on individual servers before expanding remedial measures across the affected infrastructure. “We continue to see gradual improvements to the service as our mitigation actions are applied,” the company said in an update.
It warned that users could continue to experience varying levels of disruption and email delays while recovery efforts continued.
Microsoft also said the authentication issue affected services beyond Exchange Online. Reports indicated that OneDrive for Business, SharePoint Online, Teams, Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender XDR were among the services experiencing disruption.
Outage-monitoring platform Downdetector recorded thousands of user reports at the height of the disruption, although its figures reflect reports submitted by users and do not represent the total number of people affected.

items.title: WhatsApp Bill Payments Feature Launches in India With Support for UPI, Card Payments Across 30 Categories
items.summary: WhatsApp launched its Bill Payments feature in India on Thursday. It allows users to find, manage and pay household and utility bills without leaving the messaging app. To facilitate transactions, the Meta-owned messaging platform leverages the Bharat Connect (BBPS) network. Users can access 22,722 billers across 30 categories, including electricity, gas, water, FASTag, insurance, credit card and loan repayments. The feature is being rolled out gradually and will be available to Android and iOS users across India over the coming weeks.

items.title: Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 Masuk Indonesia, Resmi Dijual 4 September
items.summary:
Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 masuk Indonesia dan akan mulai dijual pada 4 September 2026 melalui toko resmi Lenovo, baik online maupun offline. Tablet generasi terbaru ini membawa sejumlah peningkatan pada sistem audio JBL, layar, performa, dan desain kickstand dibandingkan pendahulunya.
Namun, perusahaan asal China ini masih belum mengumumkan harga dan spesifikasi Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 di Tanah Air.
Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 pertama kali diperkenalkan secara global pada 16 Juni 2026, dengan pembaruan utama pada sistem audio JBL dan layar dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya.

Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 Masuk Indonesia, Apa yang Berubah?

Walau dilengkapi dengan kemampuan speaker mumpuni, tablet baru Lenovo
items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 masuk Indonesia dan akan mulai dijual pada 4 September 2026 melalui toko resmi Lenovo, baik online maupun offline. Tablet generasi terbaru ini membawa sejumlah peningkatan pada sistem audio JBL, layar, performa, dan desain kickstand dibandingkan pendahulunya.
Namun, perusahaan asal China ini masih belum mengumumkan harga dan spesifikasi Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 di Tanah Air.
Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 pertama kali diperkenalkan secara global pada 16 Juni 2026, dengan pembaruan utama pada sistem audio JBL dan layar dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya.
Baca Juga: Lenovo IdeaTab Plus Resmi Dijual di Indonesia, Harga Mulai Rp 6,1 Jutaan
Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 Masuk Indonesia, Apa yang Berubah?
Jika dibandingkan generasi pertama Tab Plus yang mengandalkan delapan speaker JBL, kini Lenovo menambah jumlahnya menjadi 9 unit Pro Speaker System berteknologi Dolby Atmos dengan konfigurasi 7.2-channel cinematic audio.
Walau dilengkapi dengan kemampuan speaker mumpuni, tablet baru Lenovo ini bisa dipakai sebagai speaker Bluetooth mandiri. Caranya, pengguna cukup nyalakan audio di smartphone dan hubungkan langsung ke speaker Tab Plus Gen 2.
Lenovo juga menyediakan mode Dolby Audio Dynamic, Movie, dan Music agar pengalaman menikmati beragam konten di Tab Plus Gen 2 semakin imersif.
Layar naik dari panel LCD 11,5 inci 2K 90Hz pada generasi pertama menjadi LCD 12,1 inci 2.5K (2560 x 1600 piksel) 120Hz pada Gen 2, dengan dukungan Dolby Vision, HDR10, dan kecerahan hingga 800 nit dalam High Brightness Mode.
Spesifikasi Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2
Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 masuk Indonesia, spesifikasinya bagaimana?
Meskipun belum diketahui secara pasti spesifikasi tablet baru Lenovo saat rilis di Indonesia, perusahaan diketahui mengganti chipset MediaTek Helio G99 pada generasi pertama dengan MediaTek Dimensity 7400 di Gen 2.
Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 versi global tersedia dalam pilihan memori mulai dari RAM 6GB hingga 12GB, dan penyimpanan 128GB hingga 256GB dengan slot microSD hingga 2TB.
Bagaimana Desain Kickstand dan Daya Tahan Baterainya?
Kickstand di Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 masuk Indonesia. (Doc: Lenovo)
Kickstand Lenovo Tab Plus Gen 2 masuk Indonesia kini terintegrasi dan dapat diputar 360 derajat, terbagi ke dalam empat mode: Lean Mode, Theater Mode, Stand Mode, dan Hanging Mode.
Sesuai dengan namanya, Hanging Mode ini memungkinkan tablet digantung, misalnya untuk mengikuti resep di dapur.
Kapasitas baterai naik dari 8.600mAh menjadi 10.200mAh. Lenovo mengklaim daya tahan streaming YouTube hingga 15 jam dalam pengujian internal perusahaan, naik dari klaim 12 jam pada generasi pertama, dengan dukungan pengisian cepat 45W.
Tab Plus Gen 2 menjalankan Android 16, dengan janji dua kali peningkatan versi hingga Android 18 dan pembaruan keamanan sampai 2030. Perangkat kompatibel dengan Lenovo Tab Pen Plus. 
Fitur AI Live Transcript mendukung transkripsi dan penerjemahan real-time lebih dari 40 bahasa, dengan penggunaan gratis dibatasi dua jam per hari.
Lenovo IdeaTab Plus Resmi Dijual di Indonesia
Desain dari Lenovo IdeaTab Plus dengan semua varian warna
Lenovo resmi menjual IdeaTab Plus di Indonesia sebagai tablet yang menyasar kebutuhan produktivitas, mulai dari kuliah hingga bekerja. Perangkat ini membawa layar berukuran 12,1 inci dengan resolusi 2.5K, chipset MediaTek Dimensity 6400, serta sistem operasi Android. Beberapa varian juga sudah dibekali Lenovo Tab Pen dan keyboard.
Dengan ukuran layar yang cukup besar, Lenovo IdeaTab Plus mencoba menawarkan pengalaman yang lebih fleksibel dibandingkan tablet berukuran kecil. Pengguna dapat memanfaatkannya untuk membaca dokumen, mencatat materi, mengikuti meeting online, hingga mengerjakan pekerjaan dengan dukungan sejumlah aplikasi Google seperti Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, dan Gmail.
Lenovo IdeaTab Plus juga menyematkan sejumlah fitur berbasis AI seperti Lenovo AI Notes, Google Gemini, dan Circle to Search. AI Notes dapat membantu merapikan serta merangkum catatan, sementara Gemini dapat digunakan untuk mencari ide atau membantu kebutuhan menulis. Namun, fitur AI semacam ini tetap lebih tepat dipandang sebagai pendukung produktivitas, bukan pengganti seluruh pekerjaan pengguna.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Academy of Higher Education (NAHE), Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan, has concluded a four-day faculty training programme titled, “AI Literacy for Educators: Building AI-Ready Institutions,” for Lecturers and Assistant Professors serving in public sector higher education institutions (HEIs).
Thirty-two faculty members representing public sector HEIs from Islamabad and Rawalpindi attended the training in person at HEC Smart Classroom alongside more than 300 faculty members participating in the programme through university-based Smart Classrooms and Video Conference Rooms.
The programme, organised through the Smart Classroom, was designed to strengthen faculty’s capacity to understand, critically evaluate, and integrate Artificial Intelligence into teaching, learning, research, assessment, and broader academic practices.
The comprehensive professional development intervention combined conceptual understanding, practical hands-on learning, critical reflection, and the application of AI across diverse academic contexts, enabling participants to develop both foundational knowledge and practical skills.
A distinctive feature of the programme was its technology-enabled delivery through HEC Smart Classroom network as majority of the faculty members joined the training programme online from their respective universities. This arrangement allowed participants to attend live sessions in real time and engage directly with the resource person, making the sessions interactive despite distance.
Managing Director NAHE Dr. Noor Amna Malik attended the closing ceremony as chief guest. She highlighted the transformative impact of AI on higher education, noting that AI is rapidly reshaping the ways knowledge is created, taught, assessed, researched, and applied. She urged universities to prepare faculty members and students to effectively navigate an AI-enabled academic environment while ensuring that technological advancement remains firmly grounded in academic quality, ethical principles, human judgment, and institutional responsibility. She underlined that AI literacy for educators extends far beyond the ability to operate AI tools.
Dr. Malik highlighted the importance of developing a critical understanding of AI systems, including their capabilities, limitations, and implications for academic work. She also emphasised the need for faculty members to uphold academic integrity, critically evaluate AI-generated outputs, safeguard privacy and intellectual property, and maintain appropriate human oversight in teaching, assessment, research, and academic decision-making. She stressed the importance of developing AI-ready institutions, noting that the meaningful integration of AI requires capable faculty, institutional preparedness, effective governance mechanisms, ethical safeguards, and continuous professional development.
The participants received extensive practical exposure to the use of AI in curriculum and course design, lesson planning, teaching resource development, academic writing, research support, assessment design, student feedback, data analytics, communication, and professional productivity. The participants also explored contemporary AI tools and learned the principles of prompt engineering and effective human-AI interaction.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has issued fresh notices to television actor Momina Iqbal and PML-N MPA Saqib Chadhar after new evidence emerged in an ongoing harassment case.
Both Iqbal and Chadhar have been called to appear at the NCCIA office in Lahore on September 4. The agency has also formed a special investigation team to examine the latest evidence and review the records already collected during the investigation.
NCCIA Issues Fresh Notices to Momina Iqbal and Saqib Chadhar Over Harassment Case
NCCIA Punjab Deputy Director Waqas Saeed said the new team will be led by a deputy director. The team has been given one month to complete its inquiry and submit its findings to the agency’s director general.
He said that any further legal action would depend on the outcome of the investigation. He also stressed that it was too early to declare either party guilty or innocent before the inquiry was completed.
Court Withdraws Bail Pleas
The development came as a Lahore court disposed of the pre-arrest interim bail petitions filed by Saqib Chadhar and his wife. The petitions were withdrawn after the new investigating officer told the court that their arrest was not required at this stage.
The case took a new turn after the investigating officer changed. During an earlier hearing on July 28, former IO and NCCIA officer Najam Bajwa had told the court that Chadhar had been found guilty following the investigation.
However, the new investigating officer, Hassan Sajjad Naqvi, informed the court that the investigation had changed after new evidence was presented. He said there was currently no need to arrest the suspects.
According to the summons, the suspects had requested a fresh investigation based on new defence evidence. Iqbal was also asked to provide her statement regarding the newly presented material.
Iqbal attended the court hearing when the latest development was discussed. Following the statement from the investigating officer, Chadhar and his wife withdrew their bail petitions.
How the Case Started
The dispute became public earlier this year when Momina Iqbal spoke about alleged online harassment, cyberbullying and death threats. In a social media post in May, she said she and her family had experienced significant mental stress because of the alleged harassment.
Iqbal initially did not publicly name the person she accused. She said a PML-N provincial assembly member had allegedly been threatening her for an extended period. She also claimed that she had previously approached cybercrime authorities over the matter.
However, she later filed a formal complaint, accusing Chadhar, his wife and others of allegedly carrying out a campaign involving cyber harassment, stalking, intimidation, blackmail and threats.
Iqbal also alleged that Chadhar made threatening calls after she rejected his marriage proposal. She further claimed that he sent threatening WhatsApp messages and made video calls. According to her complaint, similar messages were also sent to her sister.
See Also: Defence Day Cyber Threat Alert! National CERT Orders 24/7 Monitoring of Critical Digital Infrastructure
Chadhar’s lawyer rejected the allegations and maintained that the two had known each other for several years.
The NCCIA later registered case against Chadhar on June 4 under several provisions of the PECA and Pakistan Penal Code. The allegations include unauthorised access or transmission of data, offences against modesty, cyberstalking and criminal intimidation.
The latest notices mean the case will now undergo another detailed review as investigators examine the newly presented evidence.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Stockbroking major Zerodha has received SEBI’s approval to operate as a merchant banker through its wholly owned subsidiary Zerodha Corporate Advisors Pvt Ltd.
The approval comes months after Zerodha applied for a Category I merchant banking licence through the subsidiary.
“SEBI has granted the merchant banking registration to Zerodha Corporate Advisors. We are now setting up operations and expect to be up and running over the next few months,” Mohit Mehra, whole-time director at Zerodha Corporate Advisors, told Inc42.
 
He said Zerodha Corporate Advisors’ initial focus will be on equity IPOs, “particularly new-age businesses looking to raise capital from the public markets”.
Zerodha had infused ₹55 Cr into the merchant banking business to meet the higher net worth requirement under the revised regulations, Mehra said.
“We deliberately refrained from soliciting business before the licence was approved, and will build the mandate pipeline over the coming months,” he added.
Zerodha has housed the merchant banking business in a separate entity to maintain a clear separation from its broking operations and strengthen compliance safeguards.
Zerodha Looks Beyond Stockbroking
The merchant banking foray is part of Zerodha’s broader diversification push as regulatory changes and softer trading activity weigh on its core stockbroking business.
Zerodha’s brokerage revenue fell 10.4% to ₹2,738 Cr in FY26 from ₹3,066 Cr in FY25. Net transaction charges also fell to zero from ₹400 Cr a year earlier following the implementation of SEBI’s true-to-label framework.
Despite the decline in trading-linked income, Zerodha’s net profit rose 1.2% YoY to ₹4,283 Cr in FY26 from ₹4,231 Cr in FY25. Its interest income fell about 4% YoY to ₹2,269 Cr, while revenue from delayed payment charges and its MTF business surged to ₹448 Cr from ₹22 Cr in FY25.
Zerodha’s MTF book reached around ₹9,000 Cr in FY26, with customers borrowing about ₹6,000 Cr. The business contributed roughly 10% of the company’s revenue. However, founder and CEO Nithin Kamath has cautioned against encouraging customers to borrow merely to boost revenue, citing the risks associated with leveraged investing.
Meanwhile, competition in India’s retail broking market has intensified, particularly from Groww. In July 2026, Groww had 1.31 Cr active clients, nearly twice Zerodha’s 67.62 Lakh.
Groww added more than 70,000 active clients during the month, while Zerodha lost around 38,000. Zerodha’s share of NSE’s active-client base stood at 14.88%.
However, Zerodha has maintained that active-client market share is not the best measure of its performance, pointing instead to the assets held on its platform, which stood at ₹9.05 Lakh Cr in FY26.
The company is also broadening its product portfolio, with plans to launch US stock investing, and expand its NRI business. Its venture capital arm, Rainmatter, continues to invest in startups. Zerodha is also working on enabling mutual fund transactions on its broking platform Kite.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Oppo has confirmed that ColorOS 17 will officially launch on September 17, 2026. The company is expected to introduce the new software at the ColorOS 17 Launch and Developer Conference. The event will also reportedly mark the debut of the Oppo Find X10 series.
ColorOS 17 will be based on Android 17 and will bring several changes to the user interface. One of the biggest additions is a new floating island navigation system. It will appear across the operating system and many built-in apps.
ColorOS 17 Set to Launch on September 17 Alongside Oppo Find X10 Series
The new navigation system focuses heavily on animations and touch feedback. Elements can stretch, compress, and bounce back when users interact with them. Oppo is also expected to improve overall system performance. The company claims the new software can deliver around 35% smoother interface performance, 20% faster cold app launches, and a 50% improvement in the number of apps that can remain active in the background.
ColorOS 17 has already entered closed beta testing. Testing began in early August on some newer Oppo devices, giving selected users an early look at the redesigned navigation and animations.
Following the official launch, the software is expected to expand to more than 130 devices across Oppo, OnePlus, and Realme. The rollout will likely take place in stages, depending on the device and market.
Oppo Find X10 Series Could Bring Major Hardware Upgrades
The Find X10 lineup is also expected to take the spotlight at the September 17 event. Current reports suggest Oppo could introduce three models in the series.
The standard Find X10 is rumored to feature a compact 6.59-inch 1.5K display. It could also pack an 8,000mAh battery and a dual-camera setup with two 200MP sensors. The system is expected to include a main camera and a periscope telephoto camera.
The Find X10 Pro and Find X10 Pro Max are expected to offer larger displays, measuring around 6.78 inches or more. They could also use the more powerful Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset.
The Find X10 Pro Max is expected to be the most advanced model in the lineup. Rumors suggest it could feature three 200MP cameras for the main, ultrawide, and telephoto lenses. This would make the phone one of Oppo’s most camera-focused flagships.
See Also: Realme Confirms Switch to ColorOS 17: List of Eligible Phones Revealed
All three models are expected to run ColorOS 17 out of the box.
Oppo’s September 17 event could therefore be an important launch for both its software and smartphone businesses. ColorOS 17 will introduce a refreshed user experience, while the Find X10 series could bring significant upgrades in performance, battery capacity, displays, and cameras.
However, the Find X10 specifications and even the final number of models have not been fully confirmed. Oppo is expected to reveal the official details during the launch event.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s National Cyber Emergency Response Team has issued a high-level cybersecurity advisory ahead of Defence Day, directing critical institutions to strengthen monitoring, maintain round-the-clock technical readiness, and prepare for possible cyberattacks between September 5 and 7.
The advisory calls on key public-sector bodies, critical information infrastructure operators, and sectoral and provincial CERTs to remain on heightened alert during the period. Institutions have been asked to establish dedicated cybersecurity control rooms and ensure that technical teams and designated focal persons remain available for immediate response.
The National Security Operations Centre, or NSOC, will serve as the country’s central cyber coordination point during Defence Day. It is expected to operate continuously, monitor the national cyber situation, facilitate the exchange of threat intelligence, and support a coordinated response to major incidents affecting digital infrastructure.
Authorities have also directed organizations to continuously monitor critical networks, systems, websites, and digital services and to immediately report suspicious activity, attempted intrusions, or confirmed security breaches.
Critical Systems Placed on Heightened Security
The advisory places particular emphasis on government and other sensitive digital platforms, including websites, online portals, APIs, and email services.
Institutions have been advised to activate web application firewalls and DDoS protection, ensure web-facing systems are fully updated, and apply stronger controls to administrative accounts. Multi-factor authentication has also been recommended for privileged access.
The National CERT has further instructed organizations to update operating systems, disable unnecessary services, and keep firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and intrusion prevention systems active on critical servers.
Sensitive databases should not be directly exposed through public IP addresses, while security logs should be continuously reviewed for signs of unauthorized access or unusual activity.
Officials have also stressed the need for uninterrupted coordination with the NSOC so that threat intelligence and incident information can be shared quickly across institutions.
Backup, Recovery, and Connectivity Plans Put on Standby
The advisory also focuses on operational resilience in the event of a serious cyber incident.
Critical organizations have been instructed to keep disaster recovery sites ready for immediate use and maintain offline or air-gapped backups of important systems, configurations, and data. Recovery mechanisms should also be tested in advance rather than relied upon without verification.
Data centers and security operations centers have been advised to ensure backup internet connectivity and uninterrupted power arrangements, including UPS and generator support.
Technical teams have also been told to remain prepared for rapid escalation, communication and incident response if an attack is detected.
The measures reflect growing concern over coordinated cyber threats against public-facing and critical digital systems during high-profile national events. With multiple institutions expected to operate under heightened vigilance, authorities are aiming to reduce the risk of service disruption, data compromise, and wider impact on Pakistan’s digital infrastructure.

items.title: Simple Energy Catches The Mass-Market Wave
items.summary:
After years of chasing premium and performance-focused buyers, EV startups are now setting their sights on the mass market. While EV startups initially built their propositions around consumers willing to pay a premium for longer range, connected features and differentiated riding experiences, that playbook has started to change.

items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
After years of chasing premium and performance-focused buyers, EV startups are now setting their sights on the mass market. While EV startups initially built their propositions around consumers willing to pay a premium for longer range, connected features and differentiated riding experiences, that playbook has started to change.
With electric two-wheelers moving deeper into the mainstream, manufacturers are increasingly looking beyond the early-adopter customer to the much larger pool of family and commuter buyers. Ola Electric and Ather Energy recently introduced more affordable, family-oriented scooters. Now, Bengaluru-based Simple Energy is joining the race with its new Wave range.
Earlier this month, the union government halved the incentive for registered electric two-wheelers (E2Ws) to ₹2,500 per kWh of battery capacity, capped at ₹5,000 per vehicle from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2028, compared to ₹5,000 per kWh, capped at ₹10,000 per vehicle, under the FY25 scheme.
With policy support becoming more modest, affordability is emerging as an increasingly important lever for adoption, particularly as manufacturers look to expand beyond premium early adopters and tap the much larger commuter segment in India’s $30 Bn two-wheeler market. This is the segment that Simple is also going after.
Launched at an introductory starting price of ₹1.10 Lakh (ex-showroom), the Simple Wave marks a significant expansion of the startup’s portfolio, which was previously anchored by the performance-oriented Simple One. The new lineup comprises six models across three variants. Bookings have opened across Simple Energy’s stores and website, with deliveries scheduled to begin in the last week of September.
But the Wave is about more than adding another scooter to Simple Energy’s portfolio. For the startup, it is a bet that the next leg of India’s EV adoption will come from the mass market.
From Performance To Family Scooters
Simple Energy was founded in 2019 by Suhas Rajkumar and Shreshth Mishra, with Ankit Gupta later joining as a cofounder. Its first product, the Simple One, positioned the company around performance and long-range electric mobility. The Wave represents a deliberate broadening of that proposition.
“We definitely want to scale up and become a part of the top five clubs. Hopefully, in the top three very soon, depending on how we scale from here,” founder and CEO Rajkumar said.
According to him, the family scooter is primarily about expanding Simple Energy’s presence across India by giving consumers a more affordable entry point into its portfolio. “When you make an affordable offering, it scales up your production; it scales up your volumes.”
The Wave models are intended to serve as an entry point for a larger mass audience. The shift comes at a time when the broader electric two-wheeler industry is also moving in the same direction. EV manufacturers are increasingly trying to compete for customers who would otherwise buy a conventional petrol scooter.
Ola Electric recently launched the S1Z in two variants priced at ₹79,999 and ₹99,999, with IDC-certified ranges of 179 km and 301 km. The S1Z is also the company’s first scooter range powered by its locally developed 46-series LFP Bharat Cell technology.
Ather Energy, meanwhile, launched the Konarc family scooter at a starting price of ₹99,999. Built on the company’s new EL platform, the Konarc is available in six variants across the S and Z product lines, with range options spanning 100 km to 200 km.
For these players, as well as for Simple Energy, the new launches mean competing not just against each other and fellow EV startups but against the entrenched two-wheeler industry.
Rajkumar explicitly spelt this out: “ICE products are definitely a competition. Our objective is to change the way people move from petrol to EVs. The competition is not about how we can price better or undercut the competition. It’s more to do with how much more value we can give to the consumer at that price point.”
From 1,500 Scooters To 10,000 A Month
The larger challenge for Simple Energy is not necessarily finding demand, but building enough capacity and distribution to capture the natural demand in the market for EVs.
The company currently has manufacturing capacity of around 3,000 scooters a month and says it is selling roughly 1,500 units a month. It wants to take monthly sales and manufacturing to 10,000 units by March 2027.
That would represent more than a six-fold increase from its current monthly sales run rate. Rajkumar believes the Wave can help unlock that growth, particularly as an affordable family scooter can tap into demand beyond the company’s existing customer base.
“The current tailwind of the industry kind of takes up a definite demand that is already there. And when you add a family scooter with a more affordable price tag, I think it only escalates that current demand as well,” he said.
Simple Energy also plans to substantially expand its retail footprint. The company currently has around 90 stores across 61 cities, and is targeting 160-170 outlets by March 2027.
Importantly, these are dealer-operated outlets, rather than company-owned stores. This allows Simple Energy to expand its physical presence without taking on the entire capital burden of establishing and operating each outlet.
While the company believes its existing network could potentially absorb significant additional demand, Rajkumar said the expansion is being undertaken conservatively to ensure that the retail network keeps pace with production and manufacturing capacity.
At the moment, that is the bottleneck. Rajkumar said the company’s 1,500-unit monthly sales are not primarily a result of weak demand or distribution constraints, but supply limitations.
“It’s more supply constraint, not distribution or demand. It’s the manufacturing side of it. That’s the most problematic piece for us today,” the CEO said.
This makes capacity expansion particularly important if Simple Energy is to deliver on its 10,000-unit monthly target on sales and manufacturing. The startup expects manufacturing capacity to reach 75-80% of this target by the end of the next financial year, from around 30% currently.
The company also claims that around 95% of its components are localised, an important factor as EV manufacturers increasingly seek greater control over their supply chains and costs.
Betting On Scale, While Costs Remain A Challenge
The Wave’s ₹1.10 Lakh introductory price is another important part of Simple Energy’s strategy.
The company has positioned the price as an introductory offer rather than necessarily a permanent price point. Yet despite the lower entry price, Rajkumar expects the Wave portfolio to generate a contribution margin of around 20-25% over the next eight to 12 months.
That makes the economics of the mass-market push particularly important. Affordable scooters can potentially unlock significantly higher volumes, but they also leave less room for cost inefficiencies.
And commodity inflation is already putting pressure on the sector. Rajkumar said commodity prices have increased sharply, with costs rising roughly 25-30% over the past two quarters, impacting margins across the industry.
Achieving the contribution margin in this atmosphere will be a challenge, and it’s one that Simple has dealt with throughout its existence, as Rajkumar acknowledged. “Supply chain has always been a problem since 2020. Today, the margins have dropped significantly because of the commodity price increase,” he said.
This pressure can persist for at least another 12 months, although the company anticipates some easing after 18-24 months.
In June, the startup raised ₹250 Cr through a mix of debt and equity. The capital is being deployed primarily towards manufacturing capacity and production expansion, with the balance earmarked for sales, marketing and R&D.
The fundraise is also part of the company’s broader ambition to transition into a full-stack electric vehicle OEM and eventually prepare for an IPO.
The company reported revenue of around ₹171 Cr in FY26, as the founder claimed, up sharply from roughly ₹44 Cr in FY25. Rajkumar attributed the growth largely to the underlying demand for its products rather than any single growth lever.
“For us, the demand is there. We just have to multiply our production,” he said.
That, in many ways, captures Simple Energy’s immediate challenge.
India’s electric two-wheeler market is growing rapidly, but competition is becoming considerably broader. Vahan data showed electric two-wheeler registrations falling 16.2% month-on-month to 1.72 Lakh units in August, although registrations were still up 64% year-on-year.
As Ola, Ather, Simple Energy and traditional automakers such as TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp push further into affordable EVs, the next phase of the market is likely to be less about convincing affluent early adopters and more about winning the everyday commuter.
For Simple Energy, the Wave is therefore both a product launch and a scale test. If the company succeeds, it could move closer to the top-five in the market and eventually the top-three position that it is eyeing.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Signify menggelar Signify Innovation Day Light the Future di Jakarta pada 2 September 2026. Acara ini mempertemukan sejumlah pemangku kepentingan dari sektor pemerintahan, properti, hingga industri untuk membahas pemanfaatan teknologi pencahayaan dalam pengembangan kota pintar dan layak huni serta bangunan yang lebih adaptif terhadap kebutuhan masa depan.
Pembahasan tersebut turut dikaitkan dengan agenda pembangunan berkelanjutan di Indonesia, termasuk target Net Zero Emission (NZE) pada 2060 atau lebih cepat. Dalam konteks ini, pencahayaan tidak lagi sekadar diposisikan sebagai fasilitas penerangan, tetapi juga bagian dari infrastruktur yang dapat memengaruhi efisiensi energi, keamanan, kenyamanan, dan operasional sebuah kawasan atau bangunan.
Meski demikian, penerapan teknologi pencahayaan pintar tetap membutuhkan dukungan dari sisi kebijakan, investasi, serta kesiapan infrastruktur. Efisiensi yang ditawarkan teknologi tidak otomatis menghasilkan penghematan apabila implementasinya tidak disesuaikan dengan kebutuhan di lapangan. Karena itu, Signify Innovation Day juga membahas aspek kebijakan, pembiayaan, dan penerapan teknologi secara lebih luas.

Pencahayaan untuk Kota yang Lebih Cerdas
Salah satu produk Signify yang sudah dipakai untuk berbagai keperluan stadion olahraga di indonesia (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
Salah satu sesi bertajuk “Future of Smart & Liveable Cities: Driving Sustainability Through Innovation and Circularity” membahas strategi pembangunan kota berbasis data serta penerapan prinsip sirkularitas. Diskusi melibatkan perwakilan Kementerian Dalam Negeri, Kementerian PPN/Bappenas, Dinas Bina Marga Provinsi DKI Jakarta, dan Signify Indonesia.
Salah satu contoh yang dibahas adalah transisi menuju lampu LED dan sistem pencahayaan pintar pada Penerangan Jalan Umum (PJU) di Jakarta. Teknologi semacam ini berpotensi membantu pengelolaan energi dan operasional secara lebih efisien. Namun, penerapannya juga perlu mempertimbangkan investasi awal, pemeliharaan, serta kompatibilitas dengan infrastruktur yang sudah tersedia.
Bangunan Future-Ready Tak Hanya Soal Efisiensi
Produk Signify yang sudah dipergunakan untuk beberapa layanan publik di Indonesia (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
Sesi kedua mengangkat tema “Achieving Sustainability Goals and Business Growth Through Future-Ready Buildings”. Forum ini mempertemukan praktisi dari sektor properti, hospitality, fasilitas gedung, ESG, dan green building untuk membahas hubungan antara keberlanjutan dan kebutuhan bisnis.
Dalam pembahasan tersebut, teknologi pencahayaan ditempatkan sebagai salah satu komponen dalam pengelolaan bangunan yang lebih efisien. Sistem pencahayaan pintar dapat membantu mengatur penggunaan energi sekaligus mendukung kenyamanan penghuni. Meski begitu, pencahayaan hanya menjadi salah satu bagian dari strategi bangunan berkelanjutan yang juga mencakup sistem energi, tata kelola, material, dan operasional.
Selain diskusi, Signify turut menampilkan demo sejumlah solusi pencahayaan untuk berbagai kebutuhan profesional, termasuk perkantoran, industri, data center, hotel, stadion, fasad, lanskap, dan penerangan jalan. Acara ini menunjukkan bahwa arah pengembangan pencahayaan kini semakin terintegrasi dengan isu efisiensi energi dan pengelolaan infrastruktur, meski keberhasilan implementasinya tetap bergantung pada kebutuhan serta kondisi masing-masing sektor.
Artikel berjudul Signify Dorong Pencahayaan Pintar untuk Dukung Kota dan Bangunan Berkelanjutan yang ditulis oleh Christopher Louis pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

Horizon Ultra menjadi bagian dari upaya HUMAIN membawa kemampuan AI lebih dekat ke pengguna, alih-alih sepenuhnya bergantung pada pusat data atau layanan cloud. Generasi pertama perangkat ini akan menjalankan Microsoft Windows, sehingga secara penggunaan masih berada dalam lingkungan PC yang sudah umum digunakan, terutama untuk kebutuhan perusahaan.
Namun, HUMAIN sudah menyiapkan arah berbeda untuk generasi berikutnya. Perusahaan berencana menghadirkan HUMAIN OS pada lini Horizon Ultra mulai 2027. Sistem operasi tersebut ditujukan untuk memberikan integrasi yang lebih dalam antara perangkat, kemampuan AI, dan ekosistem teknologi HUMAIN.
Baca Juga: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Punya Dua Varian, Qualcomm Konfirmasi Meluncur September
Snapdragon X2 Elite Jadi Otak Horizon Ultra
Horizon Ultra menggunakan Snapdragon X2 Elite yang memiliki CPU Qualcomm Oryon 18-core, GPU Qualcomm Adreno, serta NPU Qualcomm Hexagon. Ketiganya memungkinkan beban kerja dibagi ke komponen yang berbeda, termasuk pemrosesan AI yang dapat dijalankan secara lokal melalui NPU.
Pendekatan tersebut memungkinkan sebagian model dan fitur AI berjalan tanpa harus terus-menerus mengirimkan data ke cloud. Secara teori, pemrosesan lokal dapat membantu responsivitas dan memungkinkan data tertentu tetap berada di perangkat. Namun, kemampuan tersebut tetap bergantung pada model AI, optimasi software, serta jenis beban kerja yang dijalankan.
Menargetkan Penggunaan Enterprise
HUMAIN juga memosisikan Horizon Ultra sebagai perangkat untuk kebutuhan enterprise. Pemrosesan AI di endpoint dapat menjadi pilihan untuk skenario yang membutuhkan respons cepat, konektivitas yang terbatas, atau pengelolaan data tertentu secara lokal. Pada saat yang sama, perangkat tetap dapat terhubung ke layanan cloud ketika membutuhkan kapasitas komputasi lebih besar.
Untuk penjualan dan distribusi enterprise, HUMAIN menunjuk AlFalak sebagai mitra. Horizon Ultra yang menjalankan Windows dijadwalkan tersedia untuk pembelian perusahaan mulai 20 September 2026.
Peluncuran ini menunjukkan arah pengembangan PC yang mulai menempatkan AI sebagai bagian dari arsitektur perangkat, bukan sekadar fitur tambahan di dalam aplikasi. Meski demikian, seberapa besar manfaat pendekatan tersebut dalam penggunaan nyata masih perlu dilihat melalui pengujian performa, efisiensi, kompatibilitas aplikasi, serta pengalaman pengguna setelah perangkat tersedia di pasar.
