items.author: Shahzad Paracha
items.content:
The federal government has approved the installation of modern fire sprinkler and alarm systems in government buildings across Islamabad following the death of newborn babies in the PIMS nursery fire, sources told ProPakistani.
The decision was taken by the Secretaries Committee on Tuesday amid concerns over fire-safety compliance in federal government buildings.
The new systems will be installed in ministries, divisions and other government buildings where adequate fire-protection arrangements are currently unavailable.
Secretary Cabinet told ProPakistani that the systems would be installed in government buildings that do not already have the required fire-safety facilities.
The PIMS tragedy exposed major gaps in fire preparedness at the hospital. Investigations pointed to inadequate fire alarms and sprinkler systems, while questions were also raised about emergency exits and response procedures.
Following the incident, the Capital Development Authority (CDA) stepped up enforcement of fire and life-safety regulations in Islamabad.
CDA sealed several buildings over non-compliance, including the Shaheed-i-Millat Building, State Life Building, Trade Development Authority of Pakistan Building and Beverly Center. Parts of two hotels in Blue Area were also reportedly sealed.
The authority also imposed Rs. 500,000 fines on PIMS, Polyclinic and CDA’s Capital Hospital for violating fire and life-safety requirements.
Sources said CDA will have a key role in checking fire-safety compliance in government buildings and identifying facilities that require new fire-protection systems.
Meanwhile, the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on National Health Services has questioned fire-safety arrangements, emergency preparedness, electrical and oxygen systems, and staff training at PIMS.
The committee has also called for accountability of those responsible for the tragedy.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
New York City officials announced a one-year moratorium on students using artificial intelligence in public elementary and middle schools, the latest step by public officials to set guidelines around new technology in the classroom.
The move by the nation's largest school district is the most restrictive to date across the US, though other districts, including Los Angeles, have said they are reviewing AI policies.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani told reporters on Wednesday that schools would halt the current use of about 40 educational tools in New York City classrooms.
"Children need teachers and human connection in order to learn and grow. They need to develop skills alongside their peers, build relationships with educators and wrestle with tough problems on their own," Mamdani said at a press conference.
Major AI developers Google, Anthropic and Microsoft did not immediately reply to requests for comment.
The policy will affect about 600,000 public school students through eighth grade, while high school students will be allowed to use AI in some cases. Teachers will be permitted to use AI for lesson planning and tasks such as scheduling, the city said in a statement.
New York City public schools previously imposed a temporary ban on ChatGPT soon after its rollout in 2022. The restriction was later lifted and replaced by a custom AI-powered teaching assistant, according to Microsoft, part-owner of ChatGPT-maker OpenAI.

items.author: Muhammad Bilal
items.content:
Pakistan and Kyrgyzstan have signed an agreement to increase bilateral trade from around $16 million currently to $200 million a year within the next two years, giving fresh momentum to economic ties between the two countries.
The agreement was signed in Bishkek on Wednesday in the presence of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov. Shehbaz said he had pushed for an agreement instead of a memorandum of understanding to make the $200 million trade target a concrete commitment.
The prime minister said the two countries would prepare a practical plan to expand trade, improve trading mechanisms, promote joint investment and industrial projects and increase direct contacts between businesses. He described the current trade volume of around $16 million as far below the level warranted by the strength of bilateral relations.
The two leaders agreed that economic cooperation should move toward a more practical and results focused stage. Kyrgyzstan said it was ready to pursue joint projects in pharmaceuticals, agriculture, energy, light industry, tourism, the digital economy and virtual assets.
A major focus of the agreement is connectivity. The two sides signed a transit trade agreement aimed at facilitating the movement of goods, improving logistics and creating stronger trade links between South and Central Asia. They also agreed to simplify transport, customs and administrative procedures and increase freight movement between the two countries.
Kyrgyz President Zhaparov said Pakistan’s seaports could provide Kyrgyzstan with an important route to South Asian markets and wider international trade. The two sides also agreed to make greater use of multimodal transport and Pakistan’s ports to expand Kyrgyzstan’s trade and transit options.
Investment and industrial cooperation are also expected to become major parts of the new economic partnership. The joint statement called for greater cooperation in mining and processing, agriculture, food, textiles, light industries, pharmaceuticals, halal products and digital technologies, with an emphasis on joint ventures, local production and technology transfers.
The two countries also signed a memorandum on virtual assets, which they said could support cooperation between their financial markets, create a secure and transparent digital asset ecosystem and encourage cross border investment and technological innovation.
Another potentially significant development is cooperation involving Kyrgyzstan’s Tamchy Special Financial Investment Territory.
The two sides expressed interest in linking the platform with Pakistani banks, investment funds, financial institutions and businesses to develop joint investment projects, financial instruments and digital solutions.
The leaders also reaffirmed cooperation in energy, including the timely implementation of the CASA 1000 project and the establishment of a joint working group covering electricity, hydropower, renewable energy, energy infrastructure and modern technologies.
In total, 17 bilateral documents were signed during Prime Minister Shehbaz’s visit, covering areas including transit trade, virtual assets, medical education, education, climate change, security, extradition, postal services, e-commerce and business cooperation. The two countries also agreed to establish sister city ties between Lahore and Osh.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Meta has introduced Muse Voice Transcribe, its first real-time audio model designed for live dictation and transcription across multiple speakers and languages.
Meta says the model can handle more than 20 speakers, switch between languages automatically, and understand code-switching, where people use words from different languages within the same sentence.
Trained Across More Than 70 Languages
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg demonstrated the model in a video showing it automatically identifying different speakers and switching between languages during a conversation.
According to Zuckerberg, Muse Voice Transcribe uses adaptive delay to improve transcription accuracy. It waits longer before committing to difficult words while processing easier words more quickly.
The model was trained across more than 70 languages, with 25 languages validated at launch.
Meta says it can also handle noisy and complicated real-world audio, mid-sentence language switching, and sessions lasting around an hour with more than 20 speakers.
Zuckerberg shared the demonstration after recently returning to X following roughly three years without posting on the platform.
Muse Voice Transcribe is MSL's first real-time audio perception model — rolling out today. SOTA in streaming speech-to-text, it handles speaker diarization, and endpointing natively in a single model. pic.twitter.com/LViMDSkbim
— Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd) September 1, 2026
Meta Takes on Google Gemini
Muse Voice Transcribe arrives less than a week after Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, which offers similar audio transcription capabilities.
Google plans to integrate its model into Android and eventually Chrome.
Meta has not said whether Muse Voice Transcribe will eventually become part of its major consumer services.
Available Through Meta AI and APIs
For now, users can access the technology through Meta’s recently launched Meta AI Mac app.
Because the Mac app can provide voice features to other applications, Muse Voice Transcribe can also power dictation in other services through the app.
Developers can access the model through Muse Code and Meta’s Model API.
Meta has priced the service at $3 per 1,000 minutes of audio.
A demonstration version of Muse Voice Transcribe is also available through Meta’s research blog.
Muse Voice Transcribe is the latest release from Meta Superintelligence Lab (MSI). In recent weeks, the group has also introduced Meta’s first dedicated coding agent, an open-weight model, and the Meta AI Mac app.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
In June, a secretive unmanned Chinese spaceplane closely monitored by US military analysts released a small satellite hundreds of miles above Earth in an orbital region crowded with commercial and military satellites. The object then looped around another Chinese satellite before returning towards the spaceplane, according to US space-tracking firm LeoLabs.
Little is known about the satellite or the mission. But the US military operates a similarly secretive spaceplane resembling a small shuttle, also with no crew. Both programs reflect the rapidly evolving field of military space operations as Beijing and Washington prepare for the possibility of conflict extending into space, according to a Reuters review of documents, space-tracking data and interviews with current and former military officials.
Chinese researchers linked to the military are developing technologies ranging from satellites designed to pursue and even capture other spacecraft to systems that could extend fuel supplies while doing so, according to a Reuters review of patent-related documents, procurement notices and academic papers. The United States and Britain conducted their first joint military operation in space in the path of a suspected Chinese spy satellite, according to commercial space-tracking data.
"The Chinese are rapidly developing capabilities," including ground- and space-based weapons designed to interfere with or destroy targets, US Space Force’s Chief of Space Operations General Chance Saltzman said in July. The threat from China is "substantial," added Saltzman, who is retiring.
Satellites have become indispensable to modern warfare, as conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East have demonstrated. For decades, they have provided communications, navigation and intelligence services to armed forces on Earth, and once placed in orbit, typically remained on fixed paths. Increasingly, however, militaries view them as active weapons platforms capable of launching attacks by disrupting a satellite’s operations through jamming or laser dazzling, or even capturing enemy spacecraft.
Amid the rapidly-evolving field of military space operations, Beijing and Washington are preparing for the possibility of conflict extending into space. Cassell Bryan-Low explains https://t.co/UlkxhbMTZU pic.twitter.com/A1moHT4YXJ
— Reuters Science News (@ReutersScience) September 2, 2026
Disruption of US space capabilities would "cripple our massive military in the terrestrial sphere," affecting everything from surveillance to missile defence, said Everett Dolman, a former professor at the US Air Force's Air War College. Spaceplanes, because they are agile and capable of deploying satellites or carrying cargo, could appear to opponents as potential "space fighters," he said.
Allies join the US effort
The growing competition comes as Earth's orbit becomes increasingly crowded. SpaceX, which recently debuted on public markets, operates about 11,000 Starlink satellites and plans a constellation of larger AI-enabled data centres in space. China is building rival networks, while US President Donald Trump's Golden Dome missile defence program envisions space-based interceptors.
The United States is also refining capabilities that could prove important in a future conflict.
Read: China warns of ‘space arms race’ as Japan expands military footprint
In the joint US-British operation in September last year, US space forces working from a base in Colorado directed a US military satellite to swoop in close to a UK one as China's Shiyan 12-01 satellite passed about 83 kilometres beneath them, according to space intelligence company Slingshot Aerospace. At that altitude, specialists consider the distance relatively close.
Three space experts with military backgrounds told Reuters it appeared intended as a signal to Beijing, including at space-tracking firm COMSPOC. Andrew Turner, a retired senior British air force officer who is now a space consultant, said it was “almost certainly a strategic signal to China” to demonstrate allied unity, capability and a warning to not interfere with the UK satellite.
The US and Britain publicly announced the operation, the first known one between two members of the "Five Eyes" intelligence alliance, but did not disclose its proximity to a Chinese spacecraft. Much of what occurs in space remains classified because of its intelligence implications.
US Space Command told Reuters the mission demonstrated the ability to work with allies in space. Britain's defence ministry said space is increasingly important to military operations and the UK and its partners were conducting advanced orbital operations to protect their national and military interests. Neither commented on the operation’s proximity to the Chinese satellite.
The US Space Force’s next chief of space operations, Lieutenant General Douglas Schiess, had been involved in the operation. In an interview shortly afterwards, he said operating close to another spacecraft could help verify whether an allied satellite is functioning properly or determine whether an adversary is "doing something it shouldn't." He declined to say at the time whether another country's satellite had been nearby.
Britain recently disclosed that the mission was conducted alongside a maritime deployment to the Indo-Pacific region.
Using space not only to support military operations on Earth but also to influence their outcome is "really, really important," then UK Space Command chief Major General Paul Tedman said in April at a conference. He has since retired from the military.
China's foreign ministry said it was not familiar with the specific details of the US-British operation. More broadly, Beijing opposes the weaponisation of space and supports its peaceful use, the ministry said, while accusing Washington of stoking an arms race through efforts including the missile defence system Golden Dome and potential space-based weapons.
Read More: China sends astronaut on year-long space mission as it eyes 2030 moon landing
Asked about Shiyan 12-01 and the Chinese spaceplane, the ministry said it had no information. State news agency Xinhua has described Shiyan 12-01 as conducting space environment surveys, and the spaceplane as an experimental craft supporting the peaceful use of space.
US Space Force says its own spaceplane is carrying out a range of tests and experiments.
Space weapons
US Space Command head General Stephen Whiting has repeatedly emphasised the importance of space to modern warfare, warning that adversaries are developing capabilities to deny the United States access to key systems and reduce military effectiveness. He has said adversaries would likely seek to target US space assets early in a conflict.
To counter such threats, the US must adopt a more active warfighting posture in space, Whiting argues. That means not only protecting US systems but also being prepared to threaten or strike hostile assets if necessary. He has called for orbital interceptors and other weapons.
"We must be well-prepared for conflict in space. And if deterrence fails, we will fight and win," he told a conference in April.
Western officials warn of a range of threats, including ground-based lasers, electronic jammers, cyberattacks and anti-satellite missiles.
In orbit, the United States, China and Russia all operate manoeuvrable satellites capable of approaching and inspecting other spacecraft. Such systems could be adapted to carry weapons, including lasers or projectiles. Western officials say Beijing and Moscow have demonstrated technologies that could be used to threaten US and allied satellites.
The US has also accused Russia of developing an anti-satellite capability involving a satellite designed to carry a nuclear weapon. Moscow has denied that it is developing a space-based anti-satellite nuclear weapon.
The UK's Tedman, in an interview last fall, said militaries now see satellites as “weapon systems” that need to manoeuvre and fight. The West is “working hard to retain our strategic advantage in space,” he said.
Some specialists note that disrupting satellites remains easier from Earth than through spacecraft-on-spacecraft attacks.
In a rare disclosure about its own capabilities, the US Space Force announced in June that it had introduced an earthbound electromagnetic weapon from L3Harris Technologies designed to disable or disrupt adversary satellites.
"Dogfighting" and hunter satellites
Although the United States remains the world's leading space power, China is rapidly expanding both the number of satellites it operates and the complexity of its missions.
Chinese satellites have demonstrated what US officials describe as orbital "dogfighting," which includes multiple satellites moving in a synchronised way in proximity. Chinese spacecraft have also shown the ability to capture a defunct satellite and move it into a different orbit.
Last year, China conducted what was likely an on-orbit refuelling attempt, according to a US Space Force official. Refuelling would be a breakthrough because satellites are normally constrained by the fuel they launch with. The ability to replenish fuel could determine whether a spacecraft remains a hunter or becomes the hunted.
Chinese institutions continue to pursue new capabilities. Patent-related documents show that the maker of some of China's most advanced military aircraft acquired technology that allows satellites to autonomously calculate fuel-efficient manoeuvres while pursuing another spacecraft.
Meanwhile, a technology-transfer notice published by the National University of Defence Technology described a mature system capable of managing hundreds of satellites simultaneously for both defensive and operational purposes.
Researchers at another major Chinese university with close military ties have also been developing pursuit satellites, including concepts involving multiple spacecraft using nets to capture targets, according to patent-related documents.
The institutions and the People's Liberation Army did not respond to requests for comment. On-orbit capabilities such as refuelling and capturing another satellite could have non-military uses.
China's official military's newspaper, PLA Daily, said in a 2022 editorial that controlling space was essential for safeguarding national security, seizing the strategic initiative and achieving victory in war.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
On a selling spree, Alpha Wave has now offloaded more than 3.5 Cr shares of fintech Pine Labs via a series of block deals today, as per NSE data.
The investment firm, via its holding entity Alpha Wave Ventures II, offloaded 3.54 Cr shares of Pine Labs in a block deal at an average transaction price of ₹155.10 per share, a discount of around 4.4% to the stock’s closing price today.
By selling nearly 3.1% stake in the fintech major, Alpha Wave netted ₹550 Cr via the transaction.
Alpha Wave held 3,59,42,015 shares of Pine Labs as of the end of the June quarter. Post today’s sale, it would be left with just 4.9 Lakh shares.
ICICI Prudential Life Insurance picked up a higher volume of the shares that hit the market compared to any other buyer, buying over 1 Cr shares.
While Societe Generale bought 45.3 Lakh, Goldman Sachs purchased 41.6 Lakh shares. Domestic mutual funds like JM Financial and Edelweiss also lapped up stake in Pine Labs.
Alpha Wave has been on a selling spree of late. Just last week, it offloaded 2.94 Cr shares of omnichannel eyewear retailer Lenskart for ₹1,856.8 Cr, and also sold its entire 7.78% stake in NBFC Aye Finance for around ₹322.6 Cr.
Earlier in June, it exited logistics major Delhivery by selling its nearly 2% stake for around ₹665 Cr. Back in May as well, it had dumped an additional 3.72 Cr Lenskart shares.
That said, Pine Labs, too, has seen plenty of bulk and block deals action this year. Private equity firm Actis dumped around ₹522.6 Cr worth of stake in Pine Labs across two stake sales back in June. Prior to that, US-based Altimeter Capital sold 1.56 Cr shares of Pine Labs while Madison India Capital sold 2.48 Cr shares in May. Pine Labs’ six-month post-IPO lock-in period expired on May 13, freeing over 93 Cr shares for trade.
On the financial front, Pine Labs’ net profit jumped over 4X on a YoY basis to ₹19.6 Cr in Q1 FY27 while its operating revenue increased by 20% to ₹736.9 Cr. The company reported a net profit of ₹113 Cr in the fiscal year FY26 against a loss of ₹145 Cr in FY25 while its operating revenue grew by 19% to ₹2,711 Cr.
Shares of Pine Labs ended the day 1.52% higher at ₹162.32 on the BSE.

items.author: News Desk
items.content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has offered one of the most optimistic visions of artificial intelligence, predicting that if powerful AI develops in the right direction, the world could become “stunningly beautiful” — with many diseases cured, human lifespans doubled and poverty eliminated.
But as Amodei's company races to commercialise its rapidly advancing Claude models and reportedly prepares for what could become one of the largest initial public offerings in history, Anthropic is also facing increasingly difficult questions about the boundaries of AI power.
The debate is no longer confined to whether AI will transform productivity. It is increasingly about who gets to decide what AI systems can see, what they can do, and where the limits of their authority should lie.
Anthropic's Claude family has rapidly emerged as one of the leading competitors in the frontier AI market. The company has also made important inroads among software developers through Claude Code, its AI-powered coding tool.
According to data cited in recent industry discussions, 39% of developers globally and 47% of US developers used Claude Code between May and July this year.
The company’s growing commercial footprint has strengthened investor expectations ahead of a potential IPO, with reports suggesting Anthropic could pitch a total addressable market worth more than $30 trillion as AI transforms productivity across the global economy.
However, the company's technological success has been accompanied by growing unease among sections of the technology community and policymakers.
At the centre of the row is a fundamental question: can a company that sees itself as building AI for humanity's benefit accumulate too much power in the process?
From idealism to influence
Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees, including Amodei, who had become convinced that advanced AI needed to be developed with stronger safeguards.
The company’s identity was built around responsible AI development.
But building increasingly capable frontier models requires enormous amounts of computing power, data and capital. That creates an inherent tension.
The more capable AI becomes, the greater the incentive for companies to collect information, expand access to users and allow systems to perform increasingly complex tasks on their behalf.
Critics argue that Claude Code illustrates this tension.
Developers have raised concerns on GitHub and other technology forums over the tool's network activity and the extent to which it can interact with external systems.
Some users have reported that the software makes frequent network requests and sends information about websites or domains during operation. Other discussions have questioned whether some of these behaviours are sufficiently transparent to users.
Such reports do not, by themselves, establish that Anthropic is conducting covert surveillance. But they have contributed to a wider debate over transparency, telemetry and user consent in AI-powered development tools.
The controversy became sharper around Claude Code's permission system.
Anthropic provides a setting known as “dangerously-skip-permissions”, which allows users to bypass confirmation prompts and permit the system to execute operations directly.
The company has also introduced an “auto mode” in which a built-in risk classifier determines whether certain operations require additional permission.
The debate surrounding these features goes beyond software design. It concerns a much larger question: At what point does an AI assistant stop merely responding to a user and begin making consequential decisions on the user's behalf?
The problem of AI authority
Anthropic's stated objective is to develop powerful AI while maintaining safety controls.
But critics argue that the expansion of autonomous capabilities creates an unavoidable shift in the balance of control.
The progression is straightforward. First, the system is allowed to observe more. Then it is permitted to act. Eventually, it begins deciding when an action is safe enough to perform without asking the user.
For supporters, this is necessary if AI is to become genuinely useful. For critics, it risks creating systems that exercise authority users may not fully understand. The controversy has therefore moved beyond the technical question of whether AI models are accurate. It is increasingly about governance.
Who establishes the rules? Who defines acceptable risk? And who has the authority to change those rules?
From Silicon Valley to the state
Amodei's influence also extends beyond Anthropic's products.
In an earlier essay on AI and international security, he argued that democratic countries should work together to control critical parts of the AI supply chain, restrict adversaries' access to advanced chips and semiconductor equipment, and use AI to strengthen military capabilities.
He also called for close cooperation between governments and private AI companies. That vision reflects a broader transformation taking place in Silicon Valley. AI companies are no longer merely developing consumer applications. Their technologies are increasingly becoming part of national-security strategies.
Palantir CEO Alex Karp has similarly argued in his book The Technological Republic that technology companies should play a greater role in national defence and governance.
The convergence of technology, defence and government policy is creating a new class of corporate power.
Frontier AI companies are simultaneously technology developers, major employers, recipients of enormous investment and increasingly important participants in national-security policy. That raises another question: Can companies entrusted with developing some of the world's most powerful technologies remain merely commercial entities?
Anthropic and Washington
Anthropic's relationship with the US government exhibits the tension.
Claude has been used in US government and defence-related applications, including intelligence analysis, modelling and simulation, operational planning and cyber-related work.
But the relationship has also exposed disagreements over how far government agencies should be able to direct the use of frontier AI systems.
At issue is a fundamental clash of authority. Governments argue that systems deployed for national-security purposes must ultimately serve government objectives.
AI companies, meanwhile, insist that certain safety restrictions should remain under their control. The disagreement points to a larger problem that governments around the world are only beginning to confront. Who controls a frontier AI system when its capabilities become strategically important? The company that built it? The government that deploys it? Or regulators who establish the boundaries within which both must operate?
The lobbying battle
As the AI industry becomes more politically influential, companies are also investing heavily in Washington.
Anthropic significantly increased its federal lobbying expenditure in the first half of 2026, according to reports, while also committing tens of millions of dollars to initiatives focused on AI-risk regulation.
Critics say this creates a troubling circularity.
AI companies lobby policymakers on rules governing AI while simultaneously helping define the risks those rules are supposed to address.
Supporters counter that companies developing frontier systems possess technical expertise that governments urgently need and therefore have a legitimate role in policy discussions.
The disagreement reflects a broader struggle over who gets to define AI safety.
The China factor
The debate is unfolding against another important development: the rapidly narrowing technological gap between leading Chinese and US AI models.
Stanford's 2026 AI Index has reported that the performance gap between top Chinese and American models has narrowed considerably.
At the same time, Chinese AI companies are increasingly competing on another front — cost.
Open-source and comparatively inexpensive models are making advanced AI capabilities more accessible and potentially more substitutable.
Reports that major US technology companies have explored bringing Chinese AI models onto American cloud platforms underscore the changing competitive landscape.
For years, US technological dominance rested partly on the assumption that the most advanced AI models would remain concentrated in American companies.
That assumption is becoming harder to sustain. As the performance gap narrows, restrictions on chips, computing infrastructure and access to advanced technology may become less effective as long-term barriers.
The result is a new strategic race. It is no longer simply about building the most powerful model. It is about controlling the ecosystem around those models — chips, cloud infrastructure, data, applications, standards and regulation.
Who defines the rules?
This brings the debate back to Anthropic. Amodei's vision is undeniably ambitious. AI could potentially accelerate scientific discovery, improve medicine, raise productivity and help solve problems that have resisted human ingenuity for generations.
But the same technology could also concentrate enormous power in the hands of a small number of companies and governments.
The contradiction is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. The people building AI argue that they are trying to make the technology safe for humanity. Critics respond that safety cannot simply mean trusting the companies building the systems to define the boundaries themselves. The real challenge may therefore be less about whether AI becomes powerful.
It almost certainly will. The more consequential question is who gets to decide how that power is used. Anthropic may believe it is helping build a better future. Its critics fear that, in trying to shape that future, it could acquire too much influence over the present. And as the race between American and Chinese AI companies intensifies, that debate is no longer confined to Silicon Valley.
It is becoming a question of national power, economic competition and global governance. The future of AI may indeed be “stunningly beautiful”. But who controls the road to that future could prove just as important as the destination.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday once again ordered strict action against officials found guilty of criminal negligence in the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) fire incident, saying no leniency would be shown to those responsible for the tragedy.
On Aug 26, 14 newborn babies were killed after a fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital at PIMS in Islamabad, triggering widespread outrage and demands from people and political parties for action against those responsible.
After an inquiry committee presented its interim report, the prime minister approved the immediate suspension of eight officials and ordered departmental as well as criminal proceedings against those identified as responsible.
Read: IHC orders report on PIMS tragedy
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, immediately after returning from Kyrgyzstan, the prime minister chaired an emergency meeting on matters relating to the Ministry of Health and the PIMS fire incident.
The meeting was briefed on matters concerning the health sector, while a special briefing was given on the ongoing investigation into the PIMS fire.
وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے کرغستان سے واپس پہنچتے ہی وزرات صحت کے امور اور پمز آتشزدگی واقعے کے حوالے سے ہنگامی اجلاس کی صدارت کی.
اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیرِ صحت سید مصطفی کمال، وزیر اقتصادی امور احد خان چیمہ، سیکریٹری ہیلتھ کپٹن (ر) محمد محمود اور پمز ہسپتال کے ایگزیکٹیو… pic.twitter.com/3pZTXVgBWY
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) September 2, 2026
It was informed that, in light of the interim investigative report, implementation of the prime minister’s decisions was being ensured.
“No leniency will be shown to officials guilty of criminal negligence,” the PM Office quoted the prime minister as saying.
He also directed the health minister and health secretary to ensure their personal presence at PIMS on alternate days and oversee, under their supervision, the implementation of measures for the hospital’s improvement.
The prime minister further directed that treatment facilities at PIMS be improved and all safety measures implemented. He also ordered that the process of reforms in the health sector be accelerated.
The meeting was attended by Federal Minister for Health Syed Mustafa Kamal, Minister for Economic Affairs Ahad Khan Cheema, Health Secretary Capt (retd) Muhammad Mahmood and PIMS Executive Director Dr Muhammad Salman.
Inquiry findings
The incident sparked nationwide outrage after 14 newborns were killed, with only one newborn girl among those inside the ward rescued alive.
The tragedy prompted immediate action from the federal government, with PM Shehbaz forming a five-member inquiry committee. The committee’s interim report highlighted several deficiencies at the hospital and recommended action against eight individuals. 
Those identified by the committee and suspended on the prime minister’s orders include PIMS Executive Director Prof Dr Imran Sikandar, Joint Executive Directors Dr Mutahir Shah and Dr Owais Ali Shah, head of the neonatal department Prof Dr Sadia Riaz, senior registrars Dr Naghma and Dr Nousheela Amjad, PIMS Assistant Director Security Mohammad Usman and Capital Development Authority Emergency Services Director General Dr Abdul Rehman.
Also Read: Judicial commission may be formed if PIMS probe fails to satisfy: Mustafa Kamal
The interim report said the precise source of ignition had not yet been “conclusively established”, adding that various accounts had attributed the fire to an air conditioner, an incubator or warmer, or an electrical short circuit or overloaded plug.
“Accordingly, an internal electrical/equipment-related origin remains plausible, but it would be premature to identify any particular appliance or component as the established cause,” the report said.
The report said the Capital Emergency Services (CES) had separately found fire and life-safety arrangements to be inadequate and compromised.
It said emergency exits and escape routes were locked or obstructed, security personnel hindered aspects of the initial response, and crowd management was inadequate. According to the CES account, firefighters had to forcibly open locked fire-exit doors and other access points.
The committee recommended that smoke and heat detection systems, alarms, fire extinguishers, hydrants, emergency lighting, electrical protection systems and all designated fire exits be physically inspected, tested and documented.
It said any mandatory emergency exit found locked, obstructed or incapable of being opened immediately during an emergency should be rectified without delay.
Read More: The PIMS fire and the failures behind it: What the interim inquiry report says
At the same time, legitimate controlled access to sensitive neonatal areas should be maintained through fire-safe arrangements, the report recommended.
The committee also recommended an urgent technical inspection of all incubators, warmers, air-conditioning and IVAC installations, sockets, plugs, distribution boards, circuit breakers, earthing and other safety-critical electrical systems in high-risk clinical areas.

The Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Police on Wednesday launched a Chinese language training programme for its personnel to enhance security for Chinese engineers and foreign project staff, with the first batch of 20 Special Security Unit (SSU) personnel having completed the course.
The trained personnel have been deployed at Chinese and other foreign projects, including the Suki Kinari Hydropower Project, Peshawar Airport, Project Peshawar, RWS Khyber, Rashakai Economic Zone, Tarbela Dam in Swabi, Project Haripur, BHPP Mansehra, Dasu Dam, Bhasha Dam and SSU Lines Mardan.
Police officials said communication difficulties had persisted in the past with Chinese engineers and foreign staff due to the language barrier. The trained personnel would now be able to directly communicate security matters and coordinate in Chinese.
Read: Security of foreigners to be beefed up in KP
Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Special Security Unit Syed Ashfaq Anwar told The Express Tribune that SSU personnel had been given formal Chinese language training for the first time in the province.
He said the second batch of officers was also in the final stage of completing the foreign language course.
He said other foreign languages would also be taught to personnel in the future, as effective communication with foreign citizens had become an essential requirement of security alongside modern technology and professional training.

The Top 10 represent Egypt, Kenya, Ethiopia, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, Benin and Côte d’Ivoire, with businesses spanning agriculture, healthcare, manufacturing, enterprise technology, climate technology and education.
These ten entrepreneurs will represent the breadth, ambition and practical problem-solving shaping Africa’s business landscape at the Grand Finale.
Salma Tammam – REME-D Company for Laboratory Equipment and Chemicals (Egypt, Healthcare)
Ahmed Shaaban – Simplex for Software Development and Industrial Solutions (Egypt, Manufacturing)
Kelvin Umechukwu – Bumpa (Nigeria, Enterprise)
Naom Monari – Bena Care Limited (Kenya, HealthTech)
Louisa Gathecha – Bottle Logistics East Africa Ltd (Kenya, Industrial)
Samson Fentaye – Thur Biotech Manufacturing Plc (Ethiopia, Agritech)
Jess Roussos – BluLever Education Pty Ltd (South Africa, EdTech)
Joseph Paul – Dawa Mkononi (Tanzania, HealthTech)
Gildas Zodome – BIO PHYTO (Benin, Agritech)
Appessika Adanin Laurent Koffi – GREEN AGRO VALLEY CI (Côte d’Ivoire, Agritech)
“I started applying to ABH four years ago, and this is the first time I have made it past the application stage. Going through the financials section of the ABH application pushed me to take a much deeper look at the model, and today, it reflects not only my conviction in the business, but also its potential for growth,” said Naom Monari, founder and CEO of Bena Care.
Next stop: Kigali
1–2 December 2026 · Kigali, Rwanda · US$1.5 million in grant funding
The Top 10 will compete at the 2026 ABH Grand Finale for their share of US$1.5 million in grant funding. The Grand Prize winner will receive US$300,000, followed by US$250,000 for the first runner-up and US$150,000 for the second runner-up. Each of the remaining seven finalists will receive US$100,000.
An additional US$100,000 will support global immersion training. Beyond the grants, finalists gain access to mentorship, training, global exposure and the wider ABH Community of entrepreneurs, investors, business leaders and mentors.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Wednesday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.29 and Rs1.11 per litre, respectively, for September 3.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs346.16 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs372.03 per litre for September 3.
The latest revision comes a day after the government increased the price of petrol and HSD by Rs1.08 and 51 paisas per litre, respectively, for September 2.
Read: Govt increases petrol price by Rs1.08, HSD by 51 paisas per litre for Sept 2
On July 17, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, petroleum products constitute one of the country's largest import categories, making the economy highly vulnerable to changes in global crude oil prices. Domestic refineries satisfy only part of national demand, while the remainder is met through imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products. Consequently, every increase in international oil prices raises Pakistan's import bill, pressures foreign exchange reserves, and contributes to inflation.
Pakistan previously exercised significant government control over petroleum pricing through subsidies and administrative interventions. While these measures temporarily protected consumers, they imposed substantial fiscal costs. During periods of elevated global oil prices, successive governments delayed passing price increases to consumers, creating financial pressures for oil marketing companies, refineries, and the national budget. Large fuel subsidies widened fiscal deficits, increased public borrowing, and weakened macroeconomic stability.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Brent crude prices were marginally higher in a volatile session on Wednesday, driven by renewed military ‌strikes between the United States and Iran that have restricted world oil supply.
Brent ​crude futures rose 25 cents to $94.90 a barrel by 10:48 am ET (1448 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures ​were up 10 cents at $90.32.
"While the increase in conflicts will slow transit through the Strait of Hormuz in the near term, the market has absorbed the fact that workaround crude oil supplies can still make it to the market eventually," ​said Dennis Kissler, senior vice president of trading at BOK Financial.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
On an experimentation spree, Walmart-owned Flipkart is now looking to enter the entertainment business with short-form scripted shows, microdramas. Sources told Inc42 that the ecommerce major is looking to partner with startups like Terribly Tiny Tales, Pratilipi, among others, to produce microdramas exclusively for its platform.
Flipkart is also expected to source content from its digital media arm, Pinkvilla, which was acquired in 2025 for an undisclosed amount.
As part of the broader content push, Vivek Mohan Sharma, business head – youth, music & english entertainment at JioStar, has been roped in as the CEO of Pinkvilla, replacing founder Nandini Shenoy, sources told Inc42.
Inc42 has reached out to Flipkart for comment on the development. The story would be updated based on their response. Moneycontrol was the first to report on the development.
The microdrama offering will be integrated into Flipkart’s main app rather than launched as a standalone platform. Flipkart is testing a dedicated microdrama feed within its app, featuring personalised sections such as “Today’s top pick for you”, “Recommended Favourites” and “Flipkart user’s pick”.
The move comes as Flipkart looks to expand beyond ecommerce and build a broader consumer ecosystem around its more than 500 Mn registered users.
Flipkart’s microdrama play could eventually go beyond increasing time spent on the app, with the company potentially looking to connect content consumption with commerce.
“The idea is simple. Flipkart wants to keep users engaged on their app for a long time. Suppose you are watching a piece of content and then crave Diet Coke. You can order it without leaving the app,” said a person aware of the development.
The plans come amid a rapid growth in India’s microdrama market, which is set to reach ₹650 Cr by 2028. Platforms such as Kuku TV, Story TV, DashReels and Quick TV are competing with larger players including JioHotstar and Amazon MX Player.
The microdrama push is part of Flipkart’s broader diversification attempt beyond its mainstay ecommerce platform.
The company entered the quick commerce with Flipkart Minutes in 2024 and has since been exploring other parts of consumers’ daily lives, including food delivery and ticketing for films and live events.
Earlier this year, sources told Inc42 that Flipkart planned to launch its food-delivery service in Bengaluru by mid-August, with restaurants expected to pay a commission of 10-11% on each order. That launch, however, is yet to materialise.
Flipkart has also reportedly been considering an entry into India’s movie and live events ticketing market ahead of a potential IPO. Reuters reported that the company was weighing a separate vertical for the business, setting it up to compete with BookMyShow and Eternal’s District. There has been little visible progress on either front so far.
Taken together, the plans point to an increasingly expansive ambition at Flipkart: to move beyond being a place where people shop and become a platform that captures more of their time, attention and spending. Ecommerce, quick commerce, entertainment, food delivery and ticketing each offer another way of bringing consumers deeper into the same ecosystem.
Flipkart’s Top Deck Churn
Flipkart is also witnessing a fresh round of top deck churn, with two more vice presidents, Prathyusha Agarwal, VP and head of strategy, and Aakriti Chandra, VP overseeing talent recruitment for Ekart, exiting the company.
This takes the total number of VP-level exits to at least four in the past 10 days, Money control reported, citing sources. The exits come amid a broader organisational rejig at Flipkart. Amit Sood, VP of corporate finance and head of investor relations, has taken charge of the finance charter at Ekart.
Earlier, Gunjan Bhartia, senior VP of business finance, and Amer Hussain, VP of supply chain for Flipkart Grocery and Minutes.
The departures follow several other senior-level changes across the Flipkart group, including CEO Nandita Sinha’s exit from Myntra and Flipkart Group CFO Sriram Venkatraman stepping down.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Fintech platform Pine Labs has appointed ex-Razorpay SVP Jayaram Karthik as its COO, as the company looks to strengthen its operational capabilities and support its next phase of growth.
Karthik will lead operations and merchant experiences across India and Pine Labs’ international markets. His mandate will include building technology-enabled operating models aimed at creating seamless, trusted and locally relevant experiences for merchants.
Prior to joining Pine Labs, Karthik served as the SVP of business operations for rival payments startup Razorpay for over half a decade. Before that, he held senior operating roles at American Express, Citibank, Amazon, and Tata Play.
Pine Labs CEO Amrish Rau said the fintech’s future growth will depend not only on its products but also on how effectively technology and operations are integrated to deliver customer experiences.
The company currently operates across more than 20 countries, making operational standardisation increasingly important as it expands its global footprint, Rau added.
Karthik said his focus at Pine Labs would be on simplifying customer experiences by bringing technology, operations, and experience together.
The appointment comes as Pine Labs continues to build its international presence. Its international business grew at a 44% CAGR over the past three years and contributed around 15% of revenue in FY26. Its international revenue crossed ₹400 Cr during the year.
In FY26, the company reported revenue from operations of ₹2,711 Cr, up 19% YoY, while adjusted EBITDA rose 57% to ₹559 Cr. It reported a net profit of ₹113 Cr as against a loss of ₹145 Cr in FY25.
In the June quarter of the ongoing fiscal, its consolidated revenue from operations rose 19.6% YoY to ₹736.9 Cr, while net profit more than quadrupled to ₹19.6 Cr. Sequentially, the company’s profit declined 67% from ₹59.4 Cr.
Pine Labs has also been expanding its product portfolio. It recently launched the Pine Labs Payment Protocol (P3P), which is an infrastructure layer allowing AI agents to make UPI payments autonomously after a consumer authorises a mandate. The company is also working to extend the protocol to card payments. It has also developed SignalIQ, an AI-powered bank statement analyser and underwriting engine.
Pine Labs is also looking to embed AI across both its internal operations and customer-facing products. The company invested around ₹24 Cr in AI and R&D initiatives in FY26, including ₹20 Cr towards AI capabilities, technology infrastructure and process automation, and another ₹4 Cr on technologies such as MCP and RAG.
These investments have helped cut software testing cycle times by more than 95%, while Pine Labs estimates a 25% improvement in developer productivity and an 80% reduction in initial incident analysis time.

items.content:
Dalam sebuah acara peluncuran yang digelar kemarin malam (1/9), POCO resmi memperkenalkan flagship terbaiknya menuju akhir tahun 2026. Menemani F9 Pro, POCO F9 Ultra tampil identik seperti generasi sebelumnya. Dan meski masih memiliki banyak kesamaan, ada sejumlah poin peningkatan spesifikasi yang membuatnya semakin menarik untuk bersaing dengan flagship rilisan 2026 lainnya.
Ya, aspek performa POCO F9 Ultra memang masih sama seperti generasi sebelumnya, mengusung cip terbaik dari Qualcomm rilisan akhir tahun kemarin. Peluncuran F Ultra tahun ini memang lebih cepat, sehingga membuat POCO masih menggunakan cip generasi akhir tahun lalu, mengingat gelaran Snapdragon Summit tahun ini masih belum digelar—notabene menjadi ajang pengenalan cip generasi berikutnya.
Selain POCO F9 Ultra, juga hadir POCO F9 Pro yang pakai cip serupa namun berbeda, yakni Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V. Ya, punya satu imbuhan huruf tambahan di belakangnya, cip tersebut memiliki perbedaan pada jumlah GPU yang berkurang satu, bila dibandingkan dengan Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 standar. Lalu apa saja peningkatan spesifikasi POCO F9 Ultra?
Baca juga: POCO X8 Resmi Meluncur Global, Bawa Baterai Jumbo 8.340 mAh
Skor Antutu POCO F9 Ultra Meningkat Meski Chipset Sama
Setidaknya ada empat aspek penyegaran yang dibawa lewat POCO F9 Ultra bila dibandingkan dengan generasi sebelumnya. Ya, smartphone POCO terbaru satu ini tetap mengusung setup speaker yang diperkuat oleh BOSE. Selain membawa speaker stereo dengan output simetris, pada sisi belakang juga tetap disematkan sebuah woofer khusus untuk dentuman yang lebih menggelegar, meningkatkan pengalaman baik saat bermain game maupun akses konten hiburan favorit.
Ya, performa POCO F9 Ultra tetap didukung oleh cip Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, dipasangkan bersama RAM LPDDR5x, penyimpanan UFS 4.1, dan cip VisionBoost D8 khusus yang secara khusus membantu meningkatkan performa grafis. Menariknya, meski hardware tetap sama, POCO mengklaim skor Antutu POCO F9 Ultra bisa melampaui 4,1 juta poin, alias lebih tinggi sekitar 200 ribu poin bila dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya.
Dan untuk pengalaman main game yang lebih mulus, layar POCO F9 Ultra kini mendukung refresh rate maksimum sampai 185Hz, tetap berukuran 6,9 inci dengan tingkat kecerahan maksimum 4500 nits dan dukungan warna 12-bit. Memanfaatkan optimalisasi software hingga interpolasi, sejumlah judul game bisa berjalan dalam 185fps. POCO juga gunakan panel berjenis M11 yang diklaim lebih efisien daya, sekaligus punya masa pakai lebih awet.
Dan untuk meningkatkan pengalaman gaming, kapasitas baterai POCO F9 Ultra juga meningkat, kini mencapai 8050 mAh. POCO mengklaim hingga dua hari penggunaan penuh, dengan masa pakai baterai tetap normal sampai enam tahun. Mendukung teknologi fast charging 100W, hanya membutuhkan waktu 50 menit untuk mengisi daya sampai penuh. Plus, bisa difungsikan sebagai powerbank, bisa mengantar daya sampai 27W atau bahkan 22.5W secara nirkabel lewat teknologi reverse wireless charging.
Perkuat Fitur Fotografi dengan Sensor Beresolusi Ultra Tinggi
Berkat kapasitas baterai yang jauh lebih besar, dimensi POCO F9 Ultra sejatinya sedikit lebih bongsor dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya, sehingga meski identik tidak bisa menggunakan aksesori seperti case yang sama. Faktor satu ini mungkin juga karena spesifikasi kamera yang juga ditingkatkan, di mana sensor utamanya bawa resolusi empat kali lebih besar secara angka.
Ya, kamera POCO F9 Ultra mengusung sensor utama 200MP f/1.68 dengan OIS, pertama dalam sejarah smartphone POCO. Tetap dipasangkan dengan sensor telefoto 50MP OIS yang memberikan 5x optical zoom, serta ultra-wide 50MP dan kamera selfie 32MP. POCO juga sematkan fitur live cinematography khusus dengan teknik zoom otomatis.
Pada sekeliling woofer belakang POCO F9 Ultra, kini juga disematkan dynamic light khusus yang bisa dimanfaatkan sebagai penanda notifikasi. Sudah diluncurkan untuk pasar global, harga POCO F9 Ultra dibanderol mulai USD729 atau sekitar Rp12,9 jutaan, di mana harga tersebut merupakan harga khusus periode penjualan perdana untuk varian 12+256GB. Sementara opsi tertinggi 16GB+1TB, dibanderol USD1059 (Rp18,8 jutaan). Menurut Gizmo friends, apakah smartphone POCO terbaik akhir 2026 satu ini tetap menarik bila dijual dalam harga yang cukup tinggi tersebut?

items.author: Onsa Mustafa

Xiaomi has highlighted the durability and long-term battery performance of the new phone. Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G is backed by TÜV SÜD 5-star Battery Performance Certification, giving the device an added focus on reliability and battery health over time.
The certification is part of Xiaomi’s new REDMI Titan Quality approach. The company says this system is designed to make its smartphones more dependable during everyday use and over several years of ownership.
Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G Earns TÜV SÜD 5-Star Battery Performance Certification
The Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G has been tested for several areas that directly affect battery reliability. These include battery endurance, long-term battery health, durability, and performance under different temperatures.
The TÜV SÜD 5-star Battery Performance Certification is based on testing that examines how the battery performs through repeated charging cycles and demanding conditions. Xiaomi says the certification is intended to give users greater confidence that the phone can maintain reliable battery performance over time.
The Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G is equipped with a large 8,340mAh battery. It also supports 67W HyperCharge, allowing users to recharge the phone quickly when they need more power.
Designed to Last for Years
Battery health is a major part of the Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G’s long-term durability. Xiaomi says the battery can retain at least 80% of its original capacity after 1,600 charging cycles. The company equates this to around six years of typical use.
This means the phone is not only designed to offer long battery life when new but also to maintain useful battery capacity after years of regular charging.
The phone is also part of Xiaomi’s broader REDMI Titan Quality program. This approach focuses on the areas users depend on most, including battery performance, physical durability, and resistance to everyday conditions.
Built for Everyday Conditions
The Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G also comes with stronger protection against water and dust. Xiaomi says the Pro models feature IP66, IP68, IP69, and IP69K ratings.
The device has also passed Xiaomi’s 2-meter, 72-hour water-resistance test. It includes Underwater Mode, which is designed to make certain phone functions easier to use in underwater conditions.
Wet Touch Technology 2.0 is another durability-focused feature. It helps the display remain responsive when the screen is exposed to water, sweat, oil, or foam.

REDMI Titan Quality
With TÜV SÜD 5-star Battery Performance Certification, the Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G puts battery reliability at the center of its durability claims. The certification covers more than basic battery capacity, focusing on endurance, long-term health, durability, and temperature reliability.
Xiaomi is positioning the Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G as a smartphone designed for long-term ownership. Its large battery, fast charging, durability features, and certified battery performance all support the company’s “Built for Years” philosophy.
The message behind REDMI Titan Quality is simple: the Redmi Note 17 Pro 5G is designed not just to perform well on day one, but to remain dependable as users continue to rely on it over the years.

Inside 88-Year-Old Jagdish Farshan’s ₹43.5 Cr Bet On Quick Commerce

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
For nearly nine decades, Vadodara-based Jagdish Farshan has built its business on physical stores selling Gujarati snacks and sweets. Now, the legacy brand is turning to quick commerce to power its next phase of growth.
Jagdish Farshan has raised ₹43.5 Cr (about $4.6 Mn) in a Series A funding round led by Sharrp Ventures, the investment office of Marico founder Harsh Mariwala, along with a group of angel investors. The fundraise marks its first institutional capital raise since it was established in 1938.
The company plans to use the capital to expand its manufacturing capacity and retail distribution, and deepen its presence across quick commerce as it looks to take Gujarati snacks beyond its home market.
Jagdish Farshan currently operates 27 retail outlets, largely concentrated in central Gujarat, besides two outlets in North America. It plans to add 30-40 stores over the next two years, initially deepening its presence across Gujarat before expanding its distribution network to Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and other markets.
The larger ambition, however, is to build a pan-India presence through quick commerce.
The company is already present on Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart in Gujarat, and on BigBasket in Gujarat, Mumbai, and Pune. It also sells through its D2C website. Digital sales and exports currently account for around 15% of its revenue, while its retail business contributes the remaining 85%.
Jagdish Farshan CEO Aakash Kandoi told Inc42 that the company sees a larger opportunity in quick commerce, particularly because the longer delivery timelines associated with conventional ecommerce and D2C are less suited to impulse-led snack purchases.
“Food is something which is more like craving based. You want to eat it right then and there,” Kandoi said.
Cracking The Quick-Commerce Shelf
Jagdish Farshan is adapting its product sizes and price points for quick commerce. While mass-market namkeen brands typically sell packs priced between ₹10 and ₹40 on these platforms, the company is positioning itself in a more premium segment.
Its smallest quick-commerce pack weighs 100 grams, compared with its traditional 250-gram and 500-gram packs. Its 250-gram packs are priced between ₹110 and ₹140.
Kandoi said the company initially listed its conventional pack sizes on quick-commerce platforms but later realised that the channel required a different approach. Smaller packs, he added, lower the barrier for consumers looking to try its products.
As Jagdish Farshan expands across quick commerce and enters new markets, it is also increasing its manufacturing capacity. The company is setting up a 2.5-3 Lakh sq ft facility in Vadodara, which is expected to become operational by July next year.
Kandoi said the company is currently operating at 90% capacity, making additional manufacturing capacity critical as it enters new markets. It also plans to expand into organised general trade and modern trade.
Despite digital distribution emerging as an important growth lever, Jagdish Farshan is not abandoning its physical footprint. Its stores typically span 2,500-3,000 sq ft and combine retail with dining and a QSR format serving Gujarati delicacies such as dhokla and patra.
The company has operated its D2C website for around eight years and began performance marketing about three years ago. The website currently clocks around 250-300 orders a day. However, Kandoi said the company is not aggressively pushing its products through conventional ecommerce marketplaces.
A Legacy Brand Goes Digital
Jagdish Farshan’s digital push reflects a broader shift among India’s legacy consumer brands, which are increasingly using D2C, ecommerce, and quick commerce to expand beyond their traditional geographic markets.
Wagh Bakri, the century-old tea brand, launched its D2C website in 2015 and entered ecommerce marketplaces in 2016. It sharpened its focus on ecommerce and quick commerce after the pandemic. Digital channels now account for around 8% of its revenue and are its fastest-growing distribution channel.
Similarly, Neeru’s, which began as a tailoring shop in 1971, entered ecommerce during the Covid-19 pandemic after its brick-and-mortar business was hit. It subsequently built its own D2C channel, with online sales now accounting for around 25–30% of its business.
Established in 1938, Jagdish Farshan now offers more than 500 products and SKUs across traditional snacks, namkeen, and sweets.
Kandoi said the company has grown at a CAGR of 45% over the past five years, with the expansion funded entirely through internal accruals. The latest fundraise is intended to accelerate this growth.
He added that Jagdish Farshan was seeking an operating partner alongside capital as it prepares to move from a largely regional business to a pan-India consumer brand. Sharrp Ventures’ experience backing food and beverage brands such as Slurrp Farm, Bira 91, Troovy, and Protein Pantry, coupled with Harsh Mariwala’s experience building Marico, made it an attractive investor, he said.

items.author: Fahad Khan
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A one-hour bus ride from Lahore to Islamabad on a Jazz 4G connection can burn through half a gigabyte just buffering a single YouTube video. For students in smaller towns where fiber hasn’t reached yet, that same video might not load at all during peak hours. Saving it once, at home, on a working connection, solves both problems in one step.
Why People Download YouTube Videos for Offline Use
Package-based mobile data in Pakistan runs out fast when video is involved. A 20-minute tutorial can eat 300-500MB depending on resolution, and most daily internet bundles don’t stretch that far once messaging apps and social feeds take their share.
Travel is the other common trigger. Long intercity bus routes, train journeys through areas with patchy PTCL towers, or even flights where in-flight Wi-Fi isn’t an option all push people toward saving content in advance. Students preparing for exams also save lecture videos so they aren’t dependent on connection quality the night before a test.
YouTube’s Own Offline Feature
YouTube Premium lets subscribers download videos directly inside the app for offline playback. The video stays encrypted within YouTube’s own player, so it can’t be moved to a phone’s gallery, shared as a file, or opened in another app.
That restriction matters for anyone who wants a video available even after uninstalling the app, or who wants to transfer it to a laptop for offline editing or classroom use. Premium’s offline mode solves temporary connectivity gaps well. It doesn’t solve permanent file ownership.
Third-Party Methods to Download YouTube Videos
Browser extensions are one route, though many require constant updates whenever YouTube changes its page structure, and some come bundled with ad-injection scripts that are hard to uninstall cleanly. Dedicated desktop apps avoid that update problem but ask for installation permissions that not everyone wants to grant on a shared or work computer.
For a lighter option, a youtube link downloader skips both issues since it runs in the browser itself. You paste the video’s URL, the site fetches the available formats, and there’s nothing left behind on the device once the download finishes.
Step-by-Step: How to Download a YouTube Video Using an Online Tool
Open the YouTube video and copy its link from the address bar or the Share button.
Go to the downloader website and paste the link into the input box.
Choose a format. MP4 works for anyone who wants to keep watching the video normally, while MP3 is for saving just the audio.
Select a resolution if the tool offers one, then tap download and wait for the file to save to the device.
Lower resolutions finish faster and take up less storage, which matters most on phones with 32GB or 64GB of space where every video adds up quickly.
Is It Legal to Download YouTube Videos?
YouTube’s terms of service don’t permit downloading videos outside the app’s own offline feature, regardless of intent. Saving a video for personal, private viewing carries low practical risk. Re-uploading it elsewhere, monetizing it, or distributing it publicly is where creators and platforms actually take action, since that’s where their content or income is directly affected.
Educational and how-to content usually falls into a gray area that rights holders rarely pursue for individual downloads. Music videos and copyrighted film clips are a different case, and downloading those for anything beyond private use carries more real risk.
Tips to Download Videos Safely
Stick to tools that don’t ask for app installation or account sign-in just to save a video. Legitimate downloaders complete the job through the browser alone.
Pop-up ads are common on free tools since that’s usually how they stay funded. Closing them without clicking anywhere inside the ad window avoids most of the redirect traps that lead to spam sites. On storage, MP4 files at 720p typically run 50-100MB for a 10-minute video, so clearing out old downloads every few weeks keeps a budget phone from filling up.
Conclusion
Offline YouTube access in Pakistan comes down to picking the method that fits the situation. Premium works for anyone already paying for the subscription. A browser-based downloader works for anyone who just needs a specific video saved without extra software or a recurring cost.

Menyasar untuk mahasiswa dan profesional muda yang butuh tablet untuk bekerja, belajar, menikmati hiburan, dan bermain game, Infinix XPAD 30 tampil dengan ukuran layar beresolusi 2.5K, chipset tangguh, dan kapasitas baterai lega.
Country Manager Infinix Indonesia, Tommy Xiong, mengatakan perangkat tersebut dirancang untuk mengikuti pola aktivitas generasi muda yang kerap berubah sepanjang hari.
“Generasi muda Indonesia menjalani keseharian sangat dinamis. Dalam satu perangkat, mereka membutuhkan ruang nyaman untuk belajar dan bekerja, sekaligus performa dapat mengikuti kebutuhan hiburan dan gaming,” ujar Tommy dalam keterangan resmi, Rabu (2/9/2026).
Ia menambahkan, “kami ingin membantu mereka tetap siap menghadapi setiap aktivitas, ketika rencana berubah secara tidak terduga. Inilah makna BE UNXPADTED yang kami hadirkan.”
Spesifikasi Infinix XPAD 30 Pro, Seperti Apa?
Inifinix melengkapi tablet Android barunya ini dengan layar 11 inci beresolusi 2.5K, diklaim memberikan ruang lebih luas dan detail dengan visual lebih tajam saat pengguna membaca materi, menyusun presentasi, mengikuti kelas, menonton, atau bermain game.
Dari sisi performa, spesifikasi Infinix XPAD 30 Pro sudah ditopang oleh chipset Helio G200 Ultimate milik MediaTek. Perusahaan menyebutkan, ada alasan kenapa chip ini dipilih untuk tablet baru Infinix.
“Chipset ini dipilih untuk mendukung aktivitas belajar, multitasking, hiburan, dan gaming dalam satu perangkat,” ungkap Infinix.
Meski demikian, perusahaan belum mengungkap konfigurasi RAM dan penyimpanan Infinix XPAD 30 Pro yang akan dipasarkan di Indonesia. Detail mengenai refresh rate layar, dukungan aksesori produktivitas, kamera, konektivitas, serta sistem operasi juga belum tercantum dalam teaser awal.
Infinix XPAD 30 Pro akan dibekali baterai berkapasitas besar. Namun, angka kapasitas dan kemampuan pengisian daya belum diumumkan. Karena itu, klaim mengenai daya tahan penggunaan masih perlu menunggu spesifikasi lengkap dan pengujian setelah perangkat tersedia.
Kapan dan Berapa Harga Infinix XPAD 30 Pro?
Infinix XPAD 30 Pro akan diperkenalkan melalui kanal digital resmi Infinix Indonesia pada 8 September 2026. Penjualan online dimulai sehari kemudian, 9 September 2026 pukul 00.00 WIB, melalui sejumlah platform e-commerce dan mitra resmi perusahaan di Indonesia.
Harga Infinix XPAD 30 Pro juga belum diumumkan. Konfigurasi memori dan spesifikasi lengkap masih menunggu konfirmasi Infinix dalam acara peluncuran.
Infinix Luncurkan TV X5Q 43 Inci
Di sisi lain, Infinix resmi meluncurkan jajaran produk AIoT terbarunya di Indonesia, termasuk televisi cerdas Infinix TV X5Q 43″ yang dibanderol dengan harga kompetitif di kisaran Rp 3 jutaan.
Kehadiran produk televisi ini ditemani oleh serangkaian perangkat pintar lainnya, yaitu penyuara telinga XBUDS H5, bank daya GTPOWER POD 10K, serta kipas portabel XPOCKET FAN dan XPOCKET FAN Pro. Rangkaian peluncuran ini menegaskan langkah strategis Infinix dalam berekspansi di luar pasar ponsel pintar demi membangun ekosistem gaya hidup digital yang menyeluruh bagi pelanggannya.
“TV kini telah menjadi pusat hiburan di rumah, sehingga pengguna semakin menginginkan kualitas visual yang lebih baik, pengalaman yang lebih cerdas, dan akses hiburan yang lebih praktis tanpa harus membayar mahal,” ujar Tommy Xiong selaku Country Manager Infinix Indonesia.
“TV X5Q 43 inci kami hadirkan untuk menjawab kebutuhan tersebut melalui kombinasi teknologi QLED, Google TV 5.0, dan Dolby Audio di kisaran harga Rp 3 jutaan. Bersamaan dengan peluncuran ini, Infinix juga terus memperluas portofolio AIOT untuk menghadirkan lebih banyak pilihan perangkat yang mendukung gaya hidup digital masyarakat Indonesia,” sambungnya.
Perangkat televisi ini dirancang khusus untuk memadukan kecanggihan teknologi kecerdasan buatan, kualitas visual premium, dan antarmuka sistem hiburan terpadu. Kinerja utamanya ditopang oleh cip khusus bernama AI-Powered HyperEngine yang bertugas mengoptimalkan kontras gambar dan output suara secara otomatis agar tayangan terasa lebih hidup.
Sektor visualnya memanjakan mata melalui panel layar seluas 43 inci beresolusi Full HD yang sudah menggunakan teknologi layar sentuh QLED dan panel IPS. Desain fisiknya terlihat sangat modern dengan bingkai metalik super tipis (frameless metallic) yang membuat rasio layar-ke-bodi perangkat ini mencapai persentase 96%. Kombinasi spesifikasi kelas atas tersebut, ditambah dukungan fitur HDR10, memungkinkan panel ini memancarkan lebih dari satu miliar warna dengan tingkat kontras yang tajam.

items.content:
Veteran film star George Clooney said on Wednesday the United States would surmount an "unfortunate" time in its history under the Trump administration, calling it a government run by the "least qualified people".
Clooney spoke to the media on the opening day of the Venice Film Festival, where he is to be awarded a Golden Lion for career achievement. In a press conference that touched on his career, artificial intelligence, climate change and the state of the filmmaking industry, Clooney expressed feeling "ashamed" over the US government.
"I do believe... we're at a moment in time that's unfortunate. I think that's an understatement," said the 65-year-old star, who has spoken out against the Trump administration in the past. "There's a great word, a kakistocracy, which is a country run by the least qualified people. I think maybe we have a kakistocracy right now, but we'll get through it," he said.
Midterm elections in November may provide a "check and balance", he said, while "in 2028 with any luck we'll have some restoration into some normalcy," said Clooney.
Calling himself an optimist, Clooney said he remembered living through other dark times in the country's history. "I'm old enough to have been through 1968 in the States when every city in the United States was set on fire, and we lost Martin Luther King and Bobby Kennedy in the same year," he said.
"There was tons of violence. The Capitol was surrounded with tanks," he said.
"We've had some other difficult times, but this is one of them." He cited a tweet posted this week by US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth appearing to mock the physical appearance of an overweight female Canadian soldier presenting a medal at a youth camp.
"Where's the sense of decency in all of this? And I'm ashamed of all of that, but we will get through it," said Clooney. "And we will come out better on the other side."

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Punjab Assembly has unanimously passed a resolution calling for legislation to prevent children under the age of 16 from creating or maintaining social media accounts.
Moved by government MPA Sarah Ahmed, the resolution urged the federal government to introduce a legal framework restricting social media access for under-16s and establishing stronger safeguards for children online.
The assembly has also called on the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) to develop an effective age-verification mechanism for social media platforms. The proposed system would be designed to verify users’ ages and prevent children below 16 from opening or maintaining accounts.
Lawmakers said the state has a responsibility to protect children’s physical, mental, psychological, and moral well-being, particularly as social media exposure continues to grow.
The resolution highlighted several risks faced by children online, including cyberbullying, sexual exploitation, and exposure to inappropriate content. It also raised concerns over mental stress and other problems associated with excessive social media use.
Social media platforms urged to protect children
The Punjab Assembly also called for greater responsibility from social media companies, urging them to take steps to prevent harmful content from reaching children and provide a safer digital environment for young users.
The resolution referred to regulatory measures adopted in countries including Australia, France, China, and the United States, saying Pakistan should also introduce legislation to strengthen protections for children online.
Alongside legal restrictions, lawmakers called for digital awareness campaigns involving federal and provincial institutions. These initiatives would educate parents, teachers and children about responsible internet use, online risks and digital safety.
The assembly also stressed the need for greater coordination between federal and provincial authorities to establish a comprehensive system for protecting children in the digital space.
However, the resolution itself does not immediately impose a ban on children under 16 using social media. Any such restriction would require the federal government and Parliament to introduce and pass the necessary legislation.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Healthcare supply chain startup DocPharma has raised $2 Mn (₹19 Cr) in a Pre-Series A funding round led by Equentis, with participation from existing backer 100Unicorns, along with angel investment network Vinners and a host of undisclosed angel investors.
The startup plans to use the fresh capital to fuel expansion to 50 cities across India as well as setting up 100 new licensed dark stores.
Founded by Saquib Ali, Shashank Rai and Sagar Chauhan in 2024, DocPharma operates a quick commerce supply chain network catering to healthcare businesses, acting as a backend infrastructure for healthcare platforms.
At its core is its proprietary platform, DocPharma One, which combines warehouse management, inventory intelligence, order management and fulfillment operations.
Its dark stores carry more than 40,000 SKUs each and are supported by an AI-driven and pharmacist-led compliance infrastructure.
Its network of licensed dark stores and SaaS platform enables pharmacies, health insurers, hospitals, D2C wellness and nutraceutical brands, and pet care businesses to fulfil healthcare orders in under 30 minutes.
The startup claims that its infrastructure enables the delivery of medicines and healthcare products without requiring partner platforms to build and operate their own supply chains.
“We built this supply chain rule by rule, one licensed dark store at a time, and that discipline is what lets it hold up as we scale into 50 cities,” Rai said.
Currently, DocPharma operates across more than 12 cities and claims to have fulfilled over 8 Lakh orders with a fulfilment rate of more than 95%.
The development comes at a time when vertical quick commerce has been seeing a rapid growth, specifically in areas of quick pharma deliveries.
Investors are also bullish in expansion of these businesses. For instance, quick medicine delivery startup Plazza raised $15 Mn in a Series A funding round to strengthen its technology platform and deepen its AI-led inventory and assortment capabilities.

items.summary:
